metadata.source: GeoGuessr Official Complete Client Clue Catalog

CO.title: Yellow license plate
CO.description: In South America, yellow license plates are almost unique to Colombia.

CO.title: Language
CO.description: Colombia uses Spanish, as does most other countries in South America.

CO.title: Licenseplates
CO.description: Looking at license plates can help you find your way in the world. Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow plates.

CO.title: Taxi
CO.description: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.

CO.title: Colombian Cross
CO.description: In Colombia, signposts have white backs that form a cross shape, known as the Colombian Cross.

CO.title: Painted poles
CO.description: Colombian poles can be found painted with black-yellow-black stripes.

CO.title: Rickety fences
CO.description: It is common to find wooden fences in Colombia, often made from various pieces of wood.

CO.title: Yellow plates
CO.description: Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow license plates for personal vehicles.

CO.title: Kilometre Markers
CO.description: Two designs exist: a tall green post labelled 'Pr' and a stone marker with black lettering, both exclusive to Colombia.

CO.title: Concrete and Dark Poles
CO.description: Most poles are concrete, with dark-coloured poles more common here than nearby countries.

CO.title: Northern Arid Landscape
CO.description: The far north features pale, sandy ground and a dry, barren environment.

CO.title: Llanos Lowlands
CO.description: A broad flat plain east of the Andes with tropical grassland, savanna, and isolated trees.

CO.title: Antioquia Pole Markings
CO.description: Poles with narrow black bands top and bottom and a broad yellow middle are characteristic of Antioquia.

CO.title: Afro-Colombian Pacific Coast
CO.description: The Pacific coastline has a predominantly Afro-Colombian population.

CO.title: Leticia Vehicle
CO.description: A distinctive non-standard vehicle is used around Leticia, Colombia's southernmost Amazon settlement.

CO.title: La Guajira Desert
CO.description: Arid scrubland with scattered cacti; a highway from Uribia to Puerto Bolívar runs parallel to a railway line.

CO.title: Country Flag
CO.description: The national flag of Colombia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CO.title: .co Domain
CO.description: Web addresses in Colombia end in the country domain .co (often as .com.co). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

GLOBAL.title: Capital
GLOBAL.description: Learning the capitals of countries is a great tool when trying to make a good guess. You can often find signs pointing towards them.

GLOBAL.title: Flags
GLOBAL.description: Flags are usually found in the country they represent. Learning them can be very beneficial to figure out where you are.

GLOBAL.title: Language
GLOBAL.description: Most European countries use the latin alphabet. Greece is one of the outliers that uses their own unique set of letters, the Greek alphabet!

GLOBAL.title: Bollards
GLOBAL.description: Bollards (small road side poles) usually differs between countries. Learning details like this can make you a great guesser.

GLOBAL.title: Language
GLOBAL.description: Use language to your strength. Most languages have unique or prominent letters. The Swedish language uses the letters “Å, Ä and Ö” for example.

GLOBAL.title: Licenseplate
GLOBAL.description: Most countries in Europe use similar license plates with a blue strip to the left. Sweden included.

GLOBAL.title: No_plates_01
GLOBAL.description: In Norway, commercial license plates are green, and are often seen on vans.

GLOBAL.title: On The Right
GLOBAL.description: Vehicles drive on the right

GLOBAL.title: On The Left
GLOBAL.description: Vehicles drive on the left

GLOBAL.title: Great Basin
GLOBAL.description: Dry, open plains with scattered sagebrush and distant high mountain ranges in western and central Utah.

GLOBAL.title: General 01 Black And Yellow Signposts
GLOBAL.description: If you're in southern Africa and come across this, you know you're in Botswana.

GLOBAL.title: General 01 Street Signs
GLOBAL.description: Street names in Hungary usually end with the word "utca".

GLOBAL.title: General 01 Dashed Outer Lines
GLOBAL.description: Irish roads often have dashed yellow outlines.

GLOBAL.title: General 01 02 Overhead Arrows
GLOBAL.description: This arrow above the road marks the road during heavy snow and is mainly seen in Hokkaido.

GLOBAL.title: General 01 Road Lines
GLOBAL.description: Like many countries in Southern Africa, Namibia uses roads with single yellow outer lines and white center lines.

GLOBAL.title: Flag
GLOBAL.description: Red field with a yellow Nordic cross offset toward the hoist. Commonly flown throughout Skåne on flagpoles, homes, and businesses.

GLOBAL.title: Sun visible to the south
GLOBAL.description: The sun appears toward the south, which usually points to a northern-hemisphere location.

GLOBAL.title: Sun visible to the north
GLOBAL.description: The sun appears toward the north, which usually points to a southern-hemisphere location.

GLOBAL.title: Sun visible overhead
GLOBAL.description: The sun appears high overhead, which usually points to a location near the tropics.

GLOBAL.title: Vehicles drive on the left
GLOBAL.description: Traffic here appears to drive on the left side of the road.

GLOBAL.title: Vehicles drive on the right
GLOBAL.description: Traffic here appears to drive on the right side of the road.

BR.title: Portuguese
BR.description: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It uses letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.

BR.title: Soil
BR.description: The color of the soil can help you guess! This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.

BR.title: States
BR.description: Finding state abbreviations is common in Brazil. PR stands for Paraná. The abbreviations can be seen on the map when zoomed out.

BR.title: Ladder poles
BR.description: The poles you often see in Brazil have a ladder-like design at the base. They have horizontal sections near the bottom.

BR.title: Black signs
BR.description: Most road signs in Brazil have black backsides.

BR.title: Phone numbers
BR.description: Phone numbers in Brazil often include an area code as a separate two-digit prefix.

BR.title: Licence Plates
BR.description: Pre-2018 plates were plain white; current plates have a blue strip on top; commercial plates are red.

BR.title: Language 01 Portuguese
BR.description: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It has the letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.

BR.title: Red soil
BR.description: This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.

BR.title: Blue Kilometre Markers
BR.description: Small blue roadside posts show the route number and current kilometre.

BR.title: Chevrons
BR.description: Brazilian curve signs use yellow arrows on black boards.

BR.title: Road Markings
BR.description: Centre lines are typically double solid yellow; edge lines are white.

BR.title: White-Painted Kerbs
BR.description: Kerbstones along Brazilian roads are frequently painted white.

BR.title: Orange Roof Tiles
BR.description: Terracotta-orange clay tiles are standard roofing material nationwide.

BR.title: Transparent Satellite Dishes
BR.description: Clear or translucent satellite dishes on rooftops are common and unique in Latin America.

BR.title: Fortlev Water Tanks
BR.description: Blue Fortlev-branded rooftop water tanks are common on Brazilian homes.

BR.title: Misc 01 Phone Numbers
BR.description: Phone numbers in Brazil often include an area code as a separate two-digit prefix.

BR.title: States
BR.description: Finding state abbreviations is common in Brazil. The abbreviations can be seen on the map on certain zoom levels.

BR.title: Postcodes (CEP)
BR.description: Postal codes on street signs start with two digits indicating region or state.

BR.title: Elevation Map
BR.description: Brazil's tallest peaks cluster near the southeast coast; interior states are flatter.

BR.title: Caatinga
BR.description: Northeast interior features dry soil, thorny scrub, and succulents of the Caatinga biome.

BR.title: Amazon Rainforest
BR.description: Amazon covers 40% of Brazil with few roads through dense forest or grassy hills.

BR.title: Acre Landscape
BR.description: Acre has low grassy mounds with thinly spaced trees and roads cresting hills.

BR.title: Roraima Plains
BR.description: Roraima features expansive grasslands with wispy grass in discrete clumps and distant mountains.

BR.title: Rio Grande do Sul
BR.description: Landscape alternates between rolling hills and flat green pastures.

BR.title: Southeastern Rolling Hills
BR.description: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and Espírito Santo have gentle grass-covered rolling hills.

BR.title: Exposed Rock Mountains
BR.description: Tall mountains with bare rock faces are common in Espírito Santo and nearby regions.

BR.title: Paraná Pines
BR.description: Araucaria trees have long horizontal branches with foliage clustered at tips, found in Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.

BR.title: Coconut Palms
BR.description: Tall slender palms with long fronds grow along the northeastern coast.

BR.title: Carnaúba Palms
BR.description: Palms with compact fan-shaped leaves and spiky lower trunks, concentrated in Ceará.

BR.title: Babassu Palms
BR.description: Large palms with heavy leaflet fronds found throughout the Amazon and eastern seaboard.

BR.title: Açaí Palms
BR.description: Thin-trunked palms with downward-hanging leaflets, abundant around Belém and the Amazon basin.

BR.title: Moriche Palms
BR.description: Palms with broad, rounded fan-shaped leaves, concentrated in Amazonas, Acre, and Roraima.

BR.title: Macaw Palms
BR.description: Narrow-leaved palms with pointed spear-shaped crowns, common around Mato Grosso do Sul.

BR.title: Long-Stemmed Plants
BR.description: Tall, erect stems topped by upward-growing leaf clusters, characteristic of Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, and Paraíba.

BR.title: Tall Roadside Grass
BR.description: Exceptionally tall grass flanking roads in Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais.

BR.title: Eucalyptus Plantations
BR.description: Rows of extremely tall, straight Eucalyptus Grandis trees across southern Brazil and some in Amapá.

BR.title: Sugarcane
BR.description: Sugarcane fields concentrated in São Paulo and the northeastern coast, especially Alagoas and Pernambuco.

BR.title: Soybean Fields
BR.description: Low, bushy soybean crops in Mato Grosso, Paraná, and Goiás.

BR.title: Coffee Plantations
BR.description: Coffee cultivation dominated by Minas Gerais, with areas in Espírito Santo and northeastern São Paulo.

BR.title: Round Concrete Poles
BR.description: Cylindrical concrete poles common in southern states and São Paulo; large cities use round poles.

BR.title: Wooden Poles
BR.description: Timber utility poles prevalent in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas, and Rio de Janeiro.

BR.title: Bahia and Pernambuco Pole IDs
BR.description: Poles marked with yellow paint and black alphanumeric codes starting with a letter.

BR.title: Goiás Pole IDs
BR.description: Yellow-on-black painted codes starting with a digit, sometimes on plates.

BR.title: RN and PE Small Pole Plates
BR.description: Small yellow or orange ID plates fastened to poles in Rio Grande do Norte and Pernambuco.

BR.title: Paraná Pole IDs
BR.description: Poles identified by a painted black rectangle with yellow or white text.

BR.title: Maranhão Embedded Pole Plates
BR.description: Small beige numbered plates moulded into concrete poles, mostly in Maranhão.

BR.title: Paraná Street Name Poles
BR.description: Street names sometimes painted directly on utility poles at intersections in Paraná.

BR.title: São Paulo Asymmetric Pole Top
BR.description: Off-centre crossarm with diagonal support common in São Paulo and some other states.

BR.title: Ceará and Rondônia Unsupported Crossbar
BR.description: Asymmetric crossarm with no bracing exclusive to Ceará and Rondônia.

BR.title: Ceará and Roraima Zigzag Pole Top
BR.description: Zigzag-shaped top bar on a tall pole seen only in Ceará and Roraima.

BR.title: Pencil Poles
BR.description: Poles capped with smooth conical tips typical of Rio de Janeiro.

BR.title: Alternating Horizontal Insulators
BR.description: One central insulator above with horizontally alternating ones below in Mato Grosso and southern Acre.

BR.title: Brown Mushroom Insulators
BR.description: Brown mushroom-shaped insulators exclusive to Pernambuco.

BR.title: White Mushroom Insulators
BR.description: White mushroom-shaped insulators in Bahia and around Brasília.

BR.title: Transparent Insulators
BR.description: Clear glass or plastic insulators in Alagoas and Santa Catarina.

BR.title: Spool-Shaped Insulators
BR.description: Thread spool-shaped insulators in Rio de Janeiro, Espírito Santo, and Ceará.

BR.title: Elongated Thin Insulators
BR.description: Long, slender insulators mainly in Ceará.

BR.title: Horizontal Insulators
BR.description: Sideways-mounted insulators common in Pará and Mato Grosso.

BR.title: Long Grey Insulators
BR.description: Tall grey insulators common in Pará, Mato Grosso, Tocantins, Bahia, and other states.

BR.title: Maranhão Trident Insulators
BR.description: Black double-disc insulators arranged in a trident pattern characteristic of Maranhão.

BR.title: Lollipop Insulators
BR.description: Round or conical insulators on vertical rods above crossbars common in Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba, and Pernambuco.

BR.title: Dark Brown Insulators with Grey Bases
BR.description: Found almost exclusively in Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

BR.title: Concrete Waste Bins
BR.description: In Acre and Rondônia, Brazilian homes use concrete curbside waste baskets instead of metal.

BR.title: Two-Part Lamp Fixtures
BR.description: Dual-head street lights are common in Minas Gerais and Goiás, and also appear in several other states.

BR.title: Paraná Armless Lamps
BR.description: Northern Paraná street lights sometimes lack horizontal arms and are mounted directly on poles.

BR.title: Direct-Mounted Lamp Arms
BR.description: In several states, lamp arms are bent and run along the pole, attached directly to it rather than through a plate.

BR.title: Roraima City-Coloured Lamps
BR.description: Roraima's lamp fixtures share a shape but are painted different colours by city.

BR.title: Ceará Ornamental Lamp Arms
BR.description: Ceará street lights often have decorative, brightly painted arms, sometimes with town names.

BR.title: São Paulo Divided Highways
BR.description: São Paulo has significantly more multi-lane divided highways than other parts of Brazil.

BR.title: São Paulo Km Marker Phone Numbers
BR.description: Telephone numbers sometimes appear below kilometre marker posts in São Paulo.

BR.title: Cobblestone Streets
BR.description: Cobblestone roads are most frequent in the northeast and Rio Grande do Sul.

BR.title: Hexagonal Concrete Tiles
BR.description: Hexagonal concrete paving blocks are common in Santa Catarina and Minas Gerais.

BR.title: Acre Red Brick Roads
BR.description: Some roads in Acre are paved with red bricks.

BR.title: Irregular Cobblestone Roads
BR.description: Streets paved with uneven stones are common in southeastern Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais.

BR.title: Rough Square-Stone Roads
BR.description: Bumpy roads of roughly square-cut stones appear in western Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina.

BR.title: Brown Tile Pavements
BR.description: Brown tile footpaths, jagged or square, are typical of Rio Grande do Sul and sometimes Santa Catarina.

BR.title: European-Influenced Architecture
BR.description: Southern states, especially Santa Catarina, feature buildings with Germanic architectural style.

BR.title: Stilt Houses
BR.description: Timber houses on stilts are common in Acre and flood-prone areas of Amazonas and Pará.

BR.title: Piauí Red Gravel Shoulders
BR.description: Roads in Piauí have red gravel verges, often persisting alongside tarmac and kerbs.

BR.title: João-de-Barro Nests
BR.description: Rufous Hornero bird builds round clay nests atop utility poles across southern Brazil.

BR.title: Coastal Rio Grande do Sul Wetland
BR.description: Rio Grande do Sul's coast is an unusually flat wetland for Brazil.

BR.title: São Paulo Pole ID Paint
BR.description: Poles in São Paulo have a yellow rectangle with letters and digits indicating municipality and ID.

BR.title: Rio de Janeiro Curved Lamp Arms
BR.description: Street light arms in Rio de Janeiro are continuously curved along their entire length.

BR.title: Country Flag
BR.description: The national flag of Brazil is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BR.title: States in Web Addresses
BR.description: Web addresses on Brazilian signage sometimes carry a state abbreviation as its own segment, as in www.example.ac.gov.br for Acre.

BR.title: .br Domain
BR.description: Web addresses in Brazil end in the country domain .br (usually as .com.br). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CA.title: Canada is bilingual
CA.description: Some countries like Canada are bi-lingual, meaning they have multiple official languages. In Canada you can find both English and French.

CA.title: "Maximum" in Canada
CA.description: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French.

CA.title: Checkered signs
CA.description: In Canada, T-intersection signs are diamond-shaped and have a distinctive checkered pattern.

CA.title: The metric system
CA.description: Canada uses the metric system and thus displays speed in kilometers per hours (km/h).

CA.title: French to the east
CA.description: In Canada, written French will mainly be found in the provinces of Québec and New Brunswick.

CA.title: Communal mailboxes
CA.description: Shared mailbox units are a regular sight in Canada.

CA.title: Centre Line Markings
CA.description: Canadian roads commonly use a single yellow centre line; double yellow lines also appear.

CA.title: Missing Front Plates
CA.description: Seven provinces issue only a rear plate; vehicles without front plates exclude BC, Manitoba, and Ontario.

CA.title: Alberta Licence Plate
CA.description: White plate with bold red characters, visible through the blur as a red tint

CA.title: British Columbia Licence Plate
CA.description: British Columbia plates appear pale white with a slight bluish tint.

CA.title: Manitoba Licence Plate
CA.description: Manitoba plates are white with dark blue character shapes, a faint pale-blue area near the top, and blurred green-turquoise landscape shapes along the lower edges.

CA.title: New Brunswick Licence Plate
CA.description: New Brunswick plates appear pale white with a reddish tint.

CA.title: Newfoundland & Labrador Licence Plate
CA.description: Newfoundland and Labrador plates are pale white with a red blob in the lower-left area.

CA.title: Nova Scotia Licence Plate
CA.description: White plate with dark blue characters, visible only as blue blurred shapes.

CA.title: Ontario Licence Plate
CA.description: Dark blue plate with white characters, white trillium logo, and "A PLACE TO GROW" slogan at the bottom.

CA.title: Prince Edward Island Licence Plate
CA.description: Prince Edward Island plates are pale white with a green tint and a faint red-orange blob in the centre.

CA.title: Quebec Licence Plate
CA.description: Québec plates appear white with a dark bluish tint.

CA.title: Saskatchewan Licence Plate
CA.description: Saskatchewan plates are white with green character shapes, a faint green text-like area, and a golden wheat-sheaf graphic between the character groups.

CA.title: Alberta Provincial Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in Alberta have 'ALBERTA' written on the banner at the bottom.

CA.title: British Columbia Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in British Columbia have the BC coat of arms at the top and 'B.C.' written below the route number.

CA.title: Manitoba Provincial Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in Manitoba have 'MANITOBA' written on the banner at the bottom.

CA.title: New Brunswick Highway Shield
CA.description: New Brunswick highway shields show the white silhouette of the province with 'NB' inside.

CA.title: Newfoundland and Labrador Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in Newfoundland have 'NEWFOUNDLAND' written on the banner at the bottom.

CA.title: Nova Scotia Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in Nova Scotia show the provincial flag at the top.

CA.title: Ontario King's Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in Ontario have a black crown on top and 'ONTARIO' written at the bottom.

CA.title: Prince Edward Island Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in Prince Edward Island have 'PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND' written on the banner at the bottom.

CA.title: Quebec Autoroute Shield
CA.description: Route shields in Quebec are red on top and blue on the bottom, with a small fleur-de-lis below the route number.

CA.title: Saskatchewan Highway Shield
CA.description: Highway shields in Saskatchewan have 'SASKATCHEWAN' written on the banner at the bottom.

CA.title: Alberta Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Tall, narrow green rectangle with white numbers centered vertically, no additional symbols.

CA.title: British Columbia Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Green rectangular marker with white numbers, often with small white 'km' label below number.

CA.title: Manitoba Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Green rectangle with bold white numbers, sometimes with small provincial highway shield above or below number.

CA.title: New Brunswick Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Green rectangle with white numbers, sometimes including small white 'km' at bottom right corner.

CA.title: Newfoundland and Labrador Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Green rectangle with white numbers, typically without additional text or symbols, mounted on metal posts.

CA.title: Nova Scotia Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Green rectangle with white numbers, sometimes with small white 'km' at bottom.

CA.title: Ontario Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Ontario's kilometre marker is a tall green rectangle with white numbers above a white square at the post's bottom.

CA.title: Prince Edward Island Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Prince Edward Island uses green rectangular markers with white numbers, sometimes with a small 'km' label, often on wooden posts.

CA.title: Quebec Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Quebec's kilometre markers are green rectangles with white numbers, often with a small white 'km' below.

CA.title: Saskatchewan Kilometre Marker
CA.description: Saskatchewan's markers are green rectangles with white numbers, sometimes with a small 'km' label, usually on metal posts.

CA.title: Provincial Speed Sign Variants
CA.description: Ontario speed signs may include a black strip reading 'km/h' or 'begins'. British Columbia shows 'km/h' without the black section. Québec signs sometimes include French text.

CA.title: Alberta Bollards
CA.description: Cylindrical white bollards with two black bands wrapped all the way around are common at Alberta intersections.

CA.title: Manitoba Bollards
CA.description: Manitoba bollards are black over grey, usually with an orange stripe below the grey section; further north, rectangular wooden bollards appear.

CA.title: Québec Guardrail Bollards
CA.description: Slender white poles tipped with a red or green reflector, always mounted directly on guardrails, unique to Québec.

CA.title: Québec Fire Hydrant Markers
CA.description: Yellow markers on top of signposts indicate underground fire hydrants throughout Québec.

CA.title: Québec Rectangular Road Markers
CA.description: Small rectangular reflective markers line Québec roadsides; their colour varies.

CA.title: Ontario Diamond Road Markers
CA.description: Diamond-shaped reflective markers are placed along roadsides in Ontario; their colour varies.

CA.title: Ontario Wire Guardrails
CA.description: Ontario guardrails have round wooden posts linked by exactly three metal wires; some posts have a reflective white band.

CA.title: Northwest Territories Bollards
CA.description: Cylindrical black-and-white bollards with two notably thick black bands, broader than Alberta's.

CA.title: Transformer Orientation (BC & NB)
CA.description: Pole-mounted transformers in British Columbia and New Brunswick face the road; elsewhere they align with the wires.

CA.title: 45° Transformers (PEI & NS)
CA.description: Transformers on Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia are mounted at a 45° angle to the road; PEI ones usually have red numbers on the side.

CA.title: Ontario Pole Tops
CA.description: Ontario poles often have two insulators on the sides and one on top, attached with a distinctive bracket; multiple units can stack vertically.

CA.title: Québec Pole Tops
CA.description: Some Québec utility poles carry insulator rods that tilt slightly upward, a recognisable silhouette.

CA.title: Québec Pole Labels
CA.description: Québec utility poles sometimes display a vertical sticker split black and yellow, with a small 'Q' in the black half.

CA.title: PEI Pole Stickers
CA.description: Prince Edward Island utility poles typically bear a small white sticker.

CA.title: Saskatchewan Alternating Pole Tops
CA.description: Insulators on consecutive Saskatchewan poles alternate sides: one pole has one insulator left and two right, the next reverses this.

CA.title: Québec T-Intersection Signs
CA.description: Québec's T-intersection signs omit the chequerboard pattern entirely.

CA.title: Newfoundland T-Intersection Signs
CA.description: Newfoundland's diamond-shaped T-intersection sign sits inside a rectangular yellow border, unique to the province.

CA.title: BC Green Sign Backs
CA.description: The reverse side of road signs in British Columbia is often painted green.

CA.title: BC Hanging Signs
CA.description: In British Columbia, road signs are sometimes suspended from distinctive overhead brackets instead of posts.

CA.title: BC Concrete Barriers
CA.description: British Columbia favours solid concrete barriers over metal guardrails on highways.

CA.title: Manitoba Signpost Stickers
CA.description: Manitoba signposts sometimes carry a small green-and-white striped sticker.

CA.title: Saskatchewan Signpost Triangles
CA.description: White triangular markers are attached to Saskatchewan signposts; the number varies.

CA.title: Saskatchewan Centre Line Dashes
CA.description: White dashed lines sometimes appear between yellow centre lines on Saskatchewan roads.

CA.title: 'Arrêt' Stop Signs
CA.description: Stop signs displaying only the French word 'Arrêt' are found exclusively in Québec.

CA.title: Bilingual 'Stop/Arrêt' Signs
CA.description: Stop signs bearing both 'Stop' and 'Arrêt' are predominantly a New Brunswick feature.

CA.title: Alberta Grid Road System
CA.description: Alberta's rural roads follow a numbered grid with Township roads running east–west and Range roads running north–south.

CA.title: Alberta Cable Guardrails
CA.description: Some Alberta highways have guardrails made of short posts connected by steel cables.

CA.title: Newfoundland Pyramid Post Tops
CA.description: Wooden guardrail posts in Newfoundland and Labrador are capped with a distinctive pyramid shape.

CA.title: Newfoundland Hydrant Markers
CA.description: Fire hydrants in Newfoundland often have a diamond-shaped marker beside them.

CA.title: Newfoundland Wooden Sign Bases
CA.description: Signs in Newfoundland and Labrador are sometimes supported by wooden box bases.

CA.title: Traffic Cone Colours
CA.description: Ontario uses orange-and-black striped cones; Québec uses orange-and-white striped cones.

CA.title: Québec Red-and-White Chevrons
CA.description: Québec curve warning boards are red and white, unlike the yellow-and-black used elsewhere.

CA.title: Rectangular Street Lamps
CA.description: New Brunswick and Nova Scotia often use rectangular-shaped lamp heads on street lights.

CA.title: Western Mountains
CA.description: Major mountain ranges are concentrated in British Columbia, western Alberta, and parts of Yukon.

CA.title: Yukon Boreal Landscape
CA.description: Yukon features boreal terrain with hilly land, distant mountains, and coniferous trees lining roads.

CA.title: BC Interior
CA.description: Southern British Columbia's interior is drier and hillier with brown grasslands and pine forests.

CA.title: Great Plains
CA.description: A vast, flat agricultural area with few trees, growing drier toward the southwest near Montana.

CA.title: Canola Fields
CA.description: Bright yellow canola flower fields are found in the central southern prairies.

CA.title: Southern Saskatchewan Hills
CA.description: Southern Saskatchewan has hilly, barren terrain with numerous river valleys.

CA.title: Manitoba Aspen Trees
CA.description: Aspens with white trunks are common in Manitoba's forests, turning yellow in autumn.

CA.title: Canadian Shield Exposed Rock
CA.description: The Canadian Shield features bare rock outcrops visible along highways in eastern Canada.

CA.title: Québec City–Windsor Corridor
CA.description: Canada's most populated zone, a flat green belt mixing farmland and woodland between Québec City and Windsor.

CA.title: PEI Red Soil
CA.description: Prince Edward Island is known for its red-tinted earth and potato farming.

CA.title: Newfoundland Balsam Fir
CA.description: The balsam fir, a cone-shaped evergreen, is very common in Newfoundland.

CA.title: Area Codes
CA.description: Canadian phone numbers start with a three-digit area code in the format XXX XXX XXXX.

CA.title: Quebec Provincial Flags
CA.description: Provincial flag, Québec's Fleurdelisé, is commonly displayed on buildings and roads.

CA.title: Newfoundland Wooden Bins
CA.description: Octagonal wooden bins are common in Newfoundland driveways.

CA.title: Acadia
CA.description: Acadia is a French-speaking region in northern and eastern New Brunswick, flying a French tricolour with a yellow star.

CA.title: Gaspé Peninsula
CA.description: Inland roads wind through heavily forested mountainous terrain with frequent overcast weather.

CA.title: Cape Breton Highlands
CA.description: Northeastern Nova Scotia's Cape Breton Highlands have high elevation and dense mixed forests.

CA.title: Country Flag
CA.description: The Canadian flag is red and white with a red maple leaf in the middle.

CA.title: Flags Ns
CA.description: Nova Scotia's flag is white with a blue diagonal cross running corner to corner, and a gold shield bearing a red lion sits at the centre.

CA.title: .ca Domain
CA.description: Web addresses in Canada end in the country domain .ca. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CA.title: Icy Coverage
CA.description: You can find ice-covered Hudson Bay coverage near Sanikiluaq.

CA.title: Icy coverage
CA.description: Ice-covered Hudson Bay is found near Sanikiluaq.

ES.title: Language
ES.description: Most languages have unique words for ‘street’ or ‘road’. In Spanish you will see Calle (street) a lot!

ES.title: Roadsign
ES.description: The Spanish crosswalk signs have a lot of stripes on it, making it stand out from most of the other European ones.

ES.title: Vegetation
ES.description: Look at the vegetation! You will find more tropical trees such as palm trees as you move closer to the equator.

ES.title: Spanish chevrons
ES.description: In Spain, you can find both black and white chevrons and blue and white chevrons.

ES.title: Road markers
ES.description: Distance markers along Spanish roads are recognisable by their colourful borders and the road number printed at the top.

ES.title: Hunting signs
ES.description: In Catalonia you can find black and white signs indicating hunting grounds.

ES.title: Many stripes
ES.description: On the Spanish crossing signs there are eight stripes, the most in all of Europe.

ES.title: Licence Plates
ES.description: Standard elongated white EU plates with a single blue strip on the left edge.

ES.title: Bollards
ES.description: Hollow posts with a yellow-orange reflector on the front; rear has two small white dots or is blank.

ES.title: Ladder Poles and Wooden Poles
ES.description: Common poles include concrete 'ladder' poles with step-like indentations and plain wooden poles.

ES.title: French-Style Pole Tops
ES.description: Pole tops have an inverted-triangle with a gently upward-curving horizontal crossbar.

ES.title: High-Voltage Pylons
ES.description: High-voltage transmission towers are common.

ES.title: Guardrails
ES.description: Spain uses rounded guardrails with yellow reflectors.

ES.title: Stop Sign Font
ES.description: Spanish stop signs use a distinctively small typeface for 'STOP'.

ES.title: Sign Red Borders
ES.description: The red border on warning and prohibition signs runs right to the edge with no white outline.

ES.title: Flat Signposts
ES.description: Nearly all traffic signs, kilometre markers, and chevrons are mounted on flat-profile signposts.

ES.title: Direction Signs
ES.description: Wayfinding signs have a white background with multi-coloured road number boxes; motorways use blue.

ES.title: Dashed Outer Road Lines
ES.description: Some rural roads feature dashed edge lines; many still use solid edge lines.

ES.title: Spanish Language
ES.description: Spanish is dominant; the letter Ñ is exclusive to Spanish.

ES.title: Street Name: Calle
ES.description: 'Calle' is the standard Spanish word for street on urban signs.

ES.title: Vado Permanente Signs
ES.description: 'Vado permanente' no-parking plaques are mounted on garage doors and gates.

ES.title: Landscape Diversity
ES.description: Spain's scenery ranges from lush forests and plateaus to semi-deserts and mountains.

ES.title: Mediterranean Climate
ES.description: Most of the country has a dry Mediterranean climate reflected in vegetation and agriculture.

ES.title: Regional Road Codes
ES.description: Road markers carry region-specific letter codes; national roads use codes like E, AP, A, R, and N.

ES.title: Telephone Area Codes
ES.description: Landline numbers start with 9 plus a two-digit regional code; mobiles start with 6.

ES.title: Catalan Language
ES.description: Catalan is used in Catalonia, Valencian Community, and Balearic Islands; identified by 'i' for 'and' and grave accents.

ES.title: Catalan Street Name: Carrer
ES.description: 'Carrer' is the Catalan word for street on signs in Catalonia and the Balearics.

ES.title: Gual Permanent Signs
ES.description: 'Gual permanente' signs are common in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands.

ES.title: Basque Language
ES.description: Basque is a language isolate spoken in the Basque Country and northern Navarre with distinctive Z and K usage.

ES.title: Basque Street Name: Kalea
ES.description: 'Kalea' is the Basque word for street; Spanish 'calle' is also common.

ES.title: Basque Bilingual Sub-Signs
ES.description: Road signs often have bilingual plates with a black border; Basque usually on top in Basque Country.

ES.title: Galician Language
ES.description: Galician is closely related to Portuguese, spoken in Galicia, distinguishable by Ñ and no Ç.

ES.title: Galician Street Name: Rúa
ES.description: 'Rúa' is the Galician word for street, often accented.

ES.title: Galician Town Name Articles
ES.description: Galician place names often start with articles A, O, As, or Os.

ES.title: Andalusia Regional Flag
ES.description: Green-white-green horizontal stripes with a central coat of arms.

ES.title: Aragón Regional Flag
ES.description: Four red stripes on yellow with coat of arms on the hoist side.

ES.title: Asturias Regional Flag
ES.description: Sky blue field with a yellow Cross of the Victory in the centre.

ES.title: Balearic Islands Regional Flag
ES.description: Four red stripes on yellow with a purple canton containing a white castle.

ES.title: Basque Country Regional Flag
ES.description: Red field with green diagonal cross behind a white upright cross.

ES.title: Canary Islands Regional Flag
ES.description: Three vertical stripes of white, blue, and yellow with a central coat of arms.

ES.title: Cantabria Regional Flag
ES.description: Two horizontal stripes of white over red with a coat of arms in the upper hoist.

ES.title: Castilla-La Mancha Regional Flag
ES.description: Two vertical halves: red with yellow castle on hoist, white on fly.

ES.title: Castile and León Regional Flag
ES.description: Chequered pattern of yellow castles on red and purple lions on white in 2x2 layout.

ES.title: Catalonia Flag
ES.description: Four horizontal red stripes on a yellow field (the Senyera), displayed throughout Catalonia.

ES.title: Extremadura Flag
ES.description: Three horizontal stripes of green, white, black with the coat of arms in the centre, displayed throughout Extremadura.

ES.title: Galicia Flag
ES.description: White field with a diagonal blue stripe and the coat of arms in the centre, displayed throughout Galicia.

ES.title: La Rioja Flag
ES.description: Four horizontal stripes of red, white, green, yellow with the coat of arms in the centre, displayed throughout La Rioja.

ES.title: Madrid Flag
ES.description: Red field with seven five-pointed white stars arranged in a 4-3 pattern, displayed throughout Madrid.

ES.title: Murcia Flag
ES.description: Red field with four yellow castles in the upper hoist and seven crowns in the lower fly, displayed throughout Murcia.

ES.title: Navarre Flag
ES.description: Red field with golden chains radiating from a central emerald coat of arms, displayed throughout Navarre.

ES.title: Valencia Flag
ES.description: Four horizontal red stripes on yellow with a blue vertical band on the hoist containing a crown and heraldic motifs, displayed throughout Valencia.

ES.title: Catalan Independence Flag
ES.description: An unofficial flag in Catalan-speaking areas, based on the red-and-yellow striped Senyera pattern.

ES.title: Topography
ES.description: Spain is mountainous with major ranges like the Pyrenees, Sierra Nevada, Cantabrian Mountains, Iberian System, and Sierra Morena. The Meseta Central is a high plateau. Four main rivers define drainage basins.

ES.title: Green Northern Coast
ES.description: The far north is lush with rolling hills, hedgerows, and verdant meadows.

ES.title: Pyrenees
ES.description: Mountain range along the French border with light-grey rock faces, pine forests, and stone-walled architecture.

ES.title: Pyrenean Pine Forests
ES.description: Dense tall pine forests cover much of the Pyrenees and smaller hills in the Basque Country or Navarre.

ES.title: Castilla y León Flatlands
ES.description: Broad, gently undulating agricultural plain dominated by cereal crops and occasional sunflower fields.

ES.title: La Rioja Vineyards
ES.description: Vineyards flanked by mountain ranges to the north and south indicate La Rioja.

ES.title: Aragón Ebro Semi-Desert
ES.description: Semi-arid terrain with sandy soil and low scrubby vegetation along the Ebro basin from Navarre through Aragón.

ES.title: Aragón Arid Plains
ES.description: Flat, parched terrain in central and southern Aragón with pale rocky or red earth soil.

ES.title: Castilla la Mancha
ES.description: Flat terrain with common vineyards and olive plantations, especially in western provinces.

ES.title: Holm and Cork Oaks (Extremadura)
ES.description: Open pastures with widely spaced holm and cork oaks, typical of Extremadura and surroundings.

ES.title: Murcia Arid Landscape
ES.description: Sandy soil, medium mountains, and roadside plantations of small fruit and olive trees around Murcia.

ES.title: Murcia Hazy Mountains
ES.description: Bare, rugged mountains often seen through hazy mist in Murcia and southern Alicante.

ES.title: Sierra Nevada
ES.description: Snow-capped peaks visible from November through May. Sierra Nevada is the only mountain range in southern Spain that carries snow for most of the year.

ES.title: Málaga White Villages
ES.description: Settlements composed entirely of white-painted houses cascading down mountain slopes are a quintessential sight along the southern coast near Málaga.

ES.title: Olive Trees (General)
ES.description: Olive cultivation is widespread across more than half of Spain.

ES.title: Massive Olive Plantations (Córdoba/Jaén)
ES.description: Vast olive groves over rolling hills concentrated around Córdoba and Jaén.

ES.title: Olive Plantations
ES.description: Olive groves on flat terrain is common south of Madrid.

ES.title: Olive Plantations (East Coast)
ES.description: East-coast olive groves enclosed by fences or stone walls with visible mountains nearby.

ES.title: Eucalyptus Plantations (North Coast)
ES.description: Eucalyptus plantations line the entire northern coast, especially abundant in Galicia.

ES.title: Eucalyptus in Dry Environments
ES.description: Eucalyptus in arid areas likely places you in Huelva province or nearby.

ES.title: Orange Plantations (East Coast)
ES.description: Orange groves on the Mediterranean coast from Valencia southward, in small valleys with mountains to the west.

ES.title: Orange Plantations (Guadalquivir Basin)
ES.description: Orange orchards on open, flat terrain in the Guadalquivir river basin.

ES.title: Corn Fields
ES.description: Corn cultivated in major river basins, northern coast, and northwest Castilla y León.

ES.title: Stone Pines
ES.description: Pinus pinea has a compact, bulbous crown wider than tall. Flat forests dominated by stone pines are common near Valladolid and Huelva.

ES.title: Aleppo Pines
ES.description: Pinus halepensis has a looser, irregular crown. It is the most prevalent pine along the east coast and Balearic Islands.

ES.title: Baltic Pines
ES.description: Pinus sylvestris grows tall and slender with dark bark that sheds near the top to reveal orange-red wood. The lower trunk is usually branchless. Found mainly in the Pyrenees, Sierra de Guadarrama, and the Iberian System.

ES.title: Maritime Pines (Atlantic)
ES.description: Near the Atlantic coast, Pinus pinaster shows grey bark with red undertones and fluffy upward-pointing branches. Mature trees lose their lower branches.

ES.title: Maritime Pines (Mediterranean)
ES.description: Away from the Atlantic, Pinus pinaster has grey, deeply fissured bark with red tones. Found in mountain ranges across central and southern Spain.

ES.title: Regional Road Line Styles
ES.description: Small road markings vary by region with solid or dashed edge lines and varied centre lines.

ES.title: Kilometre Marker Shapes
ES.description: Marker posts are rectangular or square, roughly splitting the country. Andalusia's are extra tall, Madrid's show the regional flag, Biscay's have semi-circular tops.

ES.title: Kilometre Marker Border Colours
ES.description: Border colours correspond to road size: orange for large, green for medium, yellow for small roads.

ES.title: Galician Concello Signs
ES.description: Town entry signs in Galicia feature a green or blue strip at the top displaying the municipality name. The word 'Concello' (municipality) is exclusive to this region.

ES.title: Asturias Bus Stops
ES.description: Red bus stop posts bearing the CTA logo at the top are specific to Asturias.

ES.title: Asturias COGERSA Bins
ES.description: Rubbish and recycling containers marked with the COGERSA logo are recognisable even from a distance and indicate Asturias.

ES.title: Asturias Yellow Snow Poles
ES.description: Yellow roadside poles with one or two reflectors are unique to Asturias, typically found in the mountainous south of the region.

ES.title: Aragón Bollard
ES.description: Short, flat rectangular white stick with grey reflectors on both sides common on Aragón regional roads.

ES.title: Corrugated Round Signposts
ES.description: Round corrugated-metal signposts are common in Catalonia, the Basque Country, and the Balearic Islands.

ES.title: Catalan Hunting Signs
ES.description: Signs reading 'Àrea privada de Caça' mark private hunting grounds in Catalonia and sometimes the Balearics.

ES.title: Lleida/Tarragona Bollard
ES.description: A bollard with a square orange reflector on the front and a white reflector on the back is almost exclusive to the provinces of Lleida and Tarragona on the mainland.

ES.title: Catalan Single-Arrow Chevrons
ES.description: Large square chevron boards with a single directional arrow are common in Catalonia.

ES.title: Murcia Red-Arrow Chevrons
ES.description: Small square chevrons with a red arrow on a white background are exclusive to the region of Murcia.

ES.title: Madrid Bus Stops
ES.description: Round-topped red bus stop posts and green inter-urban buses indicate the Community of Madrid. Blue urban buses operate within the city centre.

ES.title: Extremadura Green-Top Bollards
ES.description: Standard Spanish bollards capped with a green top are exclusive to Extremadura.

ES.title: Castilla la Mancha Stone Markers
ES.description: Low stone markers with the regional coat of arms, blue left side and unpainted right side, line field boundaries.

ES.title: Rectangular Mesh Poles
ES.description: Steel lattice poles with rectangular cross-sections are concentrated in southern Spain, especially Murcia and southern Alicante.

ES.title: Andalusia Green-Stripe Signs
ES.description: Regional government signs have a green stripe along the left edge; smaller green-posted versions appear near nature reserves.

ES.title: Andalusia Snow Poles
ES.description: Blue-and-yellow snow marker poles unique to Andalusia.

ES.title: Slate Roofs (Northwest)
ES.description: Nearly black slate roofing dominates northwestern Spain, western Galicia, the Pyrenees near Andorra, and mountains northeast of Madrid.

ES.title: Galician Concrete Block Houses
ES.description: Large concrete blocks, sometimes textured like stone, are common building material in Galicia.

ES.title: Galician Granaries
ES.description: Elongated raised granaries called 'hórreos gallegos' or 'cabazos' are characteristic of Galician farms.

ES.title: Asturian Granaries
ES.description: Asturian hórreos are larger, squarer, elevated on four pillars; 'panera' variant sits on six or eight supports. Slate roofs indicate western Asturias.

ES.title: Basque White Houses
ES.description: Large white-rendered houses with exposed timber frames are typical of the Basque Country, Basque Navarre, and Cantabria.

ES.title: Catalan Masías
ES.description: Traditional stone farmhouses, usually isolated or in small clusters, common in Catalonia, eastern Aragón, and parts of the Valencian Community.

ES.title: White House Towns
ES.description: Entire towns of whitewashed houses are common in Andalusia and Extremadura.

ES.title: Asturias Black Car
ES.description: A black vehicle with no antenna and a visible brake light is associated with Asturias.

ES.title: Balearic Islands Landscape
ES.description: Coastal Mediterranean feel with dry Aleppo pine forests on hillsides and small agricultural patches of fruit and olive trees.

ES.title: Balearic Rock Walls
ES.description: Low dry-stone walls are extremely prevalent throughout the Balearic Islands.

ES.title: Balearic Architecture
ES.description: White-painted houses with gently inclined tile roofs are the norm; some have flat roofs.

ES.title: Formentera
ES.description: A small, low-lying island characterised by coastal scrubland. The mountains of neighbouring Ibiza are often visible from the north shore.

ES.title: Mallorca Mountains
ES.description: A tall mountain range runs along northwestern Mallorca and is visible from much of the island. No other Balearic island has peaks of comparable size.

ES.title: Canary Islands Location
ES.description: A Spanish archipelago off Africa's west coast, far from mainland Spain.

ES.title: Canary Islands Landscapes
ES.description: Diverse landscapes: volcanic mountains, pine forests, lava fields, arid zones, and Mediterranean-like countryside.

ES.title: Lanzarote Volcanic Soil
ES.description: Very dark exposed volcanic terrain, almost lunar in places, is more abundant on Lanzarote than on any other Canary Island.

ES.title: Fuerteventura
ES.description: An arid island with sparse vegetation. Orange-tinted soil is essentially unique to Fuerteventura within the Canary chain.

ES.title: Las Palmas Bollard
ES.description: Bollards with square orange front and white rear reflectors common in Las Palmas province and parts of mainland Spain.

ES.title: Lanzarote Wine Plantations
ES.description: Unique vineyards where each vine is sheltered inside a semicircular stone wall built on dark volcanic soil.

ES.title: La Graciosa
ES.description: A small, barren island north of Lanzarote with consistently overcast skies. Its two south-coast settlements consist of white, flat-roofed houses.

ES.title: Ceuta and Melilla
ES.description: Two Spanish autonomous cities on the North African coast, partially surrounded by Morocco.

ES.title: Ceuta Architecture
ES.description: North African style, flat-roofed buildings in warm tones from pale yellow to red.

ES.title: Ceuta Landscape
ES.description: Hilly Mediterranean terrain with eucalyptus and pine trees outside the urban core.

ES.title: Ceuta Black-and-White Guardrails
ES.description: Guardrails painted in alternating black and white are unique to Ceuta within Spain.

ES.title: Melilla
ES.description: North African architecture similar to Ceuta, with hazy, desaturated, and overcast imagery.

ES.title: Camino de Santiago
ES.description: Pilgrim routes marked by a yellow scallop shell on a blue background on signs and road surfaces.

ES.title: Castilla la Mancha Spring
ES.description: Early spring imagery showing dirt farm tracks between bright green fields and bare vineyards on red soil.

ES.title: AP-15 Navarra Bollards
ES.description: Flat bollards with square red reflectors, accompanied by guardrails also fitted with red reflectors. Unlike the yellow reflectors seen elsewhere in Spain.

ES.title: Barcelona Taxis
ES.description: Black cars with yellow doors, the yellow extends to the boot lid as well.

ES.title: Ebro Delta
ES.description: An exceptionally flat landscape of rice paddies and water channels. Significant mountains are visible to the south, west, and north.

ES.title: Almería Greenhouses
ES.description: Dense clusters of white-roofed greenhouses fill the lowland between Almería and Motril, particularly around the town of El Ejido.

ES.title: Bilbao Street Signs
ES.description: Street name plaques in Bilbao are set inside an ornate decorative frame not found elsewhere in Spain.

ES.title: Doñana National Park Car Meta
ES.description: A unique vehicle type appears on coverage southwest of Seville within the Doñana National Park.

ES.title: Country Flag
ES.description: The national flag of Spain is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

ES.title: .es Domain
ES.description: Web addresses in Spain end in the country domain .es. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

JP.title: Drivingside
JP.description: Check for driving direction. In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.

JP.title: Machine
JP.description: Some countries have very specific, unique niches. For example does Japan have millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.

JP.title: Vehicles
JP.description: Vehicles style differs vastly between countries. In Japan small, boxy cars is very common.

JP.title: Yellow guardrails
JP.description: Yamaguchi Prefecture in Japan is recognized for its distinctive bright yellow roadside guardrails.

JP.title: Overhead arrows
JP.description: This arrow above the road marks the road during heavy snow and is mainly seen in Hokkaido.

JP.title: Pole markings
JP.description: Japanese poles often have thin, vertical yellow lines on a black section towards the bottom.

JP.title: Japanese bollard
JP.description: Japanese bollards are white and have a circular reflector on the top.

JP.title: Islands, Regions and Prefectures
JP.description: Japan is divided into four major islands, regions grouping prefectures, and 47 prefectures.

JP.title: Driving direction
JP.description: In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.

JP.title: Japanese Writing Systems
JP.description: Japanese uses kanji, hiragana with rounded strokes, and angular katakana scripts.

JP.title: Architecture
JP.description: Building styles range from traditional rural houses to ultramodern urban high-rises.

JP.title: Round Concrete Poles
JP.description: Utility poles are round concrete with threaded screw-like protrusions and often electrical plates.

JP.title: Road Lines
JP.description: Japanese road markings include solid white edges with dashed or solid white/yellow center lines.

JP.title: White Guardrails
JP.description: Plain white guardrails are the default road barrier throughout Japan.

JP.title: Hexagonal Prefecture Road Shields
JP.description: Prefectural routes use hexagonal shields with route numbers and often kanji prefecture names.

JP.title: Common Infrastructure
JP.description: Triangular stop signs, school-zone crossings, and convex traffic mirrors are widespread.

JP.title: Retaining Walls
JP.description: Retaining walls in remote countryside indicate you are in Japan.

JP.title: Area Codes
JP.description: Telephone area codes appear on signage and increase in value moving southward.

JP.title: Regional Pole Reflector Pads
JP.description: Reflector pads on utility poles vary in design by region.

JP.title: Road Diamonds
JP.description: A standard white hollow diamond with a continuous outline. This generic variant can be found throughout Japan.

JP.title: Regional Road Diamonds
JP.description: This diamond variant has gaps in the upper-right and bottom-left corners of the outline and can be found in Hyōgo, Kyoto, Okayama and Miyagi prefectures.

JP.title: Regional Road Diamonds
JP.description: This diamond variant has two offset gaps along the upper-left and lower-right sides of the outline. It can be found in Mie and Kōchi prefectures.

JP.title: Regional Road Diamonds
JP.description: This diamond variant has four gaps around the outline, creating four separate sections, and can be found in Gunma, Chiba and Gifu prefectures.

JP.title: Road Diamonds (Nara / Wakayama)
JP.description: This diamond variant has four gaps in the outline, dividing it into four separate sections. It can be found in Nara and Wakayama prefectures.

JP.title: Regional Road Diamonds
JP.description: This diamond variant has four gaps around the corners of the outline, creating four separate sections. It can be found in Shiga, Ibaraki, Saitama, Tochigi, Niigata and Okinawa prefectures.

JP.title: Regional Road Diamonds
JP.description: This diamond variant has four gaps in the outline, with breaks along both the upper-right and lower-left sides. It can be found in Ōita and Toyama prefectures.

JP.title: Regional Road Diamonds
JP.description: This diamond variant has gaps at the middle of both the left and right sides of the outline. It can be found in Tottori, Shimane and Saga prefectures.

JP.title: Small Road Diamond
JP.description: A smaller version of the diamond with gaps at the upper-right and lower-left corners. It can be found in Hiroshima and Tokushima prefectures.

JP.title: Road Diamonds, Ishikawa / Kumamoto
JP.description: This diamond variant has gaps at the top and bottom, with the upper gap offset to the left and the lower gap offset to the right. It can be found in Kumamoto and Ishikawa prefectures.

JP.title: Road Diamonds, Yamanashi / Nagano
JP.description: This diamond variant has two gaps along the left side of the outline, creating three distinct sections. It can be found in Yamanashi and Nagano prefectures.

JP.title: Road Diamonds, Ibaraki / Niigata
JP.description: A newer crossed-line diamond in Ibaraki and Niigata alongside the traditional style.

JP.title: Thin Road Diamond
JP.description: A thinner version of the standard continuous diamond. This variant can be found in Kagoshima, Aichi, Yamaguchi and Nagano prefectures.

JP.title: Prefecture Signpost Stickers
JP.description: Signposts across Japan display small stickers specific to individual prefectures.

JP.title: Chugoku Orange Arrow on Poles
JP.description: In Chugoku, an orange arrow appears above the highest plate on utility poles.

JP.title: Shikoku Orange-Black Pole Bands
JP.description: Utility poles in Shikoku often have alternating orange and black bands.

JP.title: Kansai 120° Pole Attachments
JP.description: In Kansai, pole hardware has a roughly 120-degree angular spread.

JP.title: Shikoku 90° Pole Attachments
JP.description: Compact right-angle brackets appear regularly on Shikoku utility poles.

JP.title: Hokkaido Transformers
JP.description: Hokkaido transformers mount on cross-shaped brackets or horizontal bars, often opposite sides of a square frame.

JP.title: Tohoku Transformers
JP.description: Tohoku transformers have square mounting brackets, the Tohoku Electric Power logo, and various support bar styles.

JP.title: Kanto Transformers
JP.description: Kanto transformers sit on wooden backing boards with dual bars or circular plates with T-shaped bars.

JP.title: Hokuriku Transformers
JP.description: Hokuriku transformers have slender metal bars and compact, lantern-shaped insulators without other horizontal supports.

JP.title: Chubu Transformers
JP.description: Chubu transformers feature yellow numerals, black tap connectors, and large triangular or narrow metal supports.

JP.title: Kansai Transformers
JP.description: Kansai transformers sit on square frames with straight or zigzag bars, sometimes attached to vertical supports.

JP.title: Chugoku Transformers
JP.description: Chugoku transformers use a cross-shaped arm with a triangular brace and carry white labels with red numerals.

JP.title: Shikoku Transformers
JP.description: Shikoku transformers have a cross-shaped arm with a half-triangle brace and cap-shaped insulators with white labels.

JP.title: Kyushu Transformers
JP.description: Kyushu transformers mount on a horizontal bar ending with three insulators, facing opposite directions.

JP.title: Okinawa Transformers
JP.description: Okinawa poles have a T-shaped arm with transformers on opposite faces.

JP.title: Grey Insulator Blocks
JP.description: Grey wire-routing blocks appear in Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, and Shikoku, rarely in Hokkaido.

JP.title: Chubu Pole Top
JP.description: A pole cap with four heavy bars crowned by a circular element is typical of Chubu.

JP.title: Hokuriku Pole Top
JP.description: A tent-shaped pole cap with two filled sides is typical of Hokuriku.

JP.title: Chugoku Pole Top
JP.description: Four slender, narrow bars atop the pole are a hallmark of Chugoku.

JP.title: Kanto Tuning Fork Pole Top
JP.description: A fork-shaped pole cap with a protruding upper bar and horizontal crossbars appears mainly in Kanto.

JP.title: Chubu Tuning Fork Pole Top
JP.description: A fork-shaped pole cap with a compact upper bar and single horizontal crossbar is common in Chubu.

JP.title: Kansai Tuning Fork Pole Top
JP.description: A fork-shaped pole cap with a thin wire upper bar and horizontal crossbar is prevalent in Kansai.

JP.title: Kyushu Flat Bollards
JP.description: Flat, white bollards with a row of orange reflectors on one face are characteristic of Kyushu and Yamaguchi.

JP.title: Shikoku Black-Stripe Bollards
JP.description: On Shikoku, bollards have a dark horizontal band beneath the reflector and appear freestanding or mounted.

JP.title: Tohoku Thick Bollards
JP.description: Tohoku's bollards are wide white posts with an octagonal reflector and a yellow band below it; black versions appear on highways.

JP.title: Tohoku Striped Bollards
JP.description: Striped sleeves tapering to a narrower top and lacking reflectors are common over bollards in Tohoku, especially Akita.

JP.title: Chugoku Snow Poles
JP.description: Simple snow marker poles with slim tips are concentrated in northern Chugoku and sporadically in Iwate.

JP.title: Green Guardrail Bands
JP.description: Guardrails with green bands appear throughout Kyushu, especially in Oita and Miyazaki.

JP.title: Hokkaido Chevron Guardrail Stickers
JP.description: Arrow-patterned chevron stickers appear on guardrail tips and fence posts in Hokkaido.

JP.title: Chugoku Red-Yellow Guardrail Ends
JP.description: Red and yellow striped stickers on guardrail ends are widespread in Chugoku, excluding Yamaguchi.

JP.title: Vertical Traffic Lights
JP.description: Traffic signals are vertical in Hokkaido and the northwestern coast; elsewhere they are horizontal.

JP.title: Kagawa Black Signs
JP.description: Road side reflectors with dark boards and two yellow dots are exclusive to Kagawa.

JP.title: Kerosene Tanks
JP.description: Fuel storage tanks nicknamed "Claymores" are common northward, especially in Hokkaido and mountainous areas.

JP.title: Hot Water and Propane Tanks
JP.description: Tanks for heating and cooking appear more often in northern and mountainous prefectures, common in rural areas.

JP.title: Snow Prevention Roads
JP.description: Rows of small nozzles spray heated groundwater to prevent snow buildup, mainly along the northwestern coast.

JP.title: Ehime Cycling Routes
JP.description: Bicycle lanes in Ehime have a white outer stripe and blue inner stripe, mostly along coastal roads.

JP.title: Red-Tiled Roofs
JP.description: Houses with red roof tiles are common in Chugoku, especially Hiroshima and Shimane.

JP.title: Northern Flat/Sloped Roofs
JP.description: Northern roofs shift to flat or low-angle slopes with exterior ladders for snow removal.

JP.title: Okinawa Concrete Buildings
JP.description: Flat-roofed white concrete buildings define Okinawa architecture.

JP.title: Cabbage
JP.description: Cabbage grows prolifically in Hokkaido and parts of northern Honshu, often visible beside roads.

JP.title: Green Tea Plants
JP.description: Tea bushes grow in trimmed hedgerows with pole-mounted fans, mainly in Shizuoka and Kagoshima.

JP.title: Rice Paddies
JP.description: Rice fields north of Tokyo show green shoots in season and golden husks at harvest, often flooded.

JP.title: Japanese White Birch
JP.description: This tree species is concentrated in Chubu and Hokkaido, with some presence in Tohoku.

JP.title: Bamboo
JP.description: Bamboo is more common in southern Japan and less so heading north.

JP.title: Chinese Silver Grass
JP.description: Known as Kyushu grass, it thrives across Kyushu in large quantities.

JP.title: Sugarcane
JP.description: Sugarcane grows almost exclusively in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.

JP.title: Hokkaido Winter Coverage
JP.description: Snowy winter Google Street View is scarce in Hokkaido, mostly in the southern part.

JP.title: Nobi and Kanto Plains
JP.description: The Nobi and Kanto plains are conspicuously flat expanses in mountainous Japan.

JP.title: Okinawa Shisa Lions
JP.description: Okinawa features Shisa guardian lion statues and house plaques with local lettering.

JP.title: Trekkers and Tripods
JP.description: Trekker and tripod camera setups appear across many prefectures, creating non-standard coverage.

JP.title: Country Flag
JP.description: The national flag of Japan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

JP.title: Vending machines
JP.description: Japan has millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.

JP.title: .jp Domain
JP.description: Web addresses in Japan end in the country domain .jp (often as .co.jp). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

KR.title: Drivingside
KR.description: Check for driving direction. In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.

KR.title: Internetdomains
KR.description: Keep an eye out for internet domains. In South Korea they use .KR at the end of an internet adress.

KR.title: Language
KR.description: In written Korean you will find a lot of big circles.

KR.title: Rock walls
KR.description: Jeju Island in South Korea is known for its many rock walls made from dark volcanic stone.

KR.title: Pole markings
KR.description: South Korean utility poles often carry black-and-yellow diagonal stripes near the base. The stripes do not reach the ground.

KR.title: Licence Plates
KR.description: South Korea's plates: pre-2006 short green; post-2006 white (private) or yellow (commercial), in long and short formats.

KR.title: Autumn and Winter Coverage
KR.description: Much South Korean imagery was captured in autumn or winter, showing bare trees and muted colours.

KR.title: Spiked Pole Tops
KR.description: Most South Korean utility poles taper to a pointed spike at the top.

KR.title: Driving direction
KR.description: In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.

KR.title: Road Lines
KR.description: South Korean roads have yellow centre lines and white edge lines.

KR.title: Red Block Markings
KR.description: Red-painted block patterns occasionally appear on South Korean road surfaces.

KR.title: Yellow Warning Signs
KR.description: South Korean triangular warning signs have a yellow background.

KR.title: Arrow-Shaped Street Signs
KR.description: South Korean street name signs are blue and arrow-shaped, hung from utility poles.

KR.title: Green Direction Signs
KR.description: South Korean directional signs display white text on a green background.

KR.title: Pedestrian Crossings
KR.description: South Korean zebra crossings often use alternating yellow and white stripes.

KR.title: Pentagonal Pedestrian Crossing Signs
KR.description: Crossing signs are pentagonal on a blue background, unique to South Korea.

KR.title: House Numbers
KR.description: South Korean buildings have blue house-shaped address plaques with Hangul and Latin script.

KR.title: Wedge-Shaped Bollards
KR.description: Black-and-white wedge-shaped bollards with round yellow and grey reflectors appear along some roads.

KR.title: Mountainous Landscape
KR.description: South Korea's terrain is mostly hilly or mountainous, with elevation visible on the horizon.

KR.title: Red Brick Architecture
KR.description: Red brick is a common building material throughout South Korea.

KR.title: Traditional Tiled Roofs
KR.description: Many South Korean buildings have traditional tiled roofs with upturned edges and decorative corners.

KR.title: Area Codes
KR.description: Phone area codes increase from north to south, 02 in Seoul up to 064 on Jeju Island.

KR.title: Jeju Island Volcanic Soil
KR.description: Jeju is a volcanic island with dark volcanic dirt and visible volcanic cones.

KR.title: Country Flag
KR.description: The national flag of South Korea is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

KR.title: .kr Domain
KR.description: Web addresses in South Korea end in the country domain .kr (often as .co.kr). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MT.title: Achitecture
MT.description: Take notice of the surrounding architecture and building materials. You will see a lot of walls and building made from limestone in Malta for example.

MT.title: Drivingside
MT.description: Don’t lose track of which side the cars are driving on. Malta is one of the few European countries that drive on the left.

MT.title: English
MT.description: Learning the words for street and road in different languages can be really helpful. Triq is the Maltese word and it will only show up in Malta.

MT.title: Small island
MT.description: Roads on Malta tend to be only one or two lanes wide due to the island's small size and low population.

MT.title: Licence Plates
MT.description: Maltese plates have the European blue strip and commonly short plates.

MT.title: Limestone Rock Walls
MT.description: Dry limestone rock walls line roads and fields across Malta and are very common.

MT.title: Limestone
MT.description: You will see a lot of walls and buildings made from limestone in Malta.

MT.title: Covered Balconies
MT.description: Traditional enclosed balconies projecting from facades are a hallmark of Malta, often brightly painted.

MT.title: Nice trick for Malta
MT.description: Triq is the Maltese word for street and it will only show up in Malta.

MT.title: Bus Stops
MT.description: Maltese bus stops often display route numbers or destination names.

MT.title: Double Yellow No-Parking Lines
MT.description: Double yellow kerb lines indicate no-parking zones in Malta.

MT.title: Maltese Language
MT.description: Maltese uses Latin script with unique characters: Ċ/ċ, Ġ/ġ, Ħ/ħ, and Ż/ż on signage.

MT.title: Country Flag
MT.description: The national flag of Malta is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MT.title: .mt Domain
MT.description: Web addresses in Malta end in the country domain .mt (often as .com.mt). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MX.title: Drivingside
MX.description: In Mexico they drive on the right side of the road. As do all other non-island countries in North America.

MX.title: Infrastructure
MX.description: Utility poles will be different country to country. They come in many different colors, shapes and materials. Mexico usually have octagonal poles made of concrete.

MX.title: Taxi
MX.description: Taxi cars can often feature useful information, such as the name of the city they are driving in. CDMX is an abbreviation of the Mexican capital Ciudad De Mexico.

MX.title: Electricity meters
MX.description: Mexico, along with several Central American countries, uses circular electricity meters.

MX.title: Mexican bollards
MX.description: Mexico uses round, white bollards with a black base.

MX.title: Licence Plates
MX.description: Mexican licence plates are short, vary by state, and both front and rear plates are mandatory.

MX.title: Yellow Centre Road Lines
MX.description: Mexican roads have solid white edge lines with a single continuous yellow stripe down the middle.

MX.title: Bollards 01 Mexican Bollards
MX.description: Mexico uses round, white bollards with a black base.

MX.title: Road Shields
MX.description: National highways use curved shields with "MEXICO"; state roads use straight-edged shields with state initials.

MX.title: All-Caps Directional Signs
MX.description: Mexican directional signs feature large, bold, white uppercase lettering.

MX.title: Kilometre Markers
MX.description: Mexican highway distance markers are white posts with black text and borders.

MX.title: Cacti
MX.description: A huge diversity of cactus species makes them a common sight across Mexico.

MX.title: "ALTO" Stop Signs
MX.description: Stop signs in Mexico read "ALTO".

MX.title: Thick Arrows on Signs
MX.description: Mexican road sign arrows are distinctly thick and bold.

MX.title: Yellow-Painted Kerbs and Barriers
MX.description: Kerbs and bridge barriers are frequently painted yellow in Mexico.

MX.title: Rooftop Water Tanks
MX.description: Wide cylindrical water tanks, usually black or white, are common on Mexican rooftops.

MX.title: OXXO and Pemex Brands
MX.description: OXXO stores and Pemex fuel stations are common commercial brands along Mexican roads.

MX.title: Nahuatl-Origin Place Names
MX.description: Many towns have Nahuatl-derived names with 'x', 'tl', and endings like '-ec' and '-tlan'.

MX.title: American Car Brands and Pickup Trucks
MX.description: US vehicle brands and pickup trucks are very popular on Mexican roads.

MX.title: Area Code Regions
MX.description: The first digit of Mexican phone area codes corresponds to geographic regions.

MX.title: Postal Code Regions
MX.description: Mexican postal codes are alphabetically ordered by state and often appear on street signs.

MX.title: Aguascalientes Licence Plate
MX.description: Aguascalientes plates have a white background with a red stripe, state name, and grape cluster graphic.

MX.title: Baja California Licence Plate
MX.description: Baja California plates have a white background with blue accents and a coastline or whale tail image.

MX.title: Baja California Sur Licence Plate
MX.description: Baja California Sur plates have a white background with turquoise elements, cactus or desert motifs, and the state name.

MX.title: Campeche Licence Plate
MX.description: Campeche plates have a white background with green and red elements, often featuring a Mayan pyramid or local emblem, and the state name in green.

MX.title: Chiapas Licence Plate
MX.description: Chiapas plates have a white base with red and green details, typically showing the state outline or a jaguar head, and the state name in red.

MX.title: Chihuahua Licence Plate
MX.description: Chihuahua plates feature a white background with blue and red elements, often displaying the state coat of arms and the name 'Chihuahua' in blue.

MX.title: Coahuila Licence Plate
MX.description: Coahuila plates show a white background with green and red accents, including the state coat of arms and the word 'Coahuila' in green.

MX.title: Colima Licence Plate
MX.description: Colima plates use a white background with blue and red features, often displaying a volcano or palm tree graphic and the state name in blue.

MX.title: Durango Licence Plate
MX.description: Durango plates have a white background with green and gold elements, typically featuring a mountain or mining symbol and the state name in green.

MX.title: Guanajuato Licence Plate
MX.description: Guanajuato plates display a white background with blue and red accents, often showing a colonial building or the state coat of arms, with 'Guanajuato' in blue.

MX.title: Guerrero Licence Plate
MX.description: Guerrero plates feature a white background with green and red highlights, usually including an image of Acapulco bay or a local emblem, and 'Guerrero' in green.

MX.title: Hidalgo Licence Plate
MX.description: Hidalgo plates have a white background with blue and green elements, often displaying a mountain or aqueduct motif and the state name in blue.

MX.title: Jalisco Licence Plate
MX.description: Jalisco plates use a white background with blue and gold accents, typically featuring the state coat of arms and the name 'Jalisco' in blue.

MX.title: Mexico City Licence Plate
MX.description: Mexico City plates have a white background with pink and black elements, including the 'CDMX' abbreviation and city landmarks or the Angel of Independence.

MX.title: Estado de México Licence Plate
MX.description: Estado de México plates feature a white background with red and green accents, often showing the state coat of arms and the name 'Edomex' or 'Estado de México' in red.

MX.title: Michoacán Licence Plate
MX.description: Michoacán plates display a white background with green and red elements, typically featuring a butterfly or the state coat of arms, and 'Michoacán' in green.

MX.title: Morelos Licence Plate
MX.description: Morelos plates have a white background with purple and green accents, often showing a flower or the state coat of arms, and 'Morelos' in purple.

MX.title: Nayarit Licence Plate
MX.description: Nayarit plates use a white background with blue and green elements, typically featuring a beach or palm tree graphic and the state name in blue.

MX.title: Nuevo León Licence Plate
MX.description: Nuevo León plates feature a white background with blue and yellow accents, often displaying the state coat of arms and the name 'Nuevo León' in blue.

MX.title: Oaxaca Licence Plate
MX.description: Oaxaca plates have a white background with green and red elements, typically featuring a Zapotec motif or the state coat of arms, and 'Oaxaca' in green.

MX.title: Puebla Licence Plate
MX.description: Puebla plates display a white background with blue and red accents, often showing the state coat of arms and the name 'Puebla' in blue.

MX.title: Querétaro Licence Plate
MX.description: Querétaro plates use a white background with blue and gold elements, typically featuring an aqueduct or the state coat of arms, and 'Querétaro' in blue.

MX.title: Quintana Roo Licence Plate
MX.description: Quintana Roo plates feature a white background with turquoise and yellow accents, often displaying a palm tree or beach scene and the state name in turquoise.

MX.title: San Luis Potosí Licence Plate
MX.description: San Luis Potosí plates have a white background with green and red elements, typically featuring a mining motif or the state coat of arms, and 'San Luis Potosí' in green.

MX.title: Sinaloa Licence Plate
MX.description: Sinaloa plates display a white background with red and green accents, often showing a tomato or the state coat of arms, and 'Sinaloa' in red.

MX.title: Sonora Licence Plate
MX.description: Sonora plates feature a white background with orange and blue accents, typically displaying a desert scene or the state coat of arms, and 'Sonora' in orange.

MX.title: Tabasco Licence Plate
MX.description: Tabasco plates have a white background with green and blue elements, often featuring a river or the state coat of arms, and 'Tabasco' in green.

MX.title: Tamaulipas Licence Plate
MX.description: Tamaulipas plates use a white background with blue and green accents, typically displaying a mountain or the state coat of arms, and 'Tamaulipas' in blue.

MX.title: Tlaxcala Licence Plate
MX.description: Tlaxcala plates feature a white background with red and green elements, often showing a bull or the state coat of arms, and 'Tlaxcala' in red.

MX.title: Veracruz Licence Plate
MX.description: Veracruz plates have a white background with blue and green accents, typically featuring a harp or the state coat of arms, and 'Veracruz' in blue.

MX.title: Yucatán Licence Plate
MX.description: Yucatán plates display a white background with green and yellow elements, often showing a Mayan pyramid or the state coat of arms, and 'Yucatán' in green.

MX.title: Zacatecas Licence Plate
MX.description: Zacatecas plates feature a white background with green and red accents, typically displaying a mining cart or the state coat of arms, and 'Zacatecas' in green.

MX.title: Prickly Pear Cacti
MX.description: Prickly pear cacti, identifiable by their flat, oval-shaped pads, appear far more frequently in the central highlands.

MX.title: Pulque Agaves
MX.description: Agave salmiana has broad, smooth, curling leaves forming a crown-like silhouette, thriving in the central valley and around San Luis Potosi.

MX.title: Blue Agave Fields
MX.description: Extensive blue agave plantations for tequila are concentrated in Jalisco and Nayarit.

MX.title: Tree Yucca
MX.description: Yucca filifera and Yucca decipiens grow as single-trunked trees with oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves, concentrated in San Luis Potosi, Zacatecas, and nearby states.

MX.title: Mexican Giant Cardon Cactus
MX.description: A prevalent Baja California cactus with large sprawling arms branching from a single trunk and ribbed surface.

MX.title: Saguaro Cactus
MX.description: Found in western Sonora, featuring a tall main trunk with short, upward-curving arms.

MX.title: Organ Pipe Cactus
MX.description: Cactus with long, slender stems emerging near ground level, mainly in Sonora and occasionally Baja California Sur.

MX.title: Blue Myrtle Cactus
MX.description: Cactus with short arms curving uniformly upward, abundant in San Luis Potosi, Queretaro, and Hidalgo.

MX.title: Sugar Cane
MX.description: Sugar cane is cultivated widely but most prevalent in Veracruz.

MX.title: Coconut Palms
MX.description: Coconut palms line coastal areas, especially dense in Guerrero and Colima.
