MX.title: Sabal Palms
MX.description: Sabal palms have spiky, sun-shaped crowns giving a lollipop silhouette, growing along Mexico's east coast, Yucatan, and Nayarit.

MX.title: Attalea Rostrata Palm
MX.description: Large palm with erect, umbrella-like fronds, found mainly in Veracruz and Tabasco.

MX.title: Oil Palm Plantations
MX.description: Orderly rows of oil palms concentrated in Chiapas, with scattered plantations in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

MX.title: Boojum Trees
MX.description: Trees with alien, tentacle-like trunks nearly exclusive to southern Baja California peninsula.

MX.title: Brittlebush
MX.description: Low shrub with bright silver-grey foliage, common in Sonora near Hermosillo.

MX.title: Thin White-Barked Trees
MX.description: Slender trees with pale white bark across the Yucatan peninsula, especially in Quintana Roo.

MX.title: Golden Roadside Grass Tufts
MX.description: Lines of golden grass tufts growing immediately beside roads in Coahuila.

MX.title: Teardrop-Shaped Grass Clumps
MX.description: Grass growing in rounded, teardrop-shaped clumps typical in and around Tlaxcala.

MX.title: Red Agricultural Fields
MX.description: Fields with distinctly red soil frequent in Zacatecas and southern Durango.

MX.title: Northern Pine Forests
MX.description: Rocky, mountainous terrain with pine forests in western Chihuahua and Durango; northern pines are shorter and stunted.

MX.title: Dark Fields of Guanajuato
MX.description: Extremely dark-coloured agricultural fields common in Guanajuato.

MX.title: Reddish-Brown Hills of Northern Baja
MX.description: Hills with reddish-brown tint and large boulders in northern Baja California peninsula.

MX.title: Bright White Soil in Quintana Roo
MX.description: Intensely white, almost blinding soil in the Yucatan peninsula, most common in Quintana Roo.

MX.title: Red Fields in Northern Campeche
MX.description: Red-earth farmland bordered by dense tropical forest in northern Campeche.

MX.title: Red Brick Buildings
MX.description: Exposed red brick construction concentrated west of Mexico City in Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.

MX.title: White Concrete Block Buildings
MX.description: White concrete block structures cluster near Mexico City and become more common eastward.

MX.title: Mud Brick Buildings
MX.description: Adobe-style mud brick construction prevalent in Durango and scattered across northern arid states.

MX.title: Northern Mexican Architecture
MX.description: Homes with pastel facades, gated yards, and orange Spanish colonial roof tiles common in northern Mexico.

MX.title: Thatched Roofs
MX.description: Buildings with thatched roofing are prevalent in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi.

MX.title: Light-Coloured Rock Walls
MX.description: Low walls of pale limestone across the Yucatan peninsula, especially in Yucatan state.

MX.title: Cross on Sign Backs in Chihuahua
MX.description: Road signs in Chihuahua have a thick cross printed on their reverse side.

MX.title: Red-Banded Bollards
MX.description: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit.

MX.title: Jalisco Bollards with Crown
MX.description: Some Jalisco bollards bear a crown symbol and the word "Jalisco".

MX.title: Acorn-Shaped White Insulators
MX.description: Small white insulators resembling acorns sit atop power poles in coastal states, especially Michoacan, Colima, and Veracruz.

MX.title: Asymmetric Crossbar Poles
MX.description: Power poles with an off-centre crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.

MX.title: Wooden Poles with Lowered Crossbar
MX.description: Wooden utility poles with a noticeably lower crossbar are mainly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.

MX.title: Hanging Insulators on Concrete Poles
MX.description: Concrete power poles with insulators hanging below the crossbar are typical of the Yucatan peninsula.

MX.title: Wooden Hanging-Insulator Poles
MX.description: Wooden poles with hanging insulators are found on the Baja California peninsula.

MX.title: Single Support Beam Poles
MX.description: Utility poles with a lowered crossbar braced by a single diagonal support beam are specific to Durango.

MX.title: Mesh-Body Poles
MX.description: Utility poles with a lattice or mesh body are common in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

MX.title: White Centre Road Lines
MX.description: Roads in Tabasco commonly use white centre lines instead of yellow.

MX.title: Red-Barked Tree Fences
MX.description: Living fences made from trees with reddish bark are characteristic of Veracruz.

MX.title: Black Tar Along Centre Lines
MX.description: Black tar patches flanking yellow centre lines appear in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.

MX.title: Grainy Blue-Grey Pavement
MX.description: Coarse-textured road surfaces with a blue-grey tinge are typical of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.

MX.title: Irregular Cobblestone Pavement
MX.description: Streets paved with randomly arranged, irregular cobblestones are widespread in central Mexico, especially Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

MX.title: Hexagonal Tile Pavement
MX.description: Streets surfaced with interlocking hexagonal tiles are distinctive of Puebla and Tlaxcala.

MX.title: Three-Line Cobblestone Pavement
MX.description: A cobblestone pattern with three parallel lines of stones is mainly associated with Oaxaca.

MX.title: Mexicali Farmland and Brown Poles
MX.description: Mexicali features flat farmland, a western ridge, Washingtonia palms, and brown wooden utility poles.

MX.title: Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Ridge
MX.description: A long, flat-topped ridge in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve is visible from roads in eastern San Luis Potosi.

MX.title: Country Flag
MX.description: The national flag of Mexico is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MX.title: .mx Domain
MX.description: Web addresses in Mexico end in the country domain .mx (often as .com.mx). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

NL.title: Landscape
NL.description: Landscape can be a great clue to figure out where you are. The Netherlands is very flat for example.

NL.title: Licenseplate
NL.description: License plates on vehicles differ from country to country. In the Netherlands they are yellow, a quite rare sight!

NL.title: Sun
NL.description: You can tell what hemisphere you are in by looking at the sun. A sun to the South usually means you are on the Northern half of the globe.

NL.title: Brick roads
NL.description: Brick roads are common throughout the Netherlands.

NL.title: Dutch Language
NL.description: Dutch is a Germanic language with frequent double vowels and distinctive letter combinations like 'ij'.

NL.title: Dutch Bollards
NL.description: Dutch bollards are plain white posts with a red reflector.

NL.title: Absence of Utility Poles
NL.description: Street-level utility poles are essentially absent in the Netherlands; only large high-voltage towers appear.

NL.title: Abundant Waterways
NL.description: Canals, ditches, dikes, dams, and bridges are constant, reflecting Dutch water management.

NL.title: Tree-Lined Rural Roads
NL.description: Dutch rural roads are often bordered by rows of trees on both sides, creating a tunnel effect.

NL.title: Highly Organised Urban Planning
NL.description: Dutch towns have neat, orderly layouts with well-maintained roads and uniform row houses.

NL.title: All-White Road Markings
NL.description: Dutch road lines are entirely white, with common dashed edge lines and occasional green centre lines.

NL.title: Bicycle Paths
NL.description: Dedicated cycling lanes run alongside many roads, often reddish-pink; cycling is a primary transport mode.

NL.title: Distinctive Sidewalk Tiles
NL.description: Sidewalks typically use uniform square grey tiles in an offset pattern; historic areas may have brick paving.

NL.title: Speed Bumps with Alternating Stripes
NL.description: Dutch speed bumps have alternating long and short white warning stripes on brick or asphalt.

NL.title: Brick Rumble Strips
NL.description: Rural roads often have brick-paved rumble strips along edges, unique to the Netherlands.

NL.title: Blue Street Signs with White Text
NL.description: Street name signs are nearly always blue with white lettering; common suffixes include -straat, -weg, -laan.

NL.title: Direction Signs
NL.description: Motorist direction signs are blue with white text; cyclist signs are white with a red border.

NL.title: Blue Town Entry Signs
NL.description: Town entry signs are blue, often with decorative frames and supplementary signs.

NL.title: Green Road Markers (Hectometre Posts)
NL.description: Roadside kilometre markers are green with road numbers in coloured boxes: red for highways, yellow for regional roads.

NL.title: Road Sign Edges Visible from Behind
NL.description: Dutch road signs have edges wrapping around to the back, creating a visible border.

NL.title: Striped Signpost Markings
NL.description: Signpost poles often have black-and-white or blue-and-white striped bands.

NL.title: Bulky Yellow Signposts on Traffic Islands
NL.description: Road signs on traffic islands are often mounted on thick, bright yellow posts.

NL.title: Striped Road Barriers
NL.description: Red-and-white striped barriers are common along Dutch roads, especially rural areas.

NL.title: Brick Architecture
NL.description: Buildings are mostly red-brown brick with roofs of orange or dark grey tiles.

NL.title: Row Houses
NL.description: Nearly half of Dutch homes are row houses (terraced houses).

NL.title: Windmills and Wind Turbines
NL.description: Traditional windmills and modern wind turbines are common sights.

NL.title: Landline Area Codes
NL.description: Dutch landline numbers start with three- or four-digit area codes that are geographically grouped.

NL.title: Drenthe N-Road Hectometre Marker
NL.description: Drenthe's N-road markers have a yellow box with the road number and often a 'DR' abbreviation or provincial logo.

NL.title: Flevoland N-Road Hectometre Marker
NL.description: Flevoland's N-road markers show a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'Flevoland' or the province's blue-green logo.

NL.title: Friesland N-Road Hectometre Marker
NL.description: Friesland's N-road markers have a yellow box with the road number and often 'FR' or Frisian flag motifs.

NL.title: Gelderland N-Road Hectometre Marker
NL.description: Gelderland's N-road markers feature a yellow box with the road number and sometimes 'GLD' or the provincial logo.

NL.title: Groningen N-Road Hectometre Marker
NL.description: Groningen's N-road markers show a yellow box with the road number and often 'GR' or the provincial flag pattern.

NL.title: Limburg N-Road Hectometre Marker
NL.description: Limburg's N-road markers have a yellow box with the road number and sometimes 'LB' or a Limburg lion emblem or flag colors.

NL.title: North Brabant N-Road Hectometre Marker
NL.description: North Brabant's N-road markers feature a yellow box with the road number and sometimes 'NB' or the province's checkerboard flag motif.

NL.title: North Holland N-Road Marker
NL.description: North Holland's N-road hectometre markers show a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'NH' or the province's blue and yellow flag colors or lion emblem.

NL.title: Overijssel N-Road Marker
NL.description: Overijssel's N-road hectometre markers use a yellow box for the road number, sometimes with 'OV' or the province's wavy red-yellow-blue flag motif.

NL.title: South Holland N-Road Marker
NL.description: South Holland's N-road hectometre markers feature a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'ZH' or the province's red lion emblem or flag colors.

NL.title: Utrecht N-Road Marker
NL.description: Utrecht's N-road hectometre markers display a yellow box with the road number, sometimes including 'UT' or the province's red-and-white flag motif.

NL.title: Zeeland N-Road Marker
NL.description: Zeeland's N-road hectometre markers feature a yellow road number box, sometimes with 'ZL' or the province's blue-and-white wavy flag motif or lion emblem.

NL.title: Provincial Flags
NL.description: Friesland and Noord-Brabant flags appear frequently. The unofficial flag of the Achterhoek region is also sometimes visible.

NL.title: Frisian Bilingual Signs
NL.description: In Friesland, many town entry signs show both Dutch and Frisian place names. Street names ending in -wei or -strjitte are uniquely Frisian.

NL.title: Limburg Street Light Stickers
NL.description: Street lights in Limburg have tall, vertical white stickers with three to four digits.

NL.title: North Brabant Street Light Stickers
NL.description: Street lights in North Brabant have horizontal white stickers showing one or two digits.

NL.title: Polder Landscape
NL.description: Western and northern regions are flat, marshy polders criss-crossed by many small waterways.

NL.title: Farmland Landscape
NL.description: Southern and eastern regions have flat farmland with waterways but less marshy terrain.

NL.title: Low Hills of Southern Limburg
NL.description: Southern Limburg features gentle rolling hills contrasting with the rest of the flat country.

NL.title: Veluwe Forested Region
NL.description: The Veluwe in central Gelderland is wooded with old-growth forest, heathland, and sandy ground.

NL.title: Flevoland's Reclaimed Polder
NL.description: Flevoland was reclaimed from the sea, with straight roads, vast fields, wind turbines, and no historic buildings.

NL.title: Coastal Dunes
NL.description: Sand dunes line most of the Dutch North Sea coastline.

NL.title: Wadden Islands
NL.description: The Wadden Islands have extensive sand dunes and tourism-related signage or infrastructure.

NL.title: Large Farm Roofs in the North
NL.description: Northern farmhouses have oversized, sweeping roofs.

NL.title: Rolling Shutters on Southern Houses
NL.description: Window rolling shutters are more common in the southern half of the country.

NL.title: Country Flag
NL.description: The national flag of the Netherlands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

NL.title: .nl Domain
NL.description: Web addresses in the Netherlands end in the country domain .nl. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

RS.title: Language Duo
RS.description: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.

RS.title: Language Letters
RS.description: There are many different languages using the Cyrillic alphabet. Most of them have a few unique letters. The Serbian language is the only to feature the'Ђ' letter.

RS.title: Poles
RS.description: Utility poles will be different country to country. They come in many different colors, shapes and materials. Serbia will usually have round poles made of concrete.

RS.title: Off center
RS.description: Serbian bollards come in several designs, but most share an off-centered reflector.

RS.title: Web domain
RS.description: The top domain in Serbia is .RS, originating from its full name Republic of Serbia.

RS.title: B-Profile Guardrails
RS.description: Serbia uses B-profile guardrails exclusively.

RS.title: Chevrons
RS.description: Serbian chevrons are black arrows on a white background.

RS.title: Licence Plates
RS.description: Serbian plates are white with a blue strip on the left; agricultural vehicles have green plates.

RS.title: Serbian Cyrillic Script
RS.description: Serbian Cyrillic includes unique letters Ђ/ђ and Ћ/ћ.

RS.title: Serbian Latin Script
RS.description: Serbian Latin uses the special letters Č, Ć, Đ, Š, and Ž.

RS.title: Topography
RS.description: Vojvodina is flat; central-southern regions are hillier; mountains lie in southwest and southeast Serbia.

RS.title: Telephone Area Codes
RS.description: Serbian area codes are two digits starting with 1 to 3, varying by region.

RS.title: Vojvodina, Flat Agriculture
RS.description: Northern Serbia between Hungary and Belgrade is completely flat agricultural land.

RS.title: Central-Northern Rolling Hills
RS.description: Gentle rolling hills lie between Vojvodina and southern mountains.

RS.title: Southern Morava River Basin
RS.description: Rolling landscape with larger hills and distant mountains.

RS.title: Lush Southern Mountains
RS.description: Dense green mountains appear along the Bulgarian and Kosovo borders.

RS.title: Autumn Coverage
RS.description: Fall-colored coverage is found around Belgrade, south of Čačak and near Valjevo.

RS.title: Language 01 Bilingual
RS.description: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.

RS.title: Yellow Centre Lines on E-80
RS.description: A short E-80 section north of Pirot has yellow centre lines.

RS.title: Country Flag
RS.description: The national flag of Serbia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

RS.title: Topography (North)
RS.description: Vojvodina in the north is flat, low-lying plains.

RS.title: Topography (South)
RS.description: Central and southern Serbia are hilly, with mountains in the southwest and southeast.

TH.title: Drivingside
TH.description: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.

TH.title: Small circles
TH.description: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.

TH.title: Stopsign
TH.description: Stop signs differ between countries. In Thailand the stop signs are written in Thai.

TH.title: Many flags
TH.description: In Thailand, flags are commonly hung along streets. Besides the national flag, yellow royal banners appear frequently.

TH.title: Signposts
TH.description: Thai sign-mounting posts are thick and square-shaped, typically white, with the lower portion painted black.

TH.title: Thai plates
TH.description: In Thailand, passenger vehicles carry large white plates. Commercial vehicles have yellow plates instead.

TH.title: Driving direction
TH.description: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.

TH.title: Bollards
TH.description: Thai bollards are square with a pointed top and painted in alternating black-and-white stripes.

TH.title: Concrete Roads
TH.description: Paved concrete surfaces in Thailand typically display a large square-tile pattern.

TH.title: Utility Poles
TH.description: Thai utility poles are square-profiled concrete with a vertical row of small pinholes up the shaft.

TH.title: Language 01 Small Circles
TH.description: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.

TH.title: Yellow Centre Lines
TH.description: Thai road centre markings are yellow, either solid or dashed lines.

TH.title: Street Light Pole Markings
TH.description: The base of street light poles is painted with red-and-black or black-and-white stripes.

TH.title: Overhanging Lamp Posts
TH.description: Thai lamp posts are long and slender, arcing outward over the roadway.

TH.title: Directional Road Signs
TH.description: Minor-road directional signs are white with two stacked panels; highways have green signs often with romanised names.

TH.title: Road Signs 01 Stop Signs
TH.description: In Thailand the stop signs are written in Thai.

TH.title: Garuda Road Markers
TH.description: Thai route-number markers feature a white or black Garuda symbol; national routes are white-and-black shields, provincial routes blue-and-yellow.

TH.title: Green Village Signs
TH.description: Distinctive small green signs are widespread, especially in rural villages.

TH.title: Black Utility Boxes with Province Codes
TH.description: Small black boxes on utility infrastructure display a three-letter province code in two formats.

TH.title: Muslim Communities
TH.description: Islamic culture is concentrated in Thailand's southernmost provinces with mosques and Jawi script.

TH.title: Flat and Dry Landscapes
TH.description: Two regions north and east of Bangkok are noticeably flat and arid.

TH.title: Tall Mountains in the Northwest
TH.description: High mountain terrain is concentrated in northwestern Thailand.

TH.title: Low Forested Mountains
TH.description: Gently rounded, densely forested hills appear in the centre-north of the country.

TH.title: Exposed Rock Mountains
TH.description: Steep, rocky mountain faces with exposed rock are mostly in western Thailand and the southern peninsula.

TH.title: Red Soil
TH.description: Reddish earth is most prevalent in the northeast (Isan).

TH.title: Rubber Plantations
TH.description: Rubber tree plantations are concentrated in the south, identifiable by black tapping cups near trunks.

TH.title: Rice Cultivation Zone
TH.description: Most of Thailand's rice farming takes place within the highlighted region.

TH.title: Dry-Season Rice
TH.description: Dry-season rice is common on the central plains, often with hazy skies from wildfire smoke.

TH.title: Wet-Season Rice
TH.description: Wet-season rice paddies are concentrated in the eastern lowlands.

TH.title: Palm Oil Plantations
TH.description: Palm oil plantations are heavily concentrated on the southern peninsula.

TH.title: Short Coconut Palm Plantations
TH.description: Dense groves of short to medium coconut palms are common west of Bangkok.

TH.title: Palmyra Palms
TH.description: Large clusters of palmyra palms are typical of the eastern peninsula coast and far south.

TH.title: Sugar Cane Fields
TH.description: Sugar cane cultivation is mainly in central and eastern Thailand.

TH.title: Cassava Fields
TH.description: Cassava, a shrubby plant with hand-shaped leaves, is common on central and northeastern plains.

TH.title: Corn Fields
TH.description: Maize cultivation is concentrated in northern and central regions.

TH.title: Durian Plantations
TH.description: Durian orchards near Chanthaburi and the peninsula have cone-shaped young trees and mature trees with dark bark and pointed leaves.

TH.title: Pineapple Plantations
TH.description: Pineapple farms are concentrated southeast and southwest of Bangkok.

TH.title: Teak Trees
TH.description: Teak grows mainly in the north, recognizable by large leaves and yellow flowers.

TH.title: Pine Trees (Tenasserim Pine)
TH.description: Pinus latteri is found almost exclusively in the north and northwest.

TH.title: Garden Croton
TH.description: Garden croton is an ornamental shrub with vivid yellow, orange, and red foliage, thriving around Ranong and coastal provinces.

TH.title: Gray Corrugated Metal Roofs
TH.description: Gray corrugated metal roofing is most frequent in northern and southern regions.

TH.title: Indented Utility Poles
TH.description: Poles with a Chilean-style vertical indent are typical near Bangkok.

TH.title: Wind Turbines
TH.description: Wind farms are on western flanks of Chaiyaphum and Nakhon Ratchasima, and eastern coast in Songkhla and Nakhon Si Thammarat.

TH.title: Insulators with 7+ Ridges
TH.description: Power-line insulators with seven or more ridges appear in the southern peninsula and highways in Chiang Rai and Phayao.

TH.title: Single Insulator on Crossbar
TH.description: Poles with one insulator on the crossbar are found from Ranong and Chumphon southward.

TH.title: Two Insulators on Crossbar
TH.description: Poles with two insulators on the crossbar are common outside the southern peninsula.

TH.title: Country Flag
TH.description: The national flag of Thailand is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

TH.title: .th Domain
TH.description: Web addresses in Thailand end in the country domain .th (often as .co.th). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

SE.title: Swedish uses Å, Ä and Ö
Short dashes
SE.description: In Sweden, the outer road lines often have short, white dashed markings.

SE.title: Pedestrian crossing
SE.description: Swedish pedestrian signs feature four stripes on the crossing. A variant with a female silhouette also exists.

SE.title: Swedish bollard
SE.description: Swedish bollards are black-and-white, usually fitted with a grey reflector. Near intersections, the reflectors are often orange.

SE.title: Snow poles
SE.description: Swedish snow poles are typically orange with a tall white reflector positioned slightly above the midpoint.

SE.title: Red houses
SE.description: In the countryside Sweden, along with Norway and Finland, has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.

SE.title: Licence Plates
SE.description: Swedish plates are long and white with a blue EU strip; taxi plates have a yellow background.

SE.title: Swedish Language
SE.description: Swedish is a North Germanic language with the letters Å, Ä, and Ö.

SE.title: White Road Lines
SE.description: All road markings in Sweden are white.

SE.title: Utility Poles
SE.description: Swedish wooden utility poles often have a small black metal cap on top.

SE.title: Lamp Mounting on Wooden Poles
SE.description: Lamps on Swedish wooden poles are mounted slightly below the top with a double-bolt arrangement.

SE.title: Electricity Markers
SE.description: Wooden electricity markers with a blue and white stripe at the top are unique to Sweden.

SE.title: Directional Signs
SE.description: Most Swedish directional signs are blue with white text and an arrow, while yellow signs with black text are typically used for smaller local destinations.

SE.title: Warning Road Signs
SE.description: Swedish warning and regulatory signs have a red border with a yellow background.

SE.title: Chevron Signs
SE.description: Swedish chevrons feature yellow arrows on a blue background.

SE.title: Meeting Place Signs
SE.description: Blue signs with a large white M indicate designated meeting places on smaller roads.

SE.title: Striped Signpost Markings
SE.description: Swedish signposts often have coloured striped markings, commonly blue-and-white or red-and-yellow.

SE.title: Red-and-Yellow Road Infrastructure
SE.description: Road infrastructure and work signs in Sweden are often painted red and yellow.

SE.title: Street Name Suffixes
SE.description: Swedish street names often end in "vägen" or "gatan," abbreviated as "v" and "g" on signs.

SE.title: Landscape Overview
SE.description: Sweden has boreal forests, farmlands, lakes, mountainous north and west, and flatter south and east.

SE.title: Traditional Wooden Fences
SE.description: Traditional fences use thin vertical tree trunks with diagonal trunks stacked on top.

SE.title: Volvo Cars
SE.description: Volvo is the most popular car brand, nearly 30% of passenger vehicles.

SE.title: Swedish Church Flag
SE.description: The church flag has a red cross on yellow with a crown in the centre.

SE.title: Broad-Leafed Trees
SE.description: Broad-leafed trees grow naturally only in southern Sweden and increase further south.

SE.title: Ferns
SE.description: Ferns are mostly in southern and central Sweden, occasionally further north along the east coast.

SE.title: Treeless Mountain Tops
SE.description: Mountains with bare, treeless summits are found exclusively in northwestern Sweden.

SE.title: Far-North Boreal Vegetation
SE.description: Thin, sparse boreal trees growing on sandy soil are characteristic of Sweden's far north.

SE.title: Beech Forests
SE.description: Beech forests have barren floors carpeted with brown leaves and are restricted to southern Sweden.

SE.title: Rock Walls
SE.description: Stone walls are mainly found in southern Sweden, especially along coasts, Öland, and Gotland.

SE.title: Exposed Rocks on the West Coast
SE.description: Rounded, exposed rocky outcrops with low vegetation are common along the Swedish west coast.

SE.title: Skåne's Open Agricultural Landscape
SE.description: Skåne features open farmland with scattered trees and diverse crops.

SE.title: Lake Mälaren Landscape
SE.description: Around Lake Mälaren, flat terrain has medium fields, forests in the background, and small tree clusters in fields.

SE.title: Västergötland and Östergötland Farmlands
SE.description: Flat, open farmland with abundant wind turbines and distant forest lines.

SE.title: Halland West Coast Landscape
SE.description: Flat fields with small, round forested hills and lush vegetation characterize Halland's west coast.

SE.title: Northern Coastal Farmland (Umeå–Luleå)
SE.description: Flat, small-to-medium agricultural fields near the coast between Umeå and Luleå.

SE.title: Jämtland Hillside Farmlands
SE.description: Large farmlands on wide, steep hillsides around Lake Storsjön, usually covered in grass.

SE.title: High Coast Landscape (Västernorrland)
SE.description: Forested, rocky mountains surround winding agricultural valleys in the High Coast area.

SE.title: Södermanland Valley Fields
SE.description: Medium to small agricultural fields run through small valleys lined with forests.

SE.title: White Sand on Gotland
SE.description: White sand is often visible alongside roads on Gotland, especially northern parts and Fårö.

SE.title: Red Dirt Roads
SE.description: Unpaved roads with red soil appear mainly in Dalarna and parts of Kalmar, Norrbotten, and Västerbotten.

SE.title: Grey Dirt Roads in Northern Jämtland
SE.description: Deep grey dirt roads bordered by low green grass are common in northern Jämtland.

SE.title: Öland Island Landscape
SE.description: Öland is flat; the south is barren with small bushes, the north lusher with larger bushes and trees.

SE.title: Birch Rows Along the North Coast
SE.description: Long rows of thin birch trees line urban streets in northern coastal towns.

SE.title: Grey Metal Roofs
SE.description: Grey metal roofing on houses becomes more common further north in Sweden.

SE.title: Skåne Houses with Wooden Gable Triangles
SE.description: Houses in Skåne often have white stone or red brick walls with coloured wooden triangles on gables.

SE.title: Half-Timbered Houses
SE.description: Half-timbered architecture is mainly found in southern Skåne and parts of Halland.

SE.title: Red Brick Houses in Skåne
SE.description: Many older single-family homes in Skåne are built from red brick.

SE.title: Corrugated Metal Roof Panels with Moss
SE.description: Square corrugated metal roofs with moss are typical in southern Sweden, especially Skåne and Blekinge.

SE.title: Diamond-Tiled Roofs
SE.description: Grey diamond-shaped roof tiles are mainly found in Skåne, Blekinge, Öland, and sometimes Gotland.

SE.title: Light-Coloured Houses on the West Coast
SE.description: The west coast has many white and light yellow houses, especially between Gothenburg and Norway.

SE.title: Red Fishing Sheds on the West Coast
SE.description: Dense rows of small red sheds are typical in coastal towns along the northern west coast.

SE.title: Dalarna Wooden Craftsmanship Architecture
SE.description: Central Dalarna features red timbered houses, log portals, and distinctive "härbren" storage buildings.

SE.title: Hälsingland Farmhouses
SE.description: Hälsingland has large red farmhouses with many windows and long grand facades.

SE.title: Octagonal and Leaning-Wall Sheds
SE.description: Northern coastal agricultural sheds are octagonal or rectangular with outward-leaning red-painted log walls.

SE.title: Gotland Limestone Architecture
SE.description: Gotland houses are often limestone with dirty white facades; churches have grey or white walls with grey corners and small windows.

SE.title: Öland Uneven Stone Brick
SE.description: Uneven, irregular stone bricks characterize houses and rock walls on Öland.

SE.title: Blekinge Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Blekinge bus stop signs have a blue background with a white bus icon, often outlined in red or blue.

SE.title: Dalarna Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Dalarna bus stop signs have a white background with a red border and a white horse.

SE.title: Gävleborg Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Gävleborg bus stop signs show a yellow background with a black bus icon.

SE.title: Gotland Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Gotland bus stop signs are yellow with a green border.

SE.title: Halland Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Halland bus stop signs feature a yellow background with a black bus icon.

SE.title: Jämtland Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: In Jämtland, you can spot the Länstrafiken logo on buses and bus stop signs. The logo features a stylized “Z”.

SE.title: Jönköping Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Jönköping bus stop signs have a green background with a white bus icon.

SE.title: Kalmar Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: In Kalmar län, you can spot the Kalmar länstrafik logo on buses and bus stop signs. The logo is a stylised heart and the busses are usually yellow and red.

SE.title: Länstrafiken Kronoberg
SE.description: Kronoberg bus company is called "Länstrafiken Kronoberg".

SE.title: Norrbotten Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Norrbotten bus stop signs are white with a blue border and a blue bus icon.

SE.title: Örebro Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Örebro bus stop signs feature a yellow background with a black bus icon.

SE.title: Östergötland Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Östergötland bus stop signs are white with a blue border and a blue bus icon.

SE.title: Skåne Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: In Skåne, you can spot the Skånetrafiken logo on buses and bus stop signs.

SE.title: Södermanland Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Södermanland bus stop signs have a white background with a blue border and a blue bus icon.

SE.title: Stockholm Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Stockholm bus stop signs are white at the bottom and red at the top with a "SL" logo.

SE.title: Uppsala Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Uppsala bus stop signs have a yellow and/or grey background with a black "UL" logo.

SE.title: Värmland bus logo
SE.description: In Värmland, you can spot the "Värmlandstrafiken" logo on busses and bus stops.

SE.title: Västerbotten Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Västerbotten bus stop signs are white with a blue border and a black bus icon.

SE.title: Västernorrland Bus Stop Sign
SE.description: Västernorrland bus stop signs have a white background with a blue border and a blue bus icon.

SE.title: "VL" in Västmanland
SE.description: In Västmanland, you can see the VL logo on buses and bus stop signs.

SE.title: Västra Götaland Bus Company
SE.description: In Västra Götaland, you can spot the Västtrafik logo on blue buses and bus stop signs

SE.title: Stockholm County Red Wooden Bus Shelter
SE.description: Stockholm County's bus shelters are large, red wooden structures with steep pitched roofs and open sides.

SE.title: Västra Götaland Red Rural Bus Shelter
SE.description: Västra Götaland rural bus shelters are red-painted wood with a pronounced slanted roof.

SE.title: Skåne Red Timber Bus Shelter
SE.description: Skåne rural bus shelters are red-painted wood with a sharply angled roof.

SE.title: Uppsala County Classic Red Bus Shelter
SE.description: Uppsala County bus shelters are large red wooden structures with steeply sloped roofs.

SE.title: Östergötland Rural Red Bus Shelter
SE.description: Östergötland rural bus shelters are red-painted wood with steeply sloped roofs.

SE.title: Stockholm County Road Number Signs
SE.description: Stockholm County road signs have white numbers on a blue rectangular background, usually 100–299.

SE.title: Västra Götaland County Road Number Signs
SE.description: Västra Götaland road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, usually 40–200.

SE.title: Skåne County Road Number Signs
SE.description: Skåne road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, frequently 9–100.

SE.title: Uppsala Road Number Signs
SE.description: Uppsala County's road signs show white numbers on blue rectangles, usually 200–300.

SE.title: Södermanland Road Number Signs
SE.description: Södermanland County uses blue rectangular signs with white numbers, commonly 50–200.

SE.title: Östergötland Road Number Signs
SE.description: Östergötland County has blue rectangular signs with white numbers, typically 50–200.

SE.title: Jönköping Road Number Signs
SE.description: Jönköping County uses blue rectangular signs with white numbers, mostly 100–200.

SE.title: Kronoberg Road Number Signs
SE.description: Kronoberg County's road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, commonly 120–200.

SE.title: Kalmar Road Number Signs
SE.description: Kalmar County shows road numbers on blue rectangular signs with white digits, typically 120–200.

SE.title: Gotland Road Number Signs
SE.description: Gotland's road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, often 140–150.

SE.title: Blekinge Road Number Signs
SE.description: Blekinge County uses blue rectangular signs with white numbers, usually 20–120.

SE.title: Norrbotten Road Number Signs
SE.description: Norrbotten County has blue rectangular signs with white numbers, commonly 300–404.

SE.title: Västerbotten Road Number Signs
SE.description: Västerbotten County's road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, often 300–400.

SE.title: Västernorrland Road Number Signs
SE.description: Västernorrland County shows road numbers on blue rectangular signs with white digits, typically 300–400.

SE.title: Jämtland Road Number Signs
SE.description: Jämtland County uses blue rectangular signs with white numbers, generally 300–400.

SE.title: Dalarna Road Number Signs
SE.description: Dalarna County's road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, often 200–300.

SE.title: Gävleborg Road Number Signs
SE.description: Gävleborg County's road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, typically 200–300.

SE.title: Värmland Road Number Signs
SE.description: Värmland County features blue rectangular signs with white numbers, usually 200–300.

SE.title: Örebro Road Number Signs
SE.description: Örebro County uses blue rectangular signs with white numbers, generally 200–300.

SE.title: Västmanland Road Number Signs
SE.description: Västmanland County's road signs are blue rectangles with white numbers, often 200–300.

SE.title: Snowmobile Trail Markers
SE.description: Small red crosses mark snowmobile trails throughout northern Sweden.

SE.title: Red-Tinted Roads in Dalarna
SE.description: Paved roads in western Dalarna often have a pronounced reddish colour.

SE.title: Green Snow Poles Near Umeå
SE.description: Green snow poles occasionally appear around Umeå.

SE.title: Wedge-Shaped Bollards
SE.description: Wedge-shaped bollards like those in Germany are common in southern Sweden.

SE.title: Cylindrical Bollards
SE.description: Cylindrical bollards with a horizontal black section near the top appear near the west coast, Värmland, and southern Dalarna.

SE.title: Flat Bollards in Northern Sweden
SE.description: Flat bollards or cylindrical bollards with a black reflector rectangle appear on major roads in northern Sweden.

SE.title: Skåne Blue/Red-Striped Bollards
SE.description: Small white bollards with blue or red strips near the top are found in rural Skåne.

SE.title: Railway Crossing Sign ID Numbers
SE.description: The back of railway crossing signs has a yellow sticker with a 5-digit ID; the first digit indicates region.

SE.title: Place Name Endings
SE.description: Certain place name suffixes are region-specific, useful for pinpointing locations.

SE.title: Sámi Bilingual Signs
SE.description: Bilingual Sámi and Swedish signs appear in northern Sweden's inland areas.

SE.title: Meänkieli Language Signs
SE.description: Meänkieli appears on signs near the Finnish border, often on river names ending in "väylä."

SE.title: Area Codes on Phone Numbers
SE.description: Swedish landlines start with 3–4 digit area codes; the first two digits follow a regional pattern.

SE.title: Mistletoe Near Lake Mälaren
SE.description: Mistletoe grows mainly near Lake Mälaren, especially in Västerås.

SE.title: Orchards Near Kivik
SE.description: Most of Sweden's large orchards are around Kivik on Skåne's east coast.

SE.title: Slag Stone Buildings
SE.description: Buildings partly or fully made from blue or green slag stone appear in Bergslagen.

SE.title: Wooden Windmills on Öland
SE.description: Numerous small grey or red wooden windmills dot Öland, which has the most windmills in Sweden.

SE.title: Local City Bus Stop Signs
SE.description: Many cities and towns have unique local bus stop sign designs.

SE.title: Neon-Yellow School Bus Stop Signs
SE.description: Bright neon-yellow school bus stop signs are common in Linköping, Norrköping, and Jönköping.

SE.title: Kungsbacka Bus Stops with Blue Stripes
SE.description: Bus stops with three blue stripes indicate Kungsbacka municipality.

SE.title: Trams
SE.description: Trams are mainly in Gothenburg, with smaller networks in Norrköping and Stockholm.

SE.title: Black Bus Shelters in Västerås and Umeå
SE.description: Black bus shelters with a distinctive square ridge along the back of the roof are found in both Västerås and Umeå.

SE.title: Stockholm Street Signs
SE.description: Stockholm street signs have two rows separated by a black line and usually no black border.

SE.title: Gothenburg Blue Street Signs
SE.description: Gothenburg uses distinctive blue street signs across the entire city. They almost always feature two lines of text.

SE.title: Malmö Street Signs
SE.description: Malmö uses somewhat old-looking white street signs with black corners found throughout the city.

SE.title: Ystad Street Signs
SE.description: Street signs in Ystad resemble those in Malmö but have a yellow background instead of white.

SE.title: Vellinge Blue Street Signs
SE.description: Vellinge uses blue street signs similar to Gothenburg's but usually with one line of text.

SE.title: Falköping Yellow Street Signs
SE.description: Plain yellow street signs are distinctive to Falköping.

SE.title: Köping Blue Street Signs
SE.description: Blue street signs with a thin black outline are found in the town of Köping.

SE.title: Dalarna Dialect Street Names
SE.description: Street names ending in "gattu" or "gatu" appear near Lake Siljan in central Dalarna.

SE.title: Elfdalian Language in Älvdalen
SE.description: Elfdalian appears on street signs in Älvdalen, often ending in "-ween" or "-weg."

SE.title: Three Yellow Stripes
SE.description: Three yellow stripes appear on signposts and street lamps in Karlstad and on traffic lights in Stockholm.

SE.title: Tree Felling Advertisements
SE.description: Small yellow signs advertising tree felling services are common on poles in Stockholm suburbs.

SE.title: Sundsvall, The Dragon City (Drakstaden)
SE.description: Sundsvall is nicknamed "Drakstaden" (the Dragon City). Dragon statues and dragon-themed signs can be spotted throughout the central parts of the city.

SE.title: Country Flag
SE.description: The national flag of Sweden is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SE.title: Sverigeleden
SE.description: Square cycle route signs with a white bicycle: green is the nationwide Sverigeleden network of 39 routes, while red marks one of only 16 named national routes and narrows the area far more.

SE.title: .se Domain
SE.description: Web addresses in Sweden end in the country domain .se. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

DC.title: Australian bollards
DC.description: Australian bollards are white with a vertical red stripe towards the top.

DC.title: Au Drivingside
DC.description: In Australia they drive on the left side of the road.

DC.title: Au Yellowpoles
DC.description: In the state of Western Australia you can find yellow sign posts.

DC.title: Br Language
DC.description: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It has the letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.

DC.title: Br Redsoil
DC.description: This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.

DC.title: Br States
DC.description: Finding state abbreviations is common in Brazil. The abbreviations can be seen on the map on certain zoom levels.

DC.title: Speed signs
DC.description: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French, the official languages of Canada.

DC.title: Ch Lowcam
DC.description: In Switzerland the images were captured with a lower mounted camera. This brings us closer to the ground and makes the country feel different from most other.

DC.title: Ch Plates
DC.description: License plates in Switzerland do not feature the blue european strip on the left. Instead the red country emblem can be seen.

DC.title: Co Taxiinfo
DC.description: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.

DC.title: Co Yellowplate
DC.description: Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow license plates for personal vehicles.

DC.title: Fr Bollard
DC.description: The bollards in France are round with a pointy top. They have red or gray reflector that wraps all way around. They are reminiscent of small lighthouses.

DC.title: Gh Ghanatape
DC.description: One of the most (in)famous hints in Geoguessr is the tape on the top-right bar that can be seen when looking down. It can only be found in Ghana.

DC.title: Gh Taxiplates
DC.description: On taxi cars in Ghana you can see the panels around the tires being painted orange.

DC.title: Id Kabupaten
DC.description: Indonesia is divided into hundreds of regencies know as Kabupaten (Kab. for short). This term is unique to Indonesia.

DC.title: Id Rupiah
DC.description: The currency in Indonesia is Rupiah. It is displayed as RP.

DC.title: It Doublestrip
DC.description: The Italian license plates will have a blue strip on both sides. The front plates are also shorter than usual.

DC.title: It Signs
DC.description: Directional signs in Italy tend to be bright blue with a white capitalised text.

DC.title: Jo Taxi
DC.description: In Amman, the capital of Jordan, you will find taxis in a distinct yellow-and-green palette.

DC.title: Jp Drivingside
DC.description: In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.

DC.title: Jp Smallcars
DC.description: In Japan small, boxy cars are very common. They are called Kei cars.

DC.title: Jp Vendingmachine
DC.description: Japan has millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.

DC.title: Kr Circles
DC.description: In written Korean you will find a lot of big circles.

DC.title: Kr Drivingside
DC.description: In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.

DC.title: Lk Amongus
DC.description: The written Sri Lankan language Sinhala have letters that are very round. Some letter makes it look like there are small doodle characters among us.

DC.title: Lk Drivingside
DC.description: In Sri Lanka they drive on the left side of the road.

DC.title: Mn Barren
DC.description: The Mongolian landscape is often barren, featuring large open areas without much vegetation.

DC.title: Mn Bollard
DC.description: The Mongolian bollard is reminiscent of a bowling pin.

DC.title: Mt Drivingside
DC.description: Malta is one of the few European countries that drive on the left.

DC.title: Mt Limestone
DC.description: You will see a lot of walls and buildings made from limestone in Malta.

DC.title: Mt Triq
DC.description: Triq is the Maltese word for street and it will only show up in Malta.

DC.title: Mx Pinktaxi
DC.description: Taxi cars in the Mexican capital are white and pink. They also feature the text CDMX, an abbreviation of Ciudad De Mexico.

DC.title: Mx Poles
DC.description: Mexico usually has octagonal utility poles made of concrete.

DC.title: Nl Flat
DC.description: The Netherlands is a very flat country. You won't find many hills here.

DC.title: Nl Yellowplate
DC.description: In the Netherlands license plates are yellow, quite a rare sight in Europe.

DC.title: Pe Blackwhite
DC.description: Many signposts in Peru are square-shaped and painted in alternating black and white.

DC.title: Pe Conkcreet
DC.description: Metal signs in Peru are standing on visible concrete plinths.

DC.title: Tuk tuks
DC.description: Tuk Tuks are a common sight in Peru. They are usually referred to as mototaxi.

DC.title: Ph Boxes
DC.description: In the Philippines city abbreviations can often be found on boxes mounted on utility poles.

DC.title: Ph Conkcreet
DC.description: Roads in the Philippines are often made of big concrete blocks.

DC.title: Ph Drivingside
DC.description: They drive on the right side of the road in the Philippines.

DC.title: Pl Crossing
DC.description: Pedestrian crossing signs in Poland only features a horizontal line. No "zebra stripes" here.

DC.title: Pl Greensign
DC.description: Polish road signs often come in a distinct green color with a white text.

DC.title: Pl Holypole
DC.description: The utility poles in Poland are often thin and features a lot of holes. These holes usually don't go all the way down.

DC.title: Rs Duo
DC.description: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.

DC.title: Sn Blueplates
DC.description: Senegal uses blue license plates, the only country in Africa to do so.

DC.title: Sn Drivingside
DC.description: In Senegal they drive on the right side of the road.

DC.title: Th Circles
DC.description: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.

DC.title: Th Drivingside
DC.description: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.

DC.title: Th Stop
DC.description: In Thailand the stop signs are written in Thai.

TN.title: Djerba palm trees
TN.description: The island of Djerba is known for its many palm trees, which can be seen all across the island.

TN.title: Black license plates
TN.description: Tunisian license plates are black with white text. They are the only African country to have that.

TN.title: French and Arabic
TN.description: Tunisia is the only street view country combining French and Arabic. Bilingual signage appears frequently, with Arabic identifiable by its lines and dots.

TN.title: Arid landscape
TN.description: Bordering the Mediterranean, the Tunisian landscape is in general dry.

TN.title: Olive Tree Plantations
TN.description: Neatly arranged rows of olive trees on raked, weed-free soil frequently line Tunisian roads.

TN.title: White Road Lines
TN.description: Tunisian roads typically have white road lines.

TN.title: White Directional Signs
TN.description: Tunisian directional signs have a white background with town names in Arabic and Latin script.

TN.title: Traditional Blue Paint on Buildings
TN.description: Doors, windows, gates, and other architectural elements are sometimes painted in a distinctive traditional blue.

TN.title: Red-and-White Striped Kerbs
TN.description: Red-and-white striped kerbs are common on Tunisian roads.

TN.title: Concrete Road Markers with Coloured Tops
TN.description: White concrete markers with rounded red, yellow, or green tops are found throughout Tunisia.

TN.title: Bilingual Stop Signs
TN.description: Tunisian stop signs feature both Arabic and Latin text.

TN.title: Light Green Toyota Follow Car
TN.description: A light green Toyota follow car appears throughout northern Tunisia, never seen south of Hammamet.

TN.title: Dark Green Mazda Follow Car
TN.description: The dark green Mazda is Tunisia's most common follow car, found from Hammamet south to Djerba, with a military licence plate featuring a red strip on the left.

TN.title: Multiple Follow Cars in Tunis
TN.description: Follow cars in the capital Tunis vary, but most of them are carrying a red beacon on the roof.

TN.title: Country Flag
TN.description: The national flag of Tunisia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

TN.title: .tn Domain
TN.description: Web addresses in Tunisia end in the country domain .tn (often as .com.tn). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

PT.title: Portuguese chimneys
PT.description: In southern Portugal, you will often see small chimneys that are either square or round in shape.

PT.title: Stone walls
PT.description: Across the Azores, you will often see dry stone walls crafted from dark volcanic rock.

PT.title: Blue and yellow
PT.description: Portugal have white plates with a blue EU strip on the left and, on most vehicles, a yellow strip on the right, which is unique to Portugal.

PT.title: Street names
PT.description: The Portuguese word for street is "Rua", visible on nearly every street sign.

PT.title: Hunting signs
PT.description: Portuguese hunting signs are diamond or rectangular in a red-and-white color scheme.

PT.title: Portuguese Language
PT.description: Portuguese uses distinctive letters like Ç, Ã, Õ, Â, and Ê; Ñ does not appear.

PT.title: Eucalyptus Trees
PT.description: Eucalyptus is abundant across Portugal.

PT.title: Ladder Poles with Tall Steps
PT.description: Concrete ladder poles have unusually tall steps, often with small see-through holes.

PT.title: Bollards
PT.description: Bollards are wedge-shaped with thin white caps or flat with wide reflectors, usually white or sometimes orange.

PT.title: White Directional Signs
PT.description: Direction signs are white with black arrows floating clear of the edges.

PT.title: Kilometre Markers
PT.description: Kilometre markers are wide rectangular signs with a coloured left section and white right section; larger signs show road numbers.

PT.title: Black-and-White Waystones
PT.description: Small black-and-white stone markers are frequent along roads.

PT.title: Stop Sign Font
PT.description: Stop signs use a noticeably large font.

PT.title: Black-and-Yellow Chevrons
PT.description: Chevrons are black boards with yellow arrows.

PT.title: Pedestrian Signs, Five Stripes
PT.description: Pedestrian signs in Portugal show five stripes and a figure with a high belt.

PT.title: Guardrails with Red Reflectors
PT.description: In Portugal, guardrails have red reflectors.

PT.title: White Sign Borders
PT.description: Road signs typically have white borders.

PT.title: Diagonal Cobblestone Roads
PT.description: Cobblestone roads in Portugal have square stones laid diagonally to the road direction.

PT.title: Bright Cobblestone Sidewalks
PT.description: Portuguese pavements often use bright, pale cobblestones.

PT.title: White Houses with Orange Roofs
PT.description: White stone houses with orange clay-tile roofs are typical in Portugal.

PT.title: Painted Window and Door Borders
PT.description: Blue or yellow trim lines commonly outline windows, doors, and wall edges in Portugal.

PT.title: Decorative Tile Facades
PT.description: Portuguese buildings often have decorative mosaic tile (azulejos) facades.

PT.title: Telephone Area Codes
PT.description: Portuguese landline numbers start with 2 for geographic area codes; 29 indicates Azores or Madeira.

PT.title: Concrete Block Houses, North
PT.description: Northern Portuguese houses often use square concrete blocks with white mortar.

PT.title: Holm and Cork Oak Fields, Southeast
PT.description: Southeast fields have sparse holm and cork oaks, appearing dry in summer and lush in spring.

PT.title: Olive Plantations, East
PT.description: Olive groves concentrate in eastern Portugal, especially northeast and southeast.

PT.title: Dense Eucalyptus Forests, Northwest
PT.description: Thick eucalyptus forests are mainly in northwest Portugal.

PT.title: Maritime Pine Forests, North
PT.description: Northern Portugal has maritime pines with grey bark and reddish undertones, bare lower trunks.

PT.title: Terraced Vineyards, Douro Valley
PT.description: Steep terraced vineyards appear in the Douro wine region east of Porto.

PT.title: Citrus Plantations, South Coast
PT.description: Citrus groves concentrate along Portugal's southern coastline.

PT.title: Serra da Estrela, Rocky Highland
PT.description: Rocky mountainous highland with yellow-and-black striped snow poles.

PT.title: Sandy Pine Coast, Setúbal to Sines
PT.description: Pine forests grow on very white sandy soil along the coast between Setúbal and Sines.

PT.title: Far Southwest, Barren Flat Land
PT.description: Flat, uncultivated land with low bushes, grass, and very few trees, appearing dry.

PT.title: Country Flag
PT.description: The national flag of Portugal is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PT.title: .pt Domain
PT.description: Web addresses in Portugal end in the country domain .pt. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

KH.title: Cambodian poles
KH.description: In Cambodia, you will typically see either concrete ladder poles with rectangular sections or round poles with small holes.

KH.title: White license plates
KH.description: Cambodian plates are white with blue lettering, though the blue is often hard to see through the blur, making them look white.

KH.title: Khmer script
KH.description: The Khmer writing system has a highly recognisable script, with intricate, curvy letterforms in most fonts.

KH.title: Bollards
KH.description: Common bollards are stone posts with red-and-white stripes or red tops with embedded reflectors.

KH.title: Road Markers
KH.description: Kilometre posts are stone with white bases and rounded red tops showing road numbers and town distances.

KH.title: Chevrons
KH.description: Cambodian curve boards are black with yellow arrows but appear infrequently.

KH.title: Road Lines
KH.description: Cambodian roads have yellow centre lines; white edge lines are uncommon but always solid.

KH.title: Unpaved Roads
KH.description: Many Cambodian roads are unpaved; asphalt is mostly on main roads and in urban areas.

KH.title: Stilt Houses
KH.description: Wooden stilt houses with vertical plank walls and layered roofs are widespread in Cambodia.

KH.title: House Colour Schemes
KH.description: Traditional Cambodian stilt houses have walls in dark red-brown, light blue, or ochre orange, with doors and windows often bright blue.

KH.title: Roof Styles
KH.description: Many Cambodian homes have tiled orange or red roofs, sometimes with ornamental ridge and corner details; corrugated metal roofing is also common.

KH.title: Buddhist Temples
KH.description: Ornately decorated temples with multi-tiered roofs and Buddhist flags are found throughout Cambodia.

KH.title: Beer Advertisements
KH.description: Billboards and signs advertising Angkor, Anchor, and Cambodia Beer are ubiquitous.

KH.title: CPP Party Signs
KH.description: Distinctive blue signs from the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) often feature portraits of three party leaders.

KH.title: Central Agricultural Plain
KH.description: A flat, low-lying central plain with cultivated fields and villages.

KH.title: Northeast Landscape
KH.description: Less cultivated northeast with wild vegetation and gently rolling hills.

KH.title: Southwest Highlands
KH.description: Highest elevations with hills, low mountains, dense forest inland, and more populated coastal areas.

KH.title: White Sandy Soil
KH.description: Bright white to beige sandy soil common southeast of Phnom Penh and around the capital.

KH.title: Northern Thai Border Mountains
KH.description: Mountainous ridgeline near the Thai border with characteristic red soil; roads lie in flat lowlands south of the ridgeline.

KH.title: Rubber Tree Plantations
KH.description: Neatly rowed thin-trunked rubber trees with dark green canopies, found northeast of Phnom Penh, around Ban Lung, and near Pech Sreada.

KH.title: Road 48 Black-and-White Bollards
KH.description: Black-and-white bollards appear only on Road 48 between Tatai and the Road 4 intersection.

KH.title: Kiri Sakor Road Construction
KH.description: Road from Road 48 to Kiri Sakor is under construction with one paved lane and exposed red soil on the other side.

KH.title: Southwest Jungle Off-Roads
KH.description: Unpaved tracks northeast of Road 48 with red soil, dense jungle, and hilly terrain.

KH.title: Phnum Samkos Area
KH.description: Overcast weather, large distant mountains, unpaved brown roads, and lush wild vegetation near Phnum Samkos.

KH.title: Road 4 Red Shoulders
KH.description: Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk has wide red-brown shoulders that darken closer to the coast.

KH.title: Oil Palm Plantations
KH.description: Oil palm plantations along Road 4 and its rural offshoots just north of Preah Nob.

KH.title: Road 41
KH.description: Wide gravelly grey road southwest of Phnom Penh running north-northeast through flat agricultural terrain with distant hills.

KH.title: Unique Poles
KH.description: Utility poles on Roads 5 and 6 have three horizontal beams with hanging insulators on one side and distinctive base indents.

KH.title: Pech Sreada Rubber Plantations
KH.description: Rubber trees near Pech Sreada with bright orange soil and a barren dry-season look.

KH.title: Angkor Wat
KH.description: Massive Khmer temple complex north of Siem Reap with dark weathered stone and tourist crowds.

KH.title: Country Flag
KH.description: The national flag of Cambodia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

KH.title: .kh Domain
KH.description: Web addresses in Cambodia end in the country domain .kh (often as .com.kh). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

AR.title: Red soil
AR.description: In Argentina, red soil is mainly found in the northeastern region, particularly in the panhandle.

AR.title: License Plates Black
AR.description: Argentina uses two styles of license plates. One type has what appears to be a black dot in the middle.

AR.title: License Plates Blue
AR.description: Argentina uses two styles of license plates. One type has got a blue strip across the top.

AR.title: Argentina chevrons
AR.description: Argentina is the only South American country that has white chevrons with red arrows.

AR.title: Double poles
AR.description: Double poles with horizontal bars are commonly found in Argentina.

AR.title: Wooden Utility Poles
AR.description: Timber poles appear frequently, including unique A-frame variants.

AR.title: Road Lines
AR.description: Roads have broken white centre lines, solid double yellow dividers, or both.

AR.title: Kilometre Markers
AR.description: Distance markers have a white body with a dark band showing the route number.

AR.title: Guardrail Reflectors
AR.description: Guardrails have rectangular yellow and red reflectors.

AR.title: Wide Open Landscape
AR.description: Vast, open terrain with sparse vegetation and few people.

AR.title: City Taxi Map
AR.description: Distinctive taxi colour schemes help pinpoint locations in multiple cities.

AR.title: Western Mountains
AR.description: The far west is dominated by mountainous terrain along the Andes.

AR.title: Chaco and Formosa
AR.description: Sandy ground covered with dense low shrubs and trees.

AR.title: Grassland with Plantations
AR.description: Open grasslands dotted with scattered clusters of planted trees.

AR.title: Buenos Aires Lakes
AR.description: Roadside ponds and small bodies of water appear in Buenos Aires province.

AR.title: San Luis Red Pavement
AR.description: San Luis roads have a reddish surface bordered by tall Argentine needle-grass.

AR.title: Central South Barren Flats
AR.description: Central-south Argentina features empty, level plains with almost no vegetation.

AR.title: Tierra del Fuego Grass
AR.description: Low, windswept grass with few shrubs signals Tierra del Fuego or SE Santa Cruz.

AR.title: Entre Ríos Tree Plantations
AR.description: Argentina's densest commercial tree plantations are in Entre Ríos.

AR.title: Tierra del Fuego Beech Forests
AR.description: Dense beech forests are a hallmark of Tierra del Fuego.

AR.title: Caranday Wax Palm
AR.description: Caranday Wax Palm has short fan-shaped fronds and grows in sparse stands, mainly in Formosa.

AR.title: Caranday Palm (Trithrinax)
AR.description: Trithrinax campestris has compact fan leaves and a trunk with dried leaf matter, native to Córdoba highlands.

AR.title: Macaw Palm
AR.description: Macaw Palm has narrow, slender fronds with a pointed crown, wild in Formosa, Chaco, and Misiones.

AR.title: Cardón Cactus
AR.description: Cardón cactus grows at high altitudes in Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta, and Jujuy with branching candelabra shape.

AR.title: Toothpick Cactus
AR.description: Stetsonia coryne is a tall, branched cactus with long slender spines, found between Catamarca and Córdoba.

AR.title: Wild Sunflowers
AR.description: Wild sunflowers grow commonly along roadsides in Salta, Jujuy, and Tucumán.

AR.title: Caldén Tree
AR.description: Caldén is a medium-large deciduous tree with fine foliage and twisting branches, found mainly in La Pampa.

AR.title: Pampas Grass
AR.description: Pampas grass has tall clustered stems topped by soft white plumes, defining the Pampas region.

AR.title: Sugarcane Fields
AR.description: Sugarcane cultivation is concentrated in Tucumán, with smaller pockets in Salta and Jujuy.

AR.title: Sorghum Fields
AR.description: Sorghum crops have deep red seed heads, common in Santa Fe, Córdoba, and Buenos Aires.

AR.title: Corn Fields
AR.description: Maize cultivation is widespread in northern Argentina, especially Córdoba, Buenos Aires, and Santiago del Estero.

AR.title: Sunflower Fields
AR.description: Commercial sunflower fields are most common in southern Chaco, with some in Buenos Aires and southern Córdoba.

AR.title: Hook Poles
AR.description: Wooden utility poles with curved hook shapes appear only in La Rioja and Mendoza.

AR.title: Mendoza Single Insulator Poles
AR.description: Mendoza utility poles have one insulator mounted on the side.

AR.title: Tucumán Pole Stickers
AR.description: Tucumán utility poles often have tall white stickers with multi-digit numbers.

AR.title: Córdoba Road Markers
AR.description: Córdoba provincial roads have distinctive kilometre markers unique to the province.

AR.title: La Pampa T-Junction Signs
AR.description: La Pampa T-junctions have rectangular yellow signs with route numbers, arrows, and a chevron base.

AR.title: Jujuy Red Bricks
AR.description: Bolivia-style red brick construction appears in western Jujuy province.

AR.title: Pink Trumpet Trees
AR.description: Pink-flowering lapacho trees line streets in northern Salta towns like Orán and Tartagal.

AR.title: Jujuy Salt Pans
AR.description: Expansive salt flats are concentrated in Jujuy province.

AR.title: Córdoba Western Mountains
AR.description: Moderate-elevation mountains lie west of Córdoba city, lower than the Andes.

AR.title: Horse Trekker
AR.description: Horseback Trekker coverage exists in southwest San Juan province.

AR.title: Mendoza Vineyards
AR.description: Vineyards backed by mountains and plains indicate Mendoza wine region near the city.

AR.title: Bahía Blanca Grass Hills
AR.description: Rolling grassy hills near the coast northeast of Bahía Blanca in southern Buenos Aires.

AR.title: Monkey Puzzle Trees
AR.description: Monkey puzzle trees grow in western Neuquén, especially along provincial road 23.

AR.title: RP25 Snow Coverage
AR.description: The eastern section of the RP25 in Santa Cruz province has coverage captured under heavy snowfall.

AR.title: Country Flag
AR.description: The national flag of Argentina is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

AR.title: Stacked Concrete Crossarms
AR.description: Argentine concrete poles often carry short concrete crossarms up the upper part of the pole, sometimes alternating from one side to the other.

AR.title: .ar Domain
AR.description: Web addresses in Argentina end in the country domain .ar (usually as .com.ar). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

US.title: H-E-B supermarket chain
US.description: H-E-B is a supermarket chain that operates exclusively in Texas.

US.title: Mailboxes
US.description: Mailboxes with a small flag are a common sight in North America.

US.title: Imperial units
US.description: The US uses the imperial system, meaning speed and distances will be displayed in miles.

US.title: Triangular signs
US.description: Triangular yellow signs reading 'No Passing Zone' are found only in the US.

US.title: Road lines
US.description: US roads have yellow center lines (usually double) and white outer lines.

US.title: Speed signs
US.description: Speed signs in the US say ‘Speed Limit’.

US.title: Yield signs
US.description: US yield signs are triangles with a red border and the word “YIELD” on a white background.

US.title: One-Way Signs
US.description: US one-way signs are black rectangles with white arrows and 'ONE WAY' text.

US.title: Parking Signs
US.description: US parking signs are white metal with colored text specifying parking rules.

US.title: Green Highway Exit Signs
US.description: Large green signs with white text mark exits and distances on US highways.

US.title: Blue Highway Service Signs
US.description: Blue signs near exits list services like food, fuel, and lodging.

US.title: Rectangular Junction Signs
US.description: Rectangular signs with arrows mark junctions in the US.

US.title: Fibre Optic Cable Markers
US.description: White-and-orange fibre optic cable markers are nearly exclusive to the US.

US.title: Orange Construction Barrels
US.description: Orange plastic barrels with white stripes and black bases mark US construction zones.

US.title: Rumble Strips
US.description: Perpendicular pavement indentations, rumble strips, line edges and lane dividers on US highways.

US.title: Manufactured (Trailer) Homes
US.description: Small rectangular manufactured homes on blocks are common in rural America.

US.title: Baptist Churches
US.description: Baptist churches are widespread across the US, especially in the Southern Plains and Southeast.

US.title: US-Only Gas Station Chains
US.description: Fuel brands such as Exxon, Sunoco, Citgo, Speedway, Marathon, Phillips 66, 76, Conoco and Sinclair only operate in the US.

US.title: Overhead Traffic Light Bars
US.description: Long metal arms with traffic lights, street signs, and highway signs extend over intersections throughout the US and Canada.

US.title: Thin Metal Sign Posts
US.description: Thin metal sign posts, either perforated or U-shaped, are standard in North America.

US.title: Wooden Utility Poles
US.description: North America predominantly uses wooden utility poles.

US.title: Raised Insulators on Poles
US.description: Insulators raised slightly above the top of poles are characteristic of the US and Canada.

US.title: Long-Nose Semi-Trucks
US.description: North American semi-trucks have a long nose with the engine ahead of the cab.

US.title: Water Towers
US.description: Tall water towers are common in US and Canadian towns, often displaying town or state names.

US.title: Missing Front Plates
US.description: About 22 states require only a rear plate; vehicles without front plates likely come from these states.

US.title: Alaska Licence Plate
US.description: Gold plate with dark blue characters and a yellow-gold background, easy to identify even blurred.

US.title: Alabama Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with maroon-red characters and a large circular county emblem on the left side.

US.title: Arkansas Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with dark characters, red 'Arkansas' header, and a white diamond shape in the centre.

US.title: Arizona Licence Plate
US.description: Plate shows a desert sunset gradient with blue, red, and white bands behind the characters.

US.title: California Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with dark blue characters and a subtle red blob on top.

US.title: Colorado Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with green mountain scenery across the top and 'COLORADO' in green.

US.title: Connecticut Licence Plate
US.description: Connecticut plates appear with a blue upper area and a pale lower area.

US.title: District of Columbia Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with blue characters, red 'WASHINGTON DC' header, and a small red DC flag emblem.

US.title: Delaware Licence Plate
US.description: Dark blue plate with gold-yellow characters, distinctive even when blurred.

US.title: Florida Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with green characters and two orange blobs from the orange graphic in the centre.

US.title: Georgia Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with dark characters and a peach emblem in the centre.

US.title: Hawaii Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with dark characters and a rainbow arc across the upper portion.

US.title: Iowa Licence Plate
US.description: Blue-gradient plate with a county name across the top and dark characters on a lighter centre.

US.title: Idaho Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with a red 'IDAHO' header, dark characters, and a blue band along the bottom.

US.title: Illinois Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with dark blue characters on a reddish-maroon background with the Lincoln silhouette.

US.title: Indiana Licence Plate
US.description: White plate with dark blue characters and a simple, clean design.

US.title: Interstate and US Highway Numbering
US.description: Even-numbered Interstates and U.S. Highways generally run east–west, while odd-numbered routes run north–south. The two systems use opposite numbering directions geographically.

US.title: Three-Digit Area Codes
US.description: US phone numbers begin with a three-digit area code mapping to specific regions.
