US.title: Topographic Overview
US.description: The western US has major mountain ranges and high plateaus; the east is lower with the Appalachians as the main highland.

US.title: Forest Density Map
US.description: Eastern and northern US regions have denser tree cover than western and southwestern areas.

US.title: Corn Fields
US.description: Corn farming is concentrated in the Midwest and surrounding states.

US.title: Soybean Fields
US.description: Short, dark green crops growing in long rows across the Great Plains, Midwest, and Lower Mississippi Valley.

US.title: Canola Fields
US.description: Bright yellow canola flower fields appear in North Dakota and occasionally Montana near the Canadian border.

US.title: Cotton Fields
US.description: Fluffy white cotton fields are found in the coastal Southeast, Lower Mississippi Valley, western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona.

US.title: Rice Production Areas
US.description: US rice is grown in north-central California and the Lower Mississippi Valley. Fields resemble flat, low prairies.

US.title: Oil Pumpjacks
US.description: Short industrial metal structures that pump crude oil, common in Texas, eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.

US.title: The Great Plains
US.description: A vast flat, largely treeless region from the Canadian border to central Texas with cropland and dry grassland.

US.title: Prairie Potholes
US.description: Low-lying wetlands with marshy grasses and shallow ponds from the Montana–Saskatchewan border to the western Great Lakes.

US.title: Appalachian Mountains
US.description: A low mountain range in the eastern US, covered in forest with beech and oak trees.

US.title: Southern Pines
US.description: Tall loblolly and longleaf pines with fluffy needle clusters abundant in the southeastern US.

US.title: Reddish Soil in the Deep South
US.description: Soil ranging from yellow to deep red is common across the Deep South, from Oklahoma to South Carolina.

US.title: Dormant Southern Grass
US.description: Bermuda and St. Augustine grasses in the southern US turn beige or brown in winter.

US.title: Lower Mississippi River Valley
US.description: An extremely flat, open landscape with red soil spanning Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and northeast Louisiana.

US.title: Rocky Mountains
US.description: Jagged, rocky formations from the Canadian border to northern New Mexico, often with pine forests and snow on high peaks.

US.title: Sagebrush
US.description: Great Basin sagebrush is a short, shrubby blue-green bush common in arid interior western US.

US.title: Saguaro Cacti
US.description: Tall tube-shaped cacti with upward-curving arms, found almost exclusively in southern Arizona.

US.title: Douglas Firs in Cascadia
US.description: Extremely tall conifers with dark brown bark and dark green foliage, common in Washington and Oregon.

US.title: Pacific Temperate Rainforests
US.description: Coastal Washington, Oregon, and northern California have temperate rainforests with broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.

US.title: Southwest Mesas and Red Rock
US.description: The Four Corners region features mesas, tablelands, and reddish rock formations with red soil.

US.title: Palm Trees
US.description: Common along the Southeast coast, Gulf Coast, and Desert Southwest; Mexican Fan Palm prevalent in California.

US.title: Texas Hill Country
US.description: Dry, rocky hills west of Austin and San Antonio with yucca, prickly pear, and Texas Live Oak trees.

US.title: Rio Grande Valley
US.description: South Texas's Rio Grande Valley is flat with shrubby trees and agricultural fields bordering Mexico.

US.title: Spanish Moss
US.description: Greyish-white drapes of Spanish moss hanging from trees are a hallmark of the Deep South.

US.title: Golden Agricultural Fields
US.description: Expansive golden fields are common in eastern Washington.

US.title: Central Valley, California
US.description: California's Central Valley has vineyards, olive trees, and rolling hills at the edges.

US.title: Nebraska Sandhills
US.description: A region of rolling, grass-covered hills in north-central Nebraska.

US.title: Appalachian Ridges and Valleys
US.description: Forest-covered ridges running southwest-to-northeast with flat valleys between, from southern New York to southern Virginia.

US.title: Ouachita Mountains
US.description: Steeper, more visible mountains from eastern Oklahoma into west-central Arkansas.

US.title: Alabama Highway Shield
US.description: Highway shields in Alabama are shaped like the state of Alabama in white with the route number in black.

US.title: Arkansas Highway Shield
US.description: Arkansas shields are shaped like the outline of the state in white, with the route number in black.

US.title: California Highway Shield
US.description: White route number on a green spade-shaped shield.

US.title: Colorado Highway Shield
US.description: Colorado shields are white rectangles featuring the state flag at the top.

US.title: Connecticut Highway Shield
US.description: Connecticut shields are plain white squares with a black border, showing the route number in black.

US.title: Florida Highway Shield
US.description: Florida shields are simple white rectangles with the route number in black next to a black outline of the state.

US.title: Georgia Highway Shield
US.description: Georgia shields have a white silhouette of the state inside.

US.title: Idaho Highway Shield
US.description: Idaho shields have a white silhouette of the state inside, showing the state name in black to the right.

US.title: Illinois Highway Shield
US.description: Illinois shields are showing 'ILLINOIS' in black at the top.

US.title: Indiana Highway Shield
US.description: Indiana shields are white squares with a black border, showing 'INDIANA' at the top.

US.title: Iowa Highway Shield
US.description: Iowa highway shields are black squares with the route number in black inside a white circle.

US.title: Louisiana Highway Shield
US.description: Louisiana highway shields are shaped like the outline of the state in green, with 'LA' at the top and the route number below in white.

US.title: Maine Highway Shield
US.description: Highway shields in Maine are plain white squares with the route number in black.

US.title: Nevada Highway Shield
US.description: Some shields put the state name right on them, like Nevada's. A black square with a white banner inside showing the route number above 'NEVADA' in black.

US.title: New Mexico Highway Shield
US.description: New Mexico highway shields show the route number framed by a red ring with short red marks pointing out.

US.title: North Dakota Highway Shield
US.description: North Dakota highway shields are black squares featuring a white arrowhead silhouette with jagged edges, with the route number in black on the arrowhead and 'N' and 'D' in white at the top corners.

US.title: Oregon Highway Shield
US.description: Black route number on a white shield with an oval shape.

US.title: Rhode Island Highway Shield
US.description: Rhode Island shields are showing 'R.I.' at the top.

US.title: South Carolina Highway Shield
US.description: South Carolina shields are white rectangles with a blue border, a blue banner at the top reading 'SOUTH CAROLINA' around a small white state outline, and the route number in blue below.

US.title: Tennessee Highway Shield
US.description: Tennessee shields are white with a black border and a curved bottom, showing the route number above 'Tennessee'.

US.title: Texas Highway Shield
US.description: Texas shields are white squares with a thick black border, showing the route number in black above 'TEXAS'.

US.title: Utah Highway Shield
US.description: Utah's shield is one of the most recognisable in the US: a white beehive on a black square with the route number in black inside the beehive.

US.title: Vermont Highway Shield
US.description: Vermont shields are white with a green border, showing 'VERMONT' in a green banner at the top and the route number in green below.

US.title: Virginia Highway Shield
US.description: Highway shields in Virginia have a white shield in the middle containing the route number in black.

US.title: Adopt-a-Highway Signs
US.description: Most states have unique Adopt-a-Highway sign designs found along roadsides.

US.title: Rectangular Raised Pavement Markers
US.description: Small rectangular raised markers embedded in the road surface appear in the southern and western US, plus Massachusetts.

US.title: Snowplowable H-Shaped Pavement Markers
US.description: H-shaped pavement markers flush with the road surface are found only in a group of eastern states shown on the reference map.

US.title: Kentucky Rumble Strips
US.description: Some Kentucky roads use uniquely shaped rumble strips, thin, elongated recessed lines on the outer road edges.

US.title: Brown National Park Infrastructure
US.description: Guardrails, signs, and sign posts painted medium brown are characteristic of US national parks. Rock walls sometimes replace guardrails.

US.title: Wisconsin and Missouri Lettered County Highways
US.description: Wisconsin and Missouri use a letter system (A–ZZZ) for county highways. Wisconsin signs typically include 'County' above the letter; Missouri signs usually do not.

US.title: Concrete-Paved Highways in Iowa
US.description: Concrete paving on main highways is far more common in Iowa than in other states.

US.title: Wide-Gap Yellow Centre Lines
US.description: Double yellow centre lines with a noticeably wide gap between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon.

US.title: Thick Yellow Centre Lines, WV, VA, MD
US.description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland have centre yellow lines that are noticeably thicker than standard.

US.title: Oregon Speed Signs, 'Speed' Only
US.description: Oregon speed signs often display just the word 'Speed' rather than the standard 'Speed Limit'.

US.title: California Black Stripe Between Centre Lines
US.description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen between the two yellow centre lines on California roads.

US.title: California Three-Stripe Pole Markings
US.description: Utility poles in California typically have three yellow stripes painted near the base.

US.title: California Roads Without Centre Lines
US.description: Some smaller California roads lack a yellow centre line entirely, featuring only solid white edge lines.

US.title: Nevada Bollards
US.description: Nevada uses bollards consisting of a thin stick topped with a vertical rectangular white reflector outlined in black.

US.title: South Dakota and Montana Bollards
US.description: A dark metal post with a white diamond reflector on each side at the top is the standard bollard in South Dakota and Montana.

US.title: Wyoming Bollards
US.description: Wyoming bollards are dark metal poles with a white circular reflector at the top. The top portion of the pole is sometimes painted white or grey.

US.title: Washington State Bollards
US.description: Washington uses white or brown posts with a white rectangle on the front and two smaller white or silver squares on the back.

US.title: Utah and Idaho Numbered Streets
US.description: Streets in Utah and Idaho often have a number and cardinal direction (e.g. '600 South').

US.title: Texas Road Surface
US.description: Texas roads often have a distinctive grainy, 'salt and pepper' pavement texture.

US.title: Upper Midwest Grainy Roads
US.description: Rural roads in the Upper Midwest, especially Illinois, use grainy pavement similar to Texas but in varying colours.

US.title: Texas Signpost Reflectors
US.description: Yellow or red reflective bands are commonly wrapped around signposts in Texas.

US.title: Kansas White Signpost Reflectors
US.description: White reflectors on signposts, especially on rural stop signs, are unique to Kansas.

US.title: Minnesota Bridge Warning Signs
US.description: Yellow signs with vertical black triangles appear before major bridge crossings and guardrail ends on large highways in Minnesota.

US.title: Minnesota Stop Sign Markers
US.description: Most rural stop signs in Minnesota have a horizontal black-and-white marker attached to the post.

US.title: Wisconsin ATV Route Signs
US.description: Green 'ATV Route' signs are unique to Wisconsin.

US.title: Wisconsin/Michigan UP Pole Plates
US.description: White rectangular metal plates with an orange rectangle and diamond are found on most utility poles in Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula.

US.title: Wisconsin White Bollards
US.description: Simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

US.title: Wisconsin/Michigan UP House Number Signs
US.description: Horizontal blue, red, or green signs at driveway ends show house numbers plus town or road names in Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula.

US.title: Michigan Double Signposts
US.description: Signs mounted on two parallel posts are common in Michigan.

US.title: Michigan Wire-Hung Traffic Signs
US.description: Many Michigan intersections have stop lights and signs suspended from wires across the road, often in yellow boxes.

US.title: Ohio/Michigan/Indiana Property Markers
US.description: Vertical blue or green metal signs with white house numbers, often attached to mailboxes, are common in rural Ohio, lower Michigan, and Indiana.

US.title: West Virginia Fraction-in-Circle Signs
US.description: West Virginia street signs sometimes include a symbol resembling a fraction inside a circle.

US.title: North Carolina Numbered Street Signs
US.description: North Carolina commonly uses street signs displaying block numbers and directional arrows alongside the street name.

US.title: Oklahoma Stop Sign Markers
US.description: Green rectangular signs with three rows of numbers are commonly attached to the back of rural stop signs in Oklahoma.

US.title: Pennsylvania Intersection Route Signs
US.description: White rectangular signs showing converging state route numbers sometimes appear on signposts at Pennsylvania intersections.

US.title: Virginia Intersection Signs
US.description: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be found at intersections in Virginia.

US.title: North Carolina White Signpost Signs
US.description: White signs attached to signposts are common at intersections in North Carolina.

US.title: South Carolina Black Street Signs
US.description: Black street signs with white text are common at intersections in South Carolina.

US.title: Square Guardrails, New York and Wyoming
US.description: Guardrails with a flat horizontal bar and square vertical supports dominate in New York and Wyoming.

US.title: New Hampshire E-2 Bridge Signs
US.description: White metal signs marked 'E-2' are commonly placed at bridge ends in New Hampshire.

US.title: Vermont Stop Sign Number Plates
US.description: Small green signs with three rows of numbers appear on stop sign posts in Vermont.

US.title: New England Bridge Endpoint Markers
US.description: Small green and red rectangular signs mark ends of bridges and guardrails in Maine, New Hampshire, and Massachusetts.

US.title: New England Roadside Rock Walls
US.description: Short stone walls alongside rural roads are common in Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire.

US.title: Appalachian Wooden Fences
US.description: Dark wooden fences with several horizontal rails are common on farmland from Pennsylvania to Georgia in the central and southern Appalachians.

US.title: Coastal Stilt Houses
US.description: Houses elevated on tall stilts appear along the coast, especially in the South and on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

US.title: Short-Stilt Gulf Coast Houses
US.description: Houses raised 1–3 feet on short concrete or wood stilts are common along the western and central Gulf Coast near the coast and rivers.

US.title: Large Sloped-Roof Buildings
US.description: Buildings with oversized sloped roofs are most common in Oklahoma, Texas, and Louisiana, and occasionally in neighbouring states.

US.title: New England Shingle-Walled Houses
US.description: Coastal New England homes often have walls of overlapping wooden shingles.

US.title: Northeast Triple-Decker Houses
US.description: Older three-storey wooden 'stacked triplex' houses are common in urban New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.

US.title: Brownstone Buildings
US.description: Row houses and government buildings made of brick and sandstone, common in dense urban Northeast US and Chicago.

US.title: Red Metal Rooftops
US.description: Red metal roofs are a common sight in the southeastern U.S.

US.title: Shotgun Houses
US.description: Very narrow, one-storey wooden houses in a row, prevalent around New Orleans, Houston, Louisville, and Mississippi.

US.title: Pueblo Revival Houses
US.description: Sand-brown adobe or brick buildings with rounded edges and flat roofs, common in New Mexico.

US.title: Western Mountain Timber Buildings
US.description: Houses and commercial buildings built with dark wooden boards and timbers; metal roofs at higher elevations.

US.title: ShopRite
US.description: ShopRite is a regional supermarket chain in Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, and Maryland.

US.title: Hy-Vee
US.description: Hy-Vee is a supermarket chain mainly in Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Illinois.

US.title: Piggly Wiggly
US.description: Piggly Wiggly is a supermarket chain concentrated in the Southeast US and Wisconsin.

US.title: Publix
US.description: Publix is a supermarket chain primarily in Florida and adjacent Deep South states.

US.title: Waffle House
US.description: Waffle House restaurants are concentrated in the South and Southeast, especially Georgia.

US.title: Zaxby's
US.description: Zaxby's is a fast-food chicken chain most common in the Southeast, especially Georgia.

US.title: Whataburger
US.description: Whataburger is a hamburger chain across the South Central US, especially Texas.

US.title: Pizza Ranch
US.description: Pizza Ranch is a restaurant chain in the central US, concentrated in Iowa and Minnesota.

US.title: Tim Hortons in the US
US.description: Tim Hortons has US locations mainly near Ontario and Quebec borders, plus scattered sites in Texas and Georgia.

US.title: In-N-Out Burger
US.description: In-N-Out Burger is a fast-food chain concentrated in the Southwest, especially California.

US.title: Wawa
US.description: Wawa is a gas station and convenience store chain in the Mid-Atlantic states and Florida.

US.title: Sheetz
US.description: Sheetz is a gas station and convenience store chain in the Eastern US, concentrated in the Mid-Atlantic and Central Appalachia.

US.title: Kwik Trip
US.description: Kwik Trip operates gas stations in Wisconsin and Minnesota; in Iowa it's called 'Kwik Star'.

US.title: Casey's
US.description: Casey's is a gas station and convenience store chain across the Midwest, Plains, and parts of the Mid-South.

US.title: Kum & Go
US.description: Kum & Go is a gas station chain headquartered in Iowa, with clusters in the Ozarks, Colorado, Wyoming, and North Dakota.

US.title: Buc-ee's
US.description: Buc-ee's is a chain of oversized gas stations with many fuel pumps and large stores, found almost exclusively in Texas.

US.title: Alaska
US.description: The largest US state and the northernmost, westernmost, and easternmost state.

US.title: Hawaii
US.description: The youngest US state and the only one outside North America.

US.title: Puerto Rico
US.description: A Caribbean US territory with Commonwealth status.

US.title: American Samoa
US.description: A South Pacific island group and unorganised US territory.

US.title: Guam
US.description: An unincorporated US territory and the largest island in Micronesia.

US.title: Northern Mariana Islands
US.description: A northwest Pacific island chain and Commonwealth US territory.

US.title: US Virgin Islands
US.description: A Caribbean US territory and the only part of the US where traffic drives on the left.

US.title: US Minor Outlying Islands
US.description: A collective name for several small US island territories, including Midway Atoll.

US.title: South Florida Everglades
US.description: Dense, jungle-like forests with few inhabitants between Fort Myers and Miami. Roads are typically very straight and long.

US.title: Orlando–Lakeland Hills
US.description: Low rolling hills with lakes and farmland between Orlando and Lakeland.

US.title: Wichita Mountains
US.description: Rocky, shrubby peaks in southwest Oklahoma with some forested areas and pinkish-red rock.

US.title: Colorado Front Range
US.description: A north-south mountain ridge in central Colorado dividing the Rockies from the Great Plains.

US.title: Guadalupe Mountains
US.description: Tall, dry peaks along the New Mexico–Texas border with flat-topped foothills and shrubby vegetation.

US.title: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
US.description: Sand-brown eroded formations with more trees on the rocks and autumn foliage.

US.title: Black Hills
US.description: Moderately tall mountains with dense conifer forests and rocky outcroppings in western South Dakota and eastern Wyoming.

US.title: Country Flag
US.description: The national flag of the United States is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

US.title: Florida County Road Shield

US.title: Oregon Great Basin

US.title: Arizona County Route Shield

US.title: Idaho Great Basin

US.title: Michigan County Road Commission Shield

US.title: Utah Great Basin

US.description: Kentucky shields are black squares with a white circle inside, showing the route number in black.

US.title: Louisiana Parish Road Shield

US.title: Maine Highway Shield

US.title: Maryland Highway Shield

US.title: Montana Highway Shield

US.title: Tennessee Highway Shield

US.title: Virginia Highway Shield

US.title: West Virginia Highway hield

US.description: Wisconsin marks its state highways with a black and white sign with a triangular notch cut into the top edges and bottom.

US.title: California Carl's Jr. Branding

US.title: Nevada Carl's Jr. Branding
US.description: Nevada features only Carl's Jr. branding with the yellow star mascot.

US.title: Arizona Carl's Jr. Branding
US.description: Arizona fast food outlets display only the Carl's Jr. name and yellow star logo.

US.title: New Mexico Carl's Jr. Branding

US.title: Wyoming Dual Branding

US.title: Oklahoma Dual Branding
US.description: Oklahoma contains both Carl's Jr. and Hardee's restaurants with their respective yellow star logos.

US.title: Central US Hardee's Branding
US.description: Central US fast food locations are branded as Hardee's with a yellow star logo.

US.title: Eastern US Hardee's Branding
US.description: Eastern US uses Hardee's brand exclusively, identified by the yellow star logo.

US.title: .us Domain
US.description: Web addresses in the United States end in the country domain .us. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

US.title: Connecticut License Plates
US.description: Connecticut plates appear with a blue upper area and a pale lower area.

RU.title: Tree-lined roads
RU.description: In Russia, roads lined with trees are common in the Kaliningrad region.

RU.title: Black socks
RU.description: In Russia, signposts often have their lower sections painted black.

RU.title: Long, white plates
RU.description: Russian plates are entirely white with black text and lack the blue EU-style strip found on most European plates.

RU.title: Bollard bonanza
RU.description: Intersections in Russia frequently feature unusually large clusters of bollards, far more densely packed than in most other countries.

RU.title: Asian cars
RU.description: Japanese-made vehicles with the steering wheel on the right become increasingly common the further east you go in Russia.

RU.title: Cyrillic script
RU.description: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet. It is the only script showing up on most signs.

RU.title: Crosswalk
RU.description: Crosswalks in Russia use alternating white and yellow stripes instead of the solid white stripes seen in most other countries.

RU.title: Word for Street
RU.description: Russian word for street is улица (ulitsa), shortened to ул.

RU.title: Word for City
RU.description: Russian word for city is город (gorod), shortened to г.

RU.title: Bollard Types
RU.description: Russia has three main bollard styles: thin on a stick, black top with red reflector, and German-style.

RU.title: Wide Intersections
RU.description: Many Russian intersections are wider than usual, with dense bollards.

RU.title: Concrete Pole Support Blocks
RU.description: Concrete blocks commonly support utility poles in Russia.

RU.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
RU.description: Russian pedestrian signs show a simple figure with three stripes and often a yellow border.

RU.title: Black-and-White Striped Guardrails
RU.description: Guardrails and barriers often have alternating black and white stripes.

RU.title: Soviet-Era Apartment Blocks
RU.description: Russian urban housing mostly consists of large rectangular concrete blocks with plain facades.

RU.title: Rural Wooden Houses
RU.description: Russian rural homes are simple wooden structures with metal roofs.

RU.title: Ornate Window Frames
RU.description: Traditional Russian houses, especially log cabins, feature richly carved decorative window frames often painted blue.

RU.title: Black-and-White Pole Shields
RU.description: Pole shields with alternating black and white stripes appear frequently along highways in European Russia.

RU.title: Birch Tree Range
RU.description: Birch trees with distinctive white peeling bark grow across much of Russia except the far south and far north of western regions.

RU.title: Dense Birch Forests
RU.description: Tightly packed pure birch forests suggest areas east of the Urals, typically between Chelyabinsk and Novosibirsk Oblasts.

RU.title: Siberian Larches
RU.description: Siberian larches with needle-like leaves dominate eastern Russia, becoming more prevalent further east and at higher elevations.

RU.title: Giant Butterbur (Sakhalin Cabbage)
RU.description: Giant butterbur, or Sakhalin cabbage, is common in southern Sakhalin Oblast.

RU.title: Sosnowsky's Hogweed
RU.description: Heracleum sosnowskyi, a white-flowered plant, appears frequently around Moscow, Komi Republic, and Perm Krai.

RU.title: Fireweed
RU.description: Abundant pink or red fireweed typically signals northern Russia, commonly found north of Moscow.

RU.title: Sunflower Fields
RU.description: Sunflower fields are prevalent near the Ukrainian border and in eastern oblasts like Ulyanovsk, Samara, and northern Orenburg.

RU.title: Blue-Pod Lupines
RU.description: Blue-pod lupines appear abundantly in northern Vladimir, eastern Ivanovo, and southwestern Kostroma Oblasts.

RU.title: Black Poplar Trees
RU.description: Black poplars are typically found in southern Russia near the Ukrainian and western Kazakhstan borders.

RU.title: Russian Olive Trees
RU.description: Russian olive trees are found along the Kazakhstan border.

RU.title: Roadside Larches with Open Fields
RU.description: Sparsely planted larches along roads with open rolling fields are typical of Tatarstan and neighboring regions.

RU.title: Sandy Roadsides
RU.description: Sandy roadsides are typical in Khanty-Mansi, Yamalo-Nenets, near Nizhny Novgorod, Karelia, Murmansk, and western Sakha.

RU.title: Red Soil
RU.description: Red soil appears around Izhevsk, Perm, Arkhangelsk, Leningrad, Pskov, Volgograd, and Astrakhan.

RU.title: Kamchatka's Grey Gravelly Soil
RU.description: Kamchatka Peninsula has distinctive grey gravelly soil and many volcanoes, some close to roads near Klyuchi.

RU.title: Dark Gravelly Soil East of Yakutsk
RU.description: Extremely gravelly, sometimes dark soil characterizes terrain east of Yakutsk, starting around Keskil.

RU.title: Vladivostok Area Landscape
RU.description: Lush, diverse forests cover hilly terrain in the warmer Vladivostok region, often overcast.

RU.title: Hazy Coverage Near Mirny
RU.description: Very hazy coverage appears east and south of Mirny, especially along the Vilyuy river, with orange or white haze.

RU.title: Buryatia Landscape
RU.description: Buryatia features open grassy landscapes with shrubs and mountains, becoming lusher near Lake Baikal.

RU.title: Tuva Republic Dry Steppe
RU.description: Dry steppe mountains with a long antenna typically indicate the Tuva Republic.

RU.title: Arctic Tundra Landscape
RU.description: The far north has flat terrain with very low vegetation, characteristic of tundra.

RU.title: Omsk Oblast Landscape
RU.description: Omsk Oblast shows green agricultural fields broken by isolated birch forest patches in summer.

RU.title: Caspian Steppe
RU.description: The area west of the Caspian Sea is extremely dry and flat, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan, and Dagestan.

RU.title: Dagestan Grassy Fields
RU.description: Grassy fields with bushy vegetation and small flowers in early spring are typical of Dagestan.

RU.title: Caucasus Mountain Range
RU.description: The Caucasus is a large mountain range with Mount Elbrus, Russia's tallest peak, on the Kabardino-Balkarian and Karachay-Cherkessia border.

RU.title: Roadside Rocks in Karelia and Murmansk
RU.description: Large rocks lining roads are common in Karelia and Murmansk, less so in Perm Krai and Buryatia.

RU.title: Murmansk Oblast Landscape
RU.description: Open, hilly terrain with low shrubbery and fireweed indicates Murmansk; shorter vegetation suggests further north.

RU.title: Telephone Area Codes
RU.description: Russian area codes: start with 8 in the west, 3 in central areas, and 4 in the east or around Moscow.

RU.title: Licence Plate Regional Codes
RU.description: Unblurred plates show a regional code on the right, ordered alphabetically by federal subject type.

RU.title: Distinctive Regional Bus Stops
RU.description: Certain federal subjects have unique bus stop designs, notably Krasnoyarsk Krai, Chuvashia, Tatarstan, and Mari El.

RU.title: Thin Eastern Bollards
RU.description: Very thin bollards on sticks appear in eastern Russia starting around Omsk.

RU.title: Black Traffic Sign Bottom
RU.description: Traffic signs with black-painted bottoms are found mainly in Stavropol, Chechnya, and western Dagestan.

RU.title: Signpost Edge Clips
RU.description: Metal clips on signpost edges are typical of Leningrad Oblast and St. Petersburg.

RU.title: Outer Dashed Road Lines
RU.description: Dashed lines along road edges are mostly found in Kursk Oblast.

RU.title: Concrete Block Roads
RU.description: Roads made from individual concrete blocks appear in northern Russia, especially Komi, Nenets, and Yamalo-Nenets.

RU.title: Bilingual Town and Direction Signs
RU.description: Some republics show bilingual town and directional signs in Russian and a minority language.

RU.title: Dual Cyrillic-Latin Town Names
RU.description: Town names in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts appear near the Baltic border and around Moscow.

RU.title: Brown Tourist Signs
RU.description: Brown tourist directional signs are common in Moscow Oblast and nearby regions.

RU.title: White Limestone Brick Buildings
RU.description: White limestone brick buildings indicate Dagestan and nearby areas.

RU.title: Red Brick Buildings
RU.description: Red brick buildings are concentrated in southern Russia.

RU.title: Mosques
RU.description: Mosques are most common in Muslim-majority areas: the North Caucasus republics, Tatarstan, and Bashkortostan.

RU.title: Mari El Architecture
RU.description: Historic Mari El buildings have green roofs, red brick, and white stone details.

RU.title: Large Red Brake Light
RU.description: Large red brake light on camera car is common in Kaliningrad and some older western coverage.

RU.title: Autumn Coverage
RU.description: Autumn coverage appears in Kaliningrad, Bryansk, Tula, and Belgorod.

RU.title: Winter Coverage
RU.description: Winter coverage is common in southern Russia from Ryazan to Dagestan.

RU.title: Spring Coverage
RU.description: Spring coverage clusters around Kemerovo, Krasnoyarsk, Orenburg, Kamyshin, Lipetsk, and Moscow.

RU.title: Summer Coverage
RU.description: Summer coverage is the most common and widespread.

RU.title: Autumn Coverage
RU.description: Autumn coverage is rare, found near Kazan, Murmansk, and Ulan-Ude.

RU.title: Rural Desert Coverage
RU.description: Flat rural desert-like roads west of the Caspian Sea appear only in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan.

RU.title: Tropical Plants
RU.description: Tropical vegetation like palm trees appears only along Russia's Black Sea coast, mostly near Sochi.

RU.title: Kamchatka Trekker Coverage
RU.description: Most trekker coverage in Russia is from Kamchatka, identified by grey gravelly soil and volcanic terrain.

RU.title: Tatar Bilingual Signs
RU.description: Bilingual street signs in Tatarstan use "урамы" (ур. abbreviated) for street instead of Russian "улица".

RU.title: Bashkir Bilingual Signs
RU.description: Bilingual street signs in Bashkortostan use "урамы" for street, usually written in full.

RU.title: Chuvash Bilingual Signs
RU.description: Bilingual street signs in Chuvashia use the Chuvash word "урамӗ" for street.

RU.title: Mari Bilingual Signs
RU.description: Bilingual street signs in Mari El use the Mari word "урем" for street.

RU.title: Komi Bilingual Signs
RU.description: Bilingual street signs in the Komi Republic use the Komi word "улича" for street.

RU.title: Yellow Pole Plates in Tatarstan
RU.description: Yellow identification plates fastened to poles with metal bands are common in Tatarstan.

RU.title: Double Yellow Bands on Signposts
RU.description: In Murmansk and some Karelia roads, most signposts have two yellow bands wrapped around them.

RU.title: Cobblestone Pavement
RU.description: Cobblestone roads are common in Kaliningrad, Nizhny Tagil, and Kizel.

RU.title: Extended Insulator Bars on Poles
RU.description: Elongated insulator bars on utility poles appear in southern Chelyabinsk, eastern Orenburg, and southern Kemerovo Oblasts.

RU.title: Decorative Pedestrian Sign Holders
RU.description: Ornamental pedestrian sign mounting brackets are unique to Pskov Oblast.

RU.title: Mid-Line Rectangular Fences
RU.description: Rounded rectangular fences with a horizontal mid-line are unique to Chelyabinsk and eastern Orenburg Oblasts.

RU.title: Thin Rectangular Top Fences
RU.description: Fences with a thin rounded rectangular top are found in Syzran, Tolyatti, and Samara.

RU.title: Country Flag
RU.description: The national flag of Russia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

RU.title: .ru Domain
RU.description: Web addresses in Russia end in the country domain .ru. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MK.title: North Macedonian signs
MK.description: In North Macedonia, road signs are yellow and black, and town names appear in both Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.

MK.title: Bollard 1
MK.description: One type of bollard in North Macedonia has a trapezoid shape, colored white and black, with a red reflective strip.

MK.title: Red block
MK.description: North Macedonian plates are white and can have the blue EU strip. A noticeable red block sits near the left side.

MK.title: Guardrails
MK.description: North Macedonian guardrails are A-profile with red reflectors.

MK.title: Macedonian Cyrillic
MK.description: A Slavic language in Cyrillic with unique letters Ѓ and Ќ; road signs include Latin transliterations.

MK.title: Highway-Dominated Rural Coverage
MK.description: Rural coverage is mostly confined to highways due to limited road mapping.

MK.title: Landscape
MK.description: Countryside has dry grasslands with low hills and scattered trees.

MK.title: 'Greek Lamps' on Poles
MK.description: Distinctive lamp style on utility poles, also found in Greece and Serbia.

MK.title: Yellow Warning Signs
MK.description: Warning signs have yellow backgrounds instead of white.

MK.title: Winter Coverage Cities
MK.description: Winter imagery appears in Skopje, Tetovo, Prilep, Bitola, and Ohrid.

MK.title: Divided Roads Overview
MK.description: Several highways are divided with distinct median features.

MK.title: Obituary Posters Overview
MK.description: Cities have distinct public obituary poster styles on utility poles, identified by colour, orientation, and border design.

MK.title: Prilep Obituaries
MK.description: Vertical black posters with incomplete borders.

MK.title: Tetovo Obituaries
MK.description: Vertical black posters with two variants of cross placement.

MK.title: Prilep Rectangular Lamps
MK.description: Long rectangular lamp fixtures exclusive to Prilep.

MK.title: Prilep Rocky Hills
MK.description: Two extremely rocky, bare hills visible from parts of Prilep.

MK.title: Country Flag
MK.description: The national flag of North Macedonia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MK.title: .mk Domain
MK.description: Web addresses in North Macedonia end in the country domain .mk (often as .com.mk). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

JO.title: Black Google car
JO.description: In Jordan, the Street View coverage was captured by a black Google car.

JO.title: Arabic
JO.description: In Jordan Arabic is the official language, recognisable by its connected script of lines and dots. Commercial signage rarely includes English.

JO.title: White and red chevrons
JO.description: The chevrons in Jordan are white with red arrows.

JO.title: Licence Plates
JO.description: Jordan has white plates in long and short formats; commercial vehicles have green left band.

JO.title: Road Markings
JO.description: Yellow edge lines paired with a white centre line.

JO.title: Utility Poles
JO.description: Three common types: concrete with diagonal brace, concrete with Y-shaped crossarms, and two-legged metal towers with coils.

JO.title: Arid Landscape
JO.description: Dominated by barren desert with sparse Mediterranean greenery.

JO.title: Sandstone Architecture
JO.description: Flat-roofed buildings clad in pale sandstone blocks.

JO.title: Poor Road Quality
JO.description: Many roads have heat-buckled asphalt with warps and cracks.

JO.title: Coverage Area
JO.description: Street View covers only the far western strip on major towns and roads.

JO.title: Amman
JO.description: Jordan's capital, a hilly city of mid-rise apartments with an urban feel.

JO.title: Dead Sea
JO.description: The Dead Sea is visible directly to the west along the northern section of Highway 65.

JO.title: Highway 65
JO.description: A single-lane north–south highway with extended sandy stretches south of Feifa valley.

JO.title: Madaba Red Soil Fields
JO.description: Flat farmland around Madaba stands out for its deep red earth.

JO.title: Aqaba Mountains
JO.description: A chain of ragged, jagged peaks along the eastern and southern edges of Aqaba.

JO.title: Petra Trekker Coverage
JO.description: Trekker imagery covers Petra’s rock-hewn city, reddish gorges, cliffs, and tourist clusters.

JO.title: Country Flag
JO.description: The national flag of Jordan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

JO.title: .jo Domain
JO.description: Web addresses in Jordan end in the country domain .jo (often as .com.jo). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

NG.title: Islamic outfits
NG.description: You are more likely to see women wearing hijabs and men dressed in traditional Islamic outfits in the northern regions of Nigeria.

NG.title: Call the police!
NG.description: A police vehicle, usually white or black, trails the Nigerian Street View car in nearly every coverage. The exact model may differ from images shown.

NG.title: Trucks
NG.description: Most Nigerian coverage shows the Google car, a pickup truck with the cab and bed visible. The cab colour and other features vary.

NG.title: Bad camera
NG.description: Nigeria is currently the only mainland African country with official low-quality street view coverage.

NG.title: Licence Plates
NG.description: Nigerian plates are short and appear somewhat green through Google blur.

NG.title: Concrete Utility Poles
NG.description: Nigerian utility poles are concrete with vertical indents and a few horizontal supports.

NG.title: Poor Road Conditions
NG.description: Many Nigerian roads lack lines or have faded markings with potholes and cracked surfaces.

NG.title: Architecture
NG.description: Nigerian houses are mostly single-storey with steep metal-sheet roofs and cinder-block walls.

NG.title: City and State Names on Signage
NG.description: Storefronts and banners often display city or state names, aiding location identification.

NG.title: Topography
NG.description: Nigeria is generally flat with subtle elevation changes. Hills appear from Abuja northward and near Enugu. The tallest peaks are on the Cameroon border (Mandara Range).

NG.title: Climate Zones
NG.description: Nigeria's climate ranges from tropical rainforest in the south, drier savannah in the centre, to arid steppe in the north.

NG.title: Lagos Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: In Lagos, commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are bright yellow, often with black stripes or trim.

NG.title: Kano Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: Kano commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are typically green, sometimes with white or yellow accents.

NG.title: Rivers Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: In Rivers State, commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are usually blue, often with white or black roof sections.

NG.title: Kaduna Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: Kaduna commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are painted deep green, occasionally with yellow or black details.

NG.title: Oyo Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: Oyo commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are commonly wine red or maroon, often with white or yellow roofs.

NG.title: Enugu Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: In Enugu, commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are white with green stripes or accents.

NG.title: Anambra Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: Anambra commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are typically blue with white or yellow highlights.

NG.title: Borno Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: Borno commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are usually light or sky blue, sometimes with white or black accents.

NG.title: Delta Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: Delta commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are yellow and black, often in a two-tone pattern.

NG.title: Edo Commercial Vehicle Colours
NG.description: Edo commercial vehicles and tuk-tuks are painted red, sometimes with white or yellow roofs.

NG.title: Haystacks, Kaduna State
NG.description: Large haystacks are extremely common and almost exclusively found in Kaduna state.

NG.title: Kano Arid Cornfields
NG.description: An arid yet green agricultural landscape with abundant corn fields points to Kano state.

NG.title: Benue Green Grass and Red Soil
NG.description: Lush green grass with reddish soil, scattered tall trees, and thatched huts characterise Benue state.

NG.title: Niger Scattered Trees and Red Soil
NG.description: Scattered trees, reddish soil, and dry grass cover most of Niger state.

NG.title: Northwest Open Arid Landscape
NG.description: Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, and Katsina have an open, arid landscape with very sparse or no tree cover.

NG.title: Northeast Rocky Hills
NG.description: Savannah terrain dotted with rocky hills appears across Plateau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, and northern Taraba.

NG.title: Monolithic Mountains, Abuja Area
NG.description: Large monolithic outcrops of exposed, weathered rock are common in and around Abuja.

NG.title: Lagos Follow Car
NG.description: In Lagos, the follow car is typically a white Toyota Hilux with blue police lights on the roof.

NG.title: Kano Follow Car
NG.description: Kano's follow car is usually a silver Toyota Hilux, sometimes with a black bull bar.

NG.title: Rivers Follow Car
NG.description: In Rivers State, the follow car is most often a dark blue Toyota Hilux with a red and blue police light bar.

NG.title: Oyo Follow Car
NG.description: Oyo's follow car is a white Toyota Hilux with no visible police lights or markings.

NG.title: Kaduna Follow Car
NG.description: Kaduna's follow car is a silver Toyota Hilux, often with a blue police light bar and sometimes a front bull bar.

NG.title: Country Flag
NG.description: The national flag of Nigeria is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

NG.title: .ng Domain
NG.description: Web addresses in Nigeria end in the country domain .ng (often as .com.ng). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

BE.title: Orange signs
BE.description: In Belgium, you will often find orange signposts and sign backs.

BE.title: Belgian bollard
BE.description: The standard Belgian bollard is white and has a yellow rectangular reflector on the front and a white one on the back.

BE.title: Red text
BE.description: Belgian number plates stand out for their red-colored characters, a tint that remains visible even through blurring.

BE.title: Crossing signs
BE.description: Belgian crossing signs show a figure with a square-shaped head walking over two horizontal dotted lines.

BE.title: Guardrail Reflectors
BE.description: Belgian guardrails have yellow reflectors.

BE.title: Concrete Poles
BE.description: Utility poles are mostly square concrete with rows of small holes and often metal bands; some have oval perforations.

BE.title: Direction Signs
BE.description: Wayfinding signs in Belgium are typically blue or white. They are green on highways.

BE.title: Blue Supplementary Signs
BE.description: Regulatory signs often have a small blue auxiliary plate beneath them.

BE.title: Kilometre Markers
BE.description: Distance posts are usually green and may have red numerals.

BE.title: Chevrons
BE.description: Curve warning boards are white with a red arrow pointing toward the bend.

BE.title: Concrete Slab Roads
BE.description: Many country roads are surfaced with precast concrete slabs.

BE.title: Road Lines and Bike Lanes
BE.description: All road markings are white; dedicated cycle lanes often flank both sides of the carriageway.

BE.title: Red Brick Architecture
BE.description: Residential buildings made of distinctive red brick are widespread in northern and western Belgium.

BE.title: Southern Stone Architecture
BE.description: Buildings in southern Belgium tend to be grey stone with French architectural style.

BE.title: Street Name Signs
BE.description: Street name plaques are usually white or dark blue, squarish, and often include the municipality name.

BE.title: Town Entry Signs
BE.description: Settlements are marked by white rectangular signs with a black border and bold black municipality name.

BE.title: Priority Signs
BE.description: The orange diamond priority road sign is smaller than in neighboring countries.

BE.title: Bus Stops
BE.description: Bus stops have yellow signposts and often yellow-roofed shelters.

BE.title: Traffic Light Poles
BE.description: Traffic lights are mounted on poles painted with alternating black and yellow bands.

BE.title: Hydrant Markers
BE.description: Underground hydrants are marked by small red plates with the letter H.

BE.title: Road Gutters
BE.description: Kerbed gutters run along both edges of almost every road.

BE.title: Bicycle Path Markings
BE.description: Cycle paths are edged with short dashed lines on both sides.

BE.title: Blurred Houses
BE.description: Belgium has one of the highest rates of building-level blurring in Europe.

BE.title: Terrain
BE.description: The northwest is flat, especially along the coast; terrain gets hillier toward the southeast.

BE.title: Three Official Languages
BE.description: Belgium has three languages: Dutch in Flanders, French in Wallonia, and German in Ostbelgien.

BE.title: Bilingual Brussels
BE.description: Brussels is officially bilingual with signage in French and Dutch.

BE.title: Regional Bus Stop Differences
BE.description: Bus stop signs in Flanders and Brussels have a white rectangle at the top; Walloon stops have yellow-topped signs.

BE.title: Warning Sign Borders
BE.description: Flanders and Brussels warning signs have thick red borders without white rims.

BE.title: Phone Area Codes
BE.description: Belgian landline numbers have one or two digits after the leading zero indicating the area.

BE.title: Municipality Names on Street Signs
BE.description: Street signs often include the municipality name below the street name.

BE.title: The Ardennes
BE.description: The Ardennes in southeastern Belgium feature rolling forested hills, deep valleys, and steep gradients.

BE.title: Coastal Polders
BE.description: Near the North Sea coast and western Dutch border, terrain has polders—fields at or below sea level with drainage channels and waterways.

BE.title: North Sea Coast
BE.description: Belgian coastline features continuous rows of high-rise apartments and nearby dunes with low scrub, tall grasses, and sandy ground.

BE.title: Country Flag
BE.description: The national flag of Belgium is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BE.title: .be Domain
BE.description: Web addresses in Belgium end in the country domain .be. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

TR.title: Grainy roads
TR.description: Many roads in Turkey have a grainy look from the mix of light and dark local stones used in the asphalt.

TR.title: Stop signs
TR.description: In Turkey, stop signs say "DUR", which is unique to the country.

TR.title: Turkish bollard
TR.description: Turkish bollards are flat, white, and rectangular with a red reflector on the front. A way to remember is to think of their flag which is also red and white.

TR.title: Tall towers
TR.description: It is common in Turkey to see minarets.

TR.title: A special letter
TR.description: The written Turkish language has a special 'i', which will have a dot even when capitalized.

TR.title: Black-Orange-White Snow Poles
TR.description: Turkish snow marker poles are alternating black, orange, and white and fitted with red reflectors.

TR.title: European-Style Licence Plates
TR.description: Turkish licence plates are white, elongated European format with a blue vertical strip on the left.

TR.title: Mixed White and Yellow Road Lines
TR.description: In Turkey, road markings vary between white and yellow, sometimes mixed on the same stretch.

TR.title: Prevalence of Divided Highways
TR.description: Turkey has a high rate of dual-carriageway roads.

TR.title: Red-on-White Chevron Signs
TR.description: Turkish chevron signs are red arrows on a white background, often with a neon yellow border.

TR.title: Black-and-Yellow Upward-Arrow Chevrons
TR.description: Intersections often have black-and-yellow chevron panels with upward-pointing arrows.

TR.title: Narrow Red-and-White Chevrons
TR.description: A slim Turkish chevron variant uses red-and-white colors.

TR.title: Wide-Spaced Font on Direction Signs
TR.description: Turkish directional signs use a typeface with large gaps between letters.

TR.title: Ladder and Mesh Metal Poles
TR.description: Metal utility poles with ladder or mesh-grid patterns are widespread in Turkey.

TR.title: Varied Landscape Across Regions
TR.description: Turkey's terrain ranges from arid southeast plains to Mediterranean coasts and greener northern forests.

TR.title: Boxy Apartment Blocks
TR.description: Tall, cube-shaped apartment buildings are common in Turkish cities and towns.

TR.title: Interlocking Brick Pavements
TR.description: Sidewalks and pedestrian areas often use interlocking bricks in a repeating shape.

TR.title: Telephone Area Codes by Region
TR.description: Turkish area codes rise from 2 in the west to 4 in the east, indicating general location.

TR.title: Numbered Road System (O-Roads and D-Roads)
TR.description: Major highways have 'O-' prefixes on kilometre markers; D-roads show three-digit numbers with section and kilometre counts.

TR.title: Provincial Road Kilometre Markers
TR.description: Provincial road markers start with two digits representing the province code.

TR.title: Lush Green Landscape in the North
TR.description: Northern coastal Turkey is greener and more densely forested than other regions.

TR.title: Northeastern Treeless Grassland Valleys
TR.description: The northeast has open valleys of grass between rounded, treeless hills.

TR.title: Turkish Pines Along the Mediterranean Coast
TR.description: Turkish pines grow mainly along the Mediterranean coast.

TR.title: Tea Plantations in Rize Province
TR.description: Terraced tea fields are a hallmark of Rize Province along the northeastern Black Sea coast.

TR.title: Olive Trees on the Mediterranean Coast
TR.description: Olive groves are concentrated along Turkey's Mediterranean shoreline.

TR.title: Sunflower Fields in the Northwest
TR.description: Large sunflower plantations are typical in northwestern Turkey.

TR.title: Vineyards East of Izmir
TR.description: Most Turkish vineyards lie inland east of Izmir.

TR.title: Cotton Fields Near Sanliurfa
TR.description: Cotton cultivation is concentrated around the city of Sanliurfa in the southeast.

TR.title: Lake Van and Its Semi-Arid Surroundings
TR.description: Turkey's largest lake sits within a semi-arid basin of dry grassy hills, with scattered trees and pockets of farmland closer to the shoreline.

TR.title: Dark Volcanic Rock Between Sanliurfa and Diyarbakir
TR.description: Dark basaltic rock formations are widespread in the area stretching between Sanliurfa and Diyarbakir.

TR.title: Steep Rocky River Valleys
TR.description: Deep river gorges with rocky cliffs occur in northeast and far southeast Turkey.

TR.title: Flat Roofs in the Southeast
TR.description: Flat-roofed buildings dominate southeastern Turkey and parts of the southern coast.

TR.title: Metal Roofs in the East
TR.description: Sheet metal roofing is common in eastern Turkey.

TR.title: Yellow-on-Black Chevrons (Balikesir and Kars)
TR.description: Yellow arrows on black chevrons appear mainly around Balikesir and Kars provinces.

TR.title: Black-on-Yellow Chevrons North of Izmir
TR.description: Black arrows on yellow chevrons are common north of Izmir.

TR.title: Divided Highways Without Physical Dividers
TR.description: Four-lane highways separated only by painted double lines occur mostly in eastern Turkey.

TR.title: Vertical Water Tanks
TR.description: Upright cylindrical water tanks are common throughout most of Turkey.

TR.title: Stacked Horizontal-on-Vertical Water Tanks
TR.description: A horizontal tank atop a vertical tank is typical along the south coast extending inland toward Elazig.

TR.title: Square Water Tanks with Angled Corners
TR.description: Boxy water tanks with bevelled corners appear in the southern zone between Iskenderun and Sanliurfa.

TR.title: White Spherical Water Tanks Near Batman
TR.description: White ball-shaped water tanks cluster in the southeast, south of Batman.

TR.title: Six-Digit Pole Codes
TR.description: In European Turkey, utility poles carry a six-digit code below the yellow electrical warning sign.

TR.title: Ankara Province Street Signs
TR.description: Street name plates in Ankara Province are blue with a small semicircular cap at the top.

TR.title: Izmir Province Street Signs
TR.description: Izmir street signs are dark blue, convex, and usually feature the white Izmir emblem at the top.

TR.title: Greenhouses West of Adana
TR.description: Dense clusters of greenhouses mark the southern coast west of Adana.

TR.title: Whitewashed Buildings Around Bodrum
TR.description: Bodrum features whitewashed flat-roofed buildings often accented with blue trim or natural stonework.

TR.title: Cappadocia Rock Formations in Goreme
TR.description: The town of Goreme, located west of Kayseri, is unmistakable thanks to towering sandstone pillars with ancient cave dwellings carved into their faces.

TR.title: Mount Ararat (Agri Dagi)
TR.description: Turkey's highest peak is a dormant volcano in the far east, often visible with a smaller cone (Kucuk Agri).

TR.title: Banana Plants Near Alanya
TR.description: Banana plantations are localised around the coastal city of Alanya.

TR.title: Light-Blue Tourist Signs on Bozcaada Island
TR.description: Bozcaada island uses distinctive light-blue and grey tourist information signs, shaped either as arrows or as rectangles with a rounded top.

TR.title: Istanbul Street Sign Arrow Indicator
TR.description: Red street name plates with a coloured bottom strip are used in multiple Turkish cities. A white arrow in the lower-right corner pointing in both directions with a single arrowhead is a strong indicator of Istanbul specifically.

TR.title: Red Oval Street Signs in Trabzon and Yalvac
TR.description: Trabzon and Yalvac share a distinctive red, oval-shaped street sign design. House number plates follow the same styling.

TR.title: Green Street Signs in Bursa
TR.description: Bursa's street name plates are green with slightly raised lettering, giving the surface a textured, three-dimensional feel.

TR.title: Green Borderless Street Signs in Bolu
TR.description: Street signs in Bolu are also green, but they are completely flat and have no border or frame around the edges.

TR.title: Country Flag
TR.description: The national flag of Turkey is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

TR.title: .tr Domain
TR.description: Web addresses in Türkiye end in the country domain .tr (often as .com.tr). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

TR.title: Red Government Plates
TR.description: In Turkey, you can rarely see plates with red characters on a white background. These plates are used for government vehicles and university rectors.

CH.title: Framed Signs
CH.description: In Switzerland, many road signs have a thin metal border that gives them a clean, framed look.

CH.title: Swiss bollards
CH.description: Bollards in Switzerland can either be cylindrical with a round top or have a rounded rectangular shape with a slanted top. Both are black and white with a rectangular reflector on the front.

CH.title: Low cam
CH.description: In Switzerland the images were captured with a lower mounted camera. This brings us closer to the ground and makes the country feel different from most other.

CH.title: Direction Signs
CH.description: Sign colour signals road class: blue for main roads, white for secondary roads.

CH.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
CH.description: Swiss pedestrian signs are tall blue rectangles with seven stripes, a unique shape in Europe.

CH.title: Yellow Dashed Centre Lines
CH.description: Long dashed yellow centre lines are a strong indicator of Switzerland.

CH.title: Yellow Zebra Crossings
CH.description: Pedestrian crossings in Switzerland are painted yellow.

CH.title: Town Entry Signs
CH.description: Settlement name boards are white or blue with a metal frame and often show canton abbreviations.

CH.title: Chevrons
CH.description: Swiss curve warning boards are black with a white arrow; a less common inverted variant exists.

CH.title: Landscape
CH.description: The south is mountainous with narrow valleys; the north has farmland and forested ridges.

CH.title: Architecture
CH.description: Buildings are stone with light colours, wooden balconies, tiled gable roofs, and hinged wooden shutters.

CH.title: Bus Stop Signs
CH.description: Bus stops have signs surrounded by a thick, tubular metal frame, unique to Switzerland.

CH.title: Four Official Languages
CH.description: Switzerland has German, French, Italian, and Romansh spoken in distinct zones.

CH.title: Bernese Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Bern speed limit signs show 'GENERELL' above the number in German-speaking areas.

CH.title: Vaud Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Vaud speed limit signs show 'GÉNÉRAL' above the number in French-speaking areas.

CH.title: French Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Speed limit signs show 'Limite générale' above the number in French-speaking areas.

CH.title: Neuchâtel Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Neuchâtel speed limit signs show 'GÉNÉRAL' above the number in French-speaking areas.

CH.title: Jura Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Jura speed limit signs show 'GÉNÉRAL' above the number in French-speaking areas.

CH.title: Fribourg Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Fribourg speed limit signs show 'GENERELL' or 'GÉNÉRAL' above the number depending on language.

CH.title: Ticino Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Ticino speed limit signs show 'Limite generale' above the number in Italian-speaking areas.

CH.title: Graubünden Speed Limit Sign Text
CH.description: Graubünden speed limit signs show ‘GENERELL’, ‘GÉNÉRAL’, or ‘GENERALA’ above the number.

CH.title: Aargau Canton Code (AG)
CH.description: Aargau vehicles and town signs display the 'AG' code.

CH.title: Appenzell Ausserrhoden Canton Code (AR)
CH.description: Vehicles and signs from Appenzell Ausserrhoden show the 'AR' code.

CH.title: Appenzell Innerrhoden Canton Code (AI)
CH.description: Vehicles and signs from Appenzell Innerrhoden show the 'AI' code.

CH.title: Basel-Landschaft Canton Code (BL)
CH.description: The 'BL' code appears on license plates and signs in Basel-Landschaft.

CH.title: Basel-Stadt Canton Code (BS)
CH.description: Basel-Stadt uses the 'BS' code on plates and entry signs.

CH.title: Bern Canton Code (BE)
CH.description: The 'BE' code identifies vehicles and locations from Bern.

CH.title: Fribourg Canton Code (FR)
CH.description: Vehicles and signs from Fribourg use the 'FR' code.

CH.title: Geneva Canton Code (GE)
CH.description: The 'GE' code marks license plates and signs in Geneva.

CH.title: Glarus Canton Code (GL)
CH.description: Glarus vehicles and signs show the 'GL' code.

CH.title: Graubünden Canton Code (GR)
CH.description: The 'GR' code identifies the canton of Graubünden.

CH.title: Jura Canton Code (JU)
CH.description: Jura vehicles and signs feature the 'JU' code.

CH.title: Luzern Canton Code
CH.description: The 'LU' code is used on license plates and entry signs in Luzern.

CH.title: Neuchâtel Canton Code
CH.description: Neuchâtel vehicles and town signs display the 'NE' abbreviation.

CH.title: Nidwalden Canton Code
CH.description: The 'NW' code on license plates and entry signs marks Nidwalden.

CH.title: Obwalden Canton Code
CH.description: Obwalden is identified by the 'OW' code on license plates and entry signs.

CH.title: Schaffhausen Canton Code
CH.description: The 'SH' abbreviation is used on plates and signs in Schaffhausen.

CH.title: Schwyz Canton Code
CH.description: Schwyz vehicles and entry signs are marked with the 'SZ' code.

CH.title: Solothurn Canton Code
CH.description: The 'SO' code on license plates and town signs is used for Solothurn.

CH.title: St. Gallen Canton Code
CH.description: St. Gallen is represented by the 'SG' code on license plates and entry signs.

CH.title: Ticino Canton Code
CH.description: The 'TI' abbreviation marks vehicles and entry signs from Ticino.

CH.title: Thurgau Canton Code
CH.description: Thurgau vehicles and town signs display the 'TG' code.

CH.title: Uri Canton Code
CH.description: The 'UR' code is used on license plates and entry signs in Uri.

CH.title: Valais Canton Code
CH.description: Valais is represented by the 'VS' code on plates and town entry signs.

CH.title: Vaud Canton Code
CH.description: Vehicles and entry signs from Vaud start with 'VD'.

CH.title: Zug Canton Code
CH.description: The 'ZG' code on license plates and entry signs is unique to Zug.

CH.title: Zürich Canton Code
CH.description: Zürich vehicles and town signs display the 'ZH' code.

CH.title: Postal Code Regions
CH.description: Swiss postal codes' leading digits follow a west-to-east pattern to narrow down your region.

CH.title: High Alpine South
CH.description: Southern cantons have tall, rugged Alpine peaks with deep valleys.

CH.title: Modest Northern Hills
CH.description: Northern cantons feature gentler terrain with modest hills and lower mountains.

CH.title: Jura Mountains
CH.description: Flat terrain with a chain of mid-height, forested mountains along the northwest horizon indicates the Jura.

CH.title: Jura Limestone Outcrops
CH.description: Bare limestone rock faces jutting from wooded hillsides are typical of the Jura mountains.

CH.title: Rock Walls
CH.description: Dry-stone walls along roads and fields are common in the Jura and Italian-speaking Alps.

CH.title: Italian-Style Architecture
CH.description: Orange-yellow walls, terracotta roofs, and Italian shutters indicate Ticino.

CH.title: Bernese Arch Houses
CH.description: Bern farmhouses have massive roofs with undersides curving into a pronounced arch.

CH.title: Northeastern Timber Framing
CH.description: Ornate, often red timber-framed buildings are typical of northeastern Switzerland.

CH.title: Appenzell House Style
CH.description: Appenzell houses join living quarters to barns at a 90° roof angle with facades subdivided into window-framing squares.

CH.title: Graubünden Stone Houses
CH.description: Graubünden houses are stone-built with white painted motifs around windows and edges.

CH.title: Vaud Oversized Town Signs
CH.description: Unusually large town entry signs appear in Vaud.

CH.title: Basel-Landschaft Olive Green Infrastructure
CH.description: Signposts and sign borders painted olive green indicate Basel-Landschaft.

CH.title: Valais Wooden Bollards
CH.description: Thick wooden bollards, square or cylindrical, are common in Valais.

CH.title: Glarus Fence Reflectors
CH.description: In Glarus, reflectors are mounted directly on roadside fences.

CH.title: Geneva Bike Path Symbol
CH.description: Cycle path markings in Geneva and the valley between Martigny and Lake Geneva show a simplified stick figure atop two disconnected wheels.

CH.title: Road Divider Types
CH.description: Distinct road divider and lane-marker styles vary across regions.

CH.title: Other Fruit Tree Areas
CH.description: Fruit orchards are common near Lake Constance and northwest of Lake Geneva.

CH.title: Country Flag
CH.description: The national flag of Switzerland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CH.title: 14 Romansch Speed Limit
CH.description: In Romansh-speaking Switzerland, the speed limit sign reads “limita generala” above the number

CH.title: Italian speed limit sign
CH.description: In Italian-speaking Switzerland, the speed limit sign reads “Limite generale” above the number

CH.title: .ch Domain
CH.description: Web addresses in Switzerland end in the country domain .ch. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CH.title: CH Sticker
CH.description: CH (Confoederatio Helvetica) stickers are commonly seen on Swiss cars.

AE.title: Emirati road lines
AE.description: In the UAE, outer road lines are yellow, while the center lines can be white or yellow.

AE.title: Desert landscape
AE.description: The natural terrain in UAE is predominantly flat and arid, with open desert stretching in every direction.

AE.title: Unpaved roads
AE.description: Despite the country's wealth, it is not unusual to encounter unpaved roads in residential areas.

AE.title: United Arab Emirates
AE.description: Houses in residential areas are usually made out of this light-colored stone.

AE.title: Arabic and English
AE.description: Signage in the UAE is bilingual, with Arabic script alongside English.

AE.title: Striped signposts
AE.description: In the UAE, signposts often have alternating black-and-white stripes.

AE.title: Striped kerbs
AE.description: In the UAE, kerbs are often painted with black-and-white or black-and-yellow stripes.

AE.title: Divided roads
AE.description: Divided roads and roundabouts are very common in the UAE.

AE.title: Wooden poles
AE.description: Emirati utility poles are dark brown wood topped with three insulators on a horizontal metal bar.

AE.title: Coverage area
AE.description: UAE Street View coverage is concentrated in the northeast.

AE.title: Eastern mountains
AE.description: Mountains in the UAE appear only in the far east.

AE.title: Dubai street signs
AE.description: Street name signs in Dubai are blue with a thin metal border, not seen elsewhere in the UAE.

AE.title: UAE flag
AE.description: Horizontal stripes of green, white, and black with a vertical red band on the left.

AE.title: .ae Domain
AE.description: Web addresses in the United Arab Emirates end in the country domain .ae. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

KG.title: Red strip
KG.description: Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan feature a red strip on the left side.

KG.title: Silver car
KG.description: A silver Google car with four visible bars is used for all coverage in Kyrgyzstan.

KG.title: Winter imagery
KG.description: All Kyrgyz Street View coverage was captured in winter, so expect bare trees, dull-looking terrain, and snow in many places.

KG.title: Kyrgyz bollards
KG.description: Kyrgyzstan uses white bollards featuring a diagonal black stripe near the top.

KG.title: Mosques
KG.description: Kyrgyzstan has a majority Muslim population, so mosques are a common sight across the country.

KG.title: Kyrgyz Cyrillic Script
KG.description: Kyrgyz uses Cyrillic with extra letters Ө, Ү, and Ң.

KG.title: White-Painted Trees and Poles
KG.description: Trees and concrete poles often have lower portions painted white.

KG.title: Red-and-White Kilometre Markers
KG.description: Kilometre markers have a red-and-white triangle pattern unique to Kyrgyzstan.

KG.title: Driving Direction Map
KG.description: Knowing which way the Google car drives on Kyrgyzstan's major roads helps narrow your position.

KG.title: Southern Mirror Clue
KG.description: The car's side mirror shows less road and a more diagonal reflection in southern Kyrgyzstan.

KG.title: Black Dot on Mirror
KG.description: A small black dot on the car mirror indicates a specific Kyrgyzstan region.

KG.title: Divided Roads
KG.description: Divided roads in Kyrgyzstan cluster around Bishkek, with a major highway east to Balykchy.

KG.title: Snowy Northern Roads
KG.description: Northern roads often have heavy snow coverage and bright skies.

KG.title: Bishkek, Capital City
KG.description: Bishkek features taller multi-storey buildings and upscale outskirts; mountains lie to the south.

KG.title: South of Bishkek, Tian Shan Mountains
KG.description: South of Bishkek is hilly with snow-capped Tian Shan mountains visible to the south.

KG.title: Colourful Poles near Bishkek
KG.description: Towns east and west of Bishkek have multi-coloured poles painted yellow, green, white, and sometimes red.

KG.title: Osh, Second-Largest City
KG.description: Osh uses the southern mirror and has partly cloudy weather.

KG.title: Osh, Trees with Leaves
KG.description: Most trees in Osh retain their leaves, unlike in Bishkek.

KG.title: Jalal-Abad, Overcast Coverage
KG.description: Jalal-Abad shows the southern mirror and has distinct overcast skies with no cloud gaps.

KG.title: Talas, Red and Yellow Striped Poles
KG.description: Poles in Talas are white at the base with red and yellow stripes.

KG.title: Naryn, Orange Ridge and Snow-Capped Peaks
KG.description: Naryn has a steep orange ridge to the north and snow-capped mountains to the south.

KG.title: EM-04: Tian Shan Mountain Range Visible
KG.description: The Tian Shan mountains are visible to the south; terrain is otherwise flat.

KG.title: EM-04: Southern Agricultural Section
KG.description: This southern section has extensive agriculture, lush roadside vegetation, and nearby hills.

KG.title: EM-11: Red Soil and Snow South of Naryn
KG.description: Mountains and hills south of Naryn show a striking mix of snow and red soil.

KG.title: EM-09: Overcast East of Cholpon Ata
KG.description: East of Cholpon Ata is overcast with mountains to the north, a lake to the south, and tall roadside trees.

KG.title: EM-10: Sandy Shore with Lake and Mountains
KG.description: Lake Issyk Kul and Tian Shan mountains are visible; soil is sandy and rocky.

KG.title: EM-10: Sandy Terrain with Southern Mountains
KG.description: Mountains dominate the south; sandy roadsides persist throughout.

KG.title: EM-10: Dry Western End of Issyk Kul
KG.description: The western end of Issyk Kul has drier terrain; lake and hills sit further from the road.

KG.title: Country Flag
KG.description: The national flag of Kyrgyzstan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

KG.title: .kg Domain
KG.description: Web addresses in Kyrgyzstan end in the country domain .kg. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MO.title: Black license plates
MO.description: In Macau, cars have black licence plates.

MO.title: Portuguese signs
MO.description: Portuguese often appears alongside Chinese on signs in Macau, reflecting its history as a Portuguese colony.

MO.title: Lamp Posts
MO.description: Macau uses cylindrical grey lamp posts with black-painted bases.

MO.title: Bilingual Street Signs
MO.description: White signs with blue borders show Chinese and Portuguese street names, unique to Macau.

MO.title: Casinos and Gambling
MO.description: Casinos and gambling ads are everywhere, often with extravagant architecture.

MO.title: Dense Northern Half
MO.description: Northern Macau has tightly packed apartments, narrow gridded streets, and cars lining both sides.

MO.title: Hilly Southern Area
MO.description: Southern Macau is hilly and rural, with narrow roads winding through trees and distinctive lamp posts.

MO.title: Country Flag
MO.description: The national flag of Macau is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

EC.title: Ecuadorian bollards
EC.description: In Ecuador, bollards are typically either thin and round with two red stripes or flat with two red reflectors.

EC.title: Ladder poles
EC.description: In Ecuador you can find these poles with a large amount of indents, referred to as ladder poles.

EC.title: Concrete roads
EC.description: It is fairly common to find concrete roads in Ecuador.

EC.title: Licence Plates
EC.description: Private plates in Ecuador are white in short and long formats. Taxis and buses use orange plates.

EC.title: Double Guardrails
EC.description: Paired guardrails running in parallel are common.

EC.title: Chevron Overuse
EC.description: Road bends have a high density of chevron signs.

EC.title: Square Road Signs
EC.description: White square information signs with a standard layout are used extensively.

EC.title: Kilometre Markers
EC.description: Distance posts are green with the highway shield emblem.

EC.title: Teal Blue Sign Backs
EC.description: Some sign backs are painted teal blue; poles are thin metal.

EC.title: One-Way Street Signs
EC.description: Directional signs feature the text "UNA VIA" inside arrow shapes indicating traffic flow.

EC.title: Grey Brick Architecture
EC.description: Houses are mostly grey cinder blocks with corrugated metal roofs.

EC.title: Hexagonal Tile Pavements
EC.description: Ecuadorian roads sometimes have interlocking hexagonal tiles.

EC.title: Elevation and Terrain
EC.description: The Andes run through the center, with flat terrain on the Pacific coast and Amazon basin.

EC.title: Banana Plantations
EC.description: Large banana plantations are in the southwestern lowlands.

EC.title: Dry Coastal Belt
EC.description: An arid coastal strip lies between Guayaquil and Manta.

EC.title: Flat Guayaquil Region
EC.description: The Guayaquil area is the flattest, especially along E-25 and E-48 highways.

EC.title: Amazon Region
EC.description: Amazon lowlands are flat and densely vegetated with Cordia trichotoma trees and oil palms.

EC.title: Esmeraldas Province
EC.description: Esmeraldas has Amazon-like vegetation but is hillier.

EC.title: Southern Mountain Roads
EC.description: Southern mountain roads have twisting paths with exposed reddish-brown earth.

EC.title: Chimborazo Province
EC.description: Chimborazo is semi-arid with abundant pine trees.

EC.title: Taxi Province Letters
EC.description: Taxi plates start with the province's initial letter; same for private plates.

EC.title: Northeastern Roadside Pipeline
EC.description: A brown above-ground pipeline runs alongside some northeastern roads.

EC.title: Galápagos Islands
EC.description: Galápagos has volcanic landscapes with lava fields, scrubland, and craters; covered by trekker and boat imagery.

EC.title: Country Flag
EC.description: The national flag of Ecuador is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

EC.title: .ec Domain
EC.description: Web addresses in Ecuador end in the country domain .ec (often as .com.ec). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

LU.title: Yellow license plates
LU.description: In Luxembourg, cars have yellow license plates with a blue strip on the left side.

LU.title: Black roofs
LU.description: Luxembourg houses typically have dark slate roofs and plain, undecorated walls painted white, grey, or in pastel tones.

LU.title: Directional signs
LU.description: Luxembourg's directional signs are yellow with a thin black outline. They are arrow shaped and often feature a number in a red box .

LU.title: White signposts
LU.description: In Luxembourg, nearly all road signs are mounted on white signposts.

LU.title: Bollards
LU.description: Black-and-white wedge-shaped bollards with grey reflectors; some have a lower indent.

LU.title: Chevrons
LU.description: Chevrons are black with yellow arrows; a blue-and-yellow variant also appears.

LU.title: Upside-Down Trident Poletops
LU.description: Common pole tops shaped like inverted tridents.

LU.title: Multilingual Signage
LU.description: French dominates public signage; German and Luxembourgish also appear.

LU.title: Luxembourgish Language
LU.description: Closely related to German with umlauts, double vowels, and accented é.

LU.title: Town Entrance Signs
LU.description: Yellow framed, often bilingual signs showing road number and speed limit.

LU.title: Square-Cornered Frames
LU.description: Metal frames around signs and road infrastructure are common.

LU.title: Street Name Signs
LU.description: Typically short, white-backed signs; a common variant has slanted blue corners.

LU.title: Blue-and-White Signpost Reflectors
LU.description: Some signposts have bulky round blue-and-white reflectors.

LU.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
LU.description: Pedestrian signs display five vertical stripes.

LU.title: Bus Stop Signs
LU.description: Blue bus stop signs with a bus icon showing six windows.

LU.title: Rolling Hills Landscape
LU.description: Landscape dominated by green rolling hills with farmland and forest patches.

LU.title: Local Road Numbers
LU.description: Three-digit local road numbers grouped geographically by first digit.

LU.title: Topography
LU.description: Northern half is higher and hillier than the flatter south.

LU.title: Vineyards
LU.description: Vineyards are concentrated in the southeast.

LU.title: Country Flag
LU.description: The national flag of Luxembourg is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LU.title: .lu Domain
LU.description: Web addresses in Luxembourg end in the country domain .lu. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.
