ID.title: Ornaments on roofs
ID.description: In Bali, you can often spot murdha, decorative crown like ornaments placed along the tops of traditional roofs.

ID.title: Yellow waystones
ID.description: In Indonesia you can find yellow distance markers tilted towards the road, with a notch cut near the top. They list shorthand names for three destinations.

ID.title: West Sumatra
ID.description: West Sumatra has these unique boat-shaped roofs.

ID.title: White sections
ID.description: Most Indonesian license plates are black with white letters, often appearing as three white segments through blur.

ID.title: Street abbreviation
ID.description: In Indonesia, it is common to see the abbreviation JL for Jalan, the local word for street.

ID.title: Road Markings
ID.description: Centre lines can be white or yellow; edge lines are always white.

ID.title: Utility Poles
ID.description: Cylindrical steel or concrete poles, some painted black with red-and-white bands. Crossbars may be symmetrical or asymmetrical.

ID.title: Bollards
ID.description: Common designs include black-and-white square or round-topped posts and yellow-and-black variants with red reflectors.

ID.title: Red-and-White Banners
ID.description: Strings of small red and white pennants, the national colours, hung along roads throughout the archipelago.

ID.title: Cigarette Advertisements
ID.description: Tobacco billboards with the word 'PERINGATAN' is a common sight in Indonesia.

ID.title: Front Licence Plates on Motorcycles
ID.description: Indonesian motorcycles carry a front licence plate, unlike other Southeast Asian countries.

ID.title: General 01 Kabupaten
ID.description: Indonesia is divided into hundreds of regencies know as Kabupaten (Kab. for short). This term is unique to Indonesia.

ID.title: Cardinal Direction Words
ID.description: Addresses and province names often include directional terms: Utara (North), Timur (East), Selatan (South), Barat (West), Tengah (Central).

ID.title: Triangle Pole Connector
ID.description: A triangular brace connects the vertical pole to its horizontal crossbar in some provinces, particularly in western Java.

ID.title: Trident Pole Tops
ID.description: A three-pronged 'trident' crossbar design mainly in Central Java and Yogyakarta.

ID.title: Bali Rectangular Pole Attachment
ID.description: Poles in Bali sometimes have a distinctive rectangular bracket at the top.

ID.title: Lesser Sunda Extra-Long Pole Support
ID.description: Pole tops feature an elongated diagonal brace; some have two supports on the Lesser Sunda Islands.

ID.title: North/Central Sulawesi Pole Bracket
ID.description: An additional bracket beneath the horizontal crossbar is typical in North and Central Sulawesi and Gorontalo.

ID.title: Central Sulawesi Secondary Poles
ID.description: Slender black secondary poles beside main utility poles with two strips of tape near the top.

ID.title: Satellite Dish Direction
ID.description: Satellite dishes aim towards the equator; dish direction indicates relative position to it.

ID.title: Central Sulawesi Tricolour Bollards
ID.description: Roadside posts painted black, white, and yellow horizontal bands are specific to Central Sulawesi.

ID.title: Painted Fences on Sulawesi
ID.description: Roadside fences painted white with blue or red highlights are common on Sulawesi.

ID.title: Green Bridge Railings in Kalimantan
ID.description: Bridge guardrails and side panels painted green are characteristic of South and Central Kalimantan.

ID.title: Oil Palm Plantations
ID.description: Vast palm oil estates are concentrated on Sumatra and Kalimantan, rare on Sulawesi.

ID.title: Rice Paddies
ID.description: Most rice cultivation is on Java, with secondary areas in South Sulawesi and South Sumatra.

ID.title: Dry Lesser Sunda Landscape
ID.description: Nusa Tenggara islands are arid, with brown sparse vegetation, driest on Sumba.

ID.title: North Sumba Savannah
ID.description: Open grassland like African savannah appears in northern Sumba.

ID.title: Red Soil on Batam and Bangka Belitung
ID.description: Reddish earth is common on Batam Island and Bangka Belitung off Sumatra's east coast.

ID.title: Clay Tile Roofs on Java
ID.description: Terracotta roof tiles are mainly a Javanese feature.

ID.title: Corrugated Metal Roofs
ID.description: Sheet-metal roofing predominates in northern and outer islands like Kalimantan, Sulawesi, and Sumatra.

ID.title: Bugis Roof Vents in South Sulawesi
ID.description: Horizontal louvred openings in triangular gable ends are nearly exclusive to South Sulawesi.

ID.title: Sumba High-Peaked Roofs
ID.description: Sumba houses have extremely steep, towering roof peaks unique in Indonesia.

ID.title: North Sumatra Batak Roofs
ID.description: Batak houses have curved boat-like roofs with gentler upward sweep and no spires.

ID.title: Kalimantan Wooden Shingle Roofs
ID.description: Roofs covered in small overlapping wooden shingles are distinctive in Kalimantan.

ID.title: Gable Horn Roofs
ID.description: Roofs topped with horn-like finials at the gable peak, common in South Sulawesi, Riau, and Central/South Kalimantan.

ID.title: Regional Licence Plate Codes
ID.description: Plate prefixes indicate region: single letters on western Java, two letters on eastern Java and other islands.

ID.title: Christian Minority Regions
ID.description: Churches and Christian iconography appear in minority areas like parts of Sulawesi, Papua, NTT, and North Sumatra.

ID.title: Country Flag
ID.description: The national flag of Indonesia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

ID.title: .id Domain
ID.description: Web addresses in Indonesia end in the country domain .id (often as .co.id or .go.id). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

IN.title: Dry landscape
IN.description: Some parts of the northern Himalayan region administered by India are known for dry, high altitude landscapes with very little vegetation.

IN.title: Bad quality
IN.description: The majority of Indian coverage comes from a notoriously poor camera, recognized by low sharpness and washed-out colors.

IN.title: Underscore but above
IN.description: India has many different languages. If you see written text with a continuous line running along the top of each word, you are in the central or northern parts of the country.

IN.title: English
IN.description: As one of India's official languages, English is widely present on signs and boards across the country.

IN.title: Regional Scripts
IN.description: Distinct writing systems help narrow down the state or region in India.

IN.title: Licence Plates
IN.description: Indian plates are usually white; yellow plates are commercial vehicles, green plates are electric vehicles.

IN.title: Black and White Striped Signposts
IN.description: Road signposts in India are painted in alternating black and white stripes.

IN.title: Utility Poles
IN.description: Indian utility poles are concrete square columns topped with a trident-shaped fixture.

IN.title: Marathi Script
IN.description: Marathi in Maharashtra uses Devanagari script, distinguished by the character ळ.

IN.title: Punjabi (Gurmukhi Script)
IN.description: Gurmukhi script in Punjab has rounder letters and a broken horizontal bar, with key letters like ਨ, ਲ, and ਅ.

IN.title: Gujarati Script
IN.description: Gujarati script lacks the horizontal line across the top of words found in Hindi.

IN.title: Bengali Script
IN.description: Bengali script features many left-pointing triangular forms within its characters.

IN.title: Assamese Script
IN.description: Assamese script, based on Bengali, includes unique characters like ৰ and ৱ.

IN.title: Kannada Script
IN.description: Kannada script has flowing curves, small circles, and wavy tails on many characters.

IN.title: Telugu Script
IN.description: Telugu script resembles Kannada but has checkmark-style diacritics above letters.

IN.title: Tamil Script
IN.description: Tamil script blends curves, straight strokes, right angles, and dot-shaped diacritics.

IN.title: Oriya Script
IN.description: Oriya script is rounded with broad semi-circular arcs and sweeping curve diacritics.

IN.title: Malayalam Script
IN.description: Malayalam features smoothly rounded characters with inverted U-shaped forms.

IN.title: Manipuri (Meitei Script)
IN.description: Meitei script has many vertical strokes and sharp right-angled forms.

IN.title: Mizo Language (Latin Script)
IN.description: Mizo is commonly written in Latin script in Mizoram.

IN.title: English-Only in Meghalaya
IN.description: Meghalaya signage is almost entirely in English with no local script.

IN.title: Yellow and Black Tuk Tuks
IN.description: Yellow tuk tuks with black rooftops indicate Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, or Tamil Nadu.

IN.title: Gujarat Concrete Holey Poles
IN.description: Concrete utility poles with holes appear only in Gujarat and nearby union territories.

IN.title: Two-Section Poles
IN.description: Utility poles split into two segments are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

IN.title: Sikkim Mesh Poles
IN.description: Metallic lattice mesh utility poles are typical of Sikkim.

IN.title: Kerala Metal Holey Poles
IN.description: Perforated metal utility poles are widespread in Kerala.

IN.title: Thin Grey Metal Poles
IN.description: Slender grey metal poles, often in pairs, are common in northeastern states and Himalayan zones.

IN.title: Punjab Mint Green Electricity Counters
IN.description: Mint green electricity meter boxes with small square windows signal Punjab.

IN.title: Window-Shaped Pole Tops
IN.description: Compact metal pole tops shaped like window frames are typical of Punjab and Haryana.

IN.title: Karnataka Trident Pole Tops
IN.description: Poles with a top central insulator and two lower ones are typical of Karnataka.

IN.title: Manipur Metal Trident Poles
IN.description: Metal poles topped with a trident arrangement are exclusive to Manipur.

IN.title: Inverted Triangle Pole Tops
IN.description: Upside-down triangular attachments beneath pole tops are common in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.

IN.title: Madhya Pradesh Inverted-A Poles
IN.description: Metal brackets shaped like upside-down A's below pole tops are specific to Madhya Pradesh.

IN.title: Trapezoid Pole Connector
IN.description: Inverted trapezoid connectors link crossbars to poles, mainly in Chhattisgarh.

IN.title: West Bengal Rectangle Pole Tops
IN.description: Pole tops with tall, narrow rectangular frames are characteristic of West Bengal.

IN.title: West Bengal Double Crossbar Poles
IN.description: Poles with two horizontal crossbars joined by vertical supports are seen in West Bengal.

IN.title: Northeast Even/Uneven Pole Tops
IN.description: A distinctive pole arrangement with one even and one uneven crossbar top on the same pole in northeastern states.

IN.title: Chevron-Shaped Pole Attachment
IN.description: Diagonal bars in a '<' shape on poles, common in Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh.

IN.title: Assam/Meghalaya Double Crossbar Poles
IN.description: Poles with two crossbars and two insulators each, found in Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram.

IN.title: Assam Bent Trident Poles
IN.description: Trident-style pole top with the centre prong bent at a right angle, exclusive to Assam.

IN.title: Goa Stacked Crossbar Poles
IN.description: A shorter crossbar above a longer one on the same pole, specific to Goa.

IN.title: Tamil Nadu Pole/Tree Markings
IN.description: A black stripe flanked by two white stripes painted on poles and tree trunks, indicating Tamil Nadu.

IN.title: Delhi Pole Stripes
IN.description: Poles marked with five or more narrow alternating black and yellow bands, typical of Delhi.

IN.title: Bihar Pole Stripes
IN.description: Poles with four broader black and yellow bands, distinctive to Bihar.

IN.title: Bihar Red and White Tree Paint
IN.description: Tree trunks painted with four alternating red and white stripes near the base, mainly in Bihar.

IN.title: Kerala Yellow Pole Markings
IN.description: Compact yellow markings on utility poles, common in Kerala.

IN.title: Central India Rounded Roof Tiles
IN.description: Semi-cylindrical clay tiles laid in irregular rows on rooftops can be found across central India.

IN.title: Southern India Flat Orange Roof Tiles
IN.description: Vivid orange flat tiles with a central ridge, prevalent in Tamil Nadu.

IN.title: West Bengal Diamond-Protrusion Roof Tiles
IN.description: Flat roofing tiles with a small diamond-shaped raised element at the centre, typical of West Bengal.

IN.title: West Bengal Large Metal Hip Roofs
IN.description: Broad hip-style roofs made from corrugated metal sheeting in West Bengal and nearby areas.

IN.title: Northeast Metal Roofs with Triangle
IN.description: Sheet metal roofs with a small triangular detail near the apex, widespread in Northeast India.

IN.title: Northeast Square-Panel Houses
IN.description: Houses built from square wall panels divided by slender beams, characteristic of Northeast India.

IN.title: Thatched Roof Huts
IN.description: Thatched huts along the eastern coast and northern plains, using hay or dried palm fan leaves.

IN.title: Sikh Gurdwaras in Punjab
IN.description: Temples with white domed roofs, decorated walls, and the Khanda emblem, concentrated in Punjab.

IN.title: Wealthy Homes in Goa and Kerala
IN.description: Modern, affluent residential architecture common in prosperous Goa and Kerala.

IN.title: Chir Pines
IN.description: Trees with smooth conical or spherical canopies of long needles, found in Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and western Arunachal Pradesh.

IN.title: Khasi Pines
IN.description: Pines with long needles and irregular, rough crowns, growing in Meghalaya and Manipur.

IN.title: Euphorbia Cacti Fences
IN.description: Hedgerows of Euphorbia neriifolia cacti used as natural fencing in Gujarat, western Maharashtra, and southern Rajasthan.

IN.title: Palmyra Palms
IN.description: Tall palms with spherical fan-leaf canopies, common in southern and eastern India.

IN.title: Areca Palms
IN.description: Slender-trunk palms with compact crowns along the southwestern coast, northeastern states, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

IN.title: Date Palms
IN.description: Typical palms of the arid central interior where tropical palms are scarce.

IN.title: Oil Palm Plantations
IN.description: Primarily in Andhra Pradesh's narrow panhandle near the eastern Telangana border.

IN.title: Tea Plantations
IN.description: Located in northeastern states and the far southern hills.

IN.title: Sugarcane
IN.description: Grown mainly in northern Uttar Pradesh and parts of the southwest.

IN.title: Cotton
IN.description: Cultivated across western India, especially Gujarat and Maharashtra.

IN.title: Canola
IN.description: Grown chiefly in and around Rajasthan.

IN.title: Himalayan Mountains
IN.description: India's tallest mountain range, towering over all other terrain.

IN.title: Northern Plains
IN.description: Vast flat farmland with highly fertile soil in the Ganges Valley.

IN.title: Maharashtra Dark Soil
IN.description: Dark-coloured earth concentrated in Maharashtra and nearby areas.

IN.title: Red Soil
IN.description: Red soil along the southern west coast and Chhattisgarh–western Odisha corridor.

IN.title: Western Rajasthan Desert
IN.description: Arid, sandy terrain dominating western Rajasthan.

IN.title: Western Ghats Ridgelines
IN.description: Flat, plateau-like ridges in western Maharashtra, drier in the north and greener in the south.

IN.title: Mizoram Green Valleys
IN.description: Deep green valleys with low vegetation, flanked by eroded hills and small peaks.

IN.title: Northeast Wooden Stick Fences
IN.description: Rustic fences of thin wooden sticks woven into a square grid, common in northeastern states.

IN.title: Buddhist Prayer Flags
IN.description: Colourful prayer flags visible in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

IN.title: Andaman and Nicobar Pole Stickers
IN.description: Dark stickers with digits and a central arrow on utility poles, unique to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

IN.title: Elevated Railways
IN.description: Above-ground metro and rail lines in major cities like Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, and Mumbai.

IN.title: Grey Brick Roofs
IN.description: Rooftops of thin grey stone or brick slabs, with similar grey rock in walls and stockyards on the Telangana/Karnataka border.

IN.title: White Clay Huts
IN.description: Mud-walled huts coated in white paint in northwest Bihar and northeast Uttar Pradesh.

IN.title: Central Bihar Cross-Pattern Huts
IN.description: Timber-framed huts with criss-cross lattice walls in central Bihar.

IN.title: Japanese Cedar Trees
IN.description: Tall trees with slender, bushy canopies near the Sikkim-West Bengal boundary and Meghalaya.

IN.title: Barren Western Uttarakhand
IN.description: Hillsides northwest of Dehradun are stripped of vegetation due to deforestation and erosion.

IN.title: Gujarat Salt Flats
IN.description: Expansive salt pans and coastal marshlands with little plant life and shallow water.

IN.title: Southern Tamil Nadu Red Soil
IN.description: Flat, scrubby terrain with intensely red earth in southern Tamil Nadu.

IN.title: Country Flag
IN.description: The national flag of India is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

IN.title: .in Domain
IN.description: Web addresses in India end in the country domain .in (often as .co.in). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

SN.title: Senegalese license plates
SN.description: In Senegal, older plates are fully blue, while newer ones have just a blue strip on the left side.

SN.title: Senegalese road lines
SN.description: In Senegal, roads often have long white dashed lines along the sides.

SN.title: Big truck
SN.description: In most of the Senegal coverage a silver, white or black truck is visible.

SN.title: French colonial influence
SN.description: In Senegal, French is the official language and dominates all visible signage.

SN.title: Blue plates
SN.description: Senegal uses blue license plates, the only country in Africa to do so.

SN.title: Driving direction
SN.description: In Senegal they drive on the right side of the road.

SN.title: French-Style Infrastructure
SN.description: Senegal uses French-pattern bollards, poles, signs, and road markings.

SN.title: Kilometre Markers
SN.description: Senegalese kilometre markers are white posts with red tops showing road numbers and distances.

SN.title: Pink-Bordered Town Signs
SN.description: Senegalese town entry signs are white with a thick pink outline and bold black lettering.

SN.title: Solar-Powered Black Lamps
SN.description: Black lampposts topped with solar panels appear frequently along Senegalese roads.

SN.title: Yellow-Orange Taxis
SN.description: Yellow-orange taxis with black-painted fenders are common in Senegal.

SN.title: Northern Savannah-Desert
SN.description: North of The Gambia, terrain is flat, arid with sparse, faded foliage trees.

SN.title: Southern Green Region
SN.description: South of The Gambia, vegetation is lush and green with palm trees near the coast.

SN.title: Diourbel Rural Coverage
SN.description: Extensive rural coverage with sandy unpaved roads and scattered trees around Diourbel.

SN.title: Northwestern Coastal Dunes
SN.description: Gently rolling vegetated sand dunes characterise the northwestern coastline.

SN.title: Bakel, Dry Hills
SN.description: Dry terrain with gentle hills appears around Bakel and south to Nayé.

SN.title: Kedougou, Greener Hills
SN.description: Kedougou and Mako have more verdant vegetation and larger hills.

SN.title: Divided Highways
SN.description: Senegal has two divided highways: Dakar–Touba and Dakar–Saly.

SN.title: Saloum Delta Marshland
SN.description: Flat, slightly marshy terrain with low vegetation appears in the Saloum River Delta.

SN.title: Forest of Thiès
SN.description: Slightly hilly area with dry brown vegetation, bright orange dirt roads, and noticeable haze.

SN.title: Dakar
SN.description: Senegal's capital has dense urban fabric and taller, modern buildings.

SN.title: Country Flag
SN.description: The national flag of Senegal is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SN.title: .sn Domain
SN.description: Web addresses in Senegal end in the country domain .sn. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CY.title: White water tanks
CY.description: In Cyprus, buildings often have a white, horizontal water tank with a round lid.

CY.title: Three styles
CY.description: License plates in Cyprus can come in many colors. White and yellow for regular cars and red for rentals.

CY.title: Triangular bollards
CY.description: Cyprus has white, triangular bollards with slanted tops. A small reflector on the front is red and white on the back.

CY.title: .cy Domain
CY.description: Web addresses in Cyprus end in the country domain .cy (often as .com.cy). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

PE.title: Peruvian poles
PE.description: In Peru, you can often see concrete utility poles with three horizontal crossarms.

PE.title: Red bricks
PE.description: Red brick buildings are common near Lake Titicaca in Peru and resemble architecture frequently seen in western Bolivia.

PE.title: Licence Plates
PE.description: Peruvian plates are white or yellow; taxis have split-coloured plates, yellow on top and white on bottom.

PE.title: Road Line Markings
PE.description: Peruvian outer road lines are always white. Highways have single or double yellow centre lines. Rural mountain roads often lack a centre line.

PE.title: Triangular Concrete Bollards
PE.description: Peruvian bollards are usually red or yellow triangular concrete shapes; circular concrete variants also appear.

PE.title: Black-and-Yellow Guardrails
PE.description: Peruvian guardrails commonly have black-and-yellow diagonal stripes; other designs like sharp arrows also appear.

PE.title: Kilometre Markers
PE.description: Concrete kilometre markers painted black and white are found along Peruvian roads.

PE.title: Road Signs 01 01 Concrete Foundations
PE.description: Metal signs in Peru are standing on visible concrete plinths.

PE.title: Painted Pole Bases
PE.description: Some Peruvian utility poles have lower sections painted black or black-and-yellow stripes.

PE.title: Orange-Painted Bridges
PE.description: Peruvian bridges are often painted orange.

PE.title: Semi-Arid Mountain Landscape
PE.description: Much of Peru has dry mountain ranges and valleys with sparse vegetation.

PE.title: Vehicles 01 Tuk Tuks
PE.description: Tuk Tuks are a common sight in Peru. They are usually referred to as mototaxi.

PE.title: Red-and-White Vehicle Stickers
PE.description: Wide red-and-white reflective stickers are common on taxis and commercial vehicles in Peru.

PE.title: Sol Currency (S/.)
PE.description: The Peruvian sol, written as S/, appears on shop signs and ads.

PE.title: Political Party Logos
PE.description: Peruvian political party logos are often painted on walls and buildings.

PE.title: Terrain Overview, East vs. West
PE.description: Eastern Peru is generally flat; western Peru is mountainous.

PE.title: Climate Zones
PE.description: Western coast is arid desert; eastern lowlands are tropical rainforest; Andes create transitional climates.

PE.title: Highway Numbering System
PE.description: Western highways increase in number from north to south; Routes 1, 3, and 5 are longest.

PE.title: Tumbes Off-Road Landscapes
PE.description: Tumbes off-road areas have sandy soil with green or dry shrubs.

PE.title: Southwestern Piura, Dry Flat Terrain
PE.description: Southwest of Piura is dry, sparsely vegetated, mostly flat with gentle hills.

PE.title: Northwestern Piura, Hilly Terrain
PE.description: Northwest of Piura has similar vegetation but more hilly terrain.

PE.title: Coconut and Tall Palm Trees
PE.description: Coconut and tall palms grow in coastal farming areas north of Lima and near large coastal cities.

PE.title: Sugar Cane Fields
PE.description: Large sugar cane plantations are near northern coastal cities Chiclayo and Trujillo.

PE.title: Banana Plantations
PE.description: Bananas grow in northern coastal agricultural zones, similar to sugar cane.

PE.title: Flat Highland Plateaus
PE.description: Flat high-altitude terrain appears in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

PE.title: Scrubby Mountains in the Far North
PE.description: Far northern Peruvian mountains have low shrubs and scrubby trees, often arid near coast and Ecuador.

PE.title: Pine Plantations at High Elevation
PE.description: Planted pine forests grow at higher elevations away from coastal deserts and Amazon basin.

PE.title: Rocky Outcrops in the Central Highlands
PE.description: Exposed rock faces are common on hillsides in central Peru from Lago Chinchaycocha south to Ayacucho.

PE.title: Jagged Mountain Peaks
PE.description: Tall, sharp rocky peaks are typical from Huaraz south to Cusco, away from the coast.

PE.title: Light Green Lichen
PE.description: Pale green lichen patches cover rocks and ground at high altitudes in central and southern Peru.

PE.title: Dark Red Soil
PE.description: Reddish-tinted earth appears notably around Cusco, Ayacucho, Cajamarca, and Tarapoto.

PE.title: Southern Coastal Desert
PE.description: From Ica down to Tacna, the landscape is a barren, flat desert with distant mountains to the east.

PE.title: Coastal Agricultural Valleys
PE.description: Green farming valleys run southwest-to-northeast between barren mountains in central and southern Peru.

PE.title: Overhanging Roofs with Wooden Supports
PE.description: Buildings with outward-extending roofs on wooden supports, often brightly painted, common in northern Peru.

PE.title: Open-Front Tuk-Tuks
PE.description: Tuk-tuks with exposed front compartments mainly in northern Peru, especially near northern Amazonian regions.

PE.title: Moquegua Cylindrical Bollard
PE.description: Cylindrical bollard topped a yellow stripe can be seen in the southern parts of Peru. A version with a black stripe is exclusive to southern Moquegua.

PE.title: Ruta 5N, San Alejandro to Esperanza
PE.description: Well-maintained, straight, flat north–south road through dense rainforest.

PE.title: Ruta 28B, Kimbiri to Echarate
PE.description: Narrow paved hillside road following a river valley with faded or absent lane markings.

PE.title: Volcanoes Near Arequipa
PE.description: Volcanic peaks frequently visible in and around Arequipa in southeastern Peru.

PE.title: Lima Boulevards
PE.description: Wide, long, straight streets split by concrete or grassy strips are most common in Lima.

PE.title: Pucallpa Street Grid
PE.description: Pucallpa has a uniform street grid oriented WSW–ENE.

PE.title: Iquitos
PE.description: Isolated northeastern city with overcast skies, three-wheeled tuk-tuks, and rolling Amazonian terrain.

PE.title: Cusco
PE.description: Southern highland city encircled by mountains with red-brick and colonial Spanish architecture.

PE.title: Aguas Calientes–Cusco Train Trekker
PE.description: Trekker follows railway line connecting Aguas Calientes with Cusco.

PE.title: Country Flag
PE.description: The national flag of Peru is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PE.title: .pe Domain
PE.description: Web addresses in Peru end in the country domain .pe (often as .com.pe). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

BD.title: Bengali language
BD.description: Bengali is an official language of Bangladesh, and its script has a horizontal line across the top of each word.

BD.title: Triangular letters
BD.description: Bengali, the language in Bangladesh has got a lot of triangular shapes, something similar scripts do not feature.

BD.title: Rickshaws
BD.description: Rickshaws appear constantly throughout Bangladesh, with green motorized auto rickshaws being especially common.

BD.title: Roadside water and fields
BD.description: Ponds, canals, and agricultural plots running alongside the road are a common sight across Bangladesh.

BD.title: Licence Plates
BD.description: Vehicles in Bangladesh have licence plates in white, black, or turquoise.

BD.title: Striped Signposts
BD.description: Sign poles often have alternating black and white stripes.

BD.title: White-Painted Tree Trunks
BD.description: Roads are often lined with trees whose lower trunks are painted white.

BD.title: Red and White Bollards
BD.description: Concrete bollards alternate red and white and appear in cylindrical and square forms.

BD.title: Tin Roofs
BD.description: Corrugated metal roofing is widespread on residential buildings.

BD.title: Eastern Triangle Window Roofs
BD.description: Metal roofs in the east often have a small triangular opening below the ridge.

BD.title: Tiled Roofs
BD.description: Tile roofing appears near the Indian border within Khulna.

BD.title: Early Growth Rice
BD.description: Short green rice shoots just above water appear in Khulna, Mymensingh, and south Dhaka.

BD.title: Mid-Growth Rice
BD.description: Medium-height green rice indicates mid-season growth in Rangpur, Barishal, and Chittagong.

BD.title: Fully-Grown Rice
BD.description: Mature rice is taller, yellow or orange, with fluffy tips signaling ripeness.

BD.title: Harvested Rice
BD.description: Fields show short beige or brown stubble after harvesting.

BD.title: Off-Season Fields
BD.description: Rice paddies lie empty and bare between planting cycles.

BD.title: Vast Empty Rice Fields
BD.description: Expansive rice paddies stretch to the horizon with little else in sight.

BD.title: Eastern Chittagong Hills
BD.description: Forested hills break the flat terrain in eastern Chittagong.

BD.title: Sylhet Border Ridge
BD.description: An east-west mountain ridge runs along the Indian border near Sylhet.

BD.title: Corn Fields
BD.description: Maize fields concentrate in western divisions like Rajshahi and Rangpur.

BD.title: Jute Crops
BD.description: Tall green jute crops grow mainly in Rangpur; dried jute is seen nationwide.

BD.title: Canola Fields
BD.description: Short bright yellow canola blossoms grow north of the Padma River.

BD.title: Tea Plantations
BD.description: Tea grows in elevated southern Sylhet and occasionally in Chittagong.

BD.title: Fruit Trees and Orchards
BD.description: Isolated fruit trees and orchards appear near the Indian border in Rajshahi and Rangpur.

BD.title: Barishal Sunflowers
BD.description: Sunflower fields appear in southern Barishal.

BD.title: Barishal Watermelons
BD.description: Watermelon patches are found in southern Barishal.

BD.title: Northern Eucalyptus
BD.description: Tall eucalyptus trees with pale trunks are common in northern divisions.

BD.title: Blossoming Trees
BD.description: Flowering trees appear in Khulna, Mymensingh, and southern Dhaka during spring.

BD.title: Beach Sheoaks
BD.description: Slender evergreen Beach Sheoak trees line the Teknaf Peninsula coast and Noakhali.

BD.title: Saint Martin's Island Guard Trekker
BD.description: On Saint Martin's Island, the trekker is accompanied by a security guard.

BD.title: Country Flag
BD.description: The national flag of Bangladesh is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BD.title: .bd Domain
BD.description: Web addresses in Bangladesh end in the country domain .bd (often as .com.bd). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

LT.title: Square poles
LT.description: In Lithuania, utility poles are usually square concrete posts with a diagonal support beam.

LT.title: Lithuanian plates
LT.description: Lithuania has standard white EU plates with a blue strip on the left.

LT.title: Kilometer markers
LT.description: Small blue signs with numbers on them can be found in Lithuania. They are placed in pairs, with a 45 degree angle to the road.

LT.title: Lithuanian bollard
LT.description: Lithuanian bollards are whites and have a rectangular orange reflector on the front and a white on the back.

LT.title: Thin outline
LT.description: Lithuanian signs have a red border with a thin white outline.

LT.title: Poletop Styles
LT.description: Lithuanian poletops often have short horizontal rods holding insulators, sometimes in a trident pattern.

LT.title: Chevrons
LT.description: Lithuanian chevrons are white with red arrows; small variants have a red outline.

LT.title: Kilometre Markers
LT.description: Lithuanian blue L-shaped km markers are mounted at a 45° angle toward the road.

LT.title: Warning and Speed Sign Borders
LT.description: Lithuanian warning and speed signs have a thin red border with a thin white outline.

LT.title: Guardrails with Orange Reflectors
LT.description: Lithuanian guardrails are standard A-type with orange reflectors.

LT.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
LT.description: Lithuanian crossing signs show three stripes and a low-detail pedestrian figure.

LT.title: Bus Stop Signs
LT.description: Lithuanian bus stop signs feature a bus icon with four windows.

LT.title: Lithuanian Language
LT.description: A Baltic language with hooked vowels (Ą Ę Į Ų), Ė with a dot, and the letter Y.

LT.title: 'Gatvė' Street Label
LT.description: The word for street is gatvė, often abbreviated as g. on signs.

LT.title: Place Name Ending '-ai'
LT.description: Many Lithuanian town and village names end in -ai.

LT.title: Architecture
LT.description: Buildings are light-coloured brick with steep corrugated metal roofs; wooden and pastel-painted stone houses also appear.

LT.title: Directional Signs
LT.description: Directional signs are blue with white text and arrowheads with straight vertical back edges.

LT.title: Open Agricultural Landscape
LT.description: Lithuania has less forest cover, giving the countryside an open, agricultural feel.

LT.title: Topography
LT.description: Although Lithuania is largely flat, the southeast is the hilliest region.

LT.title: Bilingual Polish Signs
LT.description: In southeastern Lithuania, bilingual Lithuanian-Polish signs occasionally appear.

LT.title: Country Flag
LT.description: The national flag of Lithuania is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LT.title: .lt Domain
LT.description: Web addresses in Lithuania end in the country domain .lt. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

PL.title: Warning signs
PL.description: Poland's warning signs are triangular with a yellow background and a thin red border.

PL.title: Thousands of stores
PL.description: The convenience store Żabka can be found pretty much everywhere in Poland.

PL.title: Red bollards
PL.description: Polish bollards have a red band around them, with a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.

PL.title: Licence Plates
PL.description: Polish plates are long and white with the standard EU blue strip on the left.

PL.title: Double White Centre Lines
PL.description: All road markings are white in Poland. Double centre lines are extremely common.

PL.title: Guardrails with Red Reflectors
PL.description: Polish guardrails are fitted with circular red reflectors.

PL.title: White Prohibitory Signs
PL.description: Polish round prohibitory signs use a white background with a thicker red border.

PL.title: Town Entry Signs
PL.description: Polish towns have two signs: a green one with the locality name and a white-and-black one with a stylised urban silhouette, both in a Polish typeface.

PL.title: Chevrons
PL.description: Polish chevrons are white boards with red arrows.

PL.title: Polish Language
PL.description: A West Slavic language with unique diacritics like Ł, Ą, Ę, Ż, and Ń, and W replacing V.

PL.title: Flat Green Landscape
PL.description: Poland features flat terrain with gentle hills, extensive agriculture, and moderate forest cover.

PL.title: Tree-Lined Roads
PL.description: Rows of mature trees flanking both sides of roads are common across Poland.

PL.title: Tiled Sidewalks
PL.description: Polish pavements commonly use neatly laid grey or light red paving tiles in various patterns.

PL.title: Architecture
PL.description: Central European style with plain stone walls, pastel stucco, and orange, red, black, or brown roof tiles; detached homes and communist-era blocks.

PL.title: Roadside Christian Shrines
PL.description: Small roadside shrines and blue-white or yellow-white Catholic flags are frequent.

PL.title: Regional Road Numbering
PL.description: Three-digit regional road numbers cluster geographically; the first digit indicates the region, often shown in yellow boxes.

PL.title: Telephone Area Codes
PL.description: Polish landline numbers have 9 digits; the first two form an area code mapping logically across the country.

PL.title: Place Name Suffixes
PL.description: Suffixes like -owo, -ów, -ino/-yno, and -ew help identify regions within Poland.

PL.title: Kashubian-Polish Bilingual Signs
PL.description: Signs show Polish above and Kashubian below, with Kashubian featuring distinctive diacritics and letters.

PL.title: German-Polish Bilingual Signs
PL.description: Place-name signs show Polish above and German below, with German including umlauts and ß.

PL.title: Belarusian-Polish Bilingual Signs (Eastern Podlaskie)
PL.description: Signs show Polish above and Belarusian in Cyrillic below near the Belarusian border.

PL.title: Belarusian-Polish Bilingual Signs (Lublin)
PL.description: Signs show Polish above and Belarusian in Cyrillic below in eastern Lublin villages.

PL.title: Belarusian-Polish Bilingual Signs (Masovian)
PL.description: Signs show Polish above and Belarusian in Cyrillic below in eastern Masovian villages.

PL.title: Lithuanian-Polish Bilingual Signs (Warmian-Masurian)
PL.description: Signs show Polish above and Lithuanian below, with Lithuanian-specific letters, near the Lithuanian border.

PL.title: Lemko-Polish Bilingual Signs (Lesser Poland)
PL.description: Signs show Polish above and Lemko in Cyrillic below in southeastern Lesser Poland.

PL.title: Lemko-Polish Bilingual Signs (Subcarpathian)
PL.description: Signs show Polish above and Lemko in Cyrillic below in southeastern Subcarpathian villages.

PL.title: Southern Hills and Mountains
PL.description: The southern border region has hilly terrain and some mountains.

PL.title: Wooden Houses, Podlaskie
PL.description: Traditional wooden houses are concentrated in eastern Podlaskie Voivodeship.

PL.title: Tatra Mountains, Zakopane
PL.description: Poland's highest peaks near Zakopane on the Slovak border.

PL.title: Country Flag
PL.description: The national flag of Poland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PL.title: .pl Domain
PL.description: Web addresses in Poland end in the country domain .pl (often as .com.pl). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

ZA.title: South African chevrons
ZA.description: South Africa uses red and white chevron signs, and small, thin chevrons with a single arrow are common across Southern African countries.

ZA.title: Afrikaans
ZA.description: South Africa has eleven official languages. While English dominates signage, the Dutch-like language Afrikaans has had a big influence on for example city names.

ZA.title: Green directional signs
ZA.description: South African directional signs are green with yellow road numbers. Road-numbers starting with N or R are exclusive to South Africa.

ZA.title: High security
ZA.description: In South Africa, suburban homes in and around major cities are commonly enclosed behind tall walls, fences, and gates.

ZA.title: Yellow Edge Lines
ZA.description: Most South African roads feature single yellow edge lines paired with white centre lines.

ZA.title: Triple Centre Lines
ZA.description: South Africa has a pattern of three white centre lines: two solid outer lines bracketing a dashed inner one.

ZA.title: Bird Poles
ZA.description: South African poles often have 1–5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators resembling rows of perching birds.

ZA.title: Triangular Warning Signs
ZA.description: South African warning signs are red-bordered triangles on a white background.

ZA.title: Provincial Licence Plates
ZA.description: Each South African province has its own plate design; Free State plates have a greenish tint, KwaZulu-Natal plates lean bluish.

ZA.title: National Highway Map
ZA.description: South African N-roads appear with the letter N on signs and as blue pentagons with numbers on Google Maps.

ZA.title: R-Road Number Regions
ZA.description: Three-digit R-roads in South Africa are roughly grouped geographically.

ZA.title: Telephone Area Codes
ZA.description: South African landline numbers are 10 digits; the first three digits form the area code starting with 0.

ZA.title: A-Shaped Pole Tops
ZA.description: Poles with three bars forming an "A" shape appear almost exclusively in Western Cape.

ZA.title: Wide A-Shaped Pole Tops
ZA.description: A wider version of A-shaped poles with bottom insulators attached directly to the A-frame appears in Eastern Cape.

ZA.title: Trident Pole Tops
ZA.description: Three-pronged trident pole tops are nearly unique to KwaZulu-Natal.

ZA.title: Alternating Horizontal Insulators
ZA.description: Three alternating insulators projecting horizontally from the pole top are concentrated in Limpopo, Gauteng, North West, and Mpumalanga.

ZA.title: Chevron Pole Tops
ZA.description: Two diagonal bars forming a "<" shape are found mostly in Limpopo and North West.

ZA.title: Metal-Arm Pole Tops
ZA.description: One or two metal arms holding insulators are most common in Mpumalanga.

ZA.title: Red Sign-Back Stickers
ZA.description: Square red stickers on the rear of road signs appear frequently in Eastern Cape and nearby parts of Northern Cape and Free State.

ZA.title: White Chevron-Back Stickers
ZA.description: White stickers on the rear of chevron signs are common in the Cape provinces.

ZA.title: Grainy Pink Pavement
ZA.description: A coarse, slightly pinkish road surface reminiscent of Texas pavement.

ZA.title: Bird Nests on Poles
ZA.description: Large communal bird nests atop utility poles are frequent in northern Northern Cape.

ZA.title: Dry Northeast Landscape
ZA.description: Arid terrain with orange-red soil and shrub-covered hills or mountains characterises the northeast.

ZA.title: Rocky Mountains
ZA.description: Treeless rocky mountains with tall, steep sides and sharp peaks are distinctive to Western Cape.

ZA.title: Vineyards
ZA.description: Vineyards concentrate in coastal valleys of Western Cape, with clusters near Upington in Northern Cape.

ZA.title: Red Soil Desert
ZA.description: Dry expanses of red soil typify the Northern Cape interior.

ZA.title: Sugarcane
ZA.description: Sugarcane fields line much of the KwaZulu-Natal coast and patches along the Mpumalanga–Mozambique border.

ZA.title: Cook Pine Trees
ZA.description: Distinctively tall Cook pines grow mainly between East London and Durban along the southeastern coast.

ZA.title: Pine Plantations
ZA.description: Commercial pine plantations are concentrated west of Eswatini and in parts of southern KwaZulu-Natal.

ZA.title: Grassy Rolling Hills
ZA.description: Green rolling grassland stretches between Cape Town and George, usually with tall ridges visible to the north or east.

ZA.title: Flat Subtropical Coast
ZA.description: Noticeably flat terrain with lush green subtropical vegetation near the Mozambique border.

ZA.title: Metropolitan M-Routes
ZA.description: In South Africa, major urban roads are designated with the letter M.

ZA.title: Informal Pole Adverts
ZA.description: Poles and public infrastructure around Gauteng are often plastered with informal advertisements.

ZA.title: Country Flag
ZA.description: The national flag of South Africa is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

ZA.title: .za Domain
ZA.description: Web addresses in South Africa end in the country domain .za (usually as .co.za). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

DE.title: Green sticker
DE.description: In Germany, most cars have a green circular sticker on the bottom right of the windshield.

DE.title: German bollard
DE.description: German bollards are black-and-white posts fitted with white or pale grey reflectors, switching to orange at intersections.

DE.title: Yellow mailboxes
DE.description: German mailboxes are yellow and carry the black 'Deutsche Post' horn logo.

DE.title: One-way streets
DE.description: One-way street signs carrying the full word 'Einbahnstraße' are exclusive to Germany.

DE.title: Wind turbines
DE.description: Wind turbines are encountered across Germany with considerably greater frequency than in any other European nation.

DE.title: German Language
DE.description: Signs are in German, identifiable by Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß characters.

DE.title: White Sticker on Wooden Poles
DE.description: Nearly every wooden utility pole has a small rectangular white sticker on its shaft.

DE.title: Diverse Pole Tops
DE.description: Common German pole tops include horizontal crossarms with staggered insulators, inverted-triangle supports, and T-shaped arrangements.

DE.title: Dark Sign Backs
DE.description: Road sign backs are often black or dark grey, with a small inverted red triangle sticker on most signs.

DE.title: Yellow 'H' Bus Stops
DE.description: Bus stops feature a yellow-and-green 'H' symbol.

DE.title: High Bollard Density
DE.description: Bollards appear roughly every 50 metres along nearly every road.

DE.title: Yellow Town Entry Signs
DE.description: Town boundaries are marked by yellow signs with black text framed in metal, showing town, municipality, and county.

DE.title: Blue Kilometre Markers
DE.description: Distance markers are blue rectangles with rounded corners and a thin white border.

DE.title: Five-Stripe Pedestrian Signs
DE.description: The German pedestrian crossing sign shows a figure walking across five stripes.

DE.title: No-Stopping Arrow Signs
DE.description: No Stopping and No Waiting signs often include white directional arrows on the sign face.

DE.title: Phone Area Codes
DE.description: A map of German telephone area codes, useful for narrowing down regions.

DE.title: Postal Code Map
DE.description: An overview of German postal code zones, helpful for region guessing when visible on signs or buildings.

DE.title: Baden-Württemberg Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of black and gold (yellow).

DE.title: Bavaria Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of white and blue.

DE.title: Berlin Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of red, white, and red with the Berlin bear.

DE.title: Brandenburg Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of red and white with the red eagle.

DE.title: Bremen Flag
DE.description: Eight horizontal red and white stripes with a chequered pattern.

DE.title: Hamburg Flag
DE.description: A red flag with a white castle

DE.title: Hesse Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of red and white.

DE.title: Lower Saxony Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of black, red, and gold with a white horse.

DE.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of blue, white, and red with a with a yellow line in the middle. A version includes the region's coat of arms (a bull's head and a red griffin).

DE.title: North Rhine-Westphalia Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of green, white, and red.

DE.title: Rhineland-Palatinate Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of black, red, and gold with the coat of arms.

DE.title: Saarland Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of black, red, and gold with the Saarland coat of arms.

DE.title: Saxony Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of white and green.

DE.title: Saxony-Anhalt Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of yellow and black with the coat of arms.

DE.title: Schleswig-Holstein Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of blue, white, and red.

DE.title: Thuringia Flag
DE.description: Horizontal stripes of white and red.

DE.title: State Coats of Arms
DE.description: Each federal state has its own heraldic coat of arms, seen on official buildings or signs.

DE.title: Town Name Suffixes
DE.description: Certain place-name endings are concentrated in specific parts of Germany, aiding region guessing.

DE.title: Bavarian Cycling Route Signs
DE.description: Bavarian cycle route signs have a white background with a bold red border and text, often with a red bicycle symbol and directional arrows.

DE.title: North Rhine-Westphalia Cycling Route Signs
DE.description: Cycle route signs have a white background with a red border and text, including a red bicycle symbol and directional arrows.

DE.title: Saxony Cycling Route Signs
DE.description: Saxony's cycling signs have a white background with a thin green border and green text, sometimes with a green bicycle symbol.

DE.title: Lower Saxony Cycling Route Signs
DE.description: Lower Saxony cycle route signs are white with a green border and text, featuring a green bicycle symbol and directional arrows.

DE.title: Schleswig-Holstein Cycling Route Signs
DE.description: Cycle route signs have a white background, green border, green text, and a green bicycle symbol.

DE.title: Brandenburg Cycling Route Signs
DE.description: Cycle route signs have a white background, red border, red text, and a red bicycle symbol.

DE.title: Bavaria Folded Street Sign Backs
DE.description: Street sign backs are folded with ribbed edges, giving a reinforced, corrugated look.

DE.title: North Rhine-Westphalia Flat Street Sign Backs
DE.description: Street sign backs are completely flat and smooth metal.

DE.title: Saxony Folded Street Sign Backs
DE.description: Street sign backs are folded or ribbed with bent or reinforced edges.

DE.title: Lower Saxony Flat Street Sign Backs
DE.description: Street sign backs are flat, smooth metal with no ribbing or folding.

DE.title: Schleswig-Holstein Flat Street Sign Backs
DE.description: Street sign backs are flat and smooth without ribbed or folded reinforcement.

DE.title: Brandenburg Folded Street Sign Backs
DE.description: Street sign backs are folded or ribbed with visibly bent or reinforced edges.

DE.title: Bavaria Single Bar Sign Connector
DE.description: Road signs attach to posts with a single, slim vertical metal bar down the center.

DE.title: North Rhine-Westphalia Double Bar Sign Connector
DE.description: Road signs attach with two parallel vertical metal bars for a wider, robust look.

DE.title: Saxony T-Shaped Sign Connector
DE.description: Road signs feature a T-shaped metal bracket with a horizontal bar atop a vertical bar.

DE.title: Lower Saxony Double Bar Sign Connector
DE.description: Road signs attach with two vertical metal bars, sometimes with narrower spacing.

DE.title: Schleswig-Holstein Single Bar Sign Connector
DE.description: Road signs mount with a single, central vertical metal bar.

DE.title: Brandenburg T-Shaped Sign Connector
DE.description: Road signs use a T-shaped metal bracket with horizontal and vertical bars for mounting.

DE.title: German Alps
DE.description: The most mountainous terrain lies along the southern border with Austria.

DE.title: Baltic Pines
DE.description: Scots pines with orange-toned bark concentrate in the northeastern states.

DE.title: White-Painted Tree Trunks
DE.description: Roadside trees have lower trunks painted white, mainly in the northeast.

DE.title: Vineyard Regions
DE.description: Most vineyards cluster in the southwest, with some pockets further east.

DE.title: Northwestern Brick Houses
DE.description: Exposed red or brown brick houses concentrate in the northwest.

DE.title: Thatched Roofs and Rock Walls
DE.description: Straw-thatched roofs and dry-stone walls are common in North Frisian Islands and Schleswig-Holstein.

DE.title: Black Slate Fish-Scale Walls
DE.description: Building façades clad in overlapping black slate tiles resembling fish scales are widespread in central Germany.

DE.title: East German Housing Blocks
DE.description: Large prefabricated apartment slabs from the socialist period mark former East German states.

DE.title: Dark Reflector Bollards
DE.description: Bollards with noticeably darker reflectors appear in certain regions.

DE.title: NRW Green-Cap Bollards
DE.description: Some bollards have coloured plastic caps, mostly green, in North Rhine-Westphalia.

DE.title: LVR-Branded Green Caps
DE.description: Green bollard caps stamped with 'LVR' and a coat of arms appear in southern North Rhine-Westphalia.

DE.title: Bavarian Wooden Bollards
DE.description: Cylindrical timber bollards with painted tips are a Bavarian speciality.

DE.title: Orange Road Posts
DE.description: Plain orange marker posts are common in Bavaria and some other states.

DE.title: Green Tree Markers
DE.description: Miniature green tags nailed to roadside trees are typical of Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

DE.title: Bavaria Three-Section Road Markers
DE.description: White rectangular plaques divided into three panels, with the left panel showing the current road, are specific to Bavaria.

DE.title: Lower Saxony Rectangular Markers
DE.description: Unadorned rectangular road markers with softly rounded corners appear in Lower Saxony.

DE.title: Metallic-Border Road Markers
DE.description: Road markers surrounded by a thin metal frame occur in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony.

DE.title: Rhineland-Palatinate Rough Stone Triangular Posts
DE.description: Triangular rough, unpainted stone posts topped with a white plate.

DE.title: Saxony Rough Stone Triangular Posts
DE.description: Triangular rough, unpainted stone posts with a white plate attached.

DE.title: Saarland White-Painted Triangular Posts
DE.description: Triangular marker posts fully painted white, sometimes with a white plate.

DE.title: Thuringia White-Painted Triangular Posts
DE.description: Triangular roadside posts painted entirely white, sometimes with a white plate.

DE.title: Baden-Württemberg Short White or Grey Triangular Posts
DE.description: Short triangular posts usually white, sometimes grey, sometimes with a white plate.

DE.title: North Rhine-Westphalia White Triangular Posts Without Plates
DE.description: Triangular roadside posts painted fully white without any plates.

DE.title: White Bollard Plates
DE.description: Simple white information plates mounted on bollards in certain states.

DE.title: Black Disk Bollard Bases
DE.description: Bollards atop round black base disks typical of former East German states.

DE.title: Rhineland-Palatinate Orange Plates
DE.description: Information plates on bollards are orange instead of white in Rhineland-Palatinate.

DE.title: Baden-Württemberg Grey Plates
DE.description: Bollard information plates may be grey instead of white in Baden-Württemberg.

DE.title: Red-Capped White Posts
DE.description: Slim white posts topped with a red cap, common in former East Germany, especially Saxony-Anhalt.

DE.title: Fully Yellow Posts
DE.description: Solid yellow marker posts specific to Brandenburg.

DE.title: Yellow Posts with White Plates
DE.description: Yellow posts with attached white information plates indicate Saxony-Anhalt.

DE.title: East German Round Concrete Poles
DE.description: Cylindrical concrete utility poles mainly found in former East Germany.

DE.title: Trident Pole Tops
DE.description: Three-pronged pole-top assemblies in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-Württemberg.

DE.title: Triangle Pole Tops
DE.description: Inverted-triangle pole-top braces concentrated in western Germany.

DE.title: Thick Centre-Bar Pole Tops
DE.description: Pole tops with a bulging horizontal crossarm midpoint in former East German states.

DE.title: Curved Bar Pole Tops
DE.description: Pole-top crossarms that arc gently, a Bavaria-specific feature.

DE.title: Aldi Nord vs Aldi Süd
DE.description: Germany is split between Aldi Süd in the south and Aldi Nord in the north, each with distinct branding.

DE.title: Sorbian Language Signs
DE.description: Bilingual signs featuring Sorbian appear near the Polish and Czech borders.

DE.title: Saxony Half-Timbered Arch Houses
DE.description: Half-timbered houses with arched ground-floor openings concentrated in Saxony.

DE.title: Country Flag
DE.description: The national flag of Germany is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

DE.title: .de Domain
DE.description: Web addresses in Germany end in the country domain .de. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

UG.title: White car
UG.description: Street View in Kampala has a white Google car with rectangular side mirrors.

UG.title: Go capital
UG.description: Almost all Ugandan coverage is in or near the capital Kampala.

UG.title: Yellow rear plates
UG.description: Ugandan vehicles have white front plates and yellow rear plates.

UG.title: Red soil
UG.description: Soil in Uganda is distinctly red, even paved roads have a redlike tint.

UG.title: Palm Trees in the North
UG.description: Palm trees in Ugandan coverage indicate the northern section of Murchison Falls.

UG.title: Water-Filled Craters
UG.description: Large water-filled craters appear in the northern coverage of the park.

UG.title: Country Flag
UG.description: The national flag of Uganda is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

UG.title: .ug Domain
UG.description: Web addresses in Uganda end in the country domain .ug (often as .co.ug). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

BO.title: Curvy poles
BO.description: In eastern Bolivia, many wooden utility poles are noticeably curvy.

BO.title: Short white plates
BO.description: Bolivia uses short plates. They will look white or slightly blue.

BO.title: Red bricks
BO.description: Buildings featuring big exposed red bricks is a common sight in Bolivia.

BO.title: Traditional clothes
BO.description: Bowler hats and large skirts are outfits commonly seen in Bolivia.

BO.title: Road Line Colours
BO.description: Centre road markings vary between solid yellow, mixed yellow and white, or solid white; edge lines are always white.

BO.title: Concrete Slab Roads
BO.description: Many Bolivian roads are surfaced with precast concrete slabs besides asphalt.

BO.title: Cobblestone Roads
BO.description: Cobblestoned streets often have orderly stone strips separating less regular sections.

BO.title: Signposts
BO.description: Road sign poles are thick, white, and square in cross-section.

BO.title: Guardrail Markings
BO.description: Guardrail end-plates have yellow and black diagonal stripes, with yellow on the outer edge.

BO.title: Utility Poles
BO.description: Main poles are cylindrical concrete with pinholes or timber, with varied crossarm designs.

BO.title: Kilometre Markers
BO.description: Distance posts have a black 'Km' upper section and white lower section with the distance figure.

BO.title: MAS Political Graffiti
BO.description: Graffiti reading 'MAS' or 'Evo' and objects painted black, white, and blue mark the ruling party.

BO.title: Wiphala Flag
BO.description: The Wiphala is a square flag with seven colours in diagonal stripes, seen on public buildings and signage.

BO.title: Tigo Telecom Branding
BO.description: Tigo's blue logo appears frequently in Bolivian urban areas.

BO.title: Reddish Soil
BO.description: Exposed rock and earth often have a pronounced red-orange hue.

BO.title: Altiplano
BO.description: A highland plateau with grasslands ranging from green to brown, often with clumpy tufted grass.

BO.title: Northern Altiplano
BO.description: The plateau near La Paz and El Alto appears greener and more vegetated.

BO.title: Southern Altiplano
BO.description: Around Oruro and southwest roads, the plateau is more barren and dry.

BO.title: Andean Mountains
BO.description: Towering peaks run northwest to southeast between the Altiplano and tropical lowlands.

BO.title: Tropical Eastern Lowlands
BO.description: East of the Andes, terrain flattens into lush tropical farmland with distinctive pinkish soil.

BO.title: Santa Cruz Unpaved Roads
BO.description: Dirt roads near Santa Cruz have characteristic pink soil.

BO.title: Santa Cruz Tropical Setting
BO.description: Santa Cruz is Bolivia's only major city in a flat, tropical environment.

BO.title: Morochata
BO.description: A coverage pocket on Ruta 25 northwest of Cochabamba with green mountain slopes and drier terrain.

BO.title: Ruta 5 Sunset Coverage
BO.description: Ruta 5 near Chaco was captured at sunset, showing a warm golden tint on mostly concrete roads.

BO.title: Ruta 6 White Concrete
BO.description: Between Tarabuco and Zudáñez, the road is paved with almost white concrete.

BO.title: Country Flag
BO.description: The national flag of Bolivia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BO.title: .bo Domain
BO.description: Web addresses in Bolivia end in the country domain .bo (often as .com.bo). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

DK.title: White lines
DK.description: All road markings in Denmark are white. Double center lines appear frequently on Danish roads.

DK.title: Danish bollard
DK.description: The standard Danish bollard is white with a yellow reflector and a prominent dark orange band, a combination exclusive to Denmark.

DK.title: Street names
DK.description: The suffix 'vej', Danish for 'road', appears at the end of most street names.

DK.title: Framed direction signs
DK.description: Danish wayfinding signs are mounted low to the ground inside a distinctive tubular metal frame. They appear in red or blue.

DK.title: Flat landscape
DK.description: The terrain across Denmark is predominantly flat.

DK.title: General
DK.description: Red brick houses are very common in Denmark. Roofs often have orange, black or brown tiles.

DK.title: Licence Plates
DK.description: Danish plates: standard white with blue EU band, yellow for commercial vehicles, and unique 'Parrot' variant with yellow left section.

DK.title: Square-Block Edge Lines
DK.description: Danish road edges often marked by small white squares instead of dashes.

DK.title: Danish Language
DK.description: Danish is a North Germanic language with letters Æ, Ø, and Å.

DK.title: Thatched and Corrugated Roofs
DK.description: Thatched roofs are common in the countryside. Grey corrugated metal roofing also appears.

DK.title: Timber-Framed Buildings
DK.description: Half-timbered walls with exposed wooden frames are found on older and rural structures throughout Denmark.

DK.title: Bent-Pipe Signposts
DK.description: A signpost design where the tubular metal frame wraps tightly around the sign panel is unique to Denmark.

DK.title: Guardrails
DK.description: Danish road barriers use guardrails with no reflectors.

DK.title: Five-Stripe Pedestrian Signs
DK.description: The pedestrian crossing warning sign in Denmark shows five horizontal stripes, with the outermost stripes touching the edges of the triangular border.

DK.title: Town Entry and Exit Signs
DK.description: Settlements are announced by a distinctive rectangular sign displaying the town name. The exit version adds a diagonal red slash.

DK.title: Bus Stop Signs
DK.description: Danish bus stops use a compact black-and-yellow sign mounted at the top of a pole, with the timetable below.

DK.title: Red-and-White Chevrons
DK.description: Curve warning boards in Denmark are red and white and tend to be positioned close to the ground.

DK.title: Rare Street-Level Utility Poles
DK.description: Conventional roadside utility poles are uncommon in Denmark. Most visible power infrastructure consists of tall high-voltage transmission towers.

DK.title: Roadside Bicycle Paths
DK.description: Dedicated cycle lanes running alongside the carriageway are a frequent feature of Danish roads.

DK.title: PostNord Postal Boxes
DK.description: PostNord operates distinctive postal collection boxes that are easily recognisable on the street.

DK.title: Gas Station Brands
DK.description: Four fuel-station chains common in Denmark are Ingo, Ok, Uno-X, and Yx.

DK.title: Stone Bicycle-Path Bollards
DK.description: Low stone bollards occasionally line bicycle paths, sometimes with a red-painted cap.

DK.title: Road Numbering System
DK.description: Danish road numbers follow a clear east-to-west pattern with regional groupings. Starting with 200 and ending with 500.

DK.title: Ring Roads
DK.description: Major cities have numbered ring roads labelled O1 to O4, with higher numbers encircling further from the centre.

DK.title: Movia Buses (Capital Region)
DK.description: Buses in the Capital Region are typically solid yellow or yellow with white and grey accents, featuring the Movia logo.

DK.title: Midttrafik Buses (Central Denmark)
DK.description: Central Denmark Region buses are bright red with the white Midttrafik logo.

DK.title: NT Buses (North Denmark)
DK.description: Buses in North Denmark Region are bright blue, featuring the NT logo.

DK.title: Movia Buses (Region Zealand)
DK.description: Region Zealand buses use Movia branding, usually yellow with white and grey details.

DK.title: FynBus and Sydtrafik Buses (Southern Denmark)
DK.description: Southern Denmark buses are bright green (FynBus) or orange (Sydtrafik), each with their logos.

DK.title: BAT Buses (Bornholm)
DK.description: Bornholm's buses have a distinctive blue and green two-tone scheme with the BAT logo.

DK.title: Capital Region Yellow Bus Stop Sign
DK.description: Bus stop signs have a bright yellow background with a black or dark gray band at the top, often showing the Movia logo.

DK.title: Midtjylland Bus Stop Sign
DK.description: Central Denmark bus stop signs use yellow with a white or light gray section and the Midttrafik logo.

DK.title: Nordjylland Bus Stop Sign
DK.description: North Denmark bus stop signs are yellow with a black or dark gray section and the NT logo.

DK.title: Region Zealand Bus Stop Sign
DK.description: Region Zealand bus stop signs have a yellow background with a white or light gray section and the Movia logo.

DK.title: Sydtrafik Bus Stop Sign (Southern Denmark)
DK.description: Southern Denmark bus stop signs are yellow with a gray or white section and the Sydtrafik logo.

DK.title: Bornholm Bus Stop Sign
DK.description: Bornholm bus stop signs are yellow with a black or dark section and the BAT logo.

DK.title: Country Flag
DK.description: The national flag of Denmark is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

DK.title: .dk Domain
DK.description: Web addresses in Denmark end in the country domain .dk. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

GR.title: Double white lines
GR.description: You will often see worn double white center lines in Greece.

GR.title: Greek plates
GR.description: Greek license plates are either fully white or follow the standard EU layout with a blue strip on the left side.

GR.title: Wooden poles
GR.description: Most Greek utility poles are made of timber, often seen in a dark brown tone.

GR.title: Greek bollard
GR.description: Bollards in Greece are white and have a red, square reflector on the front, and a white on the back.

GR.title: Directional signs
GR.description: Arrow-shaped blue signs carry place names in two scripts: Greek lettering in yellow and a Latin transliteration in white underneath.

GR.title: Greek Alphabet
GR.description: Greek is written in its distinctive script with rounder, softer lowercase forms.

GR.title: Harp-Shaped Pole Tops
GR.description: Many Greek utility poles have a metal frame resembling a harp atop them.

GR.title: Five Vertical Insulators
GR.description: Five insulators arranged vertically, bolted to the pole or harp-shaped frames.

GR.title: Round-Shade Pole Lamps
GR.description: Compact lamps fixed to poles, capped by a circular shade over the bulb.

GR.title: Yellow Road Markings
GR.description: Yellow road lines appear frequently in Greece.

GR.title: Chevron Signs
GR.description: Curve warning boards display white arrows on a black field.

GR.title: Warning Signs
GR.description: Triangular hazard signs have a red border with a yellow interior.

GR.title: Town Entry Signs
GR.description: Settlement entrance boards are white with bold blue horizontal bands at top and bottom.

GR.title: Kilometre Markers
GR.description: Small blue roadside posts show 'km' in Greek and Latin alphabets with the distance.

GR.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
GR.description: Pedestrian figures walk across two horizontal dotted lines.

GR.title: Miniature Roadside Shrines
GR.description: Tiny church-like structures on pedestals appear frequently alongside roads.

GR.title: Mediterranean Architecture
GR.description: Stone buildings with white or pastel walls and orange tile roofs; islands feature white walls with blue doors and windows.

GR.title: Mountainous Terrain
GR.description: Greece is heavily mountainous with narrow, twisting highland roads.

GR.title: Red Soil
GR.description: Exposed red-tinted earth is widespread in the landscape.

GR.title: Winter and Autumn Coverage
GR.description: Imagery often shows dull, grey, overcast winter and autumn scenes.

GR.title: Island Coverage Map
GR.description: Numerous small islands with limited Street View; mainland and Crete have more coverage.

GR.title: Phone Area Codes
GR.description: Landline numbers start with 2, followed by region-indicating digits.

GR.title: Flat Agricultural Valleys
GR.description: Broad lowland plains around Thessaloniki and Larissa; smaller valleys scattered in north and central mainland.

GR.title: Western Mountains
GR.description: Highest peaks and most high-altitude roads are in the western mainland.

GR.title: Cycladic White-and-Blue Houses
GR.description: White-walled buildings with blue doors and shutters are found on central Cycladic islands.

GR.title: Barren Central Islands
GR.description: Smaller central islands have arid, treeless terrain with low scrub and bare rock.

GR.title: Olive Groves
GR.description: Olive cultivation is concentrated along the coast, especially Crete and southern Peloponnese.

GR.title: Citrus Orchards
GR.description: Citrus farming centers in coastal lowlands, mainly southern Peloponnese.

GR.title: Athens Taxis
GR.description: Taxis in Athens are yellow.

GR.title: Thessaloniki Taxis
GR.description: Thessaloniki taxis have blue bodies with white roofs.

GR.title: Country Flag
GR.description: The national flag of Greece is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

GR.title: .gr Domain
GR.description: Web addresses in Greece end in the country domain .gr (often as .com.gr). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

UY.title: White signposts
UY.description: You will often find thick and white wooden signposts in Uruguay.

UY.title: Triple road lines
UY.description: In Uruguay, you can find triple road markings, double yellow lines with a white dashed line running between them.

UY.title: Two faced bollards
UY.description: Bollards in Uruguay are fully white on the front, and fully yellow on the back,

UY.title: Trident poles
UY.description: A common variation of the many Uruguayan poles are the so-called trident poles with three insulators all pointing upwards.

UY.title: Typical Landscape and Weather
UY.description: Overcast skies over open grasslands with gentle hills and occasional tree plantations.

UY.title: Plain White Licence Plates
UY.description: Uruguayan licence plates are plain white with black text.

UY.title: Smudgy Camera Quality
UY.description: Much of Uruguay's coverage has a somewhat smudgy camera quality.

UY.title: Other Road Line Patterns
UY.description: Yellow-white lines and plain white lines also appear in Uruguay.

UY.title: Other Pole Designs
UY.description: Uruguay also features round poles with flat metal-sheet tops, square concrete poles, simple wooden poles with a single insulator, and occasionally Argentine-style poles.

UY.title: Guardrail Supports
UY.description: Uruguayan guardrails have small rectangular yellow or red reflectors and uniquely shaped supports.

UY.title: Green Stone Kilometre Markers
UY.description: Green-painted stone kilometre markers are unique to Uruguay.

UY.title: Yellow-and-Black Chevrons
UY.description: Uruguayan chevrons are yellow with black arrows.

UY.title: Gently Hilly Terrain
UY.description: Most of Uruguay has subtle, gentle hills despite low overall elevation. Roads almost always have at least a slight incline.

UY.title: Reddish Soil
UY.description: Reddish soil, from light pink to deep red, appears in many parts of Uruguay.

UY.title: Concrete Cube-Shaped Houses
UY.description: Many Uruguayan houses are concrete and cube-shaped, with drab, weathered walls and flat roofs.

UY.title: Short Stocky Palm Trees
UY.description: Short, stocky palm trees occasionally appear in Uruguay's countryside.

UY.title: Widespread Cattle
UY.description: Cattle outnumber people four to one, making livestock very common in rural Uruguay.

UY.title: Elevation Differences
UY.description: Uruguay's highest hills are near Minas east of Montevideo and north of Tacuarembo.

UY.title: Rocky Hills Near Minas
UY.description: The Minas area has some of Uruguay's tallest hills with exposed rock and heavy bushland.

UY.title: Dark-Soiled Northern Hills
UY.description: Northern hills have darker soil than Minas and typically lack exposed rock, with common vegetation and tree plantations.

UY.title: Tree Plantations in the North
UY.description: Commercial tree plantations are common, especially in northern and northwestern Uruguay.

UY.title: Country Flag
UY.description: The national flag of Uruguay is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

UY.title: .uy Domain
UY.description: Web addresses in Uruguay end in the country domain .uy (often as .com.uy). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

NZ.title: Red text
NZ.description: In New Zealand, Give Way signs feature red text and a small white outline.

NZ.title: New Zealand bollards
NZ.description: Bollards in New Zealand feature a red strip that wraps around the back, extending partially across the front.

NZ.title: Intersection triangles
NZ.description: Triangles can be found painted on the road at intersections in New Zealand.

NZ.title: Licence Plates
NZ.description: New Zealand plates are white with black lettering, appearing almost entirely white when blurred.

NZ.title: Concrete Utility Poles with Single Groove
NZ.description: NZ's main poles are concrete with a single long vertical groove and small silver possum guards.

NZ.title: White Sign Posts
NZ.description: NZ directional and warning signs are typically mounted on white posts; warning signs are yellow diamonds.

NZ.title: Blue Street Signs
NZ.description: New Zealand street signs are predominantly blue with white text, especially in rural areas.

NZ.title: Road Line Markings
NZ.description: NZ outer road lines are generally white; centre lines are single white dashes or solid double yellow lines.

NZ.title: Chevron Signs
NZ.description: NZ curve chevrons are black arrows on yellow with a thin black border.

NZ.title: Green Directional Signs
NZ.description: New Zealand highway direction signs are green with state highway numbers inside a red shield.

NZ.title: Bridge Markers with Red Crest
NZ.description: NZ bridge markers show highway numbers inside a red shield and a yellow marker with the river or bridge name.

NZ.title: Ferns in Forested Areas
NZ.description: Ferns are very common in New Zealand's wooded and forested areas.

NZ.title: State Highway Numbering System
NZ.description: New Zealand's two-digit state highway numbers run north to south sequentially.

NZ.title: Phone Number Area Codes
NZ.description: NZ phone numbers have seven digits preceded by a two-digit area code; numbers starting with 02 are mobile.

NZ.title: Fonterra Farm Sign Numbering
NZ.description: The leading digit on Fonterra dairy farm signs corresponds to a regional numbering pattern.

NZ.title: Waikato and Northland Landscape
NZ.description: These regions feature dry conditions and rolling hills; Northland is notably hilly.

NZ.title: West Coast Temperate Rainforests
NZ.description: The West Coast and parts of Tasman have lush temperate rainforests and rugged, densely green terrain.

NZ.title: Southland and Otago Landscape
NZ.description: Flatter parts of Southland and Otago have a cold climate with gently sloping alpine hills and sparse, stunted vegetation.

NZ.title: Southern Alps Mountain Range
NZ.description: A massive snow-covered mountain chain runs through most of the South Island with thinning vegetation further south.

NZ.title: Hawke's Bay Landscape
NZ.description: Dry, golden-grass-covered hills with sunny conditions and a white Street View car.

NZ.title: Bright Sandy Cliffs
NZ.description: Pale, sandy cliff faces common in central Manawatu-Whanganui and parts of Taranaki, Waikato, and Hawke's Bay.

NZ.title: Glacial Lakes near Queenstown
NZ.description: Numerous glacial lakes with striking teal, crystal-clear water around Queenstown in the Southern Alps region.

NZ.title: Gravel Roads in Northland
NZ.description: Unpaved gravel roads are frequent in the Northland region.

NZ.title: Tall Hedge and Tree Rows in Canterbury
NZ.description: Tall rows of hedges and trees are common across the flat Canterbury Plains with mountains visible to the west.

NZ.title: Very Tall Hedges in Bay of Plenty
NZ.description: Exceptionally tall hedges are characteristic around Tauranga in the Bay of Plenty.

NZ.title: Vineyards
NZ.description: Grape vineyards are prevalent in Marlborough and Hawke's Bay.

NZ.title: Corn Fields
NZ.description: Corn cultivation is found almost exclusively on the North Island.

NZ.title: New Zealand Flax in Neat Rows
NZ.description: NZ flax planted in orderly, straight rows indicates the Southland region.

NZ.title: Olive-Brown Square Possum Guards
NZ.description: Most utility poles in Marlborough have long, square-shaped olive-brown possum guards alongside shorter silver ones.

NZ.title: Long Cylindrical Silver Possum Guards
NZ.description: Many utility poles in Southland have tall, cylindrical silver possum guards.

NZ.title: Holey Poles
NZ.description: Concrete poles with a pattern of holes are common in Southland and Auckland.

NZ.title: Square Concrete Poles without Groove
NZ.description: Square-profile concrete poles lacking vertical grooves are most common in Southland.

NZ.title: Off-Centre Crossbars on Poles
NZ.description: Utility poles with uneven, asymmetrical crossbars appear in Otago, Marlborough, Wellington, and Taranaki.

NZ.title: Tall Metal Bar Insulator Extension
NZ.description: Poles with centre insulators atop tall vertical metal bars are frequent near the Auckland-Waikato border and elsewhere in Waikato.

NZ.title: White-Painted Crossbars
NZ.description: Some concrete poles in eastern Waikato and Whanganui have white paint on the middle section of wooden crossbars.

NZ.title: Yellow Cow-Tag on Poles
NZ.description: Most poles in Gisborne have a small yellow tag resembling a cattle ear tag.

NZ.title: Yellow Danger Triangle Warning Sticker
NZ.description: Pole stickers with a yellow hazard triangle flanked by white rectangles appear in Hawke's Bay, Taupo-Rotorua corridor, northern Waikato, and south of Auckland.
