NZ.title: Medium Black Vertical Sticker (5 Digits)
NZ.description: Medium black vertical stickers with five digits appear on poles in West Coast, Tasman, southern Canterbury, and southern Northland.

NZ.title: Long Black Vertical Sticker (6 Digits with Square)
NZ.description: Tall black vertical stickers with six digits and a small black square appear across much of the North Island and in Southland and Otago.

NZ.title: Small Black Horizontal Pole Sticker
NZ.description: Compact black horizontal stickers with multiple numbers are common in Taranaki and Wellington.

NZ.title: Small White Horizontal Pole Sticker
NZ.description: Small white horizontal stickers with several numbers appear in various North Island locations.

NZ.title: Solid White Edge Lines without Centre Lines
NZ.description: Roads with solid white edge markings but no centre line are most common in Gisborne.

NZ.title: Green Stripe Bollards
NZ.description: NZ bollards with a green stripe instead of red are common in southern Canterbury and eastern Southland.

NZ.title: Black Stripe Bollards
NZ.description: Bollards with a black stripe replacing red are frequent in Wellington.

NZ.title: Tightly Spaced Wooden Fence Posts
NZ.description: Wooden fences with closely packed posts are prevalent on the North Island, northern South Island, and around Akaroa.

NZ.title: Widely Spaced Wooden Fence Posts
NZ.description: Wooden fences with large gaps between posts are common on the South Island and in Taranaki.

NZ.title: Thin Metal Fence Posts
NZ.description: Fences with slender metal posts are found almost exclusively on the South Island.

NZ.title: Short Wooden Fence Post Extensions
NZ.description: Small pieces of wood attached to the top of fence posts slightly extend their height, often seen in Hawke's Bay and occasionally in Manawatu-Whanganui and Gisborne.

NZ.title: Long Wooden Fence Post Extensions
NZ.description: Longer wooden extensions on fence posts, taller than the short variant, are primarily found in Southland and Hawke's Bay, with occasional sightings in Otago.

NZ.title: Fruit Farms with Green Netting
NZ.description: Orchards draped in green protective netting are especially common around Tauranga and occasionally near Gisborne.

NZ.title: Country Flag
NZ.description: The national flag of New Zealand is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

NZ.title: .nz Domain
NZ.description: Web addresses in New Zealand end in the country domain .nz (usually as .co.nz). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

AT.title: Vienna street signs
AT.description: In Vienna, street signs appear as dark blue plaques, with the first number indicating the district.

AT.title: Red and white tape
AT.description: In Vienna and some smaller Austrian cities, signposts have red and white tape, resembling the Austrian flag.

AT.title: One way street
AT.description: Signs for one way streets in Austria say 'EINBAHN'.

AT.title: Black top bollards
AT.description: Austrian roadside bollards are white with a black cap, often with a small rounded knob at the very top.

AT.title: Licence Plates
AT.description: Austrian licence plates are elongated and white, featuring the blue EU band on the left edge.

AT.title: Chevrons
AT.description: Austrian curve signs have white arrows on red or red arrows on yellow boards.

AT.title: Wooden Poles
AT.description: The predominant utility pole across Austria is a rounded timber design.

AT.title: Landscape
AT.description: Most of Austria is forested mountain terrain, with eastern regions flattening into agricultural lowlands.

AT.title: Alpine Architecture
AT.description: Traditional Alpine homes have pale walls, wooden balconies, and wide overhanging dark timber roofs.

AT.title: German Language
AT.description: Austria's official language is German, recognizable by characters Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß.

AT.title: Direction Signs
AT.description: Austrian directional signs have a white face framed by a blue border with a distinctive typeface.

AT.title: Town Entrance Signs
AT.description: Town name signs are white with a blue frame and the same characteristic font.

AT.title: Green Facility Signs
AT.description: Green directional signs point to nearby amenities and local facilities.

AT.title: Pedestrian Signs
AT.description: Austrian pedestrian crossing signs show two horizontal dashed lines instead of zebra stripes.

AT.title: Four Metal Clip Mounts
AT.description: Some road signs are attached to posts using four metal clips, unique in Central Europe.

AT.title: Blue Road Markers
AT.description: Austrian kilometre posts are blue with white numerals showing one decimal place separated by a comma.

AT.title: Bus Stop Signs
AT.description: Bus stops are marked with a circular sign combining yellow and green rings around the letter H.

AT.title: Anfang/Ende Signs
AT.description: Parking restriction signs often include 'Anfang' (start) or 'Ende' (end) to mark zone boundaries.

AT.title: Dead-End Signs
AT.description: Dead-end streets are marked with an inverted white T sign.

AT.title: Yellow Gas Poles
AT.description: Bright yellow poles mark underground gas lines along Austrian roads.

AT.title: Mountainous south
AT.description: The centre and west are mountainous, while the east and north are flatter, with rolling hills.

AT.title: B-Roads Map
AT.description: B-roads have white text on blue rectangles, with higher numbers in the west.

AT.title: Burgenland State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal stripes of red and gold (yellow).

AT.title: Carinthia State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal stripes of yellow, red, and white.

AT.title: Lower Austria State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal stripes of blue and yellow.

AT.title: Salzburg State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal stripes of red and white.

AT.title: Styria State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal stripes of white and green.

AT.title: Tyrol State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal stripes of white and red.

AT.title: Upper Austria State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal stripes of white and red (narrower than Tyrol's).

AT.title: Vienna State Flag
AT.description: The Vienna coat of arms, featuring a white cross on a red shield, can be seen on flags and buildings throughout the city.

AT.title: Vorarlberg State Flag
AT.description: Horizontal red and white stripes with the state coat of arms.

AT.title: Vorarlberg Neon-Yellow Bus Stops
AT.description: Bus stops marked by neon-yellow poles.

AT.title: Vorarlberg Pole Stripes
AT.description: Poles wrapped with alternating yellow and white stripes.

AT.title: Vorarlberg White Km Markers
AT.description: White kilometre markers appear in Vorarlberg and western Salzburg.

AT.title: Salzburg Road Squares
AT.description: Large white squares painted on the road near kilometre markers.

AT.title: Burgenland Güterweg Signs
AT.description: Rural roads signed with green 'Güterweg' plates.

AT.title: Upper Austria Güterweg Signs
AT.description: 'Güterweg' signs are white with a black border.

AT.title: Lower Austria Sign Borders
AT.description: Signs sometimes have yellow and blue borders matching the state flag.

AT.title: Eastern Vineyards
AT.description: Wine-growing areas are in eastern Austria around Vienna and Lake Neusiedl.

AT.title: Highest Alps
AT.description: Austria's highest Alpine peaks cluster near the Italian border in the west.

AT.title: City-Specific Street Signs
AT.description: Vienna shows district numbers; Salzburg, Klagenfurt, and St. Pölten have unique street sign styles.

AT.title: Country Flag
AT.description: The national flag of Austria is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

AT.title: Carinthia Kärnten Bus Logo
AT.description: Carinthian buses feature the 'kärnten bus' logo in blue and yellow with stylized text.

AT.title: Burgenland Südburg Bus Logo
AT.description: Buses display the 'Südburg' logo with bold red and white text and regional motifs.

AT.title: Lower Austria NÖVOG Bus Logo
AT.description: Buses show the 'NÖVOG' or 'VOR' logo, often in blue and yellow.

AT.title: Salzburg Postbus Logo
AT.description: Buses display the 'Salzburg Verkehr' or 'Postbus' logo in red and white.

AT.title: Styria Steiermark Bus Logo
AT.description: Styrian buses carry the 'Steiermark' or 'Verbund Linie' logo in green and white.

AT.title: Tyrol VVT Bus Logo
AT.description: Tyrolean buses show the 'VVT' logo in red and white, often with the Tyrolean eagle.

AT.title: Upper Austria OÖVV Bus Logo
AT.description: Buses display the 'OÖVV' logo, usually in red and white.

AT.title: Vienna Wiener Linien Bus Logo
AT.description: Viennese buses feature the 'Wiener Linien' logo in red and white with stylized letters.

AT.title: Vorarlberg Landbus Logo
AT.description: Vorarlberg buses show the 'Landbus' or 'VVV' logo in green and yellow.

AT.title: .at Domain
AT.description: Web addresses in Austria end in the country domain .at. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

FI.title: Shorter plates
FI.description: In Finland, license plates are slightly shorter than in most other European countries, and they include the standard EU blue strip on the left.

FI.title: White outer lines
FI.description: Outer road lines on Finnish roads are always continuous solid white lines, never dashed.

FI.title: Snow poles
FI.description: Finland has orange snow poles with a single narrow white band positioned close to the top.

FI.title: Street names
FI.description: Finnish road names typically end in 'tie' (road) or 'katu' (street).

FI.title: Crossing signs
FI.description: Finnish pedestrian crossing signs feature five black stripes.

FI.title: Red Houses
FI.description: Along Sweden and Norway, Finland has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.

FI.title: Middle Road Lines
FI.description: Centre lines appear as white dashes, solid white, solid yellow, or double yellow lines.

FI.title: Bollards
FI.description: Tall black-and-white posts with a rectangular white reflector on front and two reflective dots on back.

FI.title: Finnish Language
FI.description: Finnish has long words, frequent double vowels, and special characters ä and ö.

FI.title: Yellow Sign Backgrounds
FI.description: Information and direction signs in Finland have yellow backgrounds.

FI.title: Yellow Stroke on Signs
FI.description: Red-bordered regulatory signs have a fine yellow line along the outer edge.

FI.title: Directional Signs
FI.description: Wayfinding signs have white text and arrows on a solid blue field with a white border.

FI.title: Chevrons
FI.description: Curve warning boards are black panels with yellow arrow markings.

FI.title: Wooden Utility Poles
FI.description: Plain timber poles with various top fittings; street lights often mounted directly on them.

FI.title: Lamp Mounting Style
FI.description: Street lamps on wooden poles attach at the top with a double-bolt fixture; lamp arm extends horizontally.

FI.title: Blue-and-White Signpost Markings
FI.description: Traffic sign poles often have alternating blue and white bands wrapped around them.

FI.title: Boreal Forests
FI.description: Thick coniferous forests dominated by pine and spruce, with birch trees having bright white bark.

FI.title: Autumn Foliage
FI.description: Imagery often shows vivid orange and yellow foliage in autumn.

FI.title: Lakes
FI.description: Finland has many lakes appearing frequently across the landscape.

FI.title: Architecture 01 Red Houses
FI.description: Along Sweden and Norway, Finland has many of these distinct red houses with white trim.

FI.title: Bus Stop Signs
FI.description: Two standard designs: blue-and-white and yellow-and-black.

FI.title: K-Market and S-Market
FI.description: Two supermarket chains exclusive to Finland with recognisable branding.

FI.title: Regional Road Numbers
FI.description: Local roads have three- or four-digit numbers; leading digit indicates geographic zone from south (1) to north (9).

FI.title: Lapland Snow Poles
FI.description: Major roads in Lapland have snow poles with two elongated reflectors instead of one.

FI.title: Farmland Distribution
FI.description: Agricultural fields concentrate along western and southern coasts; interior is mostly forested.

FI.title: Wind Turbines
FI.description: Wind farms cluster mainly along the western coastline.

FI.title: Stunted Northern Trees
FI.description: Northern trees are undersized with thin, spindly trunks, showing high-latitude growth.

FI.title: Snow Coverage in Northwest Lapland
FI.description: Snow regularly appears only in the extreme northwest corner of Lapland.

FI.title: Swedish Language Areas
FI.description: Coastal south and west communities use Swedish extensively, with bilingual Finnish–Swedish signs.

FI.title: Sámi Language
FI.description: Far north road signs show Finnish and Sámi names; Sámi includes the letter 'c'.

FI.title: Åland Swedish Only
FI.description: Åland is exclusively Swedish-speaking with no Finnish on signs.

FI.title: Åland Road Features
FI.description: Åland roads have reddish asphalt and dashed outer lines like Sweden.

FI.title: Åland Licence Plates
FI.description: Åland plates are white with blue text, no EU band, and shorter than Finnish plates.

FI.title: Åland Pedestrian Signs
FI.description: Some Åland crossing signs show four zebra stripes, matching Swedish design.

FI.title: Åland Bus Stops
FI.description: Bus stops have a white plate with a four-digit number, sometimes topped with a semicircle.

FI.title: Helsinki Buses
FI.description: Helsinki city buses are blue and white with a vertical split and operator logos.

FI.title: Country Flag
FI.description: The national flag of Finland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

FI.title: .fi Domain
FI.description: Web addresses in Finland end in the country domain .fi. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

VN.title: Vietnamese language
VN.description: The Vietnamese language is written in a modified Latin script that features an extensive system of diacritical marks.

VN.title: Concrete bollards
VN.description: Small concrete bollards are the most common ones in Vietnam. They have a red top.

VN.title: Electricity boxes
VN.description: Grey electricity boxes can be seen mounted to utility poles in Vietnam. They are tapered towards the bottom and have a few windows.

VN.title: Red-and-White Striped Signposts
VN.description: Vietnamese road sign posts are usually painted with red-and-white stripes.

VN.title: Yellow-Orange Road Signs
VN.description: Vietnamese road signs have a yellow-orange background.

VN.title: Waystones with Coloured Tops
VN.description: Vietnamese waystones are white with red or blue tops, showing road numbers and distances.

VN.title: Single-Arrow Chevrons
VN.description: Vietnamese chevrons are black-on-yellow or white-on-red, typically with a single arrow.

VN.title: Blue Directional Signs
VN.description: Vietnamese directional signs are blue with thin or no white borders and white arrows.

VN.title: Short Yellow Centre Dashes
VN.description: Short yellow dashes as centre road lines are common and distinctive in Vietnam.

VN.title: Concrete Block Roads
VN.description: Minor Vietnamese roads are often made of concrete blocks.

VN.title: Red-and-White Concrete Safety Barriers
VN.description: Red-and-white striped concrete barriers are common on Vietnamese mountain roads.

VN.title: Holey Concrete Poles
VN.description: Concrete poles with rows of holes, on the lower half or nearly to the top, are common in Vietnam.

VN.title: Round Poles with Pin Holes
VN.description: Vietnam often has round concrete poles with indents and small pin holes near the top.

VN.title: Inverted-Trapezoid Pole Tops
VN.description: Pole tops shaped like upside-down trapezoids are common in Vietnam.

VN.title: Double Poles
VN.description: Double utility poles of various designs are fairly common in Vietnam.

VN.title: Grain Drying on Roads
VN.description: In Vietnam, grains are often spread out on road surfaces to dry.

VN.title: Addresses on Storefronts
VN.description: Vietnamese addresses appear on signs and follow a hierarchy from specific to general with key terms like phường, xã, quận, huyện, thị xã, thành phố, tỉnh.

VN.title: Province Names and Abbreviations
VN.description: Province names and abbreviations (e.g. TG for Tien Giang) are useful parts of Vietnamese addresses.

VN.title: Area Codes
VN.description: Vietnamese area codes start with 2 followed by one or two digits, generally ordered north to south.

VN.title: Licence Plate Regional Codes
VN.description: Vietnamese licence plate codes, often painted on trucks, help determine the region.

VN.title: Regional Place Name Prefixes
VN.description: Some city name prefixes are regionally specific within Vietnam.

VN.title: Flat Agricultural Deltas
VN.description: Wide open, flat agricultural fields are most common in the Red River Delta and less so in the Mekong Delta.

VN.title: Mekong Delta, Canals and Palm Trees
VN.description: The Mekong Delta is flat and water-rich, criss-crossed by straight canals flanked by linear villages, with abundant palms.

VN.title: Central Highlands Landscape
VN.description: The Central Highlands are hilly with distant mountains, red soil, and dry rolling farmland.

VN.title: Rubber Tree Plantations
VN.description: Rubber plantations north of Ho Chi Minh City and in the Central Highlands have thin-trunked trees often wrapped in plastic and planted in dense grids.

VN.title: Tea Plantations
VN.description: Vietnamese tea plantations are mainly in the north and Lam Dong province, with compact, trimmed plants in winding hillside rows.

VN.title: Khasi Pines in the Northeast
VN.description: Clusters of Khasi pines on hills are typical of far northeastern Vietnam, especially Lang Son and Quang Ninh provinces.

VN.title: Dragonfruit Farms
VN.description: Dragonfruit farms, resembling upturned wet mops, are found around Phan Thiet and the Long An / Tien Giang border.

VN.title: Dry Sandy Coast Northeast of Phan Thiet
VN.description: The coast northeast of Phan Thiet is dry and sandy with some rocky sections.

VN.title: Black Pepper Plantations
VN.description: Black pepper vines in the Central Highlands shroud tree trunks with dense downward-pointing leaves.

VN.title: Wind Turbine Clusters
VN.description: Wind turbines appear in several clusters mostly in southern Vietnam near Dalat, Buon Ma Thuot, Pleiku, Dong Hoi, Quy Nhon, Ho Chi Minh City, and Quang Tri.

VN.title: Roof Spires in the North
VN.description: Thin spires on house roofs are almost exclusively found in northern Vietnam.

VN.title: Red River Delta, Tall Boxy Houses
VN.description: Houses around Hanoi and the Red River Delta are tall, multi-storey with gaudy Greco-Roman details.

VN.title: Mekong Delta, Low Single-Storey Houses
VN.description: Mekong Delta houses are boxy concrete and almost always single ground-level storey.

VN.title: Northwestern Stilt Houses
VN.description: Traditional wooden houses in northwestern Vietnam often have stilts, corrugated metal roofs, and triangular roof gable openings.

VN.title: Graves in Agricultural Fields
VN.description: Single graves in the middle of agricultural fields are found in the Red River Delta.

VN.title: Stick and Bamboo Fences in the North
VN.description: Wooden fences of sticks or bamboo in a grid-like pattern appear in northern Vietnam.

VN.title: Black Pole Stickers
VN.description: Poles in northern Vietnam often have black stickers with simple designs.

VN.title: Sand Dunes in Northern Khanh Hoa
VN.description: A peninsula in far northern Khanh Hoa province has sand dunes hugging a mostly divided highway.

VN.title: Hoi An Yellow Buildings
VN.description: Hoi An is identifiable by old yellow buildings with dark brown doors and details.

VN.title: Sa Pa, Touristy Mountain Town
VN.description: Sa Pa is a resort town deep in the northern mountains, overflowing with tourist shops, restaurants with excessive signage, and grand hotel buildings mixing European and Southeast Asian styles.

VN.title: Russian Cyrillic Signs Near Phan Thiet
VN.description: Near the beach resorts east of Phan Thiet, most signs include Cyrillic text alongside Vietnamese, catering to Russian tourists.

VN.title: Country Flag
VN.description: The national flag of Vietnam is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

VN.title: .vn Domain
VN.description: Web addresses in Vietnam end in the country domain .vn (often as .com.vn). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

RO.title: Holey poles
RO.description: In Romania, you will frequently come across so called holey poles, with holes running all the way down to the ground.

RO.title: Painted trees
RO.description: In Romania, trees and utility poles frequently have their lower sections painted white.

RO.title: Waystones
RO.description: Romanian road waystones are very common. They are white and can have red or blue accents. They have the road number on the side.

RO.title: Licence Plates
RO.description: Romanian plates are long, white European style with a single blue strip on the left.

RO.title: Romanian Language
RO.description: A Romance language with unique diacritics Ă/ă, Ș/ș, and Ț/ț.

RO.title: Round Concrete Poles
RO.description: Round concrete utility poles are widespread in Romania.

RO.title: Large Yellow Pole Stickers
RO.description: Extremely large yellow stickers wrapped around poles, usually with the town or city name.

RO.title: Inverted-Triangle Pole Tops
RO.description: Some pole tops have two support bars forming an upside-down triangle shape.

RO.title: Short-Dash Edge Lines
RO.description: Outer road lines made of short dashes with narrow gaps are a clue for Romania.

RO.title: Thick Centre Lines
RO.description: Centre road lines are often noticeably thicker than average.

RO.title: Directional Signs
RO.description: Blue arrow-shaped signs with white borders, often showing road numbers in red or blue.

RO.title: Town Entry Signs
RO.description: Yellow speed limit signs with city skylines, often with a white sign below showing the town name.

RO.title: Black Sign Backs
RO.description: The back sides of road signs in Romania are often painted black.

RO.title: Chevrons
RO.description: Red-on-white chevron boards frequently have a yellow frame.

RO.title: Bollards
RO.description: Thin white bollards with a red vertical strip near the top.

RO.title: Thick-Border Yield Sign
RO.description: Romanian yield signs have an extremely thick red border and thin white outline.

RO.title: Architecture
RO.description: Single-family stone houses painted in pastels with orange tile or grey metal roofs; some have painted square tile walls.

RO.title: Carpathian Mountains and Hills
RO.description: Tall forested mountains and hills dominate the centre and north of Romania.

RO.title: Agricultural Lowlands
RO.description: Flat or rolling agricultural land dominates southern and eastern Romania.

RO.title: Haystacks
RO.description: Haystacks with a stick driven straight through them are common in rural areas.

RO.title: Dacia Cars
RO.description: Dacia is the dominant car brand in Romania with over a quarter of all vehicles.

RO.title: Elevation Map
RO.description: Tallest mountains run through the centre and north; south and west are flat.

RO.title: Flat Agricultural Plains
RO.description: Flat agricultural land in south and west, with hills or mountains visible to the north or south respectively.

RO.title: Orange Tiled Roofs
RO.description: Villages with nearly all houses having orange tiled roofs are likely in the western half.

RO.title: Metal or Fake-Tile Roofs
RO.description: Villages dominated by metal or plastic fake-tiled roofs tend to be in the eastern half.

RO.title: Hungarian-Style Villages
RO.description: Near the Hungarian border, villages have long straight streets with evenly spaced single-storey houses and orange tiled roofs.

RO.title: Bilingual Hungarian Signs
RO.description: Common in central counties Covasna, Harghita, and Mureș, and near the Hungarian border.

RO.title: Decorated Wooden Gates
RO.description: Elaborately carved wooden gates are characteristic of Maramureș in the north.

RO.title: Sunflower Fields
RO.description: Sunflower crops are primarily found in the far east and far west.

RO.title: Danube Delta Boat Trekker
RO.description: A trekker aboard a green boat navigates small overgrown canals in a flat landscape in the far east.

RO.title: Country Flag
RO.description: The national flag of Romania is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

RO.title: Vaslui Street Signs
RO.description: Blue signs with white border and text, sometimes featuring the city crest.

RO.title: Timisoara Sign
RO.description: Blue signs with thick white border and bold white lettering, often including the city coat of arms.

RO.description: Blue signs with white border and text, sometimes featuring the city coat of arms.

RO.description: Blue signs with thick white border and bold white lettering, often including the city coat of arms.

RW.title: Rwanda plates
RW.description: Rwanda has long license plates, with white plates on the front and yellow plates on the back.

RW.title: Brake light
RW.description: The Google car, a large pickup truck, is fully visible in most Rwandan imagery and distinctively has a visible brake light.

RW.title: Red soil
RW.description: Most soil across Rwanda has a noticeable reddish tint.

RW.title: Bikers wear red!
RW.description: In Rwanda, all motorcyclists are required to wear red vests and helmets.

RW.title: Hazy Sky Tint
RW.description: Rwandan coverage has a noticeable haze, especially visible in the sky.

RW.title: Architecture
RW.description: Rwandan buildings are mainly brick and concrete houses with steep roofs and ventilation bricks.

RW.title: Hilly Terrain
RW.description: Rwanda's landscape is generally hilly.

RW.title: Red-Tinted Soil
RW.description: Most soil across Rwanda has a reddish tint.

RW.title: Banana Plants
RW.description: Banana plants grow abundantly throughout Rwanda.

RW.title: Bollards
RW.description: Rwandan bollards are red-and-white cylindrical shapes in several designs.

RW.title: Waystones
RW.description: White concrete waystones mark Rwandan roadsides.

RW.title: Clean Streets
RW.description: Rwandan streets are tidy and free of litter.

RW.title: Black-and-White Kerbs
RW.description: Rwandan kerbs are painted with alternating black and white stripes.

RW.title: Security Fences and Walls
RW.description: Rwandan villa neighbourhoods have many tall security fences and perimeter walls.

RW.title: District Codes on Street Signs
RW.description: Rwandan street names often include a two-letter district prefix.

RW.title: Lamppost Styles by National Road
RW.description: Lamp designs vary by national road: green roads have slightly curved arms; red roads have shorter arms with a sharp bend; blue roads have longer fully curved arms; grey roads rarely have lamps.

RW.title: Road Numbers on Lampposts
RW.description: National road numbers are painted in black on lampposts with sequential lamp numbers below.

RW.title: Tea Plantations
RW.description: Tea plantations are common in western Rwanda and a few other pockets.

RW.title: Northeast Rolling Landscape
RW.description: The northeast has rolling hills with open agricultural or grassland areas.

RW.title: Northwest Volcanoes
RW.description: Volcanoes and volcanic rocks are visible in the northwest corner.

RW.title: Kigali Luxury Villas
RW.description: Wealthier Kigali neighborhoods feature many luxury villas.

RW.title: Butare Cobblestone Streets
RW.description: Many roads in Butare are paved with cobblestones.

RW.title: Country Flag
RW.description: The national flag of Rwanda is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

RW.title: .rw Domain
RW.description: Web addresses in Rwanda end in the country domain .rw. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

UK.title: Small reflectors
UK.description: Dashed center lines with reflectors set between them are a good road marking clue for the UK.

UK.title: White and yellow
UK.description: In the UK, license plates are yellow in the rear and white on the front.

UK.title: No sign
UK.description: Pedestrian crossings in the UK do not feature signs, instead there are striped poles with a light at the top.

UK.title: Terraced houses
UK.description: Two-story, terraced buildings are extremely common in the UK.

AD.title: Stone buildings
AD.description: Stone buildings are common all across Andorra.

AD.title: Andorran plates
AD.description: License plates in Andorra lacks the blue eu-strip. Instead an orange dot can be found on the left side.

AD.title: Mountains all around
AD.description: Andorra is located in a mountain range between France and Spain, this leads to mountains being visible at all times.

AD.title: Autumn colours
AD.description: Much of the Andorran coverage was captured in October, so autumn colours on deciduous trees are common.

AD.title: Snow poles
AD.description: Wooden snow poles in various colours line roads throughout Andorra.

AD.title: Catalan language
AD.description: Andorra's official language is Catalan, recognisable by 'i' meaning 'and' and words that often end in consonants.

AD.title: Carrer street signs
AD.description: Street signs in Andorra use the Catalan word 'carrer' for street.

AD.title: Kilometre markers
AD.description: Andorran roads have distance markers labelled with CG or CS route numbers.

AD.title: Yellow guardrail reflectors
AD.description: In Andorra, guardrails have yellow reflectors.

AD.title: Bollards
AD.description: Andorran bollards are white with square orange reflectors and appear along main highways.

AD.title: Traffic cones
AD.description: Traffic cones in Andorra are yellow and turquoise-green.

AD.title: Pedestrian crossing signs
AD.description: Andorran pedestrian crossing signs show a crosswalk with 8 stripes.

AD.title: Andorran flag
AD.description: A vertical tricolour of blue, yellow, and red, sometimes with the coat of arms in the centre.

AD.title: Stone Building
AD.description: Stone buildings are common all across Andorra.

AD.title: .ad Domain
AD.description: Web addresses in Andorra end in the country domain .ad. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MY.title: Marked poles
MY.description: In mainland Malaysia, electricity poles often have black stickers on them.

MY.title: Unique stop signs
MY.description: Stop signs saying "BERHENTI" are unique to Malaysia.

MY.title: White center lines
MY.description: Two-lane roads often feature double white center lines, Malaysia is the only Southeast Asian country that does this.

MY.title: Malay plates
MY.description: Malaysian plates are black with two white sections, easily visible even through blurring.

MY.title: Street abbreviation
MY.description: In Malaysia it is common to see the abbreviation JLN for Jalan, the local word for street.

MY.title: Thick Yellow Road Bars
MY.description: Bold yellow bars painted across roads are nearly exclusive to Malaysia.

MY.title: Pole Stickers
MY.description: Malaysian utility poles often have black or white stickers, sometimes with red-and-white or red-and-blue bands below.

MY.title: Bollards
MY.description: Malaysian bollards combine black, white, grey, and red colours with consistent layout variants.

MY.title: Hexagonal Yellow Highway Shields
MY.description: Directional signs feature hexagonal yellow highway shields found only in Malaysia.

MY.title: Kilometre Markers
MY.description: Malaysian km markers use a distinctive white-and-blue scheme, often with the hexagonal highway shield.

MY.title: Malay Language
MY.description: Malay is written in Latin script and is very close to Indonesian.

MY.title: Chinese Characters
MY.description: Chinese script appears frequently on Malaysian signage, reflecting its significant ethnic Chinese population.

MY.title: Black-and-White Signposts
MY.description: Malaysian sign poles are almost always painted with alternating black-and-white stripes.

MY.title: Black-and-White Kerbs
MY.description: Kerbs painted in black-and-white are a common Malaysian roadside feature.

MY.title: Johor State Road J-Prefix
MY.description: Road signs in Johor feature a large capital 'J' at the start of the route number.

MY.title: Kedah State Road K-Prefix
MY.description: Kedah state roads have a bold 'K' prefix before the road number.

MY.title: Kelantan State Road D-Prefix
MY.description: Kelantan state roads use a 'D' prefix on their signs.

MY.title: Melaka State Road M-Prefix
MY.description: Melaka state roads start with a capital 'M'.

MY.title: Negeri Sembilan State Road N-Prefix
MY.description: Negeri Sembilan state roads begin with a large 'N'.

MY.title: Pahang State Road C-Prefix
MY.description: Pahang state roads use a 'C' prefix on their signs.

MY.title: Perak State Road A-Prefix
MY.description: Perak state roads have an 'A' prefix at the start of road numbers.

MY.title: Perlis State Road R-Prefix
MY.description: Perlis state roads have an 'R' prefix before the route number.

MY.title: Penang State Road P-Prefix
MY.description: Penang state roads start with a 'P' prefix.

MY.title: Sabah State Road SA-Prefix
MY.description: Sabah state roads use an 'SA' prefix before the route number.

MY.title: Sarawak State Road Q-Prefix
MY.description: Sarawak state roads have a 'Q' prefix at the start of the route number.

MY.title: Selangor State Road B-Prefix
MY.description: Selangor state roads feature a 'B' prefix before the route number.

MY.title: Terengganu State Road T-Prefix
MY.description: Terengganu state roads start with a 'T' prefix.

MY.title: "TEL TNB" Stickers, Johor
MY.description: Black pole stickers with "TEL TNB" text are exclusive to Johor.

MY.title: White Pole Stickers, Sarawak
MY.description: White stickers on electricity poles are found only in Sarawak.

MY.title: Double-Circle Lamp Posts, Mainland
MY.description: Lamp posts with two small circles on the support arm are mainly on Peninsular Malaysia.

MY.title: Triangular Lamp Post Support, Mainland
MY.description: Lamp posts braced by a triangular sheet-metal support are mainly a mainland feature.

MY.title: 2-1 Insulator Poles, Sarawak
MY.description: Wooden electricity poles with a 2-1 insulator layout and long diagonal support are exclusive to Sarawak.

MY.title: Parallel Poletops, Sabah
MY.description: Thin metal poles with two parallel horizontal arms at the top are exclusive to Sabah.

MY.title: Boomerang Lamp Posts, Sarawak
MY.description: Lamp posts with a boomerang-shaped sheet-metal support are found in Sarawak.

MY.title: S-Logo Bins, Negeri Sembilan / Malacca / Johor
MY.description: Rubbish bins with an "S"-like logo are found in Negeri Sembilan, Malacca, and Johor.

MY.title: Leaf-Logo Bins, Perlis / Kedah
MY.description: Rubbish bins with a leaf-like logo are found in Perlis and Kedah.

MY.title: Alam Flora Bins, Pahang / KL / Putrajaya
MY.description: Bins with a sunny landscape logo and "Alam Flora" text are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya.

MY.title: Yellow Street Name Signs, Johor
MY.description: Yellow arrow-shaped street name signs are specific to Johor.

MY.title: Green JKR Street Signs, Sabah
MY.description: Green arrow-shaped street signs with a yellow hexagonal JKR symbol are found in Sabah.

MY.title: Mountainous Sabah vs Flat Sarawak
MY.description: Sabah is mountainous with steep roads; Sarawak is generally flatter.

MY.title: Isolated Rock Formations, Perlis
MY.description: Dramatic rock formations rising sharply from flat terrain are found near the Thai border in Perlis.

MY.title: Labuan Blue Bins
MY.description: Blue cylindrical containers are common in urban areas on Labuan island.

MY.title: Country Flag
MY.description: The national flag of Malaysia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MY.title: .my Domain
MY.description: Web addresses in Malaysia end in the country domain .my (often as .com.my). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MN.title: Tent car
MN.description: In Mongolia the google car is often visible. It takes many shapes but usually a tent can be seen packed on the car.

MN.title: Unique stop sign
MN.description: The Mongolian stop signs are written in Mongolian Cyrillic. They are unique to say "ЗОГС".

MN.title: Licence Plates with Red Soyombo Symbol
MN.description: Mongolian plates are mostly white with a red Soyombo emblem on the left side.

MN.title: Cyrillic Script with Unique Letters
MN.description: Mongolian Cyrillic includes extra letters Ɵ and Ү and often uses doubled vowels like aa, ƟƟ, or ЭЭ.

MN.title: General 01 Vast Landscapes
MN.description: The Mongolian landscape is often barren, featuring large open areas without much vegetation.

MN.title: Strike!
MN.description: The Mongolian bollard is reminiscent of a bowling pin.

MN.title: Dirt Alleys and Wooden Fences
MN.description: Residential areas divided by unpaved dirt alleys lined with wooden fencing.

MN.title: Traditional Yurts (Gers)
MN.description: Round white yurts, traditional homes of Mongolian nomads, are common throughout the country.

MN.title: Livestock Herds
MN.description: Large groups of roadside animals including horses, yaks, cattle, sheep, goats, and camels.

MN.title: Street View Coverage Map
MN.description: Sparse coverage concentrated along major highways and larger towns, densest around Ulaanbaatar.

MN.title: Driving Direction Away from Ulaanbaatar
MN.description: Street View car generally heads outward from the capital, so driving direction points away from Ulaanbaatar.

MN.title: Topography: Flat East, Mountainous West
MN.description: East and south are flat, north has rolling hills, west has large mountains and rocky terrain.

MN.title: Northern Forests
MN.description: Forested areas with Siberian Larch, pine, and birch appear throughout northern Mongolia.

MN.title: Flat Grassy Plains in the Far East
MN.description: Narrow dirt tracks cut through vast, treeless grasslands in Mongolia's far east.

MN.title: Off-Road Desert Coverage in the South
MN.description: Unpaved desert tracks appear south or east of Mandalgovi.

MN.title: Paved Desert Roads in the South
MN.description: A few paved highways cross the southern desert region.

MN.title: Arid Steppe Rangeland in the Southwest
MN.description: Dry steppe rangeland with coarse soil, sparse grass, and scattered low shrubs.

MN.title: Dry Rugged Mountains in the Far West
MN.description: Barren, rugged hills and mountains with no vegetation in the far west.

MN.title: Lakes and Rivers in the West
MN.description: Lakes and rivers appear more frequently in western Mongolia.

MN.title: Snow Coverage Near Ulaanbaatar
MN.description: Snowy Street View imagery is concentrated around Ulaanbaatar.

MN.title: Fall Foliage Coverage
MN.description: Autumn imagery shows vivid orange trees and grass mainly between Lun and Hatgal, and near Ulaanbaatar.

MN.title: Rare Crop Fields
MN.description: Agricultural fields appear occasionally in Selenge and Töv provinces near Ulaanbaatar.

MN.title: Ulaanbaatar Cityscape
MN.description: The capital has high-rises, chain stores, heavy traffic, buses, pedestrians, maintained roads, and sprawling yurt suburbs on hills.

MN.title: Spare Tire Variations
MN.description: The spare tire on the back right of the Street View truck divides Mongolia into four zones by tire type and presence.

MN.title: Light Blue Tent with Forward Snorkel
MN.description: In eastern grasslands, the Street View truck has a light blue tent and a forward-facing snorkel intake.

MN.title: Orange Roof Rack Strap Patterns
MN.description: Eastern Mongolia sub-areas can be identified by orange strap arrangements on roof racks, visible from above.

MN.title: Bright Silver Tent
MN.description: A bright silver tent on the Street View truck is typical in central and northwestern Mongolia.

MN.title: Cage Roof Rack
MN.description: Near Ulaanbaatar, some coverage shows a metal cage replacing the tent, often with a green camouflage sleeping bag on top.

MN.title: White and Blue Truck in Ulaanbaatar
MN.description: Some imagery in the capital uses a truck with an ornate blue-and-white roof decal.

MN.title: Western Mongolia Snow-Capped Peaks
MN.description: Western Mongolia features the tallest mountains with glaciers and snow, and a Street View car with a green or black bag on the roof.

MN.title: Shrubland East of Uvs Lake
MN.description: East of Uvs Lake has abundant small shrubs and patchy grass on flat terrain.

MN.title: Nighttime Coverage Locations
MN.description: After-dark imagery appears in four main areas, with the car heading toward the nearest town.

MN.title: Country Flag
MN.description: The national flag of Mongolia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MN.title: Right-hand drive
MN.description: Mongolia drives on the right, yet over half of its cars are right-hand drive, largely due to used car imports from Japan.

MN.title: .mn Domain
MN.description: Web addresses in Mongolia end in the country domain .mn. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

LK.title: Sri Lanka poles
LK.description: Sri Lanka commonly uses concrete utility poles with large see through holes in the lower half, often called holey poles

LK.title: White and yellow
LK.description: Sri Lankan license plates are white in the front and yellow in the rear.

LK.title: Tapered bollards
LK.description: In Sri Lanka you can find short, tapered stone bollards. They are white with a black base.

LK.title: Language 01 Sinhala Writing
LK.description: The written Sri Lankan language Sinhala have letters that are very round. Some letter makes it look like there are small doodle characters among us.

LK.title: Waystones
LK.description: Tall white concrete posts have an indented base section with a yellow road number.

LK.title: Striped Signposts
LK.description: Black-and-white striped signposts are common.

LK.title: Road Lines (Edge Only)
LK.description: Rural roads often have white edge lines but no centre line.

LK.title: Tropical Landscape
LK.description: Lush green tropical vegetation dominates, with a patchwork of cultivated fields.

LK.title: Red and White Soil
LK.description: Reddish soil is widespread.

LK.title: Palm Trees
LK.description: Palm trees are exceptionally abundant.

LK.title: Tiled Roofs
LK.description: Houses frequently have orange or red tile roofs that weather to brownish tones.

LK.title: Buddhism
LK.description: Temples, stupas, Buddha statues, and Buddhist flags are common.

LK.title: Other Religions
LK.description: Hinduism, Islam, and Christianity have distinct regional strongholds.

LK.title: Tuk-Tuks
LK.description: Sri Lankan tuk-tuks are bulky with a black roof, typically painted green, yellow, or red.

LK.title: Area Codes
LK.description: Sri Lankan landline numbers are 10 digits, starting with a 0 area code. Mobile numbers begin with 07.

LK.title: Religious Distribution
LK.description: Buddhism dominates most of Sri Lanka except the north and east coast. Hinduism is strongest in the north, east, and around Nuwara Eliya. Islam is along the east coast. Christianity clusters in the northwest around Mannar.

LK.title: Tamil Script Distribution
LK.description: Tamil script appears in Hindu-majority areas: north, east, and central Nuwara Eliya. Tamil-only signs indicate Tamil-majority areas.

LK.title: Topography
LK.description: Hills and mountains are concentrated in central-southern Sri Lanka; the rest is relatively flat.

LK.title: Wet Southwest Climate
LK.description: The southwest receives more rainfall, producing dense, deep-green vegetation.

LK.title: Drier Climate Elsewhere
LK.description: Outside the wet southwest, the landscape is more open and scrubby with mixed brown and green tones.

LK.title: Tea Plantations
LK.description: Bright-green shrubs planted in neat rows on hillsides, concentrated in central and southwestern highlands, especially west of Nuwara Eliya.

LK.title: Country Flag
LK.description: The national flag of Sri Lanka is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LK.title: Blurred car
LK.description: In Sri Lanka, the Google car will often have blue-white-red patches.

LK.title: .lk Domain
LK.description: Web addresses in Sri Lanka end in the country domain .lk. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

IS.title: Pedestrian crossings
IS.description: In Iceland, you will see pedestrian crossing signs with four stripes at the bottom and a subtle yellow hue.

IS.title: Icelandic plates
IS.description: Icelandic license plates do not feature the blue EU strip on the left. A yellow dot can sometimes be seen in the middle.

IS.title: Yellow bollards
IS.description: Icelandic bollards are yellow and have a single white reflector. They appear on virtually every stretch of rural road across the country.

IS.title: Barren landscape
IS.description: Much of the Icelandic countryside is devoid of trees, covered instead by dark grey soil composed largely of volcanic rock.

IS.title: Icelandic language
IS.description: Written Icelandic can be recognized by a frequent use of accents and unique letters such as ð and þ.

IS.title: Volcanic Geology
IS.description: A dramatic landscape of rugged peaks, geothermal pools, lava fields, rift valleys, and rock pillars shaped by tectonic and volcanic forces.

IS.title: Yellow Directional Signs
IS.description: Road destination boards have a yellow background with a white inset panel showing the route number.

IS.title: Street Name Signs
IS.description: White plates with black text, often edged by a thin metal rim, mounted on lamp posts or traffic-light poles.

IS.title: All-White Road Markings
IS.description: All road markings in Iceland are white.

IS.title: Chevron Signs
IS.description: Curve warning boards show yellow arrows on a black field.

IS.title: Yellow Warning Signs
IS.description: Warning signs in Iceland use a yellow background.

IS.title: Road Numbering System
IS.description: Route 1 is the ring road; other routes start with digits 2–9 corresponding to regions clockwise from the south.

IS.title: Westfjords
IS.description: Narrow fjords hemmed by moderately high mountains with flat summits.

IS.title: Eastfjords
IS.description: Eastern fjords with taller, more rugged flanking mountains.

IS.title: Northern Valleys West of Akureyri
IS.description: Multiple valleys between tall, often snow-dusted peaks opening north to northeast.

IS.title: Inland Volcanic Desert
IS.description: Desolate dark volcanic gravel expanses with virtually no plant life.

IS.title: Southwest Agricultural Lowland
IS.description: Broad farming area with farmsteads, meadows, and distant surrounding mountains.

IS.title: Reykjavík
IS.description: Capital on the southern shore of a bay, mostly flat with gentle hills and a large urban footprint.

IS.title: Red Pickup Trucks
IS.description: Street View coverage uses bright red pickup trucks distinctive to southwestern Iceland.

IS.title: Red Pickup Trucks
IS.description: Street View coverage uses bright red pickup trucks distinctive to southwestern Iceland.

IS.title: Red Pickup Trucks
IS.description: Street View imagery collected using bright red pickup trucks specific to southwestern Iceland.

IS.title: Red Pickup Trucks
IS.description: Street View coverage uses bright red pickup trucks exclusive to southwestern Iceland.

IS.title: White Pickup Trucks
IS.description: Street View imagery uses white pickup trucks unique to northeastern Iceland.

IS.title: Southern Coast Glaciers
IS.description: Ice tongues from Vatnajökull ice cap spill down to the sea along the southern coast.

IS.title: Divided and Multi-Lane Highways
IS.description: Dual carriageways and roads wider than two lanes are rare, mostly around Reykjavík.

IS.title: Country Flag
IS.description: The national flag of Iceland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

IS.title: .is Domain
IS.description: Web addresses in Iceland end in the country domain .is. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

KE.title: Mobile network
KE.description: The mobile network Safaricom is exclusive to Kenya, and its branded signage appears in almost every town.

KE.title: Snorkel
KE.description: Kenyan coverage features distinctive vehicles very often equipped with a snorkel.

KE.title: Follow car
KE.description: A grey Toyota SUV can frequently be seen trailing the Street View car in Kenyan coverage.

KE.title: Yellow rear plates
KE.description: Kenyan vehicles carry long white front plates and square yellow rear plates.

KE.title: Road Lines
KE.description: Kenyan roads have solid white edge lines and yellow centre lines, solid or dashed.

KE.title: Green Directional Signs
KE.description: Kenyan directional signs have green backgrounds with white borders and lettering; route numbers are white or yellow.

KE.title: Red-and-White Road Signs
KE.description: Road signs in Kenya are mostly red and white.

KE.title: County Names on Signage
KE.description: Signs often display Kenyan county names, useful for regional identification.

KE.title: Repurposed Vans
KE.description: Colourfully wrapped repurposed vans are common throughout Kenya.

KE.title: Eucalyptus Trees
KE.description: Eucalyptus trees with long clustered leaves and smooth bark grow widely in Kenya.

KE.title: Topography
KE.description: Eastern and northern Kenya is very flat; elevation rises steadily toward the southwest.

KE.title: Regional Climates
KE.description: Kenya spans humid to very arid climate zones; use climate as a regional clue.

KE.title: White Tape on Roof
KE.description: White tape strips appear on car roofs north and south of Nairobi.

KE.title: Mombasa Coast
KE.description: Mombasa coast features white sandy soil, palm trees, and a coastal atmosphere.

KE.title: Far West (Kisumu Area)
KE.description: Northwest and southwest of Kisumu are agricultural with farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus.

KE.title: Kitui (Semi-Arid)
KE.description: Kitui area is semi-arid, hilly or mountainous, with light orange sandy soil.

KE.title: B9 Northeast
KE.description: The B9 northeast is unpaved with bright reddish-orange dirt and dense tree cover.

KE.title: Mount Kilimanjaro
KE.description: Kilimanjaro's broad silhouette is visible south from much coverage north of the mountain.

KE.title: Mara Triangle
KE.description: Flat to gently hilly savannah with no major mountains, covered by a white car.

KE.title: Aberdare National Park
KE.description: Grey-and-brown car with snorkel and rubber bands on roof rack appears near Aberdare.

KE.title: Mt Elgon Area
KE.description: Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, same grey-and-brown car appears; redder soil and greener landscape.

KE.title: Kerio–Lodwar Area
KE.description: Between Kerio and Lodwar, same car appears in sandy, dry, sparsely vegetated landscape.

KE.title: B8 Succulents
KE.description: A stretch of the B8 north of Kibaoni is lined with many succulent plants.

KE.title: Country Flag
KE.description: The national flag of Kenya is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

KE.title: Grey Pickup Truck
KE.description: In a lot of the Kenyan coverage, you can see the large grey Street View pickup truck, sometimes with a black snorkel.

KE.title: .ke Domain
KE.description: Web addresses in Kenya end in the country domain .ke (often as .co.ke). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

KZ.title: Tree trunks
KZ.description: The bottom of tree trunks in Kazakhstan are often painted white.

KZ.title: White license plates
KZ.description: Standard Kazakh plates appear mostly white when blurred, with a small blue patch visible on the left side.

KZ.title: White pickup truck
KZ.description: All Kazakh Street View imagery was captured using a white pickup truck, which may be fully visible or partially blurred out.

KZ.title: Pedestrian crossing
KZ.description: Kazakh pedestrian crossings use yellow and white stripes and have white dashes running along either side. Sometimes only the dashes appear without the stripes.

KZ.title: Kazakh Language and Alphabet
KZ.description: Kazakhstan uses Cyrillic and Latin scripts; Kazakh has unique Cyrillic letters.

KZ.title: Mostly Flat Landscape
KZ.description: Kazakhstan features varied terrain but mostly vast, open, flat rural scenery.

KZ.title: Russian-Style Infrastructure
KZ.description: Kazakhstan's built environment closely mirrors Russia's.

KZ.title: Blue Street Signs on Buildings
KZ.description: Kazakh street signs are blue with white patterns, mounted on building facades, often bilingual or trilingual.

KZ.title: Unique 90-Degree Angle Bollards
KZ.description: Distinctive bollards of two thin posts joined at a 90-degree angle.

KZ.title: Yellow and Black Chevron Signs
KZ.description: Kazakh road chevrons are predominantly yellow and black; T-intersections use red and white.

KZ.title: Urban Gas Pipes
KZ.description: Above-ground gas pipes are common throughout Kazakh cities.

KZ.title: Koshkar-Muiz Ornamental Pattern
KZ.description: The ram's-horn motif koshkar-muiz appears as decoration across Kazakhstan.

KZ.title: Ornate City Entrance Arches
KZ.description: Many Kazakh cities feature decorative and ornate entrance arches.

KZ.title: Limited Street View Coverage
KZ.description: Coverage is sparse; major roads and cities are covered, rural roads often lack imagery.

KZ.title: Seasonal Coverage Regions
KZ.description: Imagery shows summer in west/central, autumn in northeast, and winter in southeast Kazakhstan.

KZ.title: Driving Direction Map
KZ.description: Knowing travel direction on rural roads helps narrow down locations.

KZ.title: Atyrau Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: Atyrau Region area codes start with '7122', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: West Kazakhstan Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: West Kazakhstan Region area codes start with '7112', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: Mangystau Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: Mangystau Region area codes start with '7292', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: Karaganda Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: Karaganda Region area codes start with '7212', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: Kostanay Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: Kostanay Region area codes start with '7142', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: Akmola Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: Akmola Region area codes start with '7162', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: Pavlodar Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: Pavlodar Region area codes start with '7182', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: East Kazakhstan Telephone Area Codes
KZ.description: East Kazakhstan Region area codes start with '7232', shown in bold near phone icons on signs.

KZ.title: Akmola Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '03' for Akmola Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Aktobe Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '04' for Aktobe Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Almaty Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '05' for Almaty Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Atyrau Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '06' for Atyrau Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: East Kazakhstan Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '16' for East Kazakhstan Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Jambyl Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates have '08' in Jambyl Region, which can be seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: West Kazakhstan Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '07' for West Kazakhstan Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Karaganda Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '09' for Karaganda Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Kostanay Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '10' for Kostanay Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Kyzylorda Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '11' for Kyzylorda Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Mangystau Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '12' for Mangystau Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Pavlodar Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '14' for Pavlodar Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: North Kazakhstan Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '15' for North Kazakhstan Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: Turkistan Licence Plate Code
KZ.description: Licence plates start with '13' for Turkistan Region, seen on rear of trucks and buses.

KZ.title: QR Code Region Text on Street Signs
KZ.description: Some blue street signs have region text beneath the QR code.

KZ.title: Northern Birch Forests
KZ.description: Dense birch forests alongside green fields are typical of northern Kazakhstan.

KZ.title: Northwestern Green Steppe
KZ.description: Wide grassy plains are typical of northwestern Kazakhstan, especially Akmola and Kostanay.

KZ.title: Southwestern Sandy Desert
KZ.description: Sandy terrain with sparse shrubs is typical of southwestern Kazakhstan.

KZ.title: Southeastern Snow-Capped Mountains
KZ.description: Tall snow-capped mountains appear in southeastern Kazakhstan.

KZ.title: Snow Coverage Southeast of Almaty
KZ.description: Snowy roads appear southeast, especially east of Almaty.

KZ.title: Green Rolling Hills North of Bishkek
KZ.description: Lush green rolling hills occur just north of Bishkek in southern Kazakhstan.

KZ.title: West Kazakhstan Pole Paint
KZ.description: Utility poles have three bold horizontal bands: red top, white middle, black bottom, all equal width.

KZ.title: Atyrau Pole Paint
KZ.description: Poles feature three horizontal bands: blue top, white middle, black bottom, with vivid colors.

KZ.title: Akmola Pole Paint
KZ.description: Poles show a thin red stripe top, broad white middle, thin black bottom; white section is widest.

KZ.title: Kostanay Pole Paint
KZ.description: Poles have narrow alternating thin turquoise and yellow horizontal stripes.

KZ.title: Petropavl Pole Paint
KZ.description: Utility poles have thin horizontal bands of white and light grey.

KZ.title: Taraz Pole Paint
KZ.description: Poles have three bold horizontal bands: red top, yellow middle, black bottom, similar width.

KZ.title: Kyzylorda Pole and Lamp Post Paint
KZ.description: Poles show thin yellow and red stripes top, broad white below; lamp posts are white with turquoise base.

KZ.title: Baltic Pine Forests
KZ.description: Thick Baltic pine forests appear north of Shchuchinsk.

KZ.title: Country Flag
KZ.description: The national flag of Kazakhstan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

KZ.title: .kz Domain
KZ.description: Web addresses in Kazakhstan end in the country domain .kz. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

PA.title: Checkered taxis
PA.description: Yellow taxis marked with a horizontal checkered stripe are a common sight in Panama.

PA.title: Stop sign
PA.description: Like most other Spanish speaking countries in North America, stop signs in Panama say ALTO.

PA.title: Panama plates
PA.description: Front plates are not mandatory in Panama so look for the rear ones, which are short, white plates with a turquoise band across the top.

PA.title: Visible car
PA.description: Panama's Street View car is a large white pickup truck. It is either fully visible or totally hidden, leaving a large blur.

PA.title: Tropical Hilly Landscape
PA.description: Panama features tropical landscape with palms, rolling hills, and a mix of dry fields and dense vegetation.

PA.title: Living Fence Posts
PA.description: Panamanian roadside fences are often built from small living trees, with remaining posts also wooden.

PA.title: Spanish Colonial Architecture
PA.description: Panamanian buildings show Spanish colonial influence, with vivid painted concrete or brick walls and red metal-sheet or tile roofs.

PA.title: Road Lines
PA.description: Typical road markings are solid white edges with a yellow centre line; solid white edges with no centre line are nearly unique to Panama.

PA.title: Utility Poles
PA.description: Panamanian utility poles are mostly round concrete with varying insulators; blue, white, or red numbers and metal plates are common.

PA.title: Eye Warning Signs
PA.description: Red octagonal signs with a realistic eye illustration are unique to Panama.

PA.title: Phone Number Area Codes
PA.description: In Panama, the first digit of a 7-digit phone number indicates the region; two-digit codes provide more precision.

PA.title: Taxi and Bus Plate Codes
PA.description: Leading digit on taxi and bus licence plates corresponds to a province in Panama.

PA.title: Colón / Panama City Tropics
PA.description: Dense green vegetation with palms and very tall grass characterizes areas around Colón and Panama City.

PA.title: Aguadulce Agriculture
PA.description: Flat terrain with agricultural fields and distinctly brown or orange soil surrounds Aguadulce.

PA.title: Eastern Vertical Pole Plates
PA.description: Tall, narrow yellow or white plates fastened to poles with black zip ties appear in eastern provinces.

PA.title: Western Horizontal Pole Plates
PA.description: Horizontal plates attached to poles are common in western provinces; eastern vertical plates override if both appear.

PA.title: Yellow Border Plates, Colón
PA.description: Thin yellow plates with a black border, vertical or horizontal, are most common in Colón Province.

PA.title: Wind Turbines Near Penonomé
PA.description: Wind turbines are visible both south and north of Penonomé.

PA.title: Country Flag
PA.description: The national flag of Panama is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PA.title: .pa Domain
PA.description: Web addresses in Panama end in the country domain .pa (often as .com.pa). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

HU.title: Street signs
HU.description: Street names in Hungary usually end with the word "utca".

HU.title: Holey poles
HU.description: Hungary has concrete utility poles with narrow rectangular holes that continue all the way to the ground.

HU.title: Hungarian language
HU.description: Hungarian is characterized by heavy use of acute accents and notably long words. Keep an eye out for the unique letters Ű and Ő.

HU.title: Hungarian bollard
HU.description: Bollards in Hungary are black and white. They have a wedge-like profile and a red reflector on the front, and a white on the back.

HU.title: Licence Plates
HU.description: Elongated white EU-format plates; taxis have yellow, electric vehicles green plates.

HU.title: Chevron Signs
HU.description: Curve warning boards with white arrows on red; less common black on white variant.

HU.title: Green Kilometre Markers
HU.description: In Hungary, small green kilometre markers are common along the roads.

HU.title: Very Tall Sign Posts
HU.description: Road sign poles are unusually tall, often taller than the Street View camera.

HU.title: Four-Bolt Sign Mounting
HU.description: Signs fastened with four bolts in a tall rectangular pattern.

HU.title: Pedestrian Crossing Sign
HU.description: Hungarian pedestrian crossing signs have a walking figure with a belt low on the body crossing five zebra stripes.

HU.title: Road Number Shields
HU.description: Hungarian routes use green signs; M motorways use blue, both with compact shield-shaped emblems.

HU.title: Green Directional Signs
HU.description: Destination boards are green with a thin white inner border; motorways use the same layout on blue.

HU.title: Winter Coverage
HU.description: Imagery was captured during colder months, showing grey, leafless scenes.

HU.title: Architecture
HU.description: Suburbs have pale stone or rendered single-storey houses with red clay tiles; central districts have older multi-storey buildings.

HU.title: Yellow Bicycle Lane Lines
HU.description: Road markings are white except bicycle lane lines, which are yellow.

HU.title: Phone Area Codes
HU.description: Landline area codes are two digits; Budapest's code is 1.

HU.title: Road Number System
HU.description: Route numbers radiate clockwise from Budapest, indicating direction from the capital.

HU.title: Town Name Prefixes
HU.description: Many settlement names have distinctive prefixes that narrow down the region.

HU.title: Metal-Framed Street Signs
HU.description: Street name plates with thick metal borders are typical in western Hungary.

HU.title: Arrow-Shaped Street Signs
HU.description: Blue or green arrow-shaped name plates on utility poles indicate Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg county in the northeast.

HU.title: Flat Southeast Farmland
HU.description: Southeastern Hungary is flat agricultural land with wide open fields.

HU.title: Northern and Western Hills
HU.description: Forested hills and low mountains cover northern and western Hungary, with tallest peaks along the northern border.

HU.title: Puszta Grasslands
HU.description: Flat, marshy natural grasslands around Hortobágy National Park, left wild and often waterlogged.

HU.title: Tornanadaska Snowy Road
HU.description: Road east of Tornanadaska with persistent snow, roadside bollards, and a parallel railway line.

HU.title: Country Flag
HU.description: The national flag of Hungary is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

HU.title: .hu Domain
HU.description: Web addresses in Hungary end in the country domain .hu. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

NA.title: Road lines
NA.description: Like many countries in Southern Africa, Namibia uses roads with single yellow outer lines and white center lines.

NA.title: Yellow plates
NA.description: Vehicles in Namibia typically carry yellow plates on both front and rear.

NA.title: White truck
NA.description: Namibian Street View coverage was captured using a white pickup truck equipped with a short front-mounted antenna that consistently tilts slightly to the left.

NA.title: German colonial influence
NA.description: Due to its history as a German colony, Namibia retains visible Germanic influence, particularly in place names and the architectural style of some older buildings.

NA.title: Desert landscape
NA.description: Desert-like landscape dominates most of Namibia, although there are a few exceptions to this.

NA.title: Green Directional Signs with Yellow Road Numbers
NA.description: Directional signs are green with yellow route numbers using A, B, C, D, M, and sometimes F designations.

NA.title: Small Stone Bollards
NA.description: Short stone bollards are common along Namibian roadsides and intersections.

NA.title: Green-and-White Metal Bins
NA.description: Cylindrical metal rubbish bins painted green and white appear at rest stops and junctions.

NA.title: Limited Coverage on Minor Roads
NA.description: Street View in Namibia is concentrated along major highways with scattered minor road coverage.

NA.title: Pavement Type and Driving Direction Map
NA.description: Map showing road surface types and Google car travel direction on major routes.

NA.title: Telephone Area Codes by Region
NA.description: Namibian area codes help pinpoint regions or cities.

NA.title: Tall Lush Trees Indicate the North
NA.description: Tall, leafy trees on both sides of the road indicate northern Namibia.

NA.title: Agricultural Land near Oshakati
NA.description: Northern Namibia near Oshakati has cultivated fields with light sandy soil and fan palms.

NA.title: Botswana-Like Landscape East of Windhoek
NA.description: East of Windhoek features flat, dry terrain with reddish earth, short grass, shrubs, and acacia trees.

NA.title: Arid Mountains in the West and South
NA.description: Western and southern Namibia have barren, dry mountains and rocky hills.

NA.title: Greener Hills in the Northwest
NA.description: Northwest hills and mountains have more vegetation with shrubs and trees.

NA.title: Coastal Sandy Terrain with Dunes
NA.description: Flat sandy coastal areas with dunes occur around and north of Swakopmund and near Luderitz and Oranjemund.

NA.title: Southeast Ridges and Rollercoaster Roads
NA.description: Southeast has small parallel ridges with red sandy soil; roads crossing them feel bumpy.

NA.title: Kunene C46 Poor Pavement & No Yellow Edges
NA.description: Near Ruacana, C46 lacks yellow edge lines, has poor cracked pavement, and dry flat terrain.

NA.title: Omusati C46 Low Sun & No Yellow Edges
NA.description: In Omusati, C46 lacks yellow edges, has poor pavement, flat terrain with sparse trees, and low sun.

NA.title: Ohangwena C41 (M123) Cloudy No-Yellow-Edge Road
NA.description: C41 in Ohangwena lacks yellow edges, runs northwest, with cloudier skies and flat terrain.

NA.title: Kavango West B10 Dense Vegetation & Moon
NA.description: East of Nkurenkuru, B10 lacks yellow edges, has dense vegetation, and a visible moon to the east.

NA.title: Kavango East B10 E-W Road with Heavy Vegetation
NA.description: West of Eenhana, B10 runs east-west without yellow edges, bordered by heavy vegetation.

NA.title: Namibia D3615 Faded Yellow Edge Lines
NA.description: D3615 has extremely faded yellow edge lines, a white dashed centre line, and dry surroundings.

NA.title: Country Flag
NA.description: The national flag of Namibia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

NA.title: .na Domain
NA.description: Web addresses in Namibia end in the country domain .na (often as .com.na). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

LB.title: Bad camera
LB.description: Lebanon is currently the only Middle Eastern country with official low-quality camera coverage.

LB.title: Arabic, French and English
LB.description: Lebanon's official language is Arabic, but French and English signage is widespread.

LB.title: White and red plates
LB.description: Lebanese plates come in long and short formats, each with a blue strip on the left resembling European plates. Taxi plates are deep red.

LB.title: Mediterranean Landscape
LB.description: Lebanon's terrain is Mediterranean, hilly, with rocky cliffs and green vegetation.

LB.title: Metallic Mesh Poles
LB.description: Lebanon uses metallic mesh (lattice) utility poles, sometimes bright yellow; wooden poles also appear.

LB.title: Sandstone Brick Buildings
LB.description: Many Lebanese buildings are made from pale sandstone blocks.

LB.title: Zahle Agricultural Fields
LB.description: Zahle area features flat farmland with mountains visible to the northwest.

LB.title: Snow-Capped Mountains
LB.description: Snow covers mountaintops or ground in northeastern mountains east of Tripoli.

LB.title: Flat Northern Plains
LB.description: Northern Lebanon is flat and agricultural, with mountains visible to the southeast.

LB.title: Trekker Coverage Overview
LB.description: Lebanese trekker imagery is sparse, mostly around tourist sites, campuses, and trails.

LB.title: Beirut
LB.description: The capital has many modern high-rises; urban structures or infrastructure are almost always visible.

LB.title: Country Flag
LB.description: The national flag of Lebanon is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LB.title: .lb Domain
LB.description: Web addresses in Lebanon end in the country domain .lb (often as .com.lb). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CL.title: White lines
CL.description: In Chile, you will usually see all white road lines.

CL.title: Yellow or white lines
CL.description: Chile can have either fully yellow or fully white lines. The two colors are almost never combined.

CL.title: Rare bollards
CL.description: Chilean bollards are white with a white reflector on the front, and a yellow on the back. They are overall quite a rare sight.

CL.title: Concrete poles
CL.description: You will find rectangular, indented concrete poles in Chile. The upper part typically has small pinholes.

CL.title: Licence Plates
CL.description: Private vehicles have white plates; taxis and commercial vehicles have orange ones.

CL.title: Slotted Signposts
CL.description: Sign poles often have open slots cut into the upper section.

CL.title: Orange Temporary Bollards
CL.description: Bright orange temporary road markers with white stripes sometimes replace permanent bollards.

CL.title: Red Bridge Posts
CL.description: Bridge railings and fence posts are commonly painted red.

CL.title: Climate Zones
CL.description: Chile spans arid desert in the north, Mediterranean near Santiago, and cold oceanic in the south.

CL.title: Regional Road Letter System
CL.description: Regional road numbers use letters from A in the north to Y in the south, indicating latitude.

CL.title: Phone Area Codes
CL.description: Landline numbers show two-digit area codes following a geographic pattern.

CL.title: Atacama Desert
CL.description: The northern third is the Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, with barren sand and rock.

CL.title: Arica y Parinacota Landscape
CL.description: Rounded, sandy-looking mountains with carved valleys are typical of the northernmost province.

CL.title: Atacama and Coquimbo Mountains
CL.description: Jagged, uneven rock formations dominate Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

CL.title: Brownish Red Soil
CL.description: Reddish-brown earth patches indicate Atacama province.

CL.title: Eucalyptus Plantations
CL.description: Rows of eucalyptus trees in semi-arid settings point to southwestern Valparaíso.

CL.title: Santiago Region Landscape
CL.description: Semi-arid hillsides with sparse scrub surround the capital.

CL.title: Maule Province
CL.description: Greener than Santiago, with vineyards common across the province.

CL.title: Concepción Pines
CL.description: Pinus radiata with fluffy needle clusters grow mainly in Bío Bío.

CL.title: Tree-Lined Narrow Roads
CL.description: Narrow roads flanked by dense trees are common in Bío Bío and Araucanía.

CL.title: Monkey Puzzle Trees
CL.description: Araucaria araucana with stiff, scaly branches grow in eastern Araucanía highlands.

CL.title: Chilean Rhubarb
CL.description: Nalca with oversized cabbage-like leaves grows on Isla Grande de Chiloé and nearby mainland.

CL.title: Southern Green Valleys
CL.description: Deep green valleys with rocky peaks and overcast skies span southern Los Lagos to northern Aysén.

CL.title: Autumn Coverage in Southern Aysén
CL.description: Southern Aysén shows vivid orange and red autumn foliage.

CL.title: Alto Bío Bío National Reserve
CL.description: A treeless highland plateau with triple yellow centre lines and monkey puzzle trees near the east.

CL.title: Orange Street Lamps
CL.description: Warm orange street lights are common in Calama and Chañaral.

CL.title: Santiago Photocell Lamps
CL.description: Light-sensitive photocells on street lamps are common in Santiago.

CL.title: Arica Pole Markings
CL.description: Utility poles in Arica have white number markings; elsewhere in Atacama Desert they are yellow.

CL.title: Country Flag
CL.description: The national flag of Chile is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CL.title: .cl Domain
CL.description: Web addresses in Chile end in the country domain .cl. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

UA.title: Red car
UA.description: In Ukraine, you will most often see the back of a red Google car.

UA.title: Ukrainian plates
UA.description: License plates in Ukraine have a strip on the left that is blue and yellow, a representation of their flag.

UA.title: Blue and yellow
UA.description: In Ukraine you may come across various pieces of infrastructure painted blue and yellow, matching the color of their flag.

UA.title: Poor Road Quality
UA.description: Ukraine has some of the worst roads in Europe, with rural roads full of potholes and cracks.

UA.title: Ukrainian Cyrillic Script
UA.description: Ukrainian uses Cyrillic with unique letters: Є є, Ґ ґ, І і, and Ї ї.

UA.title: Word for Street, вулиця (vul.)
UA.description: The Ukrainian word for street is вулиця, abbreviated вул.

UA.title: Word for City, місто (m.)
UA.description: The Ukrainian word for city is місто, abbreviated м.

UA.title: White Town Entry Signs
UA.description: Ukrainian town entry signs are white.

UA.title: Square Concrete Utility Poles
UA.description: Ukraine uses square concrete utility poles with various tops, sometimes white-painted bases.

UA.title: Diagonal Pole Support Beams
UA.description: Utility poles often have diagonal support beams.

UA.title: Wooden Poles with Concrete Bases
UA.description: Wooden utility poles with concrete bases appear in Ukraine.

UA.title: Red Chevrons with White Arrows
UA.description: Ukrainian chevrons are red with white arrows.

UA.title: Three-Stripe Pedestrian Signs
UA.description: Pedestrian crossing signs show three stripes.

UA.title: Black-and-White Guardrails
UA.description: Guardrails and barriers are often painted black and white.

UA.title: Soviet-Era Apartment Blocks
UA.description: Cities feature large Soviet-era apartment blocks of light grey brick or concrete prefab.

UA.title: Rundown Suburban Homes
UA.description: Suburbs have vegetated areas with single-family brick houses, corrugated roofs, fenced yards, and mostly unpaved roads.

UA.title: Typical Rural Scenery
UA.description: Rural Ukraine has poor roads, flat to hilly terrain, roadside trees, open farmland, little infrastructure, and low traffic.

UA.title: Summer Coverage
UA.description: Most Ukrainian coverage was shot in summer.

UA.title: Tall Poplar Trees
UA.description: Tall, columnar poplar trees are common across Ukraine.

UA.title: Ultra-Rural Tracks Near Cities
UA.description: Ultra-rural dirt tracks near cities appear commonly in Ukraine.

UA.title: Oblast Internet Domains
UA.description: Oblast-specific second-level domains (e.g. .te.ua) appear on signs and are mostly intuitive.

UA.title: Carpathian Mountains
UA.description: Western Ukraine's Carpathians are hillier and forested with pine trees and curving roads.

UA.title: Baltic Pine Forests in the North
UA.description: Northern Ukraine near Belarus has forests of tall Baltic pines with orange-red bark.

UA.title: Drier Landscape in the South
UA.description: Southern Ukraine is warmer and drier with shrubs and open fields.

UA.title: Blooming Sunflower Fields in the South and East
UA.description: Blooming sunflower fields appear mainly in southern and eastern Ukraine by late July.

UA.title: Russian Language in the East and South
UA.description: Russian text appears in eastern and southern Ukraine with letters Ы ы and Э э.

UA.title: Polish-Style Bollards in Zakarpattia
UA.description: Bollards with red reflectors wrapping around appear in Zakarpattia Oblast.

UA.title: Hungarian Language Near the Border
