UA.description: Near the Hungarian border, signs are bilingual or monolingual Hungarian.

UA.title: Country Flag
UA.description: The national flag of Ukraine is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

UA.title: .ua Domain
UA.description: Web addresses in Ukraine end in the country domain .ua (often as .com.ua). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

BW.title: Black and yellow signposts
BW.description: If you're in southern Africa and come across this, you know you're in Botswana.

BW.title: Yellow rear plates
BW.description: Botswana and Namibia are the only countries in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are the norm.

BW.title: Arid landscape
BW.description: The terrain in Botswana is predominantly flat and arid with scattered small trees. Soil is generally sandy and pale white.

BW.title: Road numbers
BW.description: Wayfinding signs use a green background, consistent with the wider southern African convention. Only in Botswana do major roads start with an A.

BW.title: Language
BW.description: Road signage is in English; place names derive from Tswana and local languages.

BW.title: Road Line Colours
BW.description: Edge lines in Botswana are yellow and centre lines are white.

BW.title: Striped Curbs and Guardrails
BW.description: Kerbs and guardrails are painted in black-and-yellow, red-and-white, or black-and-white stripes.

BW.title: Legacy Blue Signs
BW.description: Older road signs have blue backgrounds but are being replaced by white-background signs.

BW.title: Architecture
BW.description: Housing in Botswana ranges from tin-roof shacks to single-storey bungalows and occasional traditional circular huts.

BW.title: Random Small Blurs
BW.description: Google's blurring algorithm places small random patches of blur, mostly in towns.

BW.title: Region Map
BW.description: Botswana has distinct landscape zones marked by soil colour and vegetation.

BW.title: Paved vs Unpaved Roads
BW.description: Map shows which routes are surfaced and which are dirt or gravel.

BW.title: Elevation
BW.description: Most of Botswana is flat; hills appear mainly in two areas with some isolated outcrops.

BW.title: Southeast Scrub Hills
BW.description: Between Gaborone and Lobatse are low, scrubby hills in a semi-arid setting.

BW.title: Eastern Red Soil Pocket
BW.description: North of Francistown, soil is firm, rocky red with yellowed or leafless trees.

BW.title: White Sand Region
BW.description: Mid-western interior has bright white sandy soil and parched vegetation.

BW.title: Gaborone
BW.description: The capital is more developed and affluent, mostly flat with some southern hills.

BW.title: Chobe Flood Plains
BW.description: Northern area near Chobe River has dirt tracks, dense green bush, and visible wildlife.

BW.title: Salt Pans
BW.description: Central-east has vast salt flats around Nwetwe pan, accessed by dirt roads.

BW.title: Country Flag
BW.description: The national flag of Botswana is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BW.title: Road Signs Description Striped
BW.description: Sign posts in Botswana are commonly seen striped in black and yellow.

BW.title: .bw Domain
BW.description: Web addresses in Botswana end in the country domain .bw. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

FR.title: Blue stickers
FR.description: Small blue rectangular "stickers" on utility poles are a distinctive clue for France.

FR.title: Street names
FR.description: 'Rue' is the standard French word for street and appears on countless signs throughout the country.

FR.title: Ladder poles
FR.description: France have concrete utility poles with a series of step-like indentations. This design is referred to as a 'ladder pole'.

FR.title: Road numbers
FR.description: Yellow road signs beginning with “D” are specific to France and are often placed above direction signs or on town entry signs.

FR.title: Licence Plates
FR.description: Modern French plates are white rectangles with blue bands on left and right edges.

FR.title: French Language
FR.description: French uses diacritics like é, à, â, ë, œ, ç and the suffix '-ux'.

FR.title: Pointed-Top Bollard
FR.description: White cylindrical bollard tapering to a conical point with a reflector band.

FR.title: Double-Band Bollard
FR.description: White round bollard with two indented reflective rings, sometimes green or yellow.

FR.title: Wedge-Shaped Bollard
FR.description: Tapered wedge-profile post with broad rectangular white reflectors on both faces.

FR.title: Wooden and Octagonal Metal Poles
FR.description: Rural areas have timber poles alongside slender octagonal metal ones.

FR.title: French Pole Tops
FR.description: Diamond-shaped insulators supporting three wires, known as 'French pole tops', appear most commonly atop ladder poles.

FR.title: Arrowhead Pole Tops
FR.description: A variant with insulators on top creating an arrowhead silhouette, found only in France.

FR.title: Road Signs 01 Road Numbers
FR.description: Yellow road signs beginning with “D” are specific to France and are often placed above direction signs or on town entry signs.

FR.title: Directional Signs
FR.description: Local direction signs are white with a thick black border at the arrow point; highways use blue or green backgrounds.

FR.title: Town Entrance Signs
FR.description: Settlements are announced by white signs framed with a red border and thin outer white rim.

FR.title: Road Sign Borders
FR.description: Regulatory signs have a red border with a narrow white outline; white sub-signs with black text often attached below.

FR.title: Flat Signposts
FR.description: Traffic signs often mounted on flat rectangular posts; posts and sign backs may be painted in unusual, regionally distinctive colours.

FR.title: Short Signposts
FR.description: Unusually short poles supporting traffic signs at low heights are common across France.

FR.title: Chevrons
FR.description: Curve warning boards use white arrows on a blue background, displaying one to five arrows.

FR.title: Pedestrian Signs
FR.description: Crossing signs show a figure with a detached circular head walking over five zebra stripes, enclosed by a white-outline border.

FR.title: Kilometre Markers
FR.description: Distance posts combine a yellow or red semicircle atop a white rectangle; major motorways use square markers topped in red.

FR.title: Dashed Outer Lines
FR.description: Edge markings on standard French roads are widely spaced, elongated white dashes.

FR.title: Offset Block Middle Lines
FR.description: Centre-line dashes formed by two staggered blocks, found only in France.

FR.title: Long Middle Dashes
FR.description: Centre line dashes noticeably longer than the European norm can indicate France.

FR.title: End-of-Passing-Zone Arrows
FR.description: Painted arrows indicating the end of an overtaking zone, accompanied by tightly spaced centre dashes.

FR.title: Red-White-Red Flag Markers
FR.description: Tall narrow rectangles on sticks painted red-white-red stripes, reminiscent of the Austrian flag, appear on French roads.

FR.title: Architecture
FR.description: Typical French houses are stone, unpainted or pale pastel, with simple gable roofs of orange tiles or dark slate; urban terraced houses line roads.

FR.title: Blue House Numbers
FR.description: Address plaques are predominantly blue with serif typeface and ornate numerals.

FR.title: French Car Brands
FR.description: Peugeot, Renault, and Citroën make up roughly half of all vehicles on the road.

FR.title: Administrative Divisions
FR.description: Metropolitan France has 13 regions and 96 departments; department logos appear on public infrastructure.

FR.title: Telephone Area Codes
FR.description: Phone numbers are ten digits; first pairs indicate broad zones, with 06–09 for mobile and non-regional.

FR.title: Postal Codes
FR.description: Five-digit postal codes start with the department number, also shown on licence plates.

FR.title: Department Logos
FR.description: Nearly every department has a unique logo appearing on bus stops, distance markers, and signs.

FR.title: Occitanie Region Logo
FR.description: A red-and-yellow emblem combining an Occitan cross with vertical stripes identifies Occitanie.

FR.title: Pyrénées-Orientales Senyera Flag
FR.description: Pyrénées-Orientales uses red-and-yellow stripes (Senyera pattern) as its official flag and logo.

FR.title: Red-Tinted Roads
FR.description: Asphalt with red, purple, or burgundy hues is concentrated between Paris and Dijon, roughly Burgundy.

FR.title: Dark Green Signposts
FR.description: Sign poles and backs painted dark green appear mainly in Brittany, Paris area, and some southern regions.

FR.title: Eure-et-Loir Signbacks
FR.description: In Eure-et-Loir, sign backs may have a green sticker with the department's logo on a dark green backing.

FR.title: Greyish-Green Signbacks
FR.description: Muted greyish-green sign backs on darker green posts are found in parts of Brittany, Pyrénées-Atlantiques, and near the Alps.

FR.title: Pas-de-Calais Green Signs
FR.description: Road signs have dark green posts with lighter green backs from matcha to turquoise. The green-and-blue triangle logo may appear.

FR.title: Brown Signbacks
FR.description: Signs with brown poles and backs are characteristic of Seine-et-Marne.

FR.title: Paris Metro Street Signs
FR.description: Street plaques in Paris suburbs often include the municipality name in a modern design.

FR.title: Corsican Stone Barriers
FR.description: Blocky crash barriers made from rough stone and mortar are common on Corsica.

FR.title: Topography
FR.description: Highest peaks are in the southeast (Alps) and along the Spanish border (Pyrenees). North and Atlantic coast are flat to rolling; southern interior is hillier.

FR.title: Hedge-Lined Roads
FR.description: Narrow rural lanes hemmed by tall hedges are most common in the northwest, especially Normandy.

FR.title: Stone Pines
FR.description: Umbrella-shaped stone pines line many roads along the Mediterranean coast, sometimes as far north as Nantes.

FR.title: Maritime Pine Forests
FR.description: Dense maritime pine stands cover the flat Gironde and Landes departments in the southwest.

FR.title: Wine Regions
FR.description: Major vineyard regions include Bordeaux, Mediterranean coast, Champagne, Loire Valley, Alsace, and Corsica.

FR.title: Wind Turbines
FR.description: Wind farms are more common in the northern half of France.

FR.title: Black Shingle Roofs
FR.description: Slate or dark shingle roofs dominate northwest of the Loire, near the Belgian border, south-centre, and the Pyrenees.

FR.title: Brittany Architecture
FR.description: Dark slate roofs, dark or brown stone walls, and light-coloured rendered buildings are characteristic of Brittany.

FR.title: Southern Rounded Roof Tiles
FR.description: Roofs in the south have curved overlapping tiles in terracotta to faded orange shades.

FR.title: Flemish Brick Houses
FR.description: Rows of dark red brick terraced houses with white mortar joints cluster near the Belgian border.

FR.title: Paris Surroundings Stone Walls
FR.description: Walls of rough cream-to-orange stones with red brick accents characterize towns around Paris.

FR.title: French Riviera
FR.description: Palm-lined avenues and pale multi-storey buildings with balconies typify the Côte d'Azur and southern coast.

FR.title: Basque Timber-Framed Houses
FR.description: White walls with bold, colorful timber framing matching shutters and gates are hallmarks of the Basque region.

FR.title: Alpine Architecture
FR.description: Light masonry ground floors with large wooden upper storeys and balconies are typical in eastern mountain valleys.

FR.title: Alsace Germanic Architecture
FR.description: Half-timbered facades, half-hip roofs, and fish-scale roof tiles are concentrated in Alsace.

FR.title: Minority Languages Overview
FR.description: Six minority languages are regionally significant: Alsatian, Basque, Breton, Catalan, Corsican, and Occitan.

FR.title: Breton Language
FR.description: A Celtic tongue with letters d, k, w, and ñ; 'straed' means street; bilingual signs reach east to Rennes.

FR.title: Plou- Town Name Prefix
FR.description: Place names starting with 'Plou-' cluster in northwest Brittany.

FR.title: Alsatian Language
FR.description: An Alemannic German dialect in Alsace; bilingual signs use 'gasse' or 'strasse'.

FR.title: Occitan Language
FR.description: A Romance language in southern France; street is 'carrièra' in Toulouse, 'carriero' in Avignon.

FR.title: French Basque Language
FR.description: Basque appears on bilingual signs near the Spanish border; street is 'karrika'.

FR.title: Corsican Language
FR.description: A Romance language with Italian roots; words often end in vowels like -u, -iu, -ju.

FR.title: Catalan Language
FR.description: Catalan signage in Pyrénées-Orientales; frequent cedilla (Ç); street is 'carrer'.

FR.title: Town Name Suffixes
FR.description: Town name endings vary by region and help narrow down locations in France.

FR.title: River-Based Town Names
FR.description: Many towns include a river name in '-sur-[river]' format; coastal towns end in '-sur-mer' or '-plage'.

FR.title: Lavender Fields
FR.description: Southeastern France has lavender plantations appearing as rows of small grey-green bushes when not in bloom.

FR.title: Thin Guardrails
FR.description: Thin guardrails appear on motorways in northern France around Le Mans, Tours, Paris, Reims, and Metz.

FR.title: Country Flag
FR.description: The national flag of France is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

FR.title: .fr Domain
FR.description: Web addresses in France end in the country domain .fr. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

GL.title: Quad bike
GL.description: In Tasiilaq, you can usually recognize the coverage by the quad bike with large grey handguards.

GL.title: Colorful houses
GL.description: Most residential buildings on Greenland are painted in bright colors, often red, green or blue.

GL.title: Cold barrens
GL.description: The terrain on Greenland is entirely devoid of trees and tall plants. The ground is frequently blanketed in snow.

GL.title: Close to water
GL.description: You are bound to spot water in Greenland as almost all settlements are set on the shore.

GL.title: Coverage Overview
GL.description: Street View in Greenland is fragmented into many isolated pockets along the southern western coastline, each with distinctive vehicles, weather, and terrain.

GL.title: Unusual Street View Vehicles
GL.description: Each location features its own quirky vehicle, from red tractors to snowmobiles with large boxes.

GL.title: White-Cabin Red-Roof Boat
GL.description: A boat with a white cabin topped by a red roof appears at numerous west-coast towns, mainly around Aasiaat.

GL.title: Red Square-Cabin Boat
GL.description: A vessel with a distinctive red square-shaped cabin visits several west-coast settlements, densest near Akunnaaq.

GL.title: Black-Box Boat
GL.description: A boat with a black box near the bow and a chequered pattern navigates the northern east coast.

GL.title: Bright Red Boat
GL.description: A vivid red boat operates near two east-coast settlements: off Tiilerilaaq and Kuummiit.

GL.title: Country Flag
GL.description: The national flag of Greenland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

GL.title: .gl Domain
GL.description: Web addresses in Greenland end in the country domain .gl. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

IE.title: Dashed outer lines
IE.description: Irish roads often have dashed yellow outlines.

IE.title: Irish plates
IE.description: Irish license plates are white and have the standard EU blue strip on the left.

IE.title: Give way signs
IE.description: In Ireland the triangular give way signs say 'YIELD'.

IE.title: Bilingual signs
IE.description: Irish road signs usually carry text in both English and Irish.

IE.title: Architecture
IE.description: Rural houses are cream with dark slate roofs; urban streets have terraced row houses.

IE.title: Diamond-Shaped Warning Signs
IE.description: Irish hazard warnings use yellow diamond-shaped boards, unique in Europe.

IE.title: Chevron Signs
IE.description: Curve warnings show yellow arrows on black background.

IE.title: Pole Warning Stickers
IE.description: Yellow hazard stickers on poles show a lightning bolt without electrocuted figure.

IE.title: Green-and-White Bollards
IE.description: Roadside posts in Ireland are painted green and white.

IE.title: Rounded-Corner Farm Gates
IE.description: Metal field gates almost always have rounded top corners.

IE.title: Boreens (Grass-Centre Lanes)
IE.description: Narrow rural tracks often have a grass strip down the centre.

IE.title: Green Hedgerow Landscape
IE.description: Lush farmland bordered by dense hedgerows dominates the country.

IE.title: Wooden Utility Poles with Step Rungs
IE.description: Timber poles have thin horizontal metal climbing pegs up one side.

IE.title: Double Yellow No-Parking Lines
IE.description: Double yellow lines along kerbs indicate no-parking zones.

IE.title: Pedestrian Crossing Markers
IE.description: Crossings are marked by black-and-white striped posts topped with a yellow globe, like in the UK.

IE.title: Regional Road Numbers
IE.description: Regional roads have three-digit numbers; the first digit indicates the area arranged anti-clockwise from Dublin.

IE.title: Phone Area Codes
IE.description: Landline numbers start with a two-digit area code whose first digit corresponds to a geographic region.

IE.title: Rugged West Coast
IE.description: The west coast has steep hills, low mountains, open moorland, brownish-yellow grass, and occasional bare rock.

IE.title: Donegal Rural Roads
IE.description: Very narrow, unmarked roads with grassy centers in hilly terrain are typical of County Donegal.

IE.title: Wicklow Mountains
IE.description: Upland area south of Dublin with minor roads having newer coverage and no sea views.

IE.title: Grey EV Camera Car
IE.description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the rear edge of the camera view, common in eastern Ireland.

IE.title: Grey EV Camera Car
IE.description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular marking at the rear of the camera view used in County Donegal.

IE.title: Grey EV Camera Car
IE.description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the rear edge of the camera image in County Londonderry.

IE.title: Grey EV Camera Car
IE.description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular marking at the rear of the camera view in County Tyrone.

IE.title: Grey EV Camera Car
IE.description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the back edge of the camera view in County Fermanagh.

IE.title: Grey EV Camera Car
IE.description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the rear of the camera view in County Antrim.

IE.title: Grey EV Camera Car
IE.description: A grey electric vehicle with a black semicircular shape at the back edge of the camera view in County Down.

IE.title: Sligo/Leitrim Tabletop Mountains
IE.description: Flat-topped mesa-like mountains rise above the landscape in northern counties Sligo and Leitrim.

IE.title: Hilly Cork
IE.description: Cork is notable among major Irish cities for its markedly hilly topography.

IE.title: Country Flag
IE.description: The national flag of Ireland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

IE.title: .ie Domain
IE.description: Web addresses in Ireland end in the country domain .ie. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CZ.title: Arrow Signs
CZ.description: Directional signs in Czechia taper to a solid filled arrow tip.

CZ.title: Double orange
CZ.description: The Czech bollards feature two orange reflectors stacked on top of each other on traffic side

CZ.title: Double poles
CZ.description: Round concrete utility poles are common in Czechia. They are frequently installed in joined pairs.

CZ.title: Street numbers
CZ.description: Building numbers in Czechia are displayed on small blue or red signs lined with a thin white border.

CZ.title: Wide Guardrails
CZ.description: Czechia and Slovakia use a broad variant of guardrail unique in Europe.

CZ.title: Short Metal Bar Pole Tops
CZ.description: Czech pole tops commonly have compact horizontal metal bars carrying line insulators.

CZ.title: Inverted Triangle Pole Supports
CZ.description: Angled braces supporting the crossarm create an inverted-triangle silhouette at the pole top.

CZ.title: Trident Pole Tops
CZ.description: A distinctive pole-top design with three prongs forming a trident-like profile.

CZ.title: Bolt-Mounted Lamp Bases
CZ.description: Street lamp posts often have chunky base plates secured by pairs of protruding bolts.

CZ.title: Red-and-White Striped Temporary Signposts
CZ.description: Square temporary sign poles wrapped in alternating red and white bands are common.

CZ.title: Chevrons
CZ.description: Curve warning boards are white with a red arrow; a less common variant uses red arrows on yellow.

CZ.title: Striped Gas and Water Marker Poles
CZ.description: Slender roadside poles painted in coloured stripes mark underground gas or water lines.

CZ.title: Hiking Trail Markers
CZ.description: Painted blazes with a coloured band between two white bands mark walking trails and directions.

CZ.title: Colourful Panel Apartment Blocks
CZ.description: Soviet-era prefabricated housing blocks are well maintained and decorated with bold colours and patterns.

CZ.title: Diamond-Shaped Roof Tiles
CZ.description: Roofing tiles cut into a diamond pattern are common on residential buildings.

CZ.title: Bridge End Markers
CZ.description: Dark plaques at bridge ends display the road number on the left side.

CZ.title: Czech vs Slovak Script
CZ.description: Czech uses Ř, Ě, and Ů; Slovak uses Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ, and Ĺ to distinguish their similar scripts.

CZ.title: Rolling Landscape
CZ.description: The Czech terrain is gently undulating with hills but few tall mountains.

CZ.title: Solid Edge Lines, No Centre Line
CZ.description: Many Czech roads have continuous white edge lines but no painted centre line.

CZ.title: Inset Sign Borders
CZ.description: Czech road signs have coloured borders separated from the edge by a narrow background strip.

CZ.title: Highway Sign Double Border
CZ.description: Motorway signs feature a white inner border framed by a second border in the sign's main colour.

CZ.title: Bright Red Street Name Signs
CZ.description: Street signs are vivid red plates, either wide on walls or narrow on posts; sometimes blue.

CZ.title: Black Signpost Caps
CZ.description: Czech sign poles have chunky black caps on top.

CZ.title: Five-Stripe Pedestrian Signs
CZ.description: Pedestrian crossing signs show a figure walking across five horizontal stripes.

CZ.title: Thin Road Sign Font
CZ.description: Text on Czech road signs uses a noticeably lightweight typeface.

CZ.title: Kilometre Markers
CZ.description: Czech distance markers are framed in black with a yellow outline and lack the horizontal dividing line of Slovak markers.

CZ.title: Yellow Bicycle Signs
CZ.description: Cycle route markers in Czechia are yellow, replacing white bands used in hiking markers.

CZ.title: Semi-Detached Suburban Houses
CZ.description: Czech suburban homes are often mirror-image pairs sharing a dividing wall.

CZ.title: Winter Imagery
CZ.description: Many Czech images show overcast, grey winter scenes sometimes dusted with snow.

CZ.title: Railway Crossing Signs
CZ.description: Czech level-crossing signs are bare cross shapes without backing panels.

CZ.title: Road Number Regions
CZ.description: Road numbers start with digits 1 to 6 indicating regions; 7, 8, and 9 radiate from Prague northwards.

CZ.title: Cycle Path Numbers
CZ.description: Four-digit cycle route numbers follow a clockwise sequence starting in Southern Bohemia.

CZ.title: Phone Area Codes
CZ.description: Czech phone numbers have 9 digits; the first 1-3 digits are geographic area codes.

CZ.title: Moravian Wine Region
CZ.description: About 95% of Czech wine production is in Moravia, marked by vineyards.

CZ.title: Northern Bohemia Solitary Hills
CZ.description: Northern Bohemia features rolling farmland interrupted by isolated cone-shaped hills, some with castles.

CZ.title: Timber-Framed Houses
CZ.description: Half-timbered houses are common along the northern border with Germany.

CZ.title: Timber Post-Supported Upper Floors
CZ.description: Northernmost houses have dark wooden columns supporting upper floors or balconies.

CZ.title: Dark Wooden Houses with White Stripes
CZ.description: Dark timber houses with white plaster or mortar lines are common in northern Czechia.

CZ.title: Moravian Town Houses
CZ.description: Moravian village houses face the road with long sides and have tall, wide front entrances.

CZ.title: Selské Baroko (Folk Baroque)
CZ.description: Selské Baroko features richly ornamented façades on modest village buildings near České Budějovice.

CZ.title: Single-Pane Windows
CZ.description: Simple single-pane windows are more frequent in northwestern Czechia.

CZ.title: Blue Street Signs
CZ.description: Blue-background street name plates are concentrated in eastern Czechia, especially Ostrava.

CZ.title: Slovak-Style White Street Signs
CZ.description: White street signs with blue text inside a red border indicate proximity to Slovakia.

CZ.title: White Street Signs with Red Text
CZ.description: White plates with red lettering appear mostly in eastern and southern Czechia.

CZ.title: White Street Signs with Blue Text
CZ.description: White plates with blue lettering are common in eastern and central-northern Czechia.

CZ.title: White Street Signs with Black Text
CZ.description: White plates with black text are frequent in the southeast and resemble blue-text signs.

CZ.title: Country Flag
CZ.description: The national flag of Czechia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CZ.title: .cz Domain
CZ.description: Web addresses in Czechia end in the country domain .cz. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CR.title: Stop signs
CR.description: In Costa Rica, stop signs show the word "ALTO" instead of "STOP".

CR.title: Spanish Language
CR.description: Costa Rica's official language is Spanish.

CR.title: Licence Plates
CR.description: Plates are compact white with blue characters, appearing faint light-blue due to blurring.

CR.title: Round Concrete Poles
CR.description: Utility poles have cylindrical concrete shafts.

CR.title: Beach Trekkers
CR.description: Shoreline trekker paths are mainly along the northern Pacific coast and Cocos Island.

CR.title: Forest Trekkers
CR.description: Trekker routes through woodland are mostly in the central highlands and Cocos Island.

CR.title: Urban Coverage Locations
CR.description: City-level trekker imagery focuses on San José and Cartago, with smaller amounts in Liberia and Filadelfia.

CR.title: Country Flag
CR.description: The national flag of Costa Rica is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CR.title: .cr Domain
CR.description: Web addresses in Costa Rica end in the country domain .cr (often as .co.cr). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

PH.title: Jeepneys
PH.description: In the Philippines it is common to find jeepneys in urban environments. They are often heavily decorated.

PH.title: English
PH.description: English is one of the official languages in the Philippines and appears on signs frequently.

PH.title: Licence Plates with Green Tint
PH.description: Many Philippine vehicles carry privately issued plates with a distinctive greenish tint.

PH.title: Octagonal Metal Poles
PH.description: Utility poles with octagonal cross-section are common in the Philippines.

PH.title: Side-Mounted Pole Insulators
PH.description: Single insulator atop a short vertical bar attached to the side of utility poles is common.

PH.title: Yellow and White Road Markings
PH.description: Philippine centre lines may be yellow, white, or a side-by-side combination.

PH.title: Yellow Kilometre Stones
PH.description: Tall, square-shaped yellow road markers unique to the Philippines.

PH.title: Red-on-White Chevron Signs
PH.description: Philippine road curve chevrons use red arrows on white backgrounds.

PH.title: Colourful Sign Posts
PH.description: Posts supporting road signs are frequently painted red, orange, or yellow.

PH.title: Tricycles / Tuk-Tuks
PH.description: Motorised tricycles (tuk-tuks) are ubiquitous and often outnumber cars.

PH.title: Grain Drying on Roads
PH.description: Harvested grain is often spread out on roads for drying.

PH.title: Regional Tricycle Designs
PH.description: Different islands and regions use distinct tricycle and tuk-tuk designs.

PH.title: Province Names on Signs
PH.description: Philippine province names appear often on signs and help with location.

PH.title: Phone Number Area Code
PH.description: Landline numbers start with 0 plus regional code; mobile numbers start with 09.

PH.title: Pine-Covered Mountains of Northern Luzon
PH.description: The mountain range in Northern Luzon features dry slopes with plentiful pine trees.

PH.title: Corn Fields
PH.description: Corn cultivation is a common sight all over the Philippines.

PH.title: Oil Palm Plantations
PH.description: Nearly all oil palm plantations are on Mindanao.

PH.title: Sugarcane Fields
PH.description: Most sugarcane is grown on Negros and Panay.

PH.title: Pineapple Plantations
PH.description: Large-scale pineapple farming is concentrated on Mindanao.

PH.title: Banana Plantations
PH.description: Commercial banana plantations are almost exclusively in central and southern Mindanao.

PH.title: Moluccan Albizia Trees
PH.description: These trees have pale trunks and feathery pinnate leaves clustered near the crown, mainly on eastern and central Mindanao.

PH.title: Amakan Walls with Diamond Pattern
PH.description: Houses with woven bamboo walls in a diamond pattern are found almost exclusively in the southern half of the Philippines.

PH.title: Amakan / Sawali Walls with Diagonal Weave
PH.description: Woven bamboo walls with a diagonal pattern are most prevalent on Palawan and across the northern half of the country.

PH.title: Yellow-and-Black Concrete Guardrails
PH.description: Concrete guardrails painted with alternating yellow and black stripes are specific to the Cordillera Administrative Region.

PH.title: Bicol Guardrails with Three Black Stripes
PH.description: White guardrails with a repeating set of three black stripes are unique to the Bicol region in southern Luzon.

PH.title: Chile-Style Indented Concrete Poles
PH.description: Square concrete utility poles with a visible indent on each side are found mainly north of Manila and around Bacolod on Negros.

PH.title: Square Metal Mesh Poles on Zamboanga
PH.description: Utility poles built from square metal mesh are found primarily on the Zamboanga peninsula in Mindanao.

PH.title: Muslim Majority Area in Western Mindanao
PH.description: A region in western Mindanao has a Muslim majority population.

PH.title: Mountain Dew Bottle Decorations
PH.description: Neon-green Mountain Dew bottles repurposed as decorations are common in northern Luzon.

PH.title: Country Flag
PH.description: The national flag of the Philippines is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PH.title: .ph Domain

SZ.title: Road numbers
SZ.description: Roads prefixed with the letters "MR" are found exclusively in Eswatini.

SZ.title: Bus shelters
SZ.description: Distinctive concrete bus shelters appear frequently along Eswatini's roads.

SZ.title: Yellow road lines
SZ.description: Just like most southern African countries, Eswatini's roads feature yellow outer lines.

SZ.title: Tall grass
SZ.description: Eswatini features stretches of tall grass.

SZ.title: Dark Brown Wooden Poles
SZ.description: Eswatini's utility poles are dark brown wood with side-mounted insulators.

SZ.title: Licence Plates
SZ.description: Eswatini plates are long with a green bottom section.

SZ.title: Western Highland Grasslands
SZ.description: Montane grasslands with golden grass and mountainous backdrop characterise the western highlands.

SZ.title: Pine Tree Plantations
SZ.description: Commercial pine plantations occur in select western areas.

SZ.title: Central-South Dark Green Region
SZ.description: Area with dark green vegetation and tall wooded mountains.

SZ.title: Eastern Flatlands
SZ.description: Eswatini's eastern lowlands have flat terrain with distant mountains.

SZ.title: Sugarcane Along the Eastern Border
SZ.description: Sugarcane is cultivated near the eastern boundary with Mozambique.

SZ.title: Country Flag
SZ.description: The national flag of Eswatini is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SZ.title: .sz Domain
SZ.description: Web addresses in Eswatini end in the country domain .sz. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

GH.title: Yellow and white plates
GH.description: In Ghana private vehicles carry white plates, while commercial vehicles use yellow ones. Both colours are frequently visible.

GH.title: Red soil
GH.description: The terrain in Ghana is predominantly flat and lush, with characteristic red laterite soil.

GH.title: Ghana tape
GH.description: One of the most (in)famous hints in Geoguessr is the tape on the top-right bar that can be seen when looking down. It can only be found in Ghana.

GH.title: White Road Lines
GH.description: Where present, road markings are always white; many paved roads lack markings.

GH.title: Wooden Poles
GH.description: Utility poles are timber posts with metal crossbars carrying three porcelain insulators.

GH.title: National Flag Colours
GH.description: Kerbs, poles, and fences are often painted red, gold, and green, sometimes with the black star from the flag.

GH.title: Striped Signposts
GH.description: Traffic sign poles have alternating black-and-white bands in urban areas; plain metal posts in the countryside.

GH.title: Paved vs Unpaved Roads
GH.description: Map showing which roads are surfaced and which are dirt tracks across Ghana.

GH.title: Northern Savannah
GH.description: Northern Ghana features savannah with open grassland, sparser trees, and drier, paler soil.

GH.title: Mountain Ranges near Lake Volta
GH.description: Hill and mountain ranges are concentrated around Lake Volta.

GH.title: Dense Forests
GH.description: Thick tropical forest with abundant palms is found in southwest and eastern Ghana.

GH.title: Coastal Palm Trees
GH.description: Tall palms line much of the coastline, especially along the western shore.

GH.title: East of Accra Coast
GH.description: The coastal strip east of Accra along the N1 is flat, open, and sparsely vegetated, appearing almost arid.

GH.title: Nature Reserve Car
GH.description: Several nature reserves use a different Google vehicle, white with visible side mirrors, though the characteristic Ghana roof-rack tape remains in place.

GH.title: Country Flag
GH.description: The national flag of Ghana is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

GH.title: .gh Domain
GH.description: Web addresses in Ghana end in the country domain .gh. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

LS.title: Mountains
LS.description: Bare, treeless mountains with flat tabletop profiles and prominent horizontal rock ridgelines are Lesotho's signature feature.

LS.title: Round huts
LS.description: Round thatched-roof huts appear frequently in rural Lesotho.

LS.title: Driving side
LS.description: Lesotho drives on the left, in common with its southern African neighbours.

LS.title: Short grass
LS.description: Lesotho's grasslands consist predominantly of short grass, unlike Eswatini which in general has tall grass.

LS.title: Licence Plate
LS.description: Lesotho plates are long and white with blue text and a Mokorotlo hat symbol on the left.

LS.title: Road Lines
LS.description: Lesotho's edge lines are yellow and centre lines are white.

LS.title: Triple Centre Lines
LS.description: Some Lesotho roads have a unique triple centre-line: two solid lines flanking a dashed line.

LS.title: Agave Plants
LS.description: Agave plants are widespread in Lesotho countryside.

LS.title: Traditional Basotho Blankets
LS.description: Many people, especially in rural areas, wear traditional Basotho woollen blankets.

LS.title: Free-Roaming Livestock
LS.description: Lesotho's roads are frequently shared with wandering cattle, horses, donkeys, and other farm animals.

LS.title: Flat Western Region
LS.description: The western lowlands are flat or gently hilly with visible tabletop mountains, dense coverage, settlements, and agriculture.

LS.title: Mountainous Eastern Region
LS.description: In the east, roads run along grassy mountainsides with limited coverage on six main roads.

LS.title: Country Flag
LS.description: The national flag of Lesotho is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LS.title: .ls Domain
LS.description: Web addresses in Lesotho end in the country domain .ls. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MG.title: A wild ride
MG.description: Much of the Madagascar coverage was captured using different types of transportation, including boats and cow carts.

MG.title: A personal touch
MG.description: The people capturing the Madagascar images can often be seen in them.

MG.title: Baobabs
MG.description: The famous Avenue of the Baobabs is unmistakable thanks to the enormously thick-trunked baobab trees flanking the road.

MG.title: Varying nature
MG.description: Madagascar's southern and central regions tend to be very arid, while the north is tropical and lush.

MG.title: French and Malagasy Language
MG.description: Madagascar's official languages are French and Malagasy, which uses the Latin alphabet and long, multi-syllable words.

MG.title: Limited and Mostly Trekker-Based Coverage
MG.description: Street View in Madagascar is sparse, mainly along or near the west coast, mostly from trekkers with two exceptions using a Street View car.

MG.title: Southern Atolls, Broad-Leaved Palms
MG.description: Atolls are small and have broad-leaved palms, a tree type rare elsewhere on the island.

MG.title: Country Flag
MG.description: The national flag of Madagascar is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MG.title: .mg Domain
MG.description: Web addresses in Madagascar end in the country domain .mg. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

ST.title: Bad camera
ST.description: The entire São Tomé and Príncipe street view coverage was done using official low-quality camera, with a blur completely covering the car.

ST.title: Portuguese colonial influence
ST.description: Portuguese is the primary language of São Tomé and Príncipe and can hence be seen on most signs.

ST.title: Yellow taxis
ST.description: All cabs in São Tomé and Príncipe are yellow.

ST.title: The tropics
ST.description: São Tomé and Príncipe is located on the equator so you'll find rainforest all over the country.

ST.title: .st Domain
ST.description: Web addresses in São Tomé and Príncipe end in the country domain .st. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

BT.title: Red plates
BT.description: Bhutanese vehicles carry distinctive red license plates that are easy to spot even from a distance.

BT.title: Safety blocks
BT.description: Rows of stone blocks serve as barriers along rural roads, one of the most reliable visual cues for recognising Bhutan.

BT.title: Prayer flags
BT.description: Colorful prayer flags strung alongside roads are a common sight throughout Bhutan.

BT.title: Traditional buildings
BT.description: Traditional Bhutanese buildings have ornately painted wooden window and door frames.

BT.title: Dzongkha Script
BT.description: Bhutan's national language uses a distinctive Tibetan-derived script seen only in Bhutan on Street View.

BT.title: Mountainous Terrain
BT.description: Bhutan is mostly rugged highland with steep mountain highways.

BT.title: Thin Metal Utility Poles
BT.description: Slender metal utility poles often have the lower section painted black.

BT.title: Kilometre Markers
BT.description: Bhutanese road markers have a yellow upper half and white lower half with route numbers on national highways.

BT.title: City Direction Signs
BT.description: Urban areas have red or blue signboards usually showing the town name.

BT.title: Yellow Taxis
BT.description: Bhutanese taxis have yellow roofs and yellow licence plates.

BT.title: Striped Signposts
BT.description: Sign poles painted with alternating black-and-white bands are common.

BT.title: Double White Edge Lines
BT.description: Roads with two solid white edge lines on each side appear around Thimphu in western Bhutan.

BT.title: Flat Southern Lowlands
BT.description: Flat, open terrain occurs only in Bhutan's southern border zone.

BT.title: Country Flag
BT.description: The national flag of Bhutan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BT.title: .bt Domain
BT.description: Web addresses in Bhutan end in the country domain .bt. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

CX.title: Yellow licence plates
CX.description: Vehicles on the Christmas Island carry yellow license plates.

CX.title: Australian-style bollards
CX.description: Bollards on Christmas Island are identical to the Australian ones. White with a red vertical stripe on the front.

CX.title: Crab rave
CX.description: There are areas on Christmas island with large amounts of crabs. You can also find crab-related traffic signs throughout the island.

CX.title: Silver Pickup Truck
CX.description: Coverage uses a silver pickup truck with an open flatbed behind the camera.

CX.title: Tropical Forest Landscape
CX.description: Thick tropical rainforest with unpaved tracks, white sandy soil, settlements, and palm groves.

CX.title: Rural Trail Coverage
CX.description: Beyond paved roads, narrow overgrown bush tracks lead deep into the forest.

CX.title: Built-Up Areas
CX.description: All settlements are in the northeastern corner; elsewhere is dense jungle.

CX.title: Trail Trekkers
CX.description: Short walking trails are scattered across the island, often opening to beaches or viewpoints.

CX.title: Country Flag
CX.description: The national flag of Christmas Island is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CX.title: .cx Domain
CX.description: Web addresses in Christmas Island end in the country domain .cx. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

HK.title: Air conditioners
HK.description: Wall-mounted air-conditioning units are a common sight in Hong Kong.

HK.title: Bilingual signage
HK.description: Signage in Hong Kong routinely pairs English text with traditional Chinese characters.

HK.title: Colour-coded taxis
HK.description: Taxis in distinct colors are often seen in Hong Kong. There are red, blue and green ones. They have green stickers on the bumpers.

HK.title: Towering apartment blocks
HK.description: Residential tower blocks in Hong Kong are exceptionally tall, visibly taller than their counterparts in nearby countries.

HK.title: Yellow License Plates
HK.description: Front plates in Hong Kong are white and rear plates are yellow..

HK.title: Dense Urban Skyline
HK.description: A tightly packed metropolis with modern towers and bustling streets crowded with traffic and pedestrians.

HK.title: Green Mountainous Hinterland
HK.description: Hilly subtropical greenery beyond the urban core with roads extending into rural highlands.

HK.title: Exterior Air Conditioners
HK.description: Wall-mounted air-conditioning units are ubiquitous on apartment buildings.

HK.title: Grey Lamp Posts with Wide Base
HK.description: Cylindrical grey street lamps flaring at the base, often with a small white sticker.

HK.title: Rural Wooden Utility Poles
HK.description: Round timber utility poles appear only in rural areas, often carrying meters or transformers.

HK.title: No Striped Kerbs
HK.description: Painted kerb stripes are virtually absent; grey pedestrian guardrails are common instead.

HK.title: Yellow Pedestrian Crossings
HK.description: Crosswalks and some junctions feature yellow paint markings.

HK.title: Road Markings
HK.description: White centre lines; white or yellow edge lines; concrete road surfaces common.

HK.title: Bilingual Road Signs
HK.description: White rectangular directional signs with thick black border and English and Chinese text.

HK.title: Give Way Signs
HK.description: Inverted white triangle with heavy red border and bilingual give-way text.

HK.title: Mountainside Retaining Walls
HK.description: Exposed weathered rock faces along hillside roads, sometimes with wire netting and small plaques.

HK.title: Fire Hydrants
HK.description: Typically red with domed top and three outlets; shape is a reliable identifier.

HK.title: Yellow Traffic Bollards
HK.description: Yellow posts topped with blue circle and white directional arrow at crossings and lane dividers.

HK.title: Bright Orange Litter Bins
HK.description: Vivid orange waste bins stand on pavements throughout the territory.

HK.title: Double-Decker Buses
HK.description: Most public buses are double-deckers with various color schemes; minibuses have green or red roofs.

HK.title: Boxy Village Houses
HK.description: Low-rise, boxy multi-storey houses typical of small villages in the northern New Territories.

HK.title: Mong Kok and Surrounding Kowloon
HK.description: Dense grid-pattern streets with older apartment blocks above ground-floor shops.

HK.title: Northwestern Rice Paddies
HK.description: Flat lowlands near the China border with waterlogged rice fields and Shenzhen skyline visible.

HK.title: Caribbean Coast and Tung Chung
HK.description: Matching residential towers forming a wall-like facade with palm trees lining the streets.

HK.title: Country Flag
HK.description: The national flag of Hong Kong is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

HK.title: .hk Domain
HK.description: Web addresses in Hong Kong end in the country domain .hk (often as .com.hk). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

IL.title: Yellow license plates
IL.description: License plates in Israel are yellow and have a blue strip on the left.

IL.title: Literal stop signage
IL.description: Israeli stop signs have no text. Instead they depict a raised hand, a common sign for stopping.

IL.title: Written Hebrew
IL.description: The most common text seen in Israel is Hebrew. It looks a bit blocky and has letters with mostly uniform height.

IL.title: Colorful small signs
IL.description: In Israel you can find these small sings alongside roads. They come in red, green and blue.

IL.title: .il Domain
IL.description: Web addresses in Israel end in the country domain .il (often as .co.il). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

LA.title: Lao script
LA.description: Lao writing is compact and rounded, with diacritical marks above and below characters.

LA.title: Visible car
LA.description: In Laos the google car is visible with a bars sticking out. In the capital Vientiane the car is however not visible.

LA.title: Buddhist temples
LA.description: As a predominantly Buddhist country, Laos is filled with ornately decorated temples, often featuring gold leaf detailing.

LA.title: Stop signs
LA.description: Laotian stop signs display Lao script, sometimes with 'STOP' in Latin underneath. The Lao text uses only two characters.

LA.title: Licence Plates
LA.description: Laotian plates are short and yellow; commercial plates white; government plates blue.

LA.title: Striped Curbs
LA.description: Kerbstones painted in alternating red-white, yellow-white, or black-white stripes are common.

LA.title: Utility Poles
LA.description: Laotian utility poles are square concrete columns with vertical rows of small pinholes.

LA.title: Black-and-White Bollards
LA.description: Laos uses square concrete bollards with black bands on a white body.

LA.title: Lamp Post Markings
LA.description: Some Laotian lamp posts have diagonal red-and-white stripes stopping short of the base.

LA.title: Red-and-White Concrete Bollards
LA.description: Cuboid concrete bollards painted red and white appear a few metres off the roadside.

LA.title: Communist Flags
LA.description: Laos occasionally displays red hammer-and-sickle flags.

LA.title: Palm Trees
LA.description: Palm trees are common in Luang Prabang's streetscape.

LA.title: Flat Terrain
LA.description: Savannakhet is exceptionally flat with slightly reddish soil.

LA.title: Red Soil and Dry Hills
LA.description: Pakse has vivid red soil and dry, arid vegetation with parched hills nearby.

LA.title: Country Flag
LA.description: The national flag of Laos is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LA.title: .la Domain
LA.description: Web addresses in Laos end in the country domain .la. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

NP.title: Napal plates
NP.description: Nepal uses long plates. The standard versions are white, while private vehicles carry red plates and public transport uses black ones.

NP.title: Bad camera
NP.description: All imagery in Nepal comes from a notoriously poor camera, recognized by low sharpness and washed-out colors.

NP.title: Yellow outer lines
NP.description: Nepali roads frequently have yellow edge markings, either dashed or solid, paired with white dashed center lines on wider routes.

NP.title: Concrete bollards
NP.description: Roadside bollards in Nepal are concrete with alternating black and white stripes (between 3 and 5 bands) and typically have a red mark on the cap.

NP.title: Devanagari Script
NP.description: Nepali text uses Devanagari, with a horizontal bar atop words and prominent vertical strokes.

NP.title: Utility Poles and Trident Tops
NP.description: Flat areas have square concrete poles; mountains use slender metal ones. Pole tops often have a trident shape.

NP.title: Flat South vs. Mountainous North
NP.description: Southern Nepal is flat farmland; northern half has high-altitude mountain roads with dramatic elevation changes.

NP.title: Building Styles and Triangles
NP.description: Buildings range from colourful blocky structures to smaller houses with triangular ornamental motifs.

NP.title: Black-and-White Signposts
NP.description: Sign poles feature alternating black and white stripes along their length.

NP.title: White Buddhist Stupas
NP.description: White-painted Buddhist stupas, sometimes with painted eyes, are unique to Nepal.

NP.title: District Names on Addresses
NP.description: District names often appear in postal addresses in English alongside Devanagari.

NP.title: Flat Southern Plains vs. Mountains
NP.description: The far southern strip is flat; central and northern regions have steep, rugged terrain.

NP.title: Dry Western Hills
NP.description: Western hills have an arid look with large stretches of bare, unvegetated hillside.

NP.title: Areca Palms in Southeast
NP.description: Areca palms with slender trunks and compact crowns grow mainly in southeastern lowlands.

NP.title: Canola Fields
NP.description: Canola with vivid yellow blossoms grows in southern pockets of western Nepal.

NP.title: Chir Pine Trees
NP.description: Chir pines have smooth conical crowns with long needles, prevalent in the west and near Kathmandu.

NP.title: Japanese Cedar Trees
NP.description: Japanese cedars in far eastern Nepal are tall with narrow, feathery crowns.

NP.title: Tea Plantations
NP.description: Tea cultivation occurs only in far eastern Nepal on mountain slopes and flatlands.

NP.title: Rounded Roof Tiles
NP.description: Fully rounded clay roof tiles are common south of Kathmandu and westward.

NP.title: West Bengal Style Roof Tiles
NP.description: Tiles with small diamond-shaped bumps are concentrated in far western plains.

NP.title: Irregular Rectangular Roof Tiles
NP.description: Rectangular stone tiles laid unevenly are typical of western mountain towns and central areas.

NP.title: Corrugated Metal Roofs
NP.description: Corrugated sheet metal roofs are common between Birgunj and Janakpur.

NP.title: Roof Railings in Western Nepal
NP.description: Dark concrete railings run along roof edges in parts of western Nepal, especially Tulsipur valley.

NP.title: Stick Fences
NP.description: Fences made from sticks, varying in quality, are common in the eastern flatlands.

NP.title: Sheet Metal Roofs with Triangular Window
NP.description: Roofs in the far east are sheet metal with a small triangular window below the ridge and an outward-angled section beneath it.

NP.title: Hip Roofs with Tiny Metal Ridge Protrusion
NP.description: Sheet metal hip roofs with a small metal protrusion at the ridge are found west of and around Biratnagar.

NP.title: Mosques in Southern Nepal
NP.description: Mosques cluster in Muslim-majority pockets along the southern belt near Janakpur, Birgunj, Nepalgunj, and Biratnagar.

NP.title: Cross-Topped Utility Poles
NP.description: Utility poles with a cross-shaped attachment near the top are common in eastern Nepal.

NP.title: Yellow Water Tanks
NP.description: Yellow rooftop water tanks are predominantly found in eastern Nepal.

NP.title: Country Flag
NP.description: The national flag of Nepal is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

NP.title: .np Domain
NP.description: Web addresses in Nepal end in the country domain .np (often as .com.np). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

OM.title: Colored plates
OM.description: Omani private vehicles carry yellow licence plates, whereas commercial vehicles have red ones.

OM.title: Desert landscape
OM.description: Oman is dominated by arid, sparsely vegetated terrain. The central and southern interior is largely flat, while the northern coastline has dry, rugged mountains

OM.title: Chevrons
OM.description: Chevrons in Oman are yellow with black arrows and stand out for having an unusually high number of arrow markings.

OM.title: White truck
OM.description: All Omani Street View imagery was captured using a white pickup truck. As a result, a large portion of the vehicle or a prominent front blur is typically visible.

OM.title: Arabic
OM.description: Arabic is Oman's sole official language; signage often appears in Arabic and English.

OM.title: Yellow Edge Lines with White Centre Lines
OM.description: Omani roads have yellow lines along edges and white lines down the centre.

OM.title: Black-and-Yellow Curbs
OM.description: Kerbs painted in alternating black and yellow segments are widespread on Omani roads.

OM.title: Light Stone Architecture with Ornate Fences
OM.description: Omani homes are pale stone with decorative details, enclosed by matching stone fences with elaborate gates.

OM.title: Blue Directional Signs
OM.description: Omani road signs are blue with white lettering, showing Arabic and English text.

OM.title: Striped Signposts
OM.description: Sign poles in Oman often have alternating black-and-white horizontal stripes.

OM.title: Wooden Utility Poles
OM.description: Wooden power poles in Oman have three distinct top designs, including a unique metal triangle above one variant.

OM.title: Red-and-White High Voltage Pylons
OM.description: Electricity transmission towers painted red and white stripes are common across Oman.

OM.title: Be'ah Garbage Bins
OM.description: Omani rubbish bins are black plastic or grey metal with a three-leaf logo and 'be'ah' text.

OM.title: White Taxis with Orange Panels
OM.description: Omani taxis are white with distinctive orange panels on both sides.

OM.title: Northern Dry Mountains
OM.description: Northern Oman has arid, rocky mountain terrain resembling eastern UAE.

OM.title: Southern Rolling Hills near Salalah
OM.description: The Salalah area features hilly terrain with rocky ground, scattered bushes, small trees, and green valleys.

OM.title: Green Vegetation North of Nizwa
OM.description: Mountains north of Nizwa have lush green bushes and jagged rocky peaks.

OM.title: Acacia Trees
OM.description: Short trees with flat, umbrella-shaped canopies, acacias are most prevalent in northern Oman and some coastal areas.

OM.title: Date Palm Plantations
OM.description: Groves of date palms are concentrated along Oman's northern coast.

OM.title: Red Sandy Dunes
OM.description: Dunes with a reddish hue appear near the Saudi border and in Oman's central interior.

OM.title: Country Flag
OM.description: The national flag of Oman is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

OM.title: .om Domain
OM.description: Web addresses in Oman end in the country domain .om (often as .com.om). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

QA.title: Long and short
QA.description: Qatari private vehicles carry long white plates with a maroon strip on the left. Trucks have square black plates, and police vehicles use blue plates.

QA.title: Flat desert
QA.description: Qatar is an almost entirely flat, arid desert with vast sand expanses and very little greenery.

QA.title: Crossing sign
QA.description: Qatari pedestrian crossing signs depict a man wearing a traditional thobe.

QA.title: Football fever
QA.description: Coverage taken before the 2022 FIFA World Cup frequently shows promotional banners for the event.

QA.title: Bubble antenna
QA.description: In Qatar, the Google car usually features an antenna with a small bubble on top.

QA.title: Road Lines
QA.description: Qatari roads have solid white edge lines with white or yellow centre markings; outer yellow lines appear sometimes.

QA.title: Utility Poles
QA.description: Qatari utility poles are round with three insulators, the middle raised, supported by a crossbar with diagonal braces.

QA.title: Chevrons
QA.description: Qatari chevrons are white-on-red and white-on-blue boards.

QA.title: Zone Numbers on Street Signs
QA.description: Qatar's numbered zones appear on street signs with a reference map.

QA.title: Long Antenna, Southwest
QA.description: The longest antenna variant is mostly in southwestern Qatar.

QA.title: Country Flag
QA.description: The national flag of Qatar is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

QA.title: .qa Domain
QA.description: Web addresses in Qatar end in the country domain .qa (often as .com.qa). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

HR.title: Country stickers
HR.description: Oval stickers bearing the letters 'HR' can be sometimes be spotted on Croatian vehicles.

HR.title: Web domain
HR.description: The top domain in Croatia is .HR, originating from the local name for the country, Hrvatska.

HR.title: Croatian bollard
HR.description: Croatian bollards feature either red or white reflectors that sit on top of a black section.

HR.title: Croatian plates
HR.description: Older license plates in Croatia are fully white. Newer ones feature a blue strip on the left.

HR.title: Croatian Language
HR.description: South Slavic language in Latin script; frequent 'IJE' digraph.

HR.title: Chevron Signs
HR.description: Curve warning boards with red arrow on yellow or white background.

HR.title: B-Type Square Guardrails
HR.description: Square-profile (B-type) highway guardrails, rare in Europe.

HR.title: Autumn Foliage
HR.description: Landscapes often show golden and orange leaf colors in autumn.

HR.title: Vehicles 01 Country Stickers
HR.description: Oval stickers bearing the letters 'HR' can be sometimes be spotted on Croatian vehicles.

HR.title: Yellow Directional Signs
HR.description: Road signs have a yellow background with a black border, often tapering to a point.

HR.title: Utility Poles with Alternating Hooks
HR.description: Cylindrical concrete or timber poles; wooden ones have alternating step-pegs up each side.

HR.title: Exposed Red Brick Buildings
HR.description: Bare red brick walls on houses and outbuildings are common, especially inland.

HR.title: Blue Fire Hydrants
HR.description: Hydrants are blue with two diagonally angled outlets on each side.

HR.title: Pedestrian Crossing Sign
HR.description: Sign shows a walking figure with a visible belt crossing a zebra with five stripes.

HR.title: Local Brands
HR.description: Ads for Karlovačko and Ožujsko beer; Konzum and Plodine supermarkets appear in cities.

HR.title: Phone Area Codes
HR.description: Croatian landline numbers start with zero plus regional area code.

HR.title: Flat Slavonian Northeast
HR.description: Northeast Croatia is a broad agricultural plain.

HR.title: Hilly Zagorje Northwest
HR.description: Countryside north and west of Zagreb is rolling, hilly farmland.

HR.title: Rocky Adriatic Coast
HR.description: Coast features bare limestone mountains, scrubby Mediterranean vegetation, and many islands.

HR.title: Coastal Beige Stone Houses
HR.description: Adriatic buildings are beige stone or brick, often with green shutters.

HR.title: Istria Red Soil
HR.description: Istria peninsula has earth with a reddish hue.

HR.title: Istrian Bilingual Signs
HR.description: Street name plates in western Istria show Croatian and Italian text.

HR.title: Town Names Ending in '-ec'
HR.description: Settlement names ending in '-ec' cluster in northern inland Croatia.

HR.title: Zagreb
HR.description: Capital city with metropolitan feel, apartment blocks, hilly north, and blue electric trams.

HR.title: Tram Cities
HR.description: Only Zagreb and Osijek have tram networks.

HR.title: Plain Northeast of Zadar
HR.description: Flat lowland northeast of Zadar with a mountain ridge on the northern horizon.

HR.title: Southern Cypress Trees
HR.description: Tall, narrow cypress trees near Dubrovnik.

HR.title: Country Flag
HR.description: The national flag of Croatia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LV.title: Bus stop signs
LV.description: Latvian bus stop signs feature a bus icon with five windows, distinguishing it from the four-window design used in Lithuania and Estonia.

LV.title: Latvian plates
LV.description: Latvia have standard white EU plates with a blue strip on the left.

LV.title: Kilometer markers
LV.description: Small blue signs with numbers on them can be found in Latvia. They are placed parallel to the road.

LV.title: Latvian bollard
LV.description: Latvian bollards are white and feature a vertical reflector on the front and two round ones on the back. The reflectors can be white or orange.

LV.title: Hook-Shaped Poletop Insulators
LV.description: Latvian utility poles have hook-shaped insulators in an alternating left–right–left pattern.

LV.title: Chevrons
LV.description: Latvian chevrons are white with red arrows.

LV.title: Warning and Speed Sign Borders
LV.description: Latvian warning and speed signs have a thick red border with a thin white outline.

LV.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
LV.description: Latvian crossing signs have five stripes and a pedestrian figure with long legs.

LV.title: Guardrails with White or Red Reflectors
LV.description: Latvian guardrails are standard A-type with white or red reflectors.

LV.title: Latvian Language
LV.description: A Baltic language with unique letters: vowels with macrons (Ā Ē Ī) and consonants with cedilla hooks (Ģ Ķ Ļ Ņ).

LV.title: 'Iela' Street Label
LV.description: The Latvian word for street is iela.

LV.title: Tall Rectangular House Numbers
LV.description: Latvian house number plates are often tall rectangles in several colours.

LV.title: Architecture
LV.description: Latvian buildings mix wood and white brick under steep corrugated metal roofs; pastel-painted stone and wood-brick houses are common.

LV.title: Directional Signs
LV.description: Latvian directional signs are blue with white text and stylised arrowheads.

LV.title: Open Plains South of Jelgava
LV.description: South of Jelgava features wide-open fields with less forest than elsewhere in Latvia.

LV.title: Country Flag
LV.description: The national flag of Latvia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

LV.title: .lv Domain
LV.description: Web addresses in Latvia end in the country domain .lv. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

SG.title: Street name signs
SG.description: Singaporean street signs are green with round edges. They have a very distinctive white font.

SG.title: Green buses
SG.description: In Singapore, most buses are lime-green.

SG.title: No litter
SG.description: Singapore is exceptionally clean and have orderly streets as there are heavy fines for littering.

SG.title: English
SG.description: English is the common language in Singapore, with exclusive use in numerous public services.

SG.title: Licence Plates
SG.description: Singaporean plates are mostly black with white text, unlike Malaysian and Indonesian plates.

SG.title: Directional Signs
SG.description: Singaporean directional signs are green with white English text and expressway codes like TPE.

SG.title: Road Signs on White Backing
SG.description: All road signs are mounted on square white background panels, unique to Singapore.

SG.title: Rain Trees
SG.description: Large rain trees line many main roads throughout Singapore.

SG.title: Road Surface Warnings
SG.description: Text warnings like "HUMP AHEAD" are painted directly on Singapore roads.

SG.title: Bus Stop Bollards
SG.description: Concrete bollards with black-and-yellow bands protect every bus stop in Singapore.

SG.title: Bus-Leaving Box
SG.description: A yellow box with an arrow is sometimes painted on the road at Singapore bus stops.

SG.title: Traffic Lights
SG.description: Singaporean traffic lights have a standard design with a curved metal sheet with holes.

SG.title: Neighbourhood Names on Street Signs
SG.description: Suburban streets in Singapore often include their neighbourhood name.

SG.title: Country Flag
SG.description: The national flag of Singapore is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SG.title: .sg Domain
SG.description: Web addresses in Singapore end in the country domain .sg (often as .com.sg). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

TW.title: Traditional Chinese
TW.description: Taiwanese signage uses Traditional Chinese, a complex script with intricate multi-stroke characters.

TW.title: Pole markings
TW.description: In Taiwan, nearly all utility poles carry diagonal black-and-yellow striped markings that most often run all the way down to the ground.

TW.title: Dotted bollards
TW.description: Taiwanese bollards feature two or three circular reflectors on a black rectangle.

TW.title: No parking
TW.description: Red-painted edge lines indicating no parking appear frequently, especially in urban areas, essentially unique to Taiwan.

TW.title: Double Yellow Centre Lines
TW.description: Most Taiwanese roads have double yellow centre lines with single white edge lines.

TW.title: White Edge Lines Without Centre Lines
TW.description: Roads with only white edge lines and no centre marking are common in Taiwan.

TW.title: Black-on-Yellow Chevrons
TW.description: Taiwanese chevrons have black arrows on a yellow background.

TW.title: Orange-Hooded Mirrors
TW.description: Convex road mirrors with bright orange hoods are common at Taiwanese intersections and bends.

TW.title: Concrete Drainage Ditches
TW.description: Open concrete drainage channels run alongside many Taiwanese roads.

TW.title: Distribution Transformers
TW.description: Box-shaped distribution transformers, usually dark green or grey, appear frequently in Taiwanese urban areas.

TW.title: Architecture
TW.description: Taiwanese residential buildings range from cramped multi-storey to flat single-storey homes, often boxy with white tile walls and light-green tin sheds.

TW.title: County Map and Offshore Islands
TW.description: Taiwan includes distant island groups: Kinmen, Lienchiang, Penghu, Green Island, and Orchid Island.

TW.title: Telephone Area Codes
TW.description: Taiwanese phone numbers have two-digit area codes (02–08) increasing from north to south. Mobile numbers start with 09.

TW.title: National Freeway System
TW.description: Taiwan's odd-numbered freeways run north–south, even-numbered run east–west, with numbers increasing west to east and north to south.

TW.title: Township Road Signs by County
TW.description: Taiwanese township road signs show a Chinese character indicating the county before or above the road number.

TW.title: Blue Pole Plaques, Grid Coordinates
TW.description: Blue plaques on poles encode precise coordinates with a letter for a grid rectangle and four digits for position within it.

TW.title: Central Western Plains
TW.description: Flat to gently rolling agricultural land dominates Taiwan's central western lowlands.

TW.title: Central-Eastern Mountains
TW.description: Forested mountains cover two-thirds of Taiwan with temperate or coniferous trees at higher elevations.

TW.title: Hualien–Taitung Valley
TW.description: A long, narrow north–south valley on the east coast between Hualien and Taitung, with flat plains between forested mountains.

TW.title: Yilan Plain
TW.description: A plain enclosed by mountains on three sides, featuring rice paddies and houses beside fields.

TW.title: Kinmen, Fuzzy-Leaved Trees
TW.description: Roads lined with trees bearing fuzzy foliage and red-tinged soil identify Kinmen Island.

TW.title: Miaoli and Hsinchu, Low Rolling Hills
TW.description: Gently rolling terrain with winding roads and sparse farmland.

TW.title: Areca Palms, Central and Southern Taiwan
TW.description: Areca (betel nut) palms grow extensively in mountainous areas of central and southern Taiwan.

TW.title: Coconut Palms, Southern Coast
TW.description: Coconut palms concentrate near the southern coast.

TW.title: Leafless Trees, Penghu
TW.description: Bare, leafless trees are common on Penghu.

TW.title: Coastal Fish Farms, Western Counties
TW.description: Cultivated fish ponds line the western coast from Yunlin to Pingtung.

TW.title: Tea Plantations
TW.description: Tea plantations appear in mountainous areas, especially Chiayi, Nantou, Hsinchu, and Miaoli.

TW.title: Areca Palm Plantations, Pingtung
TW.description: Neat rows of areca palms on flat plains characterize Pingtung County.

TW.title: Dense Urban Housing, Northern Taiwan
TW.description: Older, disorganized housing and tall, dingy apartment blocks are common in northern urban areas.

TW.title: Red Brick Buildings, Taoyuan
TW.description: Red brick and red tile apartment buildings are frequent in Taoyuan.

TW.title: Luxury Villas, Yilan
TW.description: Multi-storey, often gated villas characterize parts of Yilan.

TW.title: Cream-Coloured Houses, Penghu
TW.description: White-tinged cream-colored residential buildings are common on Penghu.

TW.title: Traditional Houses, Kinmen
TW.description: Small traditional-style houses with characteristic rooflines appear on Kinmen.

TW.title: Lamppost Location Stickers
TW.description: Stickers on lampposts encode location data, similar to blue pole plaques on utility poles.

TW.title: White-Speckled Pavement, East Coast
TW.description: Road surfaces with visible white speckles are common along the eastern coast.

TW.title: Red-and-White Striped Lampposts, Kinmen
TW.description: Lampposts with diagonal red-and-white stripes appear frequently on Kinmen.

TW.title: Trapezoidal-Base Lampposts, Kaohsiung
TW.description: Lampposts with red-and-white stripes on a trapezoidal base are prevalent in Kaohsiung.

TW.title: Thick Pole-Top Supports, Yunlin
TW.description: Utility poles with thicker-than-usual supports below the pole top are found in Yunlin.

TW.title: Green Square Stickers, Chiayi City
TW.description: Green square stickers appear on nearly every pole in Chiayi City.

TW.title: Bent Chevron Holders, Southern Counties
TW.description: Curved sign and chevron holders with black-and-yellow-striped stickers appear in Pingtung, Kaohsiung, and Taitung.

TW.title: Country Flag
TW.description: The national flag of Taiwan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

TW.title: .tw Domain
TW.description: Web addresses in Taiwan end in the country domain .tw (often as .com.tw). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

AU.title: Black text
AU.description: "Give way" signs in Australia have black text and a white outer border.

AU.title: Road lines
AU.description: Australia generally uses all white road lines.

AU.title: Gum Trees (Eucalyptus)
AU.description: Eucalyptus trees have pale bark and rounded clumps of foliage.

AU.title: White Road Lines
AU.description: Australian roads use white markings almost everywhere.

AU.title: Rumble Strips
AU.description: Edge lines sometimes have short white bars across them as rumble strips.

AU.title: Chevrons
AU.description: Curve warning chevrons appear as white arrows on black or black arrows on yellow.

AU.title: Green Directional Signs
AU.description: Green signs with white arrows indicate nearby towns and distances.

AU.title: Speed Limit Signs
AU.description: Speed limits show a black number in a red ring on a white rectangular plate.

AU.title: State Licence Plates
AU.description: Every Australian state has its own plate design, often visible even through blur.

AU.title: Phone Area Codes
AU.description: Australian phone numbers have an eight-digit number preceded by a two-digit state area code.

AU.title: State Bus Stops
AU.description: Bus stop designs differ by state and appear frequently in urban areas.

AU.title: Stobie Poles
AU.description: The distinctive steel-and-concrete Stobie pole with a trident or rotated-E top is a hallmark of South Australia.

AU.title: Rusty Metal Poles
AU.description: Northern Territory has rusted metal utility poles peppered with holes along their length.

AU.title: Concrete Poles
AU.description: Concrete utility poles are heavily concentrated in Victoria.

AU.title: Trident Pole Tops
AU.description: Pole tops shaped like a three-pronged fork appear in Western Australia and Victoria.

AU.title: Upward-Angled Coil Pole Tops
AU.description: Queensland electricity poles often have side-mounted coils that tilt upwards.

AU.title: Three-Coil Pole Tops
AU.description: Victoria pole tops typically carry three round coils: one vertical at the peak and one on each side.

AU.title: L-Shaped Metal Crossbars
AU.description: Tasmanian utility poles often feature a slim metal arm bent at a right angle forming an L-shape at the top.

AU.title: Blue Pole Stickers
AU.description: Round blue stickers appear on power poles throughout Queensland.

AU.title: Black Pole Markings
AU.description: Queensland power poles bear distinctive black printed marks, often with angled numbers.

AU.title: Olive-Green Possum Guards
AU.description: Tasmania's electricity poles have olive-green possum guards.

AU.title: Green Pole Bases
AU.description: Western Australian timber utility poles often have green-painted lower sections.

AU.title: Short Bollard Reflectors
AU.description: Bollards with reflectors shorter than standard are concentrated in Queensland and South Australia.

AU.title: Brown-Bottom Bollards
AU.description: Western Australian road bollards often have a brown-painted lower portion.

AU.title: Black-and-White Striped Bollards
AU.description: Bollards with alternating black and white horizontal stripes are found only in Western Australia.

AU.title: Black-and-Yellow Bollards
AU.description: Black and yellow bollards are a Queensland-only design.

AU.title: Flat Signposts
AU.description: South Australia and Western Australia occasionally use flat-profile sign poles instead of cylindrical ones.

AU.title: Yellow Signpost Stickers
AU.description: Northern Territory signposts sometimes have small yellow adhesive labels.

AU.title: Fluorescent Sign Borders
AU.description: Queensland road signs often have bright fluorescent borders.

AU.title: Red 'No Stopping' Signs
AU.description: New South Wales uses red 'No Stopping' signs; other states use white.

AU.title: Text-Based Parking Signs
AU.description: ACT 'No Stopping' and 'No Parking' signs include the restriction spelled out in words.

AU.title: White Directional Signs
AU.description: Tasmania is the only state with white-background directional road signs.

AU.title: 'C' Roads
AU.description: Route numbers prefixed with 'C' appear in Victoria and Tasmania.

AU.title: 25 km/h School Zones
AU.description: South Australia enforces a 25 km/h school zone speed limit.

AU.title: 130 km/h Speed Limit
AU.description: Northern Territory has a 130 km/h speed limit.

AU.title: Thin 'Keep Left' Signs
AU.description: A slimmer 'Keep Left' sign without an arrow appears in NSW, Queensland, and Northern Territory.

AU.title: Dark Green Property Markers
AU.description: Roadside property markers in dark green are a Western Australian feature.

AU.title: White Property Markers
AU.description: South Australia uses white property markers along its roads.

AU.title: Guardrail Endings
AU.description: Guardrails in NSW and the ACT end with a black stripe on a yellow field.

AU.title: Blue Circle Hydrant Poles
AU.description: Victoria has white hydrant indicator poles topped with a red segment and a blue circle.

AU.title: Red-Top Fire Hydrants
AU.description: Fire hydrants in Victoria have red-painted caps.

AU.title: Reddish-Orange Soil
AU.description: Western Australian ground, especially near Perth, has a reddish-orange colour.

AU.title: Brush Plants
AU.description: Brush-type shrubs with dense, bushy growth are common in Western Australia.

AU.title: Termite Mounds
AU.description: Tall brown rough, spiky structures rising from the earth are termite mounds, mainly in the Northern Territory.

AU.title: Dry Shrubland
AU.description: From Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA, arid scrub, broad-canopied gum trees, and sandy orange earth define the landscape.

AU.title: Green and Golden Fields
AU.description: A belt of verdant or golden farmland runs from southern Yorke Peninsula to Echuca with broad gum canopies.

AU.title: Tropical North Queensland
AU.description: Far north Queensland's coastal strip is lushly tropical with palms and dense dark green foliage.

AU.title: Sugarcane Fields
AU.description: Sugarcane fields dominate northern Queensland's tropical agricultural landscape.

AU.title: Inland NSW Landscape
AU.description: Interior NSW is flat with red soil and dry pale-green scrub, becoming more temperate and hilly near borders.

AU.title: Tasmania Landscape
AU.description: Tasmania has green rolling hills, roadside eucalyptus, and densely forested hilly interiors.
