AU.title: Rare Cars and Snorkels
AU.description: Cars with snorkels, protecting engines during water crossings, are concentrated in NSW and the ACT.

AU.title: Mount Gambier
AU.description: Mount Gambier in SA features chalky white soil and large pine plantations.

AU.title: Kangaroo Island
AU.description: Kangaroo Island has scrubby low eucalyptus, bushy undergrowth, and orange-tinted soil.

AU.title: Brisbane Street Signs
AU.description: Brisbane City Council street signs have a distinctive design.

AU.title: Sydney Street Signs
AU.description: City of Sydney street signs have a unique design.

AU.title: Country Flag
AU.description: The national flag of Australia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

AU.title: Bollards 01
AU.description: Australian bollards are white with a vertical red stripe towards the top.

AU.title: Driving direction
AU.description: In Australia they drive on the left side of the road.

AU.title: Yellow poles
AU.description: In the state of Western Australia you can find yellow sign posts.

AU.title: Western Australia White-Bordered Traffic Lights
AU.description: Western Australia traffic light housings have a prominent white border framing the entire signal.

AU.title: Queensland White-Bordered Traffic Lights
AU.description: Queensland's traffic lights have a bold white outline encasing the entire signal housing.

AU.title: New South Wales White-Bordered Traffic Lights
AU.description: New South Wales traffic light casings feature a thick white border around the housing.

AU.title: ACT White-Bordered Traffic Lights
AU.description: ACT traffic lights have white-bordered housings defining the signal edges.

AU.title: Tasmania White-Bordered Traffic Lights
AU.description: Tasmania's traffic signals have a wide white outline framing the housing.

AU.title: Victoria Borderless Traffic Lights
AU.description: Victoria traffic light housings lack any white border, appearing unframed.

AU.title: South Australia Borderless Traffic Lights
AU.description: South Australia traffic lights are installed without any white border.

AU.title: Northern Territory Borderless Traffic Lights
AU.description: Northern Territory traffic lights have housings with no white outline.

AU.title: Nsw Lp
AU.description: New South Wales plates are bright yellow, which stays obvious through the blur.

AU.title: Victoria License Plate
AU.description: Victorian plates are white with dark blue characters. A small blue downward-pointing triangle sits in the top middle, often showing up as just a dark dot through the blur.

AU.title: South Australia Licence Plate
AU.description: South Australian plates are white with black characters, with no colour anywhere.

AU.title: Western Australia Licence Plate
AU.description: Western Australian plates are white with blue characters under a solid blue banner carrying a small orange sun.

AU.title: Tasmania Licence Plate
AU.description: Tasmanian plates are white with blue characters and a gold emblem among the first characters. They are often visible as a white plate with a subtle dark blue divider in the center.

AU.title: Northern Territory Licence Plate
AU.description: Northern Territory plates are white with bright orange-red characters.

AU.title: Australian Capital Territory Licence Plate
AU.description: Australian Capital Territory plates are white with blue characters, sometimes visible through the blur.

AU.title: .au Domain
AU.description: Web addresses in Australia end in the country domain .au (usually as .com.au). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

AU.title: Queensland Licence Plate
AU.description: Queensland plates are white with dark red characters and border, showing through the blur as a reddish tint.

CW.title: Overflowing color
CW.description: In Curaçao road signs borders can be seen wrapping over to the back. These borders are usually blue or red.

CW.title: Unique car
CW.description: The Curaçao images were taken by a black car with visible bars, a combination unique to this island.

CW.title: Far from home
CW.description: Curaçao is part of the Netherlands and uses the Dutch language.

CW.title: .cw Domain
CW.description: Web addresses in Curaçao end in the country domain .cw. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

DO.title: Stop signs
DO.description: The Dominican Republic stop signs say 'PARE'. This is unlike most other North American countries.

DO.title: Gradient plates
DO.description: License plates in the Dominican Republic fade from yellow at the top to white at the bottom.

DO.title: Rubberized bars
DO.description: If you see bars with thick rubber strips when looking down then you are guaranteed to be in the Dominican Republic.

DO.title: Square Concrete Poles
DO.description: Electricity poles are predominantly square concrete with a reverse-L bracket at the top.

DO.title: Dark Smooth Asphalt
DO.description: Roads are notably dark, smooth asphalt, darker than typical Caribbean surfaces.

DO.title: Country Flag
DO.description: The national flag of the Dominican Republic is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

DO.title: .do Domain
DO.description: Web addresses in the Dominican Republic end in the country domain .do (often as .com.do). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

GT.title: Painted poles
GT.description: Seeing utility poles painted pink is a common occurrence in Guatemala. Other colors such as green appears as well.

GT.title: Visible bars
GT.description: All vehicle-based coverage in Guatemala uses a grey car whose roof rack and side mirrors are visible through the blur.

GT.title: Compact plates
GT.description: Guatemalan plates are compact. When blurred, they typically show either a blue or green tint.

GT.title: Tropical Rainforest Landscape
GT.description: Much of the terrain is dense tropical rainforest.

GT.title: Architecture
GT.description: Stone buildings painted pastel with corrugated metal or white cinder-block walls.

GT.title: Road Markings
GT.description: Solid white edge lines with a single yellow centre line; markings are thinner than Mexico's.

GT.title: ALTO Stop Signs
GT.description: Stop signs in Guatemala read 'ALTO'.

GT.title: Topography
GT.description: A central mountainous belt with flat terrain to the south and north.

GT.title: Flat Southern Farmland
GT.description: Southern lowlands are flat agricultural land, more developed than northern flat areas.

GT.title: Central Highlands
GT.description: The middle band is dominated by mountainous terrain.

GT.title: Gently Rolling North
GT.description: Northern Guatemala has gentle hills and undulating ground.

GT.title: Oil Palm Plantations
GT.description: Oil palm cultivation is in the southwest coast and north of the central mountains.

GT.title: Solid Green Utility Poles
GT.description: Poles painted entirely green appear mainly in the southeast and scattered eastern areas.

GT.title: Pole Plate Route Codes
GT.description: Many green poles have a white plate with the first two characters indicating the road.

GT.title: Forward-Facing Roof Bar
GT.description: Most Guatemalan cars have an upper-right roof bar angled toward the front.

GT.title: Backward-Facing Roof Bar
GT.description: In southeastern Guatemala, the upper-right roof bar points toward the rear.

GT.title: Blue Rope on Lower Bar
GT.description: Backward-bar regions often have a blue rope wrapped around the lower-right roof bar.

GT.title: Missing Black Bar Cap
GT.description: Some southern and far northeast areas have backward-facing bars without a black cap.

GT.title: Phone Code 6
GT.description: Numbers starting with 6 belong to the Guatemala Department.

GT.title: Country Flag
GT.description: The national flag of Guatemala is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

GT.title: .gt Domain
GT.description: Web addresses in Guatemala end in the country domain .gt (often as .com.gt). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

BG.title: Bilingual signs
BG.description: Road direction signs in Bulgaria are blue, arrow-shaped, and printed in both Cyrillic and Latin script.

BG.title: Cyrillic
BG.description: Bulgaria writes primarily in Cyrillic, though Latin transliterations appear on many signs.

BG.title: Metal waste bins
BG.description: It is common to spot these metal waste bins in Bulgaria.

BG.title: Licence Plates
BG.description: Bulgarian plates have a blue EU band on the left side.

BG.title: Street Word 'улица'
BG.description: Streets are labelled улица (ulitsa), often shortened to ул.

BG.title: Concrete Utility Poles
BG.description: Dominant poles are round concrete cylinders.

BG.title: Alternating Hook Insulators
BG.description: Pole tops have small insulators arranged in alternating hooks along a crossarm.

BG.title: Three Large Hook Insulators
BG.description: Poles have three oversized hook-shaped insulators pointing upward, staggered side to side.

BG.title: Chevrons
BG.description: Curve warning boards show red arrows on a white background.

BG.title: Town Entry Signs
BG.description: Settlement names appear on plain white boards with Cyrillic and Latin text in two lines.

BG.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
BG.description: Bulgarian pedestrian crossing signs show a pedestrian wearing a hat walking across four horizontal stripes.

BG.title: Bollards
BG.description: Roadside bollards have red reflectors facing traffic and white on the rear.

BG.title: Thin Road Markings
BG.description: Road line markings are noticeably narrow.

BG.title: Road Surface Quality
BG.description: Road surfaces often have fine cracks and occasional potholes.

BG.title: Orange Roof Tiles
BG.description: Houses have orange clay tile roofs with visible mortar patches and uneven tilework.

BG.title: Suburban Areas
BG.description: Suburbs have tightly packed small houses with a run-down appearance.

BG.title: Topography Overview
BG.description: The Balkan range bisects the country; broad plains lie north, Rhodope Mountains in the south, and small valleys in the west.

BG.title: Area Codes
BG.description: Telephone area codes start with a digit that narrows down the region.

BG.title: Pirin and Rila Peaks
BG.description: Sharp, pyramid-like summits of Pirin and Rila parks are visible in certain provinces.

BG.title: Wind Turbines
BG.description: Wind farms concentrate in Dobrich Province near the Black Sea coast.

BG.title: Nessebar and Sozopol Old Towns
BG.description: Historic cores feature buildings with raw stone, whitewashed walls, dark timber framing, and cobblestone lanes.

BG.title: Sofia Street Signs
BG.description: Street plaques are white with two red bands—one along the bottom edge and one across part of the top.

BG.title: Stara Zagora Street Signs
BG.description: Street plaques are brown with vivid yellow lettering.

BG.title: Country Flag
BG.description: The national flag of Bulgaria is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BG.title: .bg Domain
BG.description: Web addresses in Bulgaria end in the country domain .bg. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

PR.title: Spanish signs
PR.description: Signage throughout Puerto Rico is predominantly in Spanish despite being part of the USA.

PR.title: American influence
PR.description: US retail chains like Walmart are common in Puerto Rico. A useful differentiator from other Latin American territories where such stores are absent.

PR.title: Max speed
PR.description: Puerto Rican speed limit signs have the same design as in the US but are written entirely in Spanish.

PR.title: Area Code 787
PR.description: Phone numbers use the 787 area code, shown as (787) XXX-XXXX.

PR.title: No Front Licence Plates
PR.description: Most vehicles lack front licence plates.

PR.title: Divided Highways
PR.description: Much of the rural area has wide divided highways.

PR.title: Highway Shields
PR.description: Puerto Rico uses unique highway shield designs not found elsewhere in the US.

PR.title: Kilometre Markers
PR.description: Kilometre markers are tall green signs with "km" at the top and a large vertical number below.

PR.title: Architecture, Concrete Flat Roofs
PR.description: Most houses are concrete with flat roofs and often metal security gates.

PR.title: Drier Southern Coast
PR.description: The southern coast is noticeably more arid.

PR.title: Old San Juan
PR.description: Narrow streets, vibrant buildings, brick roads, and Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque architecture.

PR.title: Country Flag
PR.description: The national flag of Puerto Rico is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PR.title: .pr Domain
PR.description: Web addresses in Puerto Rico end in the country domain .pr (often as .com.pr). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

VI.title: Left hand drive
VI.description: The Virgin Islands is the only US territory that drives on the left side of the road.

VI.title: Visible car
VI.description: A white or red truck street view car will be visible while exploring the US Virgin Islands.

VI.title: Blue plates
VI.description: The Virgin Islands uses two types of blue plates. Dark blue and turquoise.

VI.title: Distinctive Architecture
VI.description: US Virgin Islands have a unique blend of European Renaissance, Spanish Baroque, Rococo, and Victorian styles with large arches and courtyards.

VI.title: St. Croix, Grid-Pattern Roads
VI.description: St. Croix has primary roads in a loose grid angled WSW to ENE with cross streets NNW to SSE; other islands have curvier roads.

VI.title: Country Flag
VI.description: The national flag of the US Virgin Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

VI.title: .vi Domain
VI.description: Web addresses in the United States Virgin Islands end in the country domain .vi. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

AL.title: Albanian bollard
AL.description: Bollards in Albania are white with a black, slanted top. The top features a red reflector on the front and a gray on the back.

AL.title: Albanian plates
AL.description: License plates in Albania come in two forms. One with a red strip to the left, and one featuring blue strips on each end.

AL.title: Street name
AL.description: The Albanian word for street is rruga.

AL.title: Highway shields
AL.description: Alaskan highway shields feature the Big Dipper constellation in the lower-left corner.

AL.title: Slim trees
AL.description: Alaskan trees tend to be slimmer with narrower foliage.

AL.title: Snow-capped mountains
AL.description: Tall, snowy mountain peaks are visible in much of Alaska.

AL.title: Subarctic interior
AL.description: Interior and northern Alaska have sparse undergrowth and short trees.

AL.title: Alexander Archipelago
AL.description: Towns in the panhandle's island chain sit among steep, densely forested mountains with mostly wooden buildings.

AL.title: Anchorage suburbs
AL.description: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, shopping districts, and visible mountain ranges.

AL.title: Aspen trees
AL.description: Quaking aspens with white bark and round leaves grow at lower elevations in interior and south-central Alaska.

AL.title: Agricultural fields
AL.description: Farming in Alaska occurs mainly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.

AL.title: Trans-Alaska Pipeline
AL.description: The pipeline is often visible from main roads and is a strong identifier.

AL.title: Albanian flag
AL.description: The Albanian flag is red with a black double-headed eagle in the center

AL.title: .al Domain
AL.description: Web addresses in Albania end in the country domain .al. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

NO.title: Beautiful views
NO.description: Fjords are a common sight along the Norwegian coast.

NO.title: Directional signs
NO.description: In Norway directional signs are yellow with a thin black outline.

NO.title: White signs
NO.description: Regulatory traffic signs in Norway feature a red border on a white background.

NO.title: Black and yellow
NO.description: In Norway, you can see black and yellow chevrons.

NO.title: Kiwi
NO.description: Kiwi is a store chain that only exists in Norway.

NO.title: Wooden Houses
NO.description: Norwegian homes are mostly wooden, often red-painted; black-painted houses are more common here than in neighbors.

NO.title: Road Line Markings with Long Dashes
NO.description: Smaller roads have white edge lines with long dashes; larger roads have solid edge lines and yellow center lines with an orange tint.

NO.title: Dotted Paint Pattern on Road Lines
NO.description: Norwegian road markings often use small dots of paint instead of solid lines.

NO.title: Norwegian Language Characters
NO.description: Norwegian uses special characters Æ, Ø, Å and writes "kk" where Swedish uses "ck".

NO.title: Bollards with Black Parallelogram Reflector
NO.description: Norwegian bollards are slender curved posts with a reflector inside a black parallelogram.

NO.title: Orange Snow Poles with Mid-Height Reflector
NO.description: Snow poles are orange with a narrow white reflector roughly at mid-height.

NO.title: Wooden Snow Poles with Painted Reflectors
NO.description: Thin wooden snow poles with painted reflectors are common.

NO.title: Guardrails with Wooden Posts
NO.description: Metal guardrails are often supported by wooden posts.

NO.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs with Four Stripes
NO.description: Norwegian pedestrian signs show a figure with four stripes on the crossing.

NO.title: Blue Passing Place Signs
NO.description: Smaller roads frequently display blue signs bearing a large white letter M, indicating passing places.

NO.title: Bus Stop Signs
NO.description: Norwegian bus stops are marked by a small blue sign featuring a white bus icon.

NO.title: "Sone" Speed Zone Signs
NO.description: White signs displaying the word "Sone" along with a speed limit are common in Norwegian urban areas.

NO.title: Street Name Suffixes (Vei and Gate)
NO.description: The most typical Norwegian street name endings are "vei" and "gate." When attached to a name, they become "-veien" and "-gata" or "-gate."

NO.title: Centered Street Signs on Posts
NO.description: Street name signs in Norway are typically mounted centered on top of the sign post.

NO.title: Bright Yellow Construction Signs
NO.description: Road construction zones in Norway use warning signs with a vivid yellow background.

NO.title: Sign Mounting with Four Bolts
NO.description: Norwegian road signs are fastened with four visible bolts arranged in a tall rectangular pattern.

NO.title: Distance Marker Signs
NO.description: Small white square signs show a road number at the top and the distance to the nearest town below on mid-sized roads.

NO.title: Wooden Utility Poles with Black Caps
NO.description: Utility poles in Norway are usually made of wood and often topped with a small black metal cap.

NO.title: Lamp Mounting with Single Thick Bolt
NO.description: Street lamps attached to wooden poles in Norway use a single thick bolt for mounting.

NO.title: Grass-Covered Roofs
NO.description: Traditional Norwegian buildings often feature living grass growing on their rooftops.

NO.title: Road Number First-Digit Regional Pattern
NO.description: The leading digit of Norwegian road numbers corresponds to geographic regions, with some exceptions.

NO.title: Bilingual Sámi Signs in Northern Areas
NO.description: Parts of northern Norway display signs in both Norwegian and a Sámi language, identified by letters Á, Đ, and multiple consecutive vowels.

NO.title: Bracken Ferns in Southern Norway
NO.description: Bracken ferns with tall stems and wide leaf fronds grow predominantly in southern Norway.

NO.title: Spruce Trees
NO.description: Spruce trees are concentrated in the southern half of Norway, especially in the southeast and Trondheim region.

NO.title: Pine Trees
NO.description: Pines are most prevalent along coastal areas and far inland zones within southern Norway.

NO.title: Oak Trees
NO.description: Oak trees in Norway are almost entirely restricted to the far southern part of the country.

NO.title: Maple Trees
NO.description: Maples grow primarily in southern Norway, especially around Oslo's agricultural areas.

NO.title: Brightly Coloured Moss
NO.description: Vivid, colourful moss is common from Lillehammer to Oppdal.

NO.title: Three Major Farmland Regions
NO.description: Norway's large agricultural zones are concentrated in the southeast, Trondheim surroundings, and south of Stavanger.

NO.title: Southeast Farmlands near Oslo
NO.description: The biggest farmland stretch lies in the southeast around Oslo, with flat, gently rolling terrain and smooth forested hills.

NO.title: Trondheim-Area Farmlands
NO.description: Agricultural land around Trondheim sits on steep, uneven hills more rugged than the southeast.

NO.title: Stavanger-Area Farmlands
NO.description: Farmland south of Stavanger is relatively flat with wide fields and common rock walls made of large rounded stones.

NO.title: Deep Fjords with Tall Mountains
NO.description: The deepest fjords flanked by towering mountains are concentrated between Bergen and Trondheim.

NO.title: Lofoten's Jagged Rocky Mountains
NO.description: The Lofoten Archipelago features sharp rocky peaks with very sparse tree cover.

NO.title: Northeast Norway Rolling Terrain
NO.description: Northeastern Norway has gently rolling terrain with small birch trees and patchy grass.

NO.title: Barren Highlands in the Southwest
NO.description: Treeless highland plateaus with rocky mountains along the road characterize southwestern Norway.

NO.title: Exposed Rock on the South Coast
NO.description: Bare rock outcrops with small coastal pines and low bushes are typical of Norway's southern coastline.

NO.title: Coastal Grasslands
NO.description: Roads along the far northern coast pass through open grasslands with minimal vegetation and low, distant mountains.

NO.title: White Wooden Houses
NO.description: Entire villages of all-white wooden houses are distinctive along Norway's southern coastline.

NO.title: Black Snow Poles
NO.description: Snow poles painted black are common between Bergen and Trondheim.

NO.title: Wide Black Pole Plates
NO.description: Small, wide black ID plates with alphanumeric characters appear on utility poles in southeastern Norway.

NO.title: Rusty Guardrails
NO.description: Rusty guardrails are prevalent along the southern half of Norway's west coast.

NO.title: Svalbard Archipelago
NO.description: Svalbard is a Norwegian Arctic archipelago with separate coverage and guide.

NO.title: Russian Border Road Look
NO.description: Roads near the Russian border have a humid, green look with overcast, foggy conditions and low birches and pines.

NO.title: Country Flag
NO.description: The national flag of Norway is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

NO.title: .no Domain
NO.description: Web addresses in Norway end in the country domain .no. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

EE.title: EU plates
EE.description: Estonia uses standard EU-plates. White plates with a blue strip on the left.

EE.title: Kilometer markers
EE.description: Small blue signs with numbers on them can be found in Estonia. They are placed perpendicular to the road.

EE.title: Crossing signs
EE.description: Estonian pedestrian crossing signs feature three black stripes.

EE.title: Estonian bollard
EE.description: Estonian bollards have a rounded profile. The front carries a rectangular reflector while the back has two circular ones, in either white or orange.

EE.title: Wooden Utility Poles
EE.description: Round wooden poles with diagonal braces are common; Estonia has varied pole types.

EE.title: Square Concrete Poles
EE.description: Square concrete poles appear regularly, often with diagonal bracing.

EE.title: Trident Pole Tops
EE.description: Pole tops have a single insulator pointing upward and two extending sideways.

EE.title: Metal Pole Caps
EE.description: Most wooden poles have a small metal cap at the top.

EE.title: Short-Dash Edge Lines
EE.description: Road edge markings sometimes use unusually short dashes.

EE.title: Chevrons
EE.description: Curve warning boards have a red background with white directional arrows.

EE.title: Warning and Speed Sign Borders
EE.description: Warning and speed limit signs have a narrow red border running to the edge.

EE.title: Guardrails
EE.description: Standard A-type (wavy) guardrails without reflectors.

EE.title: Bus Stop Signs
EE.description: Estonian bus stop signs show a bus icon with four windows.

EE.title: Blue-and-White Signpost Wrappings
EE.description: Signposts are commonly wrapped with alternating blue and white bands.

EE.title: Estonian Language
EE.description: Estonian uses umlauted vowels (Ä, Ö, Ü) and the letter Õ (O with tilde).

EE.title: Street Name Suffixes
EE.description: The words 'tänav' (street) and 'tee' (road) are uniquely Estonian.

EE.title: Oval Blue House Numbers
EE.description: Buildings often display blue oval-shaped house number plates.

EE.title: Architecture
EE.description: Estonian buildings combine wooden cladding, white-rendered brick, and steep corrugated metal roofs.

EE.title: Directional Signs
EE.description: Wayfinding signs are blue with white lettering and a white border; arrows sit inside the sign.

EE.title: Elevation and Hills
EE.description: The country is mostly flat with hills in the southeast and Lääne-Viru County.

EE.title: Russian Minority in Ida-Viru
EE.description: Ida-Viru County has a Russian-speaking majority with occasional bilingual Cyrillic-Estonian signs.

EE.title: Country Flag
EE.description: The national flag of Estonia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

EE.title: .ee Domain
EE.description: Web addresses in Estonia end in the country domain .ee. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

FO.title: No trees
FO.description: The Faroe Islands are virtually devoid of natural tree growth, the vegetation consists almost entirely of grass and low shrubs.

FO.title: Rugged landscape
FO.description: The terrain on Faroe Islands is defined by sweeping fjords bordered by steep, green mountains.

FO.title: Small bollards
FO.description: The bollards on Faroe Islands are yellow and quite small.

FO.title: Architecture
FO.description: Timber houses with raised stone basements and corrugated metal or turf roofs.

FO.title: Faroese Language
FO.description: Faroese uses special letters including Ø, distinguishing it from Icelandic.

FO.title: Yellow Guardrail Reflectors
FO.description: Metal guardrails fitted with yellow reflectors, unique in northern Europe.

FO.title: Directional Signs
FO.description: Wayfinding signs in the Faroe Islands have a yellow background with a black border.

FO.title: Klakkur Trekker
FO.description: Two pyramid-shaped snow-capped peaks visible to the south from Klakkur.

FO.title: Gjógv Trekker
FO.description: Southward view of village and snow-dusted mountain ridges from Gjógv.

FO.title: Koltur Boat Trekker
FO.description: Grey inflatable 'RIB62' with passengers in high-visibility clothing en route to Koltur.

FO.title: Country Flag
FO.description: The national flag of the Faroe Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

FO.title: .fo Domain
FO.description: Web addresses in the Faroe Islands end in the country domain .fo. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

GI.title: The rock of Gibraltar
GI.description: A massive limestone mountain towers Gibraltar and is visible from virtually everywhere.

GI.title: Right hand traffic
GI.description: Despite being a British territory, Gibraltar drives on the right, the opposite of the UK mainland.

GI.title: Yellow Rear Licence Plates
GI.description: Vehicles display yellow rear plates, matching the UK system.

GI.title: English Language
GI.description: English is the primary language on official signage in a Mediterranean coastal setting.

GI.title: Mediterranean Architecture
GI.description: Dense pastel-coloured buildings with louvred window shutters, usually painted green, blue, or brown.

GI.title: Christmas Decorations
GI.description: Street View coverage was captured in December, showing festive Christmas decorations throughout the town.

GI.title: Barbary Macaques
GI.description: Wild Barbary macaques roam the Rock, the only free-living monkey population in Europe.

GI.title: Country Flag
GI.description: The national flag of Gibraltar is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

GI.title: .gi Domain
GI.description: Web addresses in Gibraltar end in the country domain .gi. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

IT.title: Italian bollard
IT.description: Bollards in Italy are white with a black top. They have a red reflector on the front and a white on the back.

IT.title: Street names
IT.description: The Italian word for street is 'Via'.

IT.title: Outer lines
IT.description: Solid white outer lines without any center lines is a common sight in Italy.

IT.title: Double stripes
IT.description: The Italian license plates will have a blue strip on both sides. The front plates are also shorter than usual.

IT.title: Italian Language
IT.description: Recognisable by abundant double consonants, frequent 'i', accented vowels (ì, é, à), and words ending in vowels.

IT.title: Mediterranean Landscape
IT.description: Gently rolling farmland with forested mountain valleys.

IT.title: Architecture
IT.description: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs and outward-swinging bi-fold wooden shutters.

IT.title: Round Concrete Utility Poles
IT.description: Cylindrical concrete poles are widespread, unlike the wood or metal poles common in other Mediterranean countries.

IT.title: White Pole Sticker
IT.description: Timber utility poles often have a small white identification sticker.

IT.title: Concrete Trident Pole Tops
IT.description: A three-pronged concrete frame tops most poles, Italy's common insulator mount.

IT.title: Double Guardrails
IT.description: Two guardrail beams stacked on the same posts are common along Italian roads.

IT.title: Red Guardrail Reflectors
IT.description: Italian guardrails have red reflectors on their faces.

IT.title: Flared Guardrail Ends
IT.description: Guardrails typically end by flattening, widening, and curving away from the road.

IT.title: Black Sign Backs
IT.description: The reverse side of road signs is often painted black or dark grey.

IT.title: Road Signs 01 Blue Signs
IT.description: Directional signs in Italy tend to be bright blue with a white capitalised text.

IT.title: Highway Sign Colours
IT.description: National roads have blue signs with white-and-blue borders; motorways have green signs with white-and-green borders.

IT.title: Kilometre Markers
IT.description: White square stones show a Roman numeral on top (hundreds of metres) and an Arabic numeral below (kilometres from origin).

IT.title: Road Number Prefixes
IT.description: Route numbers start with SS (state), SR (regional), or SP (provincial).

IT.title: Chevron Signs
IT.description: In Italy, curve warning boards show white arrows on a black background.

IT.title: Street Name Signs
IT.description: White plates with a narrow blue border and black lettering.

IT.title: Pedestrian Crossing Sign
IT.description: A walking figure crosses five zebra stripes and has no visible belt.

IT.title: 'Passo Carrabile' No-Parking Signs
IT.description: No-parking signs labelled 'passo carrabile' are common in built-up areas.

IT.title: Phone Area Codes
IT.description: Area code leading digits increase broadly from west to east, then southward.

IT.description: Road and street signs appear in both Italian and German in South Tyrol.

IT.title: Aosta Valley French Signs
IT.description: French text appears alongside Italian, with street names pairing 'via' and 'rue'.

IT.title: Po Valley
IT.description: A vast, flat agricultural basin in the north, often shrouded in haze.

IT.title: Bari Peninsula Olive Groves
IT.description: The southeastern heel has olive plantations, pale rock walls, and reddish earth.

IT.title: Alpine Mountains
IT.description: Broad, towering mountain ranges separated by deep valleys in the far north.

IT.title: Sicilian Landscape
IT.description: Dry, undulating farmland with craggy rock formations defines much of Sicily's interior.

IT.title: Sardinia Grey Rock Outcrops
IT.description: Grey boulders protrude from the ground, especially in northeast Sardinia.

IT.title: Southern Cacti
IT.description: Prickly-pear and other cacti grow abundantly in the far south: Sicily, southern Sardinia, and Apulia.

IT.title: Citrus Orchards
IT.description: Citrus cultivation is concentrated in eastern Sicily and southern Calabria.

IT.title: Rice Paddies
IT.description: Rice fields cluster in the western and central Po Valley, with some on Sardinia.

IT.title: Tuscan Brown-Grey Brick Buildings
IT.description: Rough-hewn, unpainted brown-grey stone is typical in and around Tuscany.

IT.title: Alpine Architecture
IT.description: Sturdy white-walled buildings with exposed timber detailing are typical of the Alpine north.

IT.title: Aosta Valley Grey Stone Buildings
IT.description: Irregular grey stone masonry with an Alpine character marks Aosta Valley buildings.

IT.title: Veneto Wooden Shutters
IT.description: Heavy wooden shutters on black iron hinges are common in Veneto.

IT.title: Apulian Flat-Roofed Houses
IT.description: Pale, flat-roofed two- or three-storey buildings give parts of Apulia a Middle-Eastern feel.

IT.title: Slovene Bilingual Signs
IT.description: Near Slovenia, road signs show both Italian and Slovene text.

IT.title: Vulcano White Stripe
IT.description: A near-white band of exposed earth traces the upper slopes of Vulcano volcano, visible from afar.

IT.title: Country Flag

LI.title: Rhine valley
LI.description: As Liechtenstein is located in a valley, mountains are always visible, especially to the east.

LI.title: Liechtenstein bollard
LI.description: Bollards in Liechtenstein are rounded with a round top. They are black and white and feature a vertical reflector on the front.

LI.title: White plates
LI.description: Liechtenstein license plates are black with white text with an emblem slightly to the left. It will appear as black or red.

LI.title: Low cam
LI.description: All Liechtenstein imagery is captured with a low-mounted camera.

LI.title: LIEmobil Bus Stops
LI.description: Bus stop signs are green-and-white with a black frame and 'LIEMOBIL' across the top.

LI.title: Direction Signs
LI.description: Directional signs are white for minor roads and blue for major roads, each with a pointed arrowhead.

LI.title: Pedestrian Signs
LI.description: Pedestrian crossing signs have seven stripes and a tall rectangular shape.

LI.title: Yellow-and-Black Road Separators
LI.description: Striped road separators have a rounded top, small knob, and three bands of yellow and black.

LI.title: Metal Sign Borders
LI.description: Road signs commonly have a round grey metal border.

LI.title: Architecture
LI.description: Architecture ranges from traditional Alpine chalets to modern structures, more modern in larger settlements.

LI.title: Eastern Mountain Coverage
LI.description: Mountains are visible in every direction east of the central ridge.

LI.title: Blue Street Signs
LI.description: Blue street signs with a thin white border appear in the south and around Bendern.

LI.title: Flat Black Signs
LI.description: Plain flat black street signs indicate eastern Liechtenstein.

LI.title: Brown Fraktur-Style Signs
LI.description: Brown street signs with traditional German-style typeface and white border are found in Vaduz and northern towns.

LI.title: Country Flag
LI.description: The national flag of Liechtenstein is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

XX.title: General 01 61 Mailboxes

XX.title: General 01 H E B Supermarket Chain
XX.description: H-E-B is a supermarket chain that operates exclusively in Texas.

XX.title: General 01 57 Argentina Chevrons
XX.description: Argentina is the only South American country that has white chevrons with red arrows.

XX.title: General 01 29 Vienna Street Signs
XX.description: In Vienna, street signs appear as dark blue plaques, with the first number indicating the district.

XX.title: General 01 30 Red And White Tape
XX.description: In Vienna and some smaller Austrian cities, signposts have red and white tape, resembling the Austrian flag.

XX.title: General 01 04 Orange Signs
XX.description: In Belgium, you will often find orange signposts and sign backs.

XX.title: Pole 01 Ladder Poles
XX.description: The poles you often see in Brazil have a ladder-like design at the base. They have horizontal sections near the bottom.

XX.title: General 01 62 Bilingual Signs
XX.description: Road direction signs in Bulgaria are blue, arrow-shaped, and printed in both Cyrillic and Latin script.

XX.title: Pole 01 01 Cambodian Poles
XX.description: In Cambodia, you will typically see either concrete ladder poles with rectangular sections or round poles with small holes.

XX.title: Road Signs 01 Checkered Signs
XX.description: In Canada, T-intersection signs are diamond-shaped and have a distinctive checkered pattern.

XX.title: General 01 25 Colombian Cross
XX.description: In Colombia, signposts have white backs that form a cross shape, known as the Colombian Cross.

XX.title: General 01 53 Arrow Signs
XX.description: Directional signs in Czechia taper to a solid filled arrow tip.

XX.title: General 01 08 Ecuadorian Bollards
XX.description: In Ecuador, bollards are typically either thin and round with two red stripes or flat with two red reflectors.

XX.title: General 01 20 Green Sticker
XX.description: In Germany, most cars have a green circular sticker on the bottom right of the windshield.

XX.title: General 01 24 Double White Lines
XX.description: You will often see worn double white center lines in Greece.

XX.title: General 01 44 Pedestrian Crossings
XX.description: In Iceland, you will see pedestrian crossing signs with four stripes at the bottom and a subtle yellow hue.

XX.title: General 01 11 Dry Landscape
XX.description: Some parts of the northern Himalayan region administered by India are known for dry, high altitude landscapes with very little vegetation.

XX.title: Road 01 01 Yellow Guardrails
XX.description: Yamaguchi Prefecture in Japan is recognized for its distinctive bright yellow roadside guardrails.

XX.title: General 01 03 Black Google Car
XX.description: In Jordan, the Street View coverage was captured by a black Google car.

XX.title: General 01 46 Tree Trunks
XX.description: The bottom of tree trunks in Kazakhstan are often painted white.

XX.title: General 01 19 Rock Walls
XX.description: Jeju Island in South Korea is known for its many rock walls made from dark volcanic stone.

XX.title: License Plates 01 01 Red Strip
XX.description: Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan feature a red strip on the left side.

XX.title: General 01 16 Square Poles
XX.description: In Lithuania, utility poles are usually square concrete posts with a diagonal support beam.

XX.title: License Plates 01 02 Black License Plates
XX.description: In Macau, cars have black licence plates.

XX.title: General 01 07 Portuguese Signs
XX.description: Portuguese often appears alongside Chinese on signs in Macau, reflecting its history as a Portuguese colony.

XX.title: General 01 02 North Macedonian Bollards
XX.description: One type of bollard in North Macedonia has a trapezoid shape, colored white and black, with a red reflective strip.

XX.title: General 01 01 North Macedonian Signs
XX.description: In North Macedonia, road signs are yellow and black, and town names appear in both Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.

XX.title: General 01 40 Marked Poles
XX.description: In mainland Malaysia, electricity poles often have black stickers on them.

XX.title: General 01 17 Electricity Meters
XX.description: Mexico, along with several Central American countries, uses circular electricity meters.

XX.title: General 01 42 Tent Car
XX.description: In Mongolia the google car is often visible. It takes many shapes but usually a tent can be seen packed on the car.

XX.title: Vehicles 01 01 Call The Police
XX.description: A police vehicle, usually white or black, trails the Nigerian Street View car in nearly every coverage. The exact model may differ from images shown.

XX.title: Misc 01 Islamic Outfits
XX.description: You are more likely to see women wearing hijabs and men dressed in traditional Islamic outfits in the northern regions of Nigeria.

XX.title: License Plates 01 Green License Plates

XX.title: General 01 64 Black And Yellow

XX.title: Pole 01 02 Peruvian Poles
XX.description: In Peru, you can often see concrete utility poles with three horizontal crossarms.

XX.title: General 01 54 Jeepneys
XX.description: In the Philippines it is common to find jeepneys in urban environments. They are often heavily decorated.

XX.title: Architecture 01 Portuguese Chimneys
XX.description: In southern Portugal, you will often see small chimneys that are either square or round in shape.

XX.title: General 01 38 Stone Walls

XX.title: General 01 41 Black Socks
XX.description: In Russia, signposts often have their lower sections painted black.

XX.title: General 01 18 South African Chevrons
XX.description: South Africa uses red and white chevron signs, and small, thin chevrons with a single arrow are common across Southern African countries.

XX.title: General 01 60 Road Markers
XX.description: Distance markers along Spanish roads are recognisable by their colourful borders and the road number printed at the top.

XX.title: Road Signs 01 01 Spanish Chevrons
XX.description: In Spain, you can find both black and white chevrons and blue and white chevrons.

XX.title: General 01 43 Sri Lanka Poles
XX.description: Sri Lanka commonly uses concrete utility poles with large see through holes in the lower half, often called holey poles

XX.title: General 01 59 Tall Grass
XX.description: Eswatini features stretches of tall grass.

XX.title: Road Signs 01 02 Framed Signs
XX.description: In Switzerland, many road signs have a thin metal border that gives them a clean, framed look.

XX.title: General 01 39 Stop Signs
XX.description: In Turkey, stop signs say "DUR", which is unique to the country.

XX.title: General 01 50 Red Car
XX.description: In Ukraine, you will most often see the back of a red Google car.

XX.title: General 01 06 Emirati Road Lines
XX.description: In the UAE, outer road lines are yellow, while the center lines can be white or yellow.

XX.title: General 01 27 Triple Road Lines
XX.description: In Uruguay, you can find triple road markings, double yellow lines with a white dashed line running between them.

XX.title: General 01 31 Vietnamese Language

MC.title: Rich microstate
MC.description: Monaco is a tiny, but rich country. Buildings look fancy and streets are clean.

MC.title: City only
MC.description: There are no rural areas in Monaco, everything is urban.

MC.title: Boat parking
MC.description: Monaco has multiple marinas filled with fancy boats. There is even street view out on the water.

MC.title: Location
MC.description: A European microstate on the French Riviera, west of the Italian border.

MC.title: Licence Plates

MC.title: Hilly Terrain
MC.description: Monaco's terrain is hilly with Mediterranean vegetation in open patches.

MC.title: Palm Trees
MC.description: Ornamental palm trees line Monaco's streets and boulevards.

MC.title: Tunnels
MC.description: Much of Monaco's coverage passes through tunnels.

MC.title: Parked Mopeds
MC.description: Rows of parked mopeds line many Monaco streets.

ME.title: Mountainous landscape
ME.description: The landscape in Montenegro is very mountainous. The mountains tend to be lush and covered in green vegetation.

ME.title: Red dot
ME.description: Montenegrin license plates are white and feature a blue strip on the left. They also have red coat of arms close to the center.

ME.title: Montenegrin bollard
ME.description: Montenegrin bollards are white with a red reflector on the front, a white reflector on the back, and a black top.

ME.title: Cosmic encounters
ME.description: Image artifacts in the sky are common to see in Montenegro. These are referred to as 'Rifts' by the community.

ME.title: Chevrons
ME.description: Montenegro uses black-on-white and red-on-yellow chevrons.

ME.title: Utility Poles
ME.description: Montenegro uses simple round concrete or wooden utility poles.

ME.title: Northern Agricultural Valleys
ME.description: Green valleys with deforested hillsides cleared for farming are common in northern Montenegro.

ME.title: Dry Mountains Around Podgorica
ME.description: Barren, treeless mountains characterise the area around and south of Podgorica. Vineyards are also common.

ME.title: Pine Forests
ME.description: Pine forests appear mainly in the east, with smaller patches in the north and north of Nikšić.

ME.title: Podgorica
ME.description: The capital and largest city, identifiable by modern buildings, wide roads, and updated infrastructure.

ME.title: Cemi River Valley Terraces

SM.title: Small plates

SM.title: Italian influence

SM.title: Rolling Agricultural Hills

SM.title: Round Concrete Poles

SM.title: Yellow-and-Burgundy Chevrons
SM.description: Chevrons are yellow boards with burgundy-red arrows, unique to San Marino.

SM.title: Lime-Green Bins
SM.description: In San Marino, bright lime-green rubbish bins appear frequently along streets.

SM.title: Country Flag
SM.description: The national flag of San Marino is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SM.title: .sm Domain
SM.description: Web addresses in San Marino end in the country domain .sm. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

SK.title: Double orange
SK.description: Slovak bollards have two orange reflectors on the front and a white reflector on the back.

SK.title: Small arrows
SK.description: Slovak direction signs have a blue background and small white arrows.

SK.title: Street signs
SK.description: In Slovakia, street name signs are commonly white with blue lettering and a thin red border.

SK.title: Wide Guardrails
SK.description: Broad guardrails are unique to Slovakia and Czechia.

SK.title: Paired Concrete Utility Poles
SK.description: Broad cylindrical concrete poles often mounted side by side.

SK.title: Short Metal Bar Pole Tops
SK.description: Compact horizontal metal bars carrying line insulators.

SK.title: Inverted Triangle Pole Supports
SK.description: Two angled braces create upside-down triangle silhouette.

SK.title: Trident Pole Tops
SK.description: Three-pronged pole top with two outer arms angled upward.

SK.title: Bolt-Mounted Lamp Post Bases
SK.description: Chunky base plates secured by opposing pairs of bolts.

SK.title: Red-and-White Striped Temporary Signposts
SK.description: Square poles wrapped in alternating red and white bands.

SK.title: Striped Gas and Water Marker Poles
SK.description: Slender roadside poles painted in coloured stripes indicating underground lines.

SK.title: Three-Stripe Hiking Trail Markers
SK.description: Coloured band between two white bands; sometimes arrow-shaped.

SK.title: Colourful Prefabricated Apartment Blocks
SK.description: Soviet-era panel buildings often repainted in vibrant colours and patterns.

SK.title: Diamond-Shaped Roof Tiles
SK.description: Roofing composed of small diamond-shaped tiles is widespread.

SK.title: Black Bridge Marker Signs
SK.description: Dark plaques near bridge ends display the road number on the left side.

SK.title: Slovak vs Czech Language Differences
SK.description: Slovak uses unique accented letters like L with caron (Ľ) and O with circumflex (Ô); Czech uses others like R with caron (Ř) and U with ring (Ů).

SK.title: Landscape Contrast
SK.description: Slovakia alternates between dramatic mountains and flat lowlands.

SK.title: Blue Directional Signs with Small Arrows
SK.description: Road direction signs have a blue background with compact white arrows.

SK.title: Sign Border Flush with Edge
SK.description: Painted borders run right up to the physical edge of Slovak road signs.

SK.title: Highway Signs with Edge-Flush Borders
SK.description: Motorway signs in blue or green have a white border touching the panel edge.

SK.title: White House Number Signs
SK.description: Building numbers appear on white plaques with thin red or black borders.

SK.title: Sign Post Cap Styles
SK.description: Sign post tops are open, capped with grey metal discs, or thin black caps.

SK.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
SK.description: Signs feature five crossing stripes with either a simple figure or closely bunched stripes.

SK.title: Bold Road Sign Font
SK.description: Road signs use a notably heavy, bold typeface.

SK.title: Two-Section Kilometre Markers
SK.description: Distance markers have upper and lower sections separated by a black line; road number is on top.

SK.title: Cycling Signs Marked with "C"
SK.description: Cycle route signs display the letter C and resemble Czechoslovak hiking markers.

SK.title: Window Shutters
SK.description: Houses with window shutters appear frequently.

SK.title: Hip-End Roofs Facing the Road
SK.description: Residential buildings often have narrow gable ends facing the street with hipped roofs.

SK.title: Grey Metal Roofs
SK.description: Unpainted grey sheet-metal roofing is widespread, especially in the east.

SK.title: Spring Coverage
SK.description: Most imagery was captured in spring.

SK.title: Railway Crossing Sign with White Background
SK.description: Level crossing warning signs are mounted on white rectangular panels.

SK.title: Double Sign Posts on Small Signs
SK.description: Small road signs are often supported by two parallel posts.

SK.title: New Wedge-Shaped Bollard with Red Reflector
SK.description: A new wedge-shaped bollard with a red front reflector is introduced.

SK.title: Wooden Poles and White Concrete Supports
SK.description: Wooden utility poles with white concrete braces appear somewhat often.

SK.title: Phone Number Area Codes
SK.description: Telephone numbers are ten digits with the first two or three digits as area codes.

SK.title: Road Numbering System
SK.description: Roads have three- or four-digit numbers. Three-digit 500-560 and four-digit roads increase west to east.

SK.title: Topography Overview
SK.description: Highest mountains are central and north; flattest terrain is southwest and southeast.

SK.title: Western Lowlands
SK.description: Southwestern plains have perfectly flat agricultural fields stretching to the horizon.

SK.title: Eastern Lowlands
SK.description: Broad farmland with distant hills or ridges defines the eastern lowland region.

SK.title: Hungarian-Majority Areas in the South
SK.description: Southern areas have Hungarian-speaking populations with bilingual street names.

SK.title: Yellow Circle Markings on Poles
SK.description: Concrete poles with painted yellow circles are concentrated in Nitra and Trnava regions.

SK.title: Yellow Lamp Posts with Blue Bases
SK.description: Lamp posts have yellow bodies with blue bases, mainly in the east.

SK.title: Northern Mountain Valleys
SK.description: Two broad valleys flanked by tall, jagged peaks lie in the north. The nearest mountain range side helps tell them apart.

SK.title: Pine Forests
SK.description: Dense pine woodland is characteristic of western Slovakia.

SK.title: Rusyn Bilingual Signs
SK.description: Town entry signs in northeastern Presov may include Rusyn text in Cyrillic script.

SK.title: Zilina Trolleybuses
SK.description: Trolleybuses in Zilina have a green-yellow-white livery; overhead poles match in yellow and green.

SK.title: Country Flag
SK.description: The national flag of Slovakia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SK.title: .sk Domain
SK.description: Web addresses in Slovakia end in the country domain .sk. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

SI.title: Hilly landscape
SI.description: Slovenia's terrain is generally very hilly and heavily forested, with occasional patches of agriculture.

SI.title: Slovenian bollard
SI.description: Slovenian bollards are white with a black top. The front reflector is bright red and the back reflector is white.

SI.title: House numbers
SI.description: Slovenian house number plates are typically red with white text.

SI.title: Alpine architecture
SI.description: Slovenian buildings are alpine-inspired with light-colored walls and dark wooden details.

SI.title: Hilly Forested Landscape
SI.description: Slovenia is very hilly and heavily forested with some agriculture.

SI.title: Deep Forest Roads
SI.description: Many roads run deep through dense forest in Slovenia.

SI.title: Slovene Language
SI.description: Slovene is a Slavic language using special letters Č, Š, and Ž.

SI.title: Directional Signs
SI.description: Yellow signs with black borders.

SI.title: Kilometre Markers
SI.description: Road number in a yellow rectangle top left, second number right, black divider, distance below.

SI.title: Chevrons
SI.description: Red arrows on white background; sometimes black arrows on white.

SI.title: Pedestrian Signs
SI.description: Five stripes and a simply drawn person with no belt.

SI.title: Dashed Outer Road Lines
SI.description: Long dashed edge lines on roads.

SI.title: Red House Numbers
SI.description: Red plates with white text.

SI.title: Kozolec Drying Racks
SI.description: Open-sided wooden sheds with thin beams and visible gaps.

SI.title: Northwestern Alpine Region
SI.description: Tallest mountains in the alpine northwest.

SI.title: Eastern Plains
SI.description: Flat or rolling agricultural fields with no mountains or tall hills.

SI.title: Adriatic Coast
SI.description: White cliffs, Mediterranean vegetation, vineyards, and Mediterranean-style architecture.

SI.title: Southeast Valley
SI.description: Wide east–west valley with mountains to north and south.

SI.title: Bilingual Italian Signs
SI.description: Slovenian-Italian bilingual signs in the westernmost coastal region.

SI.title: Country Flag
SI.description: The national flag of Slovenia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SI.title: .si Domain
SI.description: Web addresses in Slovenia end in the country domain .si. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

IM.title: Old camera
IM.description: The images on Isle of Man were captured by an older camera, identifiable by lower resolution and a big bottom blur.

IM.title: Red stripe
IM.description: License plates on Isle of Man are yellow on the rear and white in the front. They have a red strip to the left.

IM.title: Yellow flowers
IM.description: Gorse shrubs, bushes with vivid yellow flowers, are commonly found on Isle of Man.

IM.title: Hilly Farmland Landscape
IM.description: Undulating green pastures crossed by narrow roads dominate the scenery.

IM.title: Whitewashed Houses
IM.description: White-rendered walls on houses and boundary walls are common, giving an Irish feel.

IM.title: Striped Kerbs
IM.description: Alternating black-and-white painted kerbstones appear intermittently along main roads.

IM.title: Blue Bollards
IM.description: Blue-painted roadside bollards are frequent in built-up areas.

IM.title: Generally Hilly Terrain
IM.description: The island's interior is mostly hilly, with some flat pockets.

IM.title: Flat Northern Plain
IM.description: The northern tip is flat compared to the rest, with mountains visible on the southern horizon.

IM.title: Blue-Base Lamp Posts with Parish Codes
IM.description: Lamp posts have blue-painted bases and a blue sticker with two-letter parish codes outside Douglas.

IM.title: All-Green Lamp Posts
IM.description: Entirely green street lights are found mainly in Ramsey and Castletown, with some in other parishes.

IM.title: Country Flag
IM.description: The national flag of the Isle of Man is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

IM.title: .im Domain
IM.description: Web addresses in the Isle of Man end in the country domain .im (often as .co.im). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

JE.title: Old camera
JE.description: The images on Jersey were captured by an older camera, identifiable by lower resolution and a big bottom blur.

JE.title: White and yellow
JE.description: License plates on Jersey are yellow on the rear and white in the front, with a small red emblem to the left. This can be hard to see.

JE.title: Worlds collide
JE.description: Even though Jersey is part of the UK, French can be seen written on signs and many locations have French names.

JE.title: Yellow booth
JE.description: Phone booths on Jersey are painted yellow.

JE.title: Architecture
JE.description: Buildings mix northern-French and British styles with pastel walls and slate roofs.

JE.title: Red Granite
JE.description: Local red granite is used widely, giving buildings a warm reddish tone.

JE.title: Cornish Palms
JE.description: Cordyline australis palms are common ornamental garden plants.

JE.title: Yellow Give-Way Lines
JE.description: Junctions use yellow give-way lines instead of white.

JE.title: Cycling Route Signs
JE.description: Cycle network marked with 'Green Lane' markers and blue route plates with maps.

JE.title: Asymmetric Sign Attachments
JE.description: Many road signs are off-centre on their posts.

JE.title: Parish Coat of Arms on Street Signs
JE.description: Street signs display the parish's heraldic emblem.

JE.title: St Helier Capital
JE.description: The capital has taller buildings, tighter streets, and a livelier urban feel.

JE.title: Country Flag
JE.description: The national flag of Jersey is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

JE.title: .je Domain
JE.description: Web addresses in Jersey end in the country domain .je (often as .co.je). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

AS.title: Tropical
AS.description: The vegetation on American Samoa is tropical. All land not used by humans is covered in dense jungle.

AS.title: Black truck
AS.description: On the main American Samoa island, Tutuila, the rear of a rusted black pickup truck is visible.

AS.title: Country Flag
AS.description: The national flag of American Samoa is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

AS.title: .as Domain
AS.description: Web addresses in American Samoa end in the country domain .as. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

GU.title: Green signs
GU.description: Street signs in Guam are green.

GU.title: Road reflectors
GU.description: Roads on Guam are often studded with an unusually high amount of road reflectors.

GU.title: Heavy poles
GU.description: Utility poles on Guam are almost always made of concrete and tend to be noticeably thick.

GU.title: Tropical Vegetation
GU.description: Guam has thick, low-growing tropical vegetation.

GU.title: East Asian and Russian Signage
GU.description: Commercial signs often feature Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and Russian text.

GU.title: Hilly South
GU.description: The southern part of Guam is hillier and more rugged.

GU.title: Flat North
GU.description: Northern Guam is mostly flat and low-lying.

GU.title: Country Flag
GU.description: The national flag of Guam is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

GU.title: .gu Domain
GU.description: Web addresses in Guam end in the country domain .gu. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

MP.title: Wooden poles
MP.description: The Northern Mariana Islands uses wooden utility poles.

MP.title: Blue signs
MP.description: On Northern Mariana Islands street signs are blue.

MP.title: Fancy trees
MP.description: Flame Trees appear on the Northern Mariana Islands. Its wide crown covered in bright red flowers is easy to spot.

MP.title: Tropical Landscape
MP.description: The islands feature dense, low tropical vegetation throughout.

MP.title: Abundant Road Reflectors
MP.description: Roads have a very high density of reflectors, shared with Guam.

MP.title: East Asian Language Signage
MP.description: Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and Russian text appear frequently on commercial signs.

MP.title: Commercial Areas
MP.description: Denser commercial zones are along Saipan's southern west coast.

MP.title: Country Flag
MP.description: The national flag of the Northern Mariana Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MP.title: .mp Domain
MP.description: Web addresses in the Northern Mariana Islands end in the country domain .mp. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

PY.title: Yellow on black
PY.description: Chevrons in Paraguay are yellow with black arrows.

PY.title: Visible car
PY.description: Coverage in Paraguay has a visible Google car. It appears to be black or silver.

PY.title: Road lines
PY.description: Paraguay tends to have white solid outer lines and a single dashed yellow center line.

PY.title: Dark signs
PY.description: The backs of road signs in Paraguay are usually quite dark.

PY.title: Crosses
PY.description: In Paraguay some smaller road signs have a design that resembles a cross on their backside.

PY.title: .py Domain
PY.description: Web addresses in Paraguay end in the country domain .py (often as .com.py). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

AQ.title: Snow and ice
AQ.description: The vast majority of Antarctica is blanketed in snow and ice.

AQ.title: Dark soil
AQ.description: Wherever bare ground is exposed in Antarctica, it is consistently dark in colour.

AQ.title: Penguins
AQ.description: Penguins appear in parts of the Antarctic coverage and confirm the southern hemisphere.

AQ.title: Ross Island Western Tip
AQ.description: The western tip features very dark, barren rocky ground with almost no snow cover.

AQ.title: Ross Island Cabin
AQ.description: A small wooden cabin with a grey metal roof south of the island's eastern tip.

AQ.title: McMurdo Interior Tripods
AQ.description: Tripod footage inside several of McMurdo Station's buildings.

AQ.title: McMurdo Wooden Hut
AQ.description: A small wooden hut on the station's eastern side with interior tripod footage.

AQ.title: McMurdo Ice Trekker
AQ.description: A trekker walks across a frozen surface surrounded by machinery southeast of the station.

AQ.title: Mainland Dry Valleys
AQ.description: A surreal, barren landscape of empty valleys on the mainland west of Ross Island.

AQ.title: South of McMurdo
AQ.description: A wide, snowy expanse with scattered low hills south of McMurdo Station.

AQ.title: Country Flag
AQ.description: The national flag of Antarctica is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BY.title: Language
BY.description: Signage is in Belarusian or Russian, both using Cyrillic script.

BY.title: Country Flag
BY.description: The national flag of Belarus is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BM.title: General Landscape
BM.description: Landscape has thick low greenery, small trees, dense bushes, and scattered detached houses.

BM.title: Licence Plates
BM.description: Plates are elongated, entirely white, with black numbers centered.

BM.title: Road Markings
BM.description: Most roads have a single solid yellow centreline and no edge markings.

BM.title: Zig-Zag Lines
BM.description: White zig-zag road markings appear in some locations.

BM.title: Pastel Stone Houses
BM.description: Bermuda's signature architecture features stone homes painted in soft pastels with bright white stepped roofs.

BM.title: Palm Trees
BM.description: Palm trees are abundant throughout the islands.

BM.title: Turquoise Water
BM.description: The ocean around Bermuda has a strikingly pale turquoise colour.

BM.title: Country Flag
BM.description: The national flag of Bermuda is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BA.title: White Bollard with Angled Top (No Black Cap or Band)
BA.description: Slim white rectangular bollard with the top corner cut off at a diagonal angle. There is NO black cap at the top and NO black band around the shaft. A small rectangular reflector sits on a small dark patch just below the angled top.

BA.title: White Bollard with Solid Black Block on Top
BA.description: Slim white rectangular bollard with a thick solid black block sitting flat on top, like a hat. The rectangular reflector is on the white shaft, BELOW the black cap.

BA.title: White Bollard with Wide Black Band (White Tip Above)
Country Flag
BA.description: The national flag of Bosnia and Herzegovina is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

BA.title: .ba Domain
BA.description: Web addresses in Bosnia and Herzegovina end in the country domain .ba. Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

IO.title: Palm-Lined Sand Beaches
IO.description: Sandy shorelines fringed with palm trees.

IO.title: Coconut Palm Forests
IO.description: Dense coconut palm stands along the coast.

IO.title: Interior Grassy Clearings
IO.description: Open grassy fields ringed by low bushes and palms on larger islands.

IO.title: Offshore Trekker Footage
IO.description: Imagery taken from shallow water offshore.

IO.title: Country Flag
IO.description: The national flag of the British Indian Ocean Territory is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CN.title: Simplified Chinese Script
CN.description: Mainland China uses simplified Chinese characters with fewer brush strokes.

CN.title: Blue Licence Plates
CN.description: Vehicles display blue-backed number plates with white characters.

CN.title: Museum Interiors
CN.description: Much coverage consists of indoor museum photography, concentrated around Beijing and Shanghai.

CN.title: Country Flag
CN.description: The national flag of China is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

CC.title: Landscape
CC.description: Flat, low-lying terrain of white sand with coconut palms and mowed grass, less forested than Christmas Island.

CC.title: Coastal Trekkers
CC.description: Walking routes along shorelines with white sand, ocean on one side and palm trees on the other.

CC.title: Horsburgh Island
CC.description: Pulau Luar's inland trekker passes through dry, yellow grassland with thin vegetation.

CC.title: Country Flag
CC.description: The national flag of the Cocos Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

EG.title: Sandstone Architecture
EG.description: Built environment features sandstone construction from ancient monuments to medieval fortifications.

EG.title: Arabic Script
EG.description: Egypt uses Arabic script. It appears on signs, identifiable by flowing connected letters and diacritical dots.

EG.title: Country Flag
EG.description: The national flag of Egypt is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

FK.title: Carcass Island
FK.description: Wide-open grassy plains with the sea clearly visible in many directions. The terrain can become stony and rugged in places.

FK.title: West Point Island
FK.description: Broad treeless grassland with a yellowish tint to the vegetation. Unlike Carcass Island, the ocean is not readily visible from most vantage points.

FK.title: West Point Bay Boat Trekker
FK.description: A marine trekker captured from a boat in West Point Bay, showing golden-brown hillsides in the background and the MS National Geographic Explorer anchored in the bay.

FK.title: New Island Beach
FK.description: A stretch of sandy shoreline where figures wearing red and blue outdoor jackets can be spotted.

FK.title: New Island Inland
FK.description: The interior of New Island is characterised by exposed dark brown earth, sometimes criss-crossed by vehicle tracks.

FK.title: New Island Cliffs
FK.description: Dramatic, sheer coastal cliffs dropping straight into the ocean are a prominent feature of New Island's trekker route.

FK.title: Country Flag
FK.description: The national flag of the Falkland Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

HA.title: Licence Plates
HA.description: Hawaiian plates are white with an arched rainbow; front plates are mandatory.

HA.title: Hawaiian Language
HA.description: Hawaiian place names appear on signs, using eight consonants and vowel endings.

HA.title: Lush Tropical Vegetation
HA.description: Dense tropical greenery lines Hawaiian roadsides.

HA.title: Volcanic Topography
HA.description: Hawaiian terrain features volcano-shaped slopes, cliffs, valleys, and craters.

HA.title: Architecture
HA.description: Homes are light-coloured wooden structures with dark volcanic rock retaining walls.

HA.title: Yellow Pole Bands
HA.description: Some Hawaiian utility poles have wide yellow bands painted around them.

HA.title: Guitar-Pick Highway Shields
HA.description: State highway markers are guitar pick-shaped with yellow-painted posts.

HA.title: Raised Pavement Marker Pattern
HA.description: Hawaiian road reflectors follow a pattern: one, four close, then one again.

HA.title: Kauai
HA.description: Kauai has deep red earth, steep hills, and dense jungle-like growth.

HA.title: Oʻahu
HA.description: Oʻahu features steep green hills visible from suburban areas.

HA.title: Molokaʻi
HA.description: Molokaʻi has vivid red soil, dry vegetation, and a prominent eastern volcano.

HA.title: Lānaʻi, Coastal
HA.description: Lānaʻi's coast is hilly with dry grass and scrubby bushes, few buildings.

HA.title: Maui, Central Isthmus
HA.description: Maui's central valley is dry grassland between two mountain ranges.

HA.title: Maui, Coastal Areas
HA.description: Maui's coast is greener with banana plants, palms, and mountain backdrops.

HA.title: Big Island, Interior
HA.description: Big Island's interior has grassy plains with lava rock and volcanic summits.

HA.title: Big Island, Coastal
HA.description: Big Island's coast is lusher with trees and ferns; towns are mostly here.

IC.title: Licence Plates
IC.description: Plain white plates with blue lettering, no blue EU-style strip.

IC.title: Yellow Bollards
IC.description: Yellow delineator posts with a single white reflector on most rural roads.

IC.title: Barren Treeless Landscape
IC.description: Countryside lacks trees, covered by dark grey volcanic soil.

IC.title: Volcanic Geology
IC.description: Landscape shaped by tectonic and volcanic forces: rugged peaks, geothermal pools, lava fields, rift valleys, and rock pillars.

IC.title: Yellow Directional Signs
IC.description: Destination boards have yellow backgrounds with a white inset panel showing route numbers.

IC.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signs
IC.description: Pedestrian figure crosses four zebra stripes; sign background often has a faint yellow tinge.

IC.title: Icelandic Language
IC.description: Features letters ð (Ð), þ, æ, and accented vowels á, é, í, ó, ö, ú, ý.

IC.title: Street Name Signs
IC.description: White plates with black text, often edged by a thin metal rim, mounted on lamp posts or traffic-light poles.

IC.title: All-White Road Markings
IC.description: All road markings—centre lines, edge lines, lane dividers—are white.

IC.title: Chevron Signs
IC.description: Curve warning boards show yellow arrows on a black field.

IC.title: Yellow Warning Signs
IC.description: Hazard signs use a yellow background.

IC.title: Road Numbering System
IC.description: Route 1 is a ring road; other routes start with digits 2–9 assigned clockwise by region.

IC.title: Westfjords
IC.description: Narrow fjords surrounded by moderately high, flat-topped mountains.

IC.title: Eastfjords
IC.description: Eastern coast fjords with taller, more rugged mountains than the Westfjords.

IC.title: Northern Valleys West of Akureyri
IC.description: Valleys between tall, often snow-dusted peaks opening north to northeast.

IC.title: Inland Volcanic Desert
IC.description: Desolate dark volcanic gravel expanses with almost no plant life in eastern interior highlands.

IC.title: Southwest Agricultural Lowland
IC.description: A broad, level farming area with farmsteads, meadows, and pastures. Surrounding mountains appear unusually distant.

IC.title: Reykjavík
IC.description: The capital sits on the southern shore of a bay, on mostly flat ground with gentle hills and a large urban footprint.

IC.title: Akureyri
IC.description: Iceland's second city occupies a north–south valley along the western shore of a bay, flanked by mountain ranges.

IC.title: Southern Coast Glaciers
IC.description: Tongues of ice from the Vatnajökull ice cap spill down towards the sea along the southern coastline.

IC.title: Divided and Multi-Lane Highways
IC.description: Dual carriageways and roads wider than two lanes are rare, mostly around Reykjavík and near major intersections.

IC.title: Country Flag
IC.description: The national flag of Iceland is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

IQ.title: Iraqi National Museum Only
IQ.description: Entire Street View coverage is a single trekker walk-through inside the Iraqi National Museum in Baghdad.

IQ.title: Courtyard with Date Palms
IQ.description: Small patio with date palms and a diagonal path, the only outdoor scene.

JA.title: Islands, Regions and Prefectures
JA.description: Japan is divided into four major islands, regions grouping prefectures, and 47 prefectures.

JA.title: Japanese Writing Systems
JA.description: Japanese uses kanji, hiragana with rounded strokes, and angular katakana scripts.

JA.title: Katakana Script
JA.description: Katakana, angular and geometric, is used for foreign words in signage and ads.

JA.title: Useful Kanji for Place Names
JA.description: Eight kanji recur in place names; compass and suffix kanji aid navigation.

JA.title: Architecture
JA.description: Japan’s buildings range from traditional rural houses to ultramodern urban high-rises.

JA.title: Round Concrete Poles
JA.description: Utility poles are round concrete with screw-like protrusions, often with electrical plates and reflectors.

JA.title: Pole Reflectors
JA.description: Pole reflectors are compact, elevated, with vertical or diagonal yellow and white stripes.

JA.title: Licence Plates
JA.description: Vehicle plates are white with green characters; kei cars have yellow plates with black lettering.

JA.title: Road Lines
JA.description: Road markings combine solid white edges with dashed or solid white/yellow center lines; no yellow edge lines.

JA.title: Bollards
JA.description: Default bollards are plain white posts with round reflectors; some show kanji or extra attachments.

JA.title: White Guardrails
JA.description: Plain white guardrails are the standard road barriers.

JA.title: Hexagonal Prefecture Road Shields
JA.description: Prefectural routes use hexagonal shields with route numbers and kanji prefecture names.

JA.title: Common Infrastructure
JA.description: Distinctive triangular stop signs, school-zone crossings, and convex traffic mirrors are common.

JA.title: Retaining Walls
JA.description: Retaining walls in remote countryside indicate Japan.

JA.title: Area Codes
JA.description: Telephone area codes on signs increase southward.

JA.title: Utility Pole Plates
JA.description: Utility poles have region-specific identification plates.

JA.title: Regional Pole Reflector Pads
JA.description: Reflector pads on utility poles vary by region.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Large Filled
JA.description: A large white diamond with a small central hole; wide and bold, common across Japan.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Narrow Filled
JA.description: A filled diamond with narrow, elongated proportions.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Tall Thin
JA.description: A tall, thin diamond outline with a small center hole.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Crossed Outline (Medium)
JA.description: A medium diamond with overlapping sides creating a crossed-line pattern.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Crossed Outline (Nara / Wakayama)
JA.description: A crossed-line diamond like the medium variant but taller.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Crossed Outline (Standard)
JA.description: A crossed-line diamond used in central and southern prefectures.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Small Crossed Outline
JA.description: A smaller crossed-line diamond with compact proportions.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Very Small
JA.description: The smallest diamond variant, distinguished by its size.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Kagawa
JA.description: A clean, tall outline diamond with thin lines, specific to Kagawa Prefecture.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Aomori
JA.description: A newer crossed-line diamond pattern appearing in Aomori alongside the traditional filled style.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Thick Outline
JA.description: A thick-stroked outline diamond with a prominent centre hole and bold, heavy lines.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Ishikawa / Kumamoto
JA.description: A clean outline diamond with moderate line weight, used in Ishikawa and Kumamoto.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Yamanashi / Nagano
JA.description: A crossed-line diamond used in Yamanashi and as a newer pattern in Nagano.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Nara
JA.description: A newer, smaller crossed-line diamond appearing in Nara alongside the traditional style.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Ibaraki / Niigata
JA.description: A newer crossed-line diamond appearing in Ibaraki and Niigata alongside their traditional style.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Saga
JA.description: A newer, small thick-outlined diamond appearing in Saga alongside the traditional very-small style.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Shizuoka
JA.description: A clean outline diamond with thin, delicate lines, specific to Shizuoka Prefecture.

JA.title: Road Diamonds, Thin Outline
JA.description: A wide outline diamond with thick strokes but an open, airy feel. Used in several prefectures as a newer alternate pattern.

JA.title: Prefecture Signpost Stickers
JA.description: Signposts across Japan often display small stickers specific to individual prefectures.

JA.title: Chugoku Guy Wires: Orange Bulge
JA.description: Guy wires in the Chugoku region have an orange cover with a large bulge near the bottom.

JA.title: Hokuriku Guy Wires: Black-Yellow Bottle Stripes
JA.description: Guy wires in the Hokuriku area have a bottle-shaped cover with black and yellow stripes.

JA.title: Kansai Guy Wires: Yellow with Flat Top
JA.description: Guy wires in the Kansai (Kinki) region have a yellow cover with a flat lid at the top.

JA.title: Chiba Guy Wires: Wide Black-Yellow Stripes
