JA.description: Guy wires in Chiba Prefecture have wide alternating black and yellow stripes.

JA.title: Chugoku Orange Arrow on Poles
JA.description: In Chugoku, an orange arrow is visible above the highest plate on utility poles.

JA.title: Shikoku Orange-Black Pole Bands
JA.description: Utility poles in Shikoku often have alternating orange and black bands wrapped around them.

JA.title: Kansai 120° Pole Attachments
JA.description: In Kansai, pole hardware with roughly 120-degree angular spread is common.

JA.title: Shikoku 90° Pole Attachments
JA.description: Compact right-angle brackets attached to utility poles appear regularly in Shikoku.

JA.title: Hokkaido Transformers
JA.description: In Hokkaido, a cross-shaped bracket or lone transformer sits on horizontal bars; multiple transformers are on opposing sides of a square frame.

JA.title: Tohoku Transformers
JA.description: Tohoku transformers have square mounting brackets and the Tohoku Electric Power logo, often on circular plates with zigzag or straight bars.

JA.title: Kanto Transformers
JA.description: Kanto transformers with two or three insulators sit on wooden backing boards with dual bars or circular plates with T-shaped bars.

JA.title: Hokuriku Transformers
JA.description: Hokuriku transformers are secured by slender metal bars and have compact, lantern-shaped insulators without other horizontal supports.

JA.title: Chubu Transformers
JA.description: Chubu transformers have yellow numerals, black tap connectors, and are supported by large triangular bars or narrow metal brackets.

JA.title: Kansai Transformers
JA.description: Kansai transformers sit on square frames with straight or zigzag bars along the bottom edge, sometimes attached to vertical supports.

JA.title: Chugoku Transformers
JA.description: Chugoku uses a cross-shaped arm with a triangular brace and elongated or compact insulators; transformers have white labels with red numerals.

JA.title: Shikoku Transformers
JA.description: Shikoku uses a cross-shaped arm with a half-triangle brace and cap-shaped insulators; transformers often have white labels with black numerals.

JA.title: Kyushu Transformers
JA.description: In Kyushu, a horizontal bar ends with three insulators; transformers face opposite directions, 180 degrees apart.

JA.title: Okinawa Transformers
JA.description: Okinawa poles have a T-shaped arm with transformers on directly opposing faces.

JA.title: Grey Insulator Blocks
JA.description: Grey, insulator-like wire-routing blocks appear in Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, and Shikoku.

JA.title: Chubu Pole Top
JA.description: A pole cap of four heavy bars crowned by a circular element is characteristic of Chubu.

JA.title: Hokuriku Pole Top
JA.description: A tent-shaped pole cap with two filled sides is typical of Hokuriku.

JA.title: Chugoku Pole Top
JA.description: Four slender, narrow bars at the top of the pole are a hallmark of Chugoku.

JA.title: Kanto Tuning Fork Pole Top
JA.description: A fork-shaped pole cap with an upper bar protruding beyond each side and horizontal crossbars beneath, common in Kanto.

JA.title: Chubu Tuning Fork Pole Top
JA.description: A fork-shaped pole cap with a compact upper bar and single horizontal crossbar below, frequent in Chubu.

JA.title: Kansai Tuning Fork Pole Top
JA.description: A fork-shaped pole cap with a thin wire upper bar and horizontal crossbar underneath, prevalent in Kansai.

JA.title: Snow Shoulder Arrows
JA.description: Road-edge marker arrows guide drivers along snowy shoulders, appearing almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

JA.title: Kyushu Flat Bollards
JA.description: Flat white bollards with a row of orange reflectors on one face, plain white on the reverse, characteristic of Kyushu and Yamaguchi.

JA.title: Shikoku Black-Stripe Bollards
JA.description: Bollards on Shikoku with a dark horizontal band beneath the reflector, freestanding or mounted.

JA.title: Tohoku Thick Bollards
JA.description: Wide white posts with octagonal reflector and single yellow band below, common in Tohoku.

JA.title: Akita Prefecture Bollard
JA.description: Similar to Tohoku bollards but with two yellow bands beneath the octagonal reflector.

JA.title: Toyama Prefecture Bollard
JA.description: Extendable bollard with one reflector and red band below, specific to Toyama.

JA.title: Okayama Prefecture Bollard
JA.description: Bollard with eight-sided reflector, red band below, and tapered slope, found only in Okayama.

JA.title: Aomori Prefecture Bollard
JA.description: Extendable post with single round reflector flanked by two yellow bands, found in Aomori.

JA.title: Tohoku Striped Bollards
JA.description: Painted striped sleeves over bollards, tapering upward and lacking reflectors, common in Tohoku.

JA.title: Chugoku Snow Poles
JA.description: Simple snow marker poles with slim tips, concentrated in northern Chugoku.

JA.title: Green Guardrail Bands
JA.description: Guardrails with green banding throughout Kyushu, especially Oita and Miyazaki.

JA.title: Yamaguchi Yellow Guardrails
JA.description: Bright yellow guardrails exclusive to Yamaguchi Prefecture.

JA.title: Hokkaido Chevron Guardrail Stickers
JA.description: Arrow-patterned chevron stickers on guardrail tips and posts, common in Hokkaido.

JA.title: Chugoku Red-Yellow Guardrail Ends
JA.description: Red and yellow striped stickers on guardrail ends, widespread in Chugoku except Yamaguchi.

JA.title: Vertical Traffic Lights
JA.description: Traffic signals oriented vertically in Hokkaido and northwest coast; horizontal elsewhere.

JA.title: Kagawa Black Signs
JA.description: Dark boards with two yellow dots, exclusive to Kagawa, sometimes with arrows.

JA.title: Kerosene Tanks (Claymores)
JA.description: Fuel storage tanks nicknamed "Claymores," common northward and in Hokkaido.

JA.title: Hot Water and Propane Tanks
JA.description: Heating and cooking tanks common in northern and mountainous rural areas.

JA.title: Snow Prevention Roads (Shosetsu)
JA.description: Roads with small nozzles spraying heated groundwater to prevent snow, mainly on northwest coast.

JA.title: Ehime Cycling Routes
JA.description: Bicycle lanes marked by white outside and blue inside stripes, mainly along Ehime's coast.

JA.title: Red-Tiled Roofs
JA.description: Houses with red roof tiles, common in Chugoku, especially Hiroshima and Shimane.

JA.title: Northern Flat/Sloped Roofs
JA.description: Northern roofs are flat or low-sloped with exterior ladders for snow removal.

JA.title: Okinawa Concrete Buildings
JA.description: Flat-roofed white concrete buildings define Okinawa architecture.

JA.title: Cabbage (Hokkaido)
JA.description: Cabbage grows prolifically in Hokkaido and northern Honshu, often beside roads.

JA.title: Green Tea Plants
JA.description: Neatly trimmed tea bushes with pole fans, mainly from Shizuoka and Kagoshima.

JA.title: Rice Paddies
JA.description: Rice fields north of Tokyo with green shoots or golden husks in flooded paddies.

JA.title: Japanese White Birch
JA.description: Tree species concentrated in Chubu and Hokkaido, less so in Tohoku.

JA.title: Bamboo
JA.description: Bamboo is more common in southern areas and less so northward.

JA.title: Chinese Silver Grass
JA.description: Kyushu grass thrives across Kyushu island in large quantities.

JA.title: Sugarcane
JA.description: Sugarcane grows almost entirely on Kyushu and Okinawa islands.

JA.title: Hokkaido Winter Coverage
JA.description: Snowy winter Street View is scarce on Hokkaido, mostly in the south.

JA.title: Nobi and Kanto Plains
JA.description: Nobi and Kanto plains are flat expanses in mountainous Japan.

JA.title: Okinawa Shisa Lions
JA.description: Okinawa has Shisa guardian lions and house plaques with local lettering.

JA.title: Trekkers and Tripods
JA.description: Many trekker and tripod camera setups create non-standard coverage.

JA.title: Country Flag
JA.description: The national flag of Japan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

ML.title: Coverage Overview
ML.description: Mali has very limited coverage: ten small trekker segments across seven locations.

ML.title: Historic Mud-Brick Mosques
ML.description: Tripod segments focus on historic mud-brick mosques with wooden sticks protruding from walls and adobe interiors.

ML.title: Pinpointable vs Non-Pinpointable Coverage
ML.description: Mosque exterior coverage including surrounding streets can appear in pinpointable maps. Interiors are not pinpointable.

ML.title: Arid Landscape
ML.description: The country is very dry with sandy, barren settings that distinguish Malian tripod coverage.

ML.title: Sidi Yahiya Mosque Exterior
ML.description: Streets mix sand and bread-slice-shaped tiles. Buildings are peachy-orange bricks with brown undertones. The area feels busier than around Djingareyber mosque.

ML.title: Sidi Yahiya Mosque Interior
ML.description: Yellow-painted walls with unpainted bricks at the base. Courtyard has brick walls and bright square tile floor.

ML.title: Djingareyber Mosque Exterior
ML.description: Brick buildings along a paved street with rectangular tiles.

ML.title: Djingareyber Mosque Interior
ML.description: Yellow-painted walls, wide rounded archways, and red carpet throughout.

ML.title: Sankoré Mosque Exterior
ML.description: Surrounded by very sandy ground with a prominent pyramid-shaped tower.

ML.title: Sankoré Mosque Doors
ML.description: Ornately carved wooden doors decorated with metal details.

ML.title: Sankoré Mosque Interior
ML.description: Blue carpet, yellow-painted walls, and a low ceiling held up by wooden beams.

ML.title: Country Flag
ML.description: The national flag of Mali is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

MQ.title: Coastal Southern Trekker
MQ.description: A walking trek along the southern coast passes orange-roofed houses, open stretches with ocean views, and ends at a car park with stalls.

MQ.title: Country Flag
MQ.description: The national flag of Martinique is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PK.title: Urdu and English Signage
PK.description: Urdu is the national language on signs, using a script related to Arabic with softer fonts; English is also common.

PK.title: Licence Plates
PK.description: Pakistani plates are short with region-specific designs, mostly showing Punjab designs with a green strip.

PK.title: Mughal Gardens
PK.description: Coverage includes large, orderly gardens enclosed by stone walls featuring historic temples or fortresses.

PK.title: Brightly Coloured Baggy Trousers
PK.description: Vibrantly coloured, loose-fitting trousers are extremely common on pedestrians.

PK.title: Jallo, Hazy Suburbs
PK.description: An eastern suburb of Lahore with semi-urban, lower-income housing under a thick haze.

PK.title: Katas, Hazy Hills
PK.description: Coverage north of Sargodha with hilly terrain under a hazy sky.

PK.title: Patriata, Pine-Covered Hills
PK.description: Forested hills thick with tall pines northeast of Islamabad, partly captured from an aerial lift.

PK.title: Country Flag
PK.description: The national flag of Pakistan is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PN.title: Dense Tropical Forest
PN.description: Pitcairn Island is semi-tropical and thickly forested, with narrow dirt tracks winding through the trees.

PN.title: Red Soil
PN.description: Pitcairn's exposed soil is characteristically deep red.

PN.title: Country Flag
PN.description: The national flag of the Pitcairn Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

RE.title: French Infrastructure
RE.description: Standard French signs, bollards, and poles appear throughout Réunion.

RE.title: Mountainous Volcanic Island
RE.description: Réunion is a volcanic island with coastal roads, lush green mountains, palms, ferns, pine trees, and flowering plants.

RE.title: Bus Stop Designs
RE.description: Réunion has six bus stop styles: yellow, L-shaped (white or olive), pink, orange, green, and red, each in specific areas.

RE.title: Sugarcane Regions
RE.description: Sugarcane plantations appear in the northeast and southwest, with southwest fields in more built-up areas.

RE.title: Route du Volcan
RE.description: A barren volcanic landscape with brown-red soil, scattered shrubs, and white stones lining the road edges.

RE.title: Eastern N2, Sparse Population
RE.description: The least populated island area with an undivided N2 road through dense vegetation or open terrain.

RE.title: Country Flag
RE.description: The national flag of Réunion is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

PM.title: Licence Plates
PM.description: Saint Pierre and Miquelon plates are white or yellow, short or long, with a blue EU strip on the left; front plates are optional.

PM.title: Colourful Wooden Houses
PM.description: Homes are boxy wooden panel buildings often painted in bold colours.

PM.title: Grassy Coastal Landscape
PM.description: Flat to gently rolling grassland terrain with visible coastline.

PM.title: Saint-Pierre Island Rural Trekker
PM.description: A rural trekker on Saint-Pierre island with rockier terrain and tree-lined paths.

PM.title: Country Flag
PM.description: The national flag of Saint Pierre and Miquelon is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SL.title: Hilly Forested Landscape
SL.description: Slovenia's terrain is very hilly and heavily forested, with patches of agriculture.

SL.title: Deep Forest Roads
SL.description: Many Slovenian roads run deep through dense forest.

SL.title: Alpine Architecture
SL.description: Slovenian buildings are alpine-inspired with light walls, dark wood details, and semi-steep half-hipped roofs.

SL.title: Slovene Language
SL.description: A Slavic language using special letters Č, Š, and Ž.

SL.title: Bollards
SL.description: Slovenian bollards are white with black tops; front reflectors are red, back reflectors white.

SL.title: Directional Signs
SL.description: Slovenian directional signs are yellow with a black border.

SL.title: Kilometre Markers
SL.description: Slovenian kilometre markers show road number in a yellow rectangle, a second number, a black divider, and distance below.

SL.title: Chevrons
SL.description: Slovenian chevrons usually have red arrows on white; sometimes black arrows on white.

SL.title: Pedestrian Signs
SL.description: Slovenian pedestrian signs show five stripes and a simply drawn person with no belt.

SL.title: Dashed Outer Road Lines
SL.description: Slovenian roads often have long dashed edge lines.

SL.title: Street Signs
SL.description: Slovenian street signs are usually white with metal borders on posts; red variants attach to house walls.

SL.title: Red House Numbers
SL.description: Slovenian house number plates are typically red with white text.

SL.title: Kozolec Drying Racks
SL.description: Open-sided wooden sheds with visible gaps, typical of Slovenia.

SL.title: Northwestern Alpine Region
SL.description: Slovenia's tallest mountains are in the alpine northwest.

SL.title: Eastern Plains
SL.description: Flat or rolling agricultural fields with no mountains indicate eastern Slovenia.

SL.title: Adriatic Coast
SL.description: White cliffs, Mediterranean vegetation, vineyards, and Mediterranean-style architecture near Slovenia's Adriatic coast.

SL.title: Southeast Valley
SL.description: A wide east–west valley with mountains visible to north and south in southeastern Slovenia.

SL.title: Bilingual Italian Signs
SL.description: Bilingual Slovenian-Italian signs appear in Slovenia's western coastal region.

SL.title: Country Flag
SL.description: The national flag of Slovenia is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

SJ.title: Barren Arctic Landscape
SJ.description: Treeless mountains with moss and grasses; often overcast sky.

SJ.title: Russian Language on Signs
SJ.description: Russian text appears on some signs.

SJ.title: Longyearbyen
SJ.description: Svalbard's largest settlement, characterised by boxy, minimalistic buildings.

SJ.title: Pyramiden
SJ.description: An abandoned-feeling settlement with Soviet-style apartment blocks and little human activity. Pyramidal mountains are visible in the distance.

SJ.title: Barentsburg
SJ.description: The most desolate of Svalbard's three settlements. Multi-coloured apartment blocks sit near the hilltop, and coverage is notably more overcast and gloomy.

SJ.title: NW Spitsbergen National Park Ship
SJ.description: A large ship circles the Northwest Spitsbergen National Park. Coverage darkens toward the east as the sun sets.

SJ.title: Wooden-Deck Boat
SJ.description: A boat with a wooden deck can be found at specific locations around the archipelago.

SJ.title: Country Flag
SJ.description: The national flag of Svalbard and Jan Mayen is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

TZ.title: Extremely Limited Coverage
TZ.description: Tanzania has very sparse coverage: trekkers in Gombe National Park, some on Mount Kilimanjaro, and spill coverage from the Kenyan border.

TZ.title: Country Flag
TZ.description: The national flag of Tanzania is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

GB.title: Double Yellow Road Lines
GB.description: Paired yellow lines along the kerbside mark no-stopping zones in towns and cities.

GB.title: Standard Bollard
GB.description: Squat, barrel-shaped posts with black base and cap separated by a white band; red reflector faces traffic, white faces away.

GB.title: Wooden Poles with Steps
GB.description: Timber utility poles have thin horizontal metal rungs bolted up one side.

GB.title: Chevron Signs
GB.description: Curve warning boards use white arrows on a black background.

GB.title: Triangular Warning Signs
GB.description: Warning signs are red-bordered triangles on a white background.

GB.title: Direction Signs
GB.description: Directional signs are blue (motorways), green (primary routes), and white (local roads), with 'A', 'M', or 'B' prefixes.

GB.title: White Street Signs
GB.description: Low-mounted white plaques with black lettering, often on two short posts; suburban versions may show cul-de-sac pictograms.

GB.title: Give Way Signs
GB.description: Inverted-triangle yield signs read 'GIVE WAY' in large text.

GB.title: Pole Warning Stickers
GB.description: Yellow hazard stickers on utility poles depict a human figure struck by lightning.

GB.title: Yellow Traffic Bollard
GB.description: Yellow reflective panels on traffic-island bollards indicate which side traffic should pass.

GB.title: Square-Cornered Metal Gates
GB.description: Farm gates made from tubular metal with square-angled corners.

GB.title: Green Countryside with Hedgerows
GB.description: Rural areas have green pastures, dense hedgerows lining narrow lanes, and rolling hills.

GB.title: Red Brick Buildings
GB.description: Red brick construction is common in residential and commercial buildings.

GB.title: Suburban Layout
GB.description: Residential estates have rows of near-identical semi-detached homes with manicured gardens and cul-de-sacs.

GB.title: Chimney Pots
GB.description: Brick chimney stacks topped with multiple cylindrical terracotta pots.

GB.title: Black-and-White Timber Framing
GB.description: Buildings feature black timber frames against white-rendered walls.

GB.title: Country Flags
GB.description: Flags of England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland appear on buildings or flagpoles.

GB.title: Cornwall A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Major A-roads start with '3' (e.g. A30, A39) on green signs with white numbers.

GB.title: Devon A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Main A-roads start with '3' (e.g. A38, A377) on green signs with white numbers.

GB.title: Dorset A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Primary A-roads start with '3' (e.g. A35, A354) on green signs with white numbers.

GB.title: Somerset A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Major A-roads start with '3' (e.g. A37, A361) on green signs with white numbers.

GB.title: Wiltshire A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Main A-roads start with '3' (e.g. A303, A346) on green signs with white numbers.

GB.title: Gloucestershire A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Major A-roads start with '4' (e.g. A40, A417) on green signs with white numbers.

GB.title: Bristol A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Primary A-roads start with '4' (e.g. A4, A432) on green signs with white numbers.

GB.title: Cumbria A-Road Numbering
GB.description: In Cumbria, major A-roads typically start with '6', such as A66 or A685. Signs are green with bold white digits, sometimes outlined in white.

GB.title: Cheshire A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Cheshire's main A-roads often begin with '5' or '6', such as A56 or A534. Signs are green with large white numbers, sometimes outlined in white.

GB.title: Lancashire A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Lancashire's major A-roads usually start with '5' or '6', such as A59 or A683. Signs are green with bold white numbers, sometimes outlined in white.

GB.title: Greater Manchester A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Greater Manchester's primary A-roads typically start with '5' or '6', such as A56 or A635. Signs are green with prominent white numbers, sometimes bordered in white.

GB.title: Merseyside A-Road Numbering
GB.description: Merseyside's main A-roads are generally in the '5' series, such as A580 or A5036. Signs are green with large white numbers, sometimes outlined in white.

GB.title: Northern Ireland A-Road Numbering
GB.description: In Northern Ireland, A-roads can start with any digit from 1 to 8, such as A1 or A6. Signs are green with white numbers, sometimes with a white border.

GB.title: Phone Area Codes
GB.description: Landline numbers start with 0 followed by nine or ten digits; the first two to four digits form the area code.

GB.title: City Name on Bins
GB.description: Public rubbish bins in urban areas often display the local council or city name.

GB.title: Scottish Highlands Landscape
GB.description: Open, semi-barren terrain with imposing mountains characterises the Highlands, often brown and yellow in early spring.

GB.title: Scottish Red-and-White Bollards
GB.description: Chunky, round-topped bollards with a red-and-grey reflective band encircling the post appear mainly in Scotland.

GB.title: Scottish Passing Place Signs
GB.description: Diamond-shaped white signs reading 'Passing Place' are exclusive to Scotland's single-track roads.

GB.title: Welsh Language
GB.description: Welsh appears alongside English on road signs throughout Wales, identifiable by D, W, Y, and the double-L digraph (Ll).

GB.title: 'Araf' Road Markings
GB.description: The word 'Araf' (Welsh for 'Slow') painted on roads alongside English is found only in Wales.

GB.title: Scottish Gaelic Language
GB.description: A Celtic language with accent marks and clusters like bh, dh, fh, mh, ai, ea, eo, and ui. Bilingual signs appear mainly north of Glasgow.

GB.title: Cornish Palms
GB.description: Cabbage trees (Cordyline australis), called Cornish palms, are most common along southwest England's coast and Jersey.

GB.title: Northern Ireland Lamppost Stickers
GB.description: Small black stickers with yellow text sometimes appear on street lights in Northern Ireland.

GB.title: London Street Signs
GB.description: London's distinctive street plaques show the road name in black lettering, with the postcode and borough name printed in red beneath.

GB.title: .uk Domain
GB.description: Web addresses in the United Kingdom end in the country domain .uk (usually as .co.uk, and never .gb). Look for it on shop signs, billboards, and text painted on vans and trucks.

UM.title: Albatrosses Everywhere
UM.description: Albatrosses are present in nearly every location on Midway Atoll.

UM.title: Runway Coverage
UM.description: Much of Midway Atoll coverage is on two runways, where albatrosses may be scarce.

UM.title: Other Islands, Trekker Coverage
UM.description: Islands beyond Midway have trekker coverage, low bushy vegetation, and many birds.

UM.title: Well-Paved East-West Runway
UM.description: A nicely paved east-west runway runs on the southern side of Midway Atoll.

UM.title: Deteriorating North-South Runway
UM.description: A north-south runway on Midway has poor pavement worsening toward the north.

UM.title: Small Village on Eastern Midway
UM.description: A small settlement is on the eastern side of Midway Atoll.

UM.title: Southeast Island
UM.description: The least distinctive island, with a small central lake and many birds in the sky.

UM.title: Lisianski Island, Large Bushes
UM.description: Lisianski Island coverage is along the shoreline, encircled by large bushes.

UM.title: Laysan Island, Clear Skies
UM.description: Laysan Island coverage has almost no cloud cover.

UM.title: French Frigate Shoals, Most Birds
UM.description: A long, thin island with a shabby runway and the highest bird density in the chain.

UM.title: Western Runway Corner, Most Common Spawn
UM.description: The western corner of Midway Atoll runway is a common GeoGuessr spawn location.

UM.title: Country Flag
UM.description: The national flag of the US Minor Outlying Islands is visible on flagpoles, official buildings, and occasionally on shop fronts or houses.

VU.title: Location
VU.description: Vanuatu is a Pacific island nation northeast of Brisbane, between the Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, and Fiji.

VU.title: Dark Volcanic Soil
VU.description: Vanuatu's volcanic island has dark volcanic soil frequently appearing along paths.

VU.title: Dense Tropical Forest
VU.description: Much of Vanuatu's coverage passes through dense tropical forest.

VU.title: Black Sand Beach
VU.description: A beach with black volcanic sand appears on the east side of Ambrym Island.

GE.title: Georgian language
GE.description: Georgian uses its own unique script, Mkhedruli, with rounded letters and no uppercase. It is one of the world’s most distinctive languages.

GE.title: Georgia's flag
GE.description: Georgia's flag features one large red cross and four smaller red crosses on a white background.

XK.title: License plates
XK.description: In Kosovo, license plates have a blue strip on the left side.

co-licenseplate.title: Yellow license plate
co-licenseplate.description: In South America, yellow license plates are almost unique to Colombia.

br-language.title: Portuguese
br-language.description: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It uses letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.

br-soil.title: Soil
br-soil.description: The color of the soil can help you guess! This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.

br-states.title: States
br-states.description: Finding state abbreviations is common in Brazil. PR stands for Paraná. The abbreviations can be seen on the map when zoomed out.

ca-bilingual.title: Canada is bilingual
ca-bilingual.description: Some countries like Canada are bi-lingual, meaning they have multiple official languages. In Canada you can find both English and French.

ca-maximum.title: "Maximum" in Canada
ca-maximum.description: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French.

co-language.title: Language
co-language.description: Colombia uses Spanish, as does most other countries in South America.

co-licenseplates.title: Licenseplates
co-licenseplates.description: Looking at license plates can help you find your way in the world. Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow plates.

co-taxi.title: Taxi
co-taxi.description: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.

es-language.title: Language
es-language.description: Most languages have unique words for ‘street’ or ‘road’. In Spanish you will see Calle (street) a lot!

es-roadsign.title: Roadsign
es-roadsign.description: The Spanish crosswalk signs have a lot of stripes on it, making it stand out from most of the other European ones.

es-vegetation.title: Vegetation
es-vegetation.description: Look at the vegetation! You will find more tropical trees such as palm trees as you move closer to the equator.

greece-capital.title: Capital
greece-capital.description: Learning the capitals of countries is a great tool when trying to make a good guess. You can often find signs pointing towards them.

greece-flags.title: Flags
greece-flags.description: Flags are usually found in the country they represent. Learning them can be very beneficial to figure out where you are.

greece-language.title: Language
greece-language.description: Most European countries use the latin alphabet. Greece is one of the outliers that uses their own unique set of letters, the Greek alphabet!

jp-drivingside.title: Drivingside
jp-drivingside.description: Check for driving direction. In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.

jp-machine.title: Machine
jp-machine.description: Some countries have very specific, unique niches. For example does Japan have millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.

jp-vehicles.title: Vehicles
jp-vehicles.description: Vehicles style differs vastly between countries. In Japan small, boxy cars is very common.

kr-drivingside.title: Drivingside
kr-drivingside.description: Check for driving direction. In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.

kr-internetdomains.title: Internetdomains
kr-internetdomains.description: Keep an eye out for internet domains. In South Korea they use .KR at the end of an internet adress.

kr-language.title: Language
kr-language.description: In written Korean you will find a lot of big circles.

mt-achitecture.title: Achitecture
mt-achitecture.description: Take notice of the surrounding architecture and building materials. You will see a lot of walls and building made from limestone in Malta for example.

mt-drivingside.title: Drivingside
mt-drivingside.description: Don’t lose track of which side the cars are driving on. Malta is one of the few European countries that drive on the left.

mt-language.title: English
mt-language.description: Learning the words for street and road in different languages can be really helpful. Triq is the Maltese word and it will only show up in Malta.

mx-drivingside.title: Drivingside
mx-drivingside.description: In Mexico they drive on the right side of the road. As do all other non-island countries in North America.

mx-infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
mx-infrastructure.description: Utility poles will be different country to country. They come in many different colors, shapes and materials. Mexico usually have octagonal poles made of concrete.

mx-taxi.title: Taxi
mx-taxi.description: Taxi cars can often feature useful information, such as the name of the city they are driving in. CDMX is an abbreviation of the Mexican capital Ciudad De Mexico.

nl-landscape.title: Landscape
nl-landscape.description: Landscape can be a great clue to figure out where you are. The Netherlands is very flat for example.

nl-licenseplate.title: Licenseplate
nl-licenseplate.description: License plates on vehicles differ from country to country. In the Netherlands they are yellow, a quite rare sight!

nl-sun.title: Sun
nl-sun.description: You can tell what hemisphere you are in by looking at the sun. A sun to the South usually means you are on the Northern half of the globe.

rs-language-duo.title: Language Duo
rs-language-duo.description: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.

rs-language-letters.title: Language Letters
rs-language-letters.description: There are many different languages using the Cyrillic alphabet. Most of them have a few unique letters. The Serbian language is the only to feature the'Ђ' letter.

rs-poles.title: Poles
rs-poles.description: Utility poles will be different country to country. They come in many different colors, shapes and materials. Serbia will usually have round poles made of concrete.

swe-bollards.title: Bollards
swe-bollards.description: Bollards (small road side poles) usually differs between countries. Learning details like this can make you a great guesser.

swe-language.title: Language
swe-language.description: Use language to your strength. Most languages have unique or prominent letters. The Swedish language uses the letters “Å, Ä and Ö” for example.

swe-licenseplate.title: Licenseplate
swe-licenseplate.description: Most countries in Europe use similar license plates with a blue strip to the left. Sweden included.

th-drivingside.title: Drivingside
th-drivingside.description: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.

th-language.title: Small circles
th-language.description: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.

th-stopsign.title: Stopsign
th-stopsign.description: Stop signs differ between countries. In Thailand the stop signs are written in Thai.

se-language.title: Swedish uses Å, Ä and Ö

dc-au-ausbollard.title: Australian bollards
dc-au-ausbollard.description: Australian bollards are white with a vertical red stripe towards the top.

dc-au-drivingside.title: Au Drivingside
dc-au-drivingside.description: In Australia they drive on the left side of the road.

dc-au-yellowpoles.title: Au Yellowpoles
dc-au-yellowpoles.description: In the state of Western Australia you can find yellow sign posts.

dc-br-language.title: Br Language
dc-br-language.description: Brazil is the only South American country that uses the Portuguese language. It has the letter “Ç”, something Spanish does not.

dc-br-redsoil.title: Br Redsoil
dc-br-redsoil.description: This iron rich, red soil is primarily found in Brazil.

dc-br-states.title: Br States
dc-br-states.description: Finding state abbreviations is common in Brazil. The abbreviations can be seen on the map on certain zoom levels.

dc-ca-speedsign.title: Speed signs
dc-ca-speedsign.description: Speed signs in Canada say ‘Maximum’. This word works in both English and French, the official languages of Canada.

dc-ch-lowcam.title: Ch Lowcam
dc-ch-lowcam.description: In Switzerland the images were captured with a lower mounted camera. This brings us closer to the ground and makes the country feel different from most other.

dc-ch-plates.title: Ch Plates
dc-ch-plates.description: License plates in Switzerland do not feature the blue european strip on the left. Instead the red country emblem can be seen.

dc-co-taxiinfo.title: Co Taxiinfo
dc-co-taxiinfo.description: Taxi cars will often feature useful information such as the name of the city they are driving in.

dc-co-yellowplate.title: Co Yellowplate
dc-co-yellowplate.description: Colombia is the only country in South America that uses all yellow license plates for personal vehicles.

dc-fr-bollard.title: Fr Bollard
dc-fr-bollard.description: The bollards in France are round with a pointy top. They have red or gray reflector that wraps all way around. They are reminiscent of small lighthouses.

dc-gh-ghanatape.title: Gh Ghanatape
dc-gh-ghanatape.description: One of the most (in)famous hints in Geoguessr is the tape on the top-right bar that can be seen when looking down. It can only be found in Ghana.

dc-gh-taxiplates.title: Gh Taxiplates
dc-gh-taxiplates.description: On taxi cars in Ghana you can see the panels around the tires being painted orange.

dc-id-kabupaten.title: Id Kabupaten
dc-id-kabupaten.description: Indonesia is divided into hundreds of regencies know as Kabupaten (Kab. for short). This term is unique to Indonesia.

dc-id-rupiah.title: Id Rupiah
dc-id-rupiah.description: The currency in Indonesia is Rupiah. It is displayed as RP.

dc-it-doublestrip.title: It Doublestrip
dc-it-doublestrip.description: The Italian license plates will have a blue strip on both sides. The front plates are also shorter than usual.

dc-it-signs.title: It Signs
dc-it-signs.description: Directional signs in Italy tend to be bright blue with a white capitalised text.

dc-jo-taxi.title: Jo Taxi
dc-jo-taxi.description: In Amman, the capital of Jordan, you will find taxis in a distinct yellow-and-green palette.

dc-jp-drivingside.title: Jp Drivingside
dc-jp-drivingside.description: In Japan they drive on the left side of the road.

dc-jp-smallcars.title: Jp Smallcars
dc-jp-smallcars.description: In Japan small, boxy cars are very common. They are called Kei cars.

dc-jp-vendingmachine.title: Jp Vendingmachine
dc-jp-vendingmachine.description: Japan has millions of vending machines, making them a common sight here.

dc-kr-circles.title: Kr Circles
dc-kr-circles.description: In written Korean you will find a lot of big circles.

dc-kr-drivingside.title: Kr Drivingside
dc-kr-drivingside.description: In South Korea they drive on the right side of the road.

dc-lk-amongus.title: Lk Amongus
dc-lk-amongus.description: The written Sri Lankan language Sinhala have letters that are very round. Some letter makes it look like there are small doodle characters among us.

dc-lk-drivingside.title: Lk Drivingside
dc-lk-drivingside.description: In Sri Lanka they drive on the left side of the road.

dc-mn-barren.title: Mn Barren
dc-mn-barren.description: The Mongolian landscape is often barren, featuring large open areas without much vegetation.

dc-mn-bollard.title: Mn Bollard
dc-mn-bollard.description: The Mongolian bollard is reminiscent of a bowling pin.

dc-mt-drivingside.title: Mt Drivingside
dc-mt-drivingside.description: Malta is one of the few European countries that drive on the left.

dc-mt-limestone.title: Mt Limestone
dc-mt-limestone.description: You will see a lot of walls and buildings made from limestone in Malta.

dc-mt-triq.title: Mt Triq
dc-mt-triq.description: Triq is the Maltese word for street and it will only show up in Malta.

dc-mx-pinktaxi.title: Mx Pinktaxi
dc-mx-pinktaxi.description: Taxi cars in the Mexican capital are white and pink. They also feature the text CDMX, an abbreviation of Ciudad De Mexico.

dc-mx-poles.title: Mx Poles
dc-mx-poles.description: Mexico usually has octagonal utility poles made of concrete.

dc-nl-flat.title: Nl Flat
dc-nl-flat.description: The Netherlands is a very flat country. You won't find many hills here.

dc-nl-yellowplate.title: Nl Yellowplate
dc-nl-yellowplate.description: In the Netherlands license plates are yellow, quite a rare sight in Europe.

dc-pe-blackwhite.title: Pe Blackwhite
dc-pe-blackwhite.description: Many signposts in Peru are square-shaped and painted in alternating black and white.

dc-pe-conkcreet.title: Pe Conkcreet
dc-pe-conkcreet.description: Metal signs in Peru are standing on visible concrete plinths.

dc-pe-tuktuk.title: Tuk tuks
dc-pe-tuktuk.description: Tuk Tuks are a common sight in Peru. They are usually referred to as mototaxi.

dc-ph-boxes.title: Ph Boxes
dc-ph-boxes.description: In the Philippines city abbreviations can often be found on boxes mounted on utility poles.

dc-ph-conkcreet.title: Ph Conkcreet
dc-ph-conkcreet.description: Roads in the Philippines are often made of big concrete blocks.

dc-ph-drivingside.title: Ph Drivingside
dc-ph-drivingside.description: They drive on the right side of the road in the Philippines.

dc-pl-crossing.title: Pl Crossing
dc-pl-crossing.description: Pedestrian crossing signs in Poland only features a horizontal line. No "zebra stripes" here.

dc-pl-greensign.title: Pl Greensign
dc-pl-greensign.description: Polish road signs often come in a distinct green color with a white text.

dc-pl-holypole.title: Pl Holypole
dc-pl-holypole.description: The utility poles in Poland are often thin and features a lot of holes. These holes usually don't go all the way down.

dc-rs-duo.title: Rs Duo
dc-rs-duo.description: Serbian can be written in both Cyrillic or Latin letters. You can often find both written on signs here.

dc-sn-blueplates.title: Sn Blueplates
dc-sn-blueplates.description: Senegal uses blue license plates, the only country in Africa to do so.

dc-sn-drivingside.title: Sn Drivingside
dc-sn-drivingside.description: In Senegal they drive on the right side of the road.

dc-th-circles.title: Th Circles
dc-th-circles.description: In the written Thai language there is a lot of small circles on the letters.

dc-th-drivingside.title: Th Drivingside
dc-th-drivingside.description: In Thailand they drive on the left side of the road.

dc-th-stop.title: Th Stop
dc-th-stop.description: In Thailand the stop signs are written in Thai.

no_plates_01.title: No_plates_01
no_plates_01.description: In Norway, commercial license plates are green, and are often seen on vans.

br-ladder-poles.title: Ladder poles
br-ladder-poles.description: The poles you often see in Brazil have a ladder-like design at the base. They have horizontal sections near the bottom.

tn-djerba-palms.title: Djerba palm trees
tn-djerba-palms.description: The island of Djerba is known for its many palm trees, which can be seen all across the island.

ca-checkered-signs.title: Checkered signs
ca-checkered-signs.description: In Canada, T-intersection signs are diamond-shaped and have a distinctive checkered pattern.

pt-chimneys.title: Portuguese chimneys
pt-chimneys.description: In southern Portugal, you will often see small chimneys that are either square or round in shape.

kh-poles.title: Cambodian poles
kh-poles.description: In Cambodia, you will typically see either concrete ladder poles with rectangular sections or round poles with small holes.

ar-red-soil.title: Red soil
ar-red-soil.description: In Argentina, red soil is mainly found in the northeastern region, particularly in the panhandle.

us-heb.title: H-E-B supermarket chain
us-heb.description: H-E-B is a supermarket chain that operates exclusively in Texas.

ru-kaliningrad-trees.title: Tree-lined roads
ru-kaliningrad-trees.description: In Russia, roads lined with trees are common in the Kaliningrad region.

es-chevrons.title: Spanish chevrons
es-chevrons.description: In Spain, you can find both black and white chevrons and blue and white chevrons.

mk-road-signs.title: North Macedonian signs
mk-road-signs.description: In North Macedonia, road signs are yellow and black, and town names appear in both Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.

mk-bollard-1.title: Bollard 1
mk-bollard-1.description: One type of bollard in North Macedonia has a trapezoid shape, colored white and black, with a red reflective strip.

jo-google-car.title: Black Google car
jo-google-car.description: In Jordan, the Street View coverage was captured by a black Google car.

jp-yamaguchi-guardrails.title: Yellow guardrails
jp-yamaguchi-guardrails.description: Yamaguchi Prefecture in Japan is recognized for its distinctive bright yellow roadside guardrails.

ng-northern-clothing.title: Islamic outfits
ng-northern-clothing.description: You are more likely to see women wearing hijabs and men dressed in traditional Islamic outfits in the northern regions of Nigeria.

be-orange-signs.title: Orange signs
be-orange-signs.description: In Belgium, you will often find orange signposts and sign backs.

tr-grainy-roads.title: Grainy roads
tr-grainy-roads.description: Many roads in Turkey have a grainy look from the mix of light and dark local stones used in the asphalt.

ch-framed-signs.title: Framed Signs
ch-framed-signs.description: In Switzerland, many road signs have a thin metal border that gives them a clean, framed look.

ae-road-lines.title: Emirati road lines
ae-road-lines.description: In the UAE, outer road lines are yellow, while the center lines can be white or yellow.

kg-license-plates.title: Red strip
kg-license-plates.description: Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan feature a red strip on the left side.

mo-license-plates.title: Black license plates
mo-license-plates.description: In Macau, cars have black licence plates.

mo-portuguese-signs.title: Portuguese signs
mo-portuguese-signs.description: Portuguese often appears alongside Chinese on signs in Macau, reflecting its history as a Portuguese colony.

ec-bollards.title: Ecuadorian bollards
ec-bollards.description: In Ecuador, bollards are typically either thin and round with two red stripes or flat with two red reflectors.

lu-license-plates.title: Yellow license plates
lu-license-plates.description: In Luxembourg, cars have yellow license plates with a blue strip on the left side.

id-bali-crowns.title: Ornaments on roofs
id-bali-crowns.description: In Bali, you can often spot murdha, decorative crown like ornaments placed along the tops of traditional roofs.

in-dry-landscape.title: Dry landscape
in-dry-landscape.description: Some parts of the northern Himalayan region administered by India are known for dry, high altitude landscapes with very little vegetation.

sn-license-plates.title: Senegalese license plates
sn-license-plates.description: In Senegal, older plates are fully blue, while newer ones have just a blue strip on the left side.

sn-dashed-lines.title: Senegalese road lines
sn-dashed-lines.description: In Senegal, roads often have long white dashed lines along the sides.

cy-water-tanks.title: White water tanks
cy-water-tanks.description: In Cyprus, buildings often have a white, horizontal water tank with a round lid.

pe-poles.title: Peruvian poles
pe-poles.description: In Peru, you can often see concrete utility poles with three horizontal crossarms.

bd-bengali.title: Bengali language
bd-bengali.description: Bengali is an official language of Bangladesh, and its script has a horizontal line across the top of each word.

lt-poles.title: Square poles
lt-poles.description: In Lithuania, utility poles are usually square concrete posts with a diagonal support beam.

mx-electricity-counters.title: Electricity meters
mx-electricity-counters.description: Mexico, along with several Central American countries, uses circular electricity meters.

pl-warning-signs.title: Warning signs
pl-warning-signs.description: Poland's warning signs are triangular with a yellow background and a thin red border.

za-chevrons.title: South African chevrons
za-chevrons.description: South Africa uses red and white chevron signs, and small, thin chevrons with a single arrow are common across Southern African countries.

kr-jeju-walls.title: Rock walls
kr-jeju-walls.description: Jeju Island in South Korea is known for its many rock walls made from dark volcanic stone.

de-green-sticker.title: Green sticker
de-green-sticker.description: In Germany, most cars have a green circular sticker on the bottom right of the windshield.

se-short-lines.title: Short dashes
se-short-lines.description: In Sweden, the outer road lines often have short, white dashed markings.

ug-google-car.title: White car
ug-google-car.description: Street View in Kampala has a white Google car with rectangular side mirrors.

nl-brick-roads.title: Brick roads
nl-brick-roads.description: Brick roads are common throughout the Netherlands.

bo-curvy-poles.title: Curvy poles
bo-curvy-poles.description: In eastern Bolivia, many wooden utility poles are noticeably curvy.

gr-faded-lines.title: Double white lines
gr-faded-lines.description: You will often see worn double white center lines in Greece.

co-colombian-cross.title: Colombian Cross
co-colombian-cross.description: In Colombia, signposts have white backs that form a cross shape, known as the Colombian Cross.

uy-signposts.title: White signposts
uy-signposts.description: You will often find thick and white wooden signposts in Uruguay.

uy-triple-road-lines.title: Triple road lines
uy-triple-road-lines.description: In Uruguay, you can find triple road markings, double yellow lines with a white dashed line running between them.

nz-give-way.title: Red text
nz-give-way.description: In New Zealand, Give Way signs feature red text and a small white outline.

at-vienna-signs.title: Vienna street signs
at-vienna-signs.description: In Vienna, street signs appear as dark blue plaques, with the first number indicating the district.

at-red-white-tape.title: Red and white tape
at-red-white-tape.description: In Vienna and some smaller Austrian cities, signposts have red and white tape, resembling the Austrian flag.

fi-license-plates.title: Shorter plates
fi-license-plates.description: In Finland, license plates are slightly shorter than in most other European countries, and they include the standard EU blue strip on the left.

vn-language.title: Vietnamese language
vn-language.description: The Vietnamese language is written in a modified Latin script that features an extensive system of diacritical marks.

ro-holey-poles.title: Holey poles
ro-holey-poles.description: In Romania, you will frequently come across so called holey poles, with holes running all the way down to the ground.

rw-license-plates.title: Rwanda plates
rw-license-plates.description: Rwanda has long license plates, with white plates on the front and yellow plates on the back.

uk-lines-reflectors.title: Small reflectors
uk-lines-reflectors.description: Dashed center lines with reflectors set between them are a good road marking clue for the UK.

ad-stone-buildings.title: Stone buildings
ad-stone-buildings.description: Stone buildings are common all across Andorra.

ar-license-plates-black.title: License Plates Black
ar-license-plates-black.description: Argentina uses two styles of license plates. One type has what appears to be a black dot in the middle.

ar-license-plates-blue.title: License Plates Blue
ar-license-plates-blue.description: Argentina uses two styles of license plates. One type has got a blue strip across the top.

pt-azores-rock.title: Stone walls
pt-azores-rock.description: Across the Azores, you will often see dry stone walls crafted from dark volcanic rock.

tr-stop.title: Stop signs
tr-stop.description: In Turkey, stop signs say "DUR", which is unique to the country.

my-black-sticker.title: Marked poles
my-black-sticker.description: In mainland Malaysia, electricity poles often have black stickers on them.

ru-black-socks.title: Black socks
ru-black-socks.description: In Russia, signposts often have their lower sections painted black.

mn-tent-car.title: Tent car
mn-tent-car.description: In Mongolia the google car is often visible. It takes many shapes but usually a tent can be seen packed on the car.

lk-holey-poles.title: Sri Lanka poles
lk-holey-poles.description: Sri Lanka commonly uses concrete utility poles with large see through holes in the lower half, often called holey poles

is-pedestrian-signs.title: Pedestrian crossings
is-pedestrian-signs.description: In Iceland, you will see pedestrian crossing signs with four stripes at the bottom and a subtle yellow hue.

ke-safaricom.title: Mobile network
ke-safaricom.description: The mobile network Safaricom is exclusive to Kenya, and its branded signage appears in almost every town.

kz-tree-trunks.title: Tree trunks
kz-tree-trunks.description: The bottom of tree trunks in Kazakhstan are often painted white.

pa-taxis.title: Checkered taxis
pa-taxis.description: Yellow taxis marked with a horizontal checkered stripe are a common sight in Panama.

hu-utca.title: Street signs
hu-utca.description: Street names in Hungary usually end with the word "utca".

na-road-lines.title: Road lines
na-road-lines.description: Like many countries in Southern Africa, Namibia uses roads with single yellow outer lines and white center lines.

lb-bad-quality.title: Bad camera
lb-bad-quality.description: Lebanon is currently the only Middle Eastern country with official low-quality camera coverage.

cl-white-lines.title: White lines
cl-white-lines.description: In Chile, you will usually see all white road lines.

ua-red-car.title: Red car
ua-red-car.description: In Ukraine, you will most often see the back of a red Google car.

bw-signposts.title: Black and yellow signposts
bw-signposts.description: If you're in southern Africa and come across this, you know you're in Botswana.

ng-police-car.title: Call the police!
ng-police-car.description: A police vehicle, usually white or black, trails the Nigerian Street View car in nearly every coverage. The exact model may differ from images shown.

fr-blue-strips.title: Blue stickers
fr-blue-strips.description: Small blue rectangular "stickers" on utility poles are a distinctive clue for France.

in-camera-quality.title: Bad quality
in-camera-quality.description: The majority of Indian coverage comes from a notoriously poor camera, recognized by low sharpness and washed-out colors.

gl-tasiilaq.title: Quad bike
gl-tasiilaq.description: In Tasiilaq, you can usually recognize the coverage by the quad bike with large grey handguards.

ie-yellow-lines.title: Dashed outer lines
ie-yellow-lines.description: Irish roads often have dashed yellow outlines.

cz-arrow-signs.title: Arrow Signs
cz-arrow-signs.description: Directional signs in Czechia taper to a solid filled arrow tip.

cr-stop-signs.title: Stop signs
cr-stop-signs.description: In Costa Rica, stop signs show the word "ALTO" instead of "STOP".

ph-jeepneys.title: Jeepneys
ph-jeepneys.description: In the Philippines it is common to find jeepneys in urban environments. They are often heavily decorated.

bw-license-plates.title: Yellow rear plates
bw-license-plates.description: Botswana and Namibia are the only countries in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are the norm.

bw-nature.title: Arid landscape
bw-nature.description: The terrain in Botswana is predominantly flat and arid with scattered small trees. Soil is generally sandy and pale white.

bw-roadnumbers.title: Road numbers
bw-roadnumbers.description: Wayfinding signs use a green background, consistent with the wider southern African convention. Only in Botswana do major roads start with an A.

sz-roadnumbers.title: Road numbers
sz-roadnumbers.description: Roads prefixed with the letters "MR" are found exclusively in Eswatini.

sz-busshelter.title: Bus shelters
sz-busshelter.description: Distinctive concrete bus shelters appear frequently along Eswatini's roads.

sz-roadline.title: Yellow road lines
sz-roadline.description: Just like most southern African countries, Eswatini's roads feature yellow outer lines.

gh-license-plates.title: Yellow and white plates
gh-license-plates.description: In Ghana private vehicles carry white plates, while commercial vehicles use yellow ones. Both colours are frequently visible.

gh-nature.title: Red soil
gh-nature.description: The terrain in Ghana is predominantly flat and lush, with characteristic red laterite soil.

ke-snorkel.title: Snorkel
ke-snorkel.description: Kenyan coverage features distinctive vehicles very often equipped with a snorkel.

ke-followcar.title: Follow car
ke-followcar.description: A grey Toyota SUV can frequently be seen trailing the Street View car in Kenyan coverage.

ke-license-plates.title: Yellow rear plates
ke-license-plates.description: Kenyan vehicles carry long white front plates and square yellow rear plates.

ls-mountains.title: Mountains
ls-mountains.description: Bare, treeless mountains with flat tabletop profiles and prominent horizontal rock ridgelines are Lesotho's signature feature.

ls-architecture.title: Round huts
ls-architecture.description: Round thatched-roof huts appear frequently in rural Lesotho.

ls-vehicles.title: Driving side
ls-vehicles.description: Lesotho drives on the left, in common with its southern African neighbours.

ls-grass.title: Short grass
ls-grass.description: Lesotho's grasslands consist predominantly of short grass, unlike Eswatini which in general has tall grass.

mg-vehicles.title: A wild ride
mg-vehicles.description: Much of the Madagascar coverage was captured using different types of transportation, including boats and cow carts.

mg-people.title: A personal touch
mg-people.description: The people capturing the Madagascar images can often be seen in them.

mg-baobabs.title: Baobabs
mg-baobabs.description: The famous Avenue of the Baobabs is unmistakable thanks to the enormously thick-trunked baobab trees flanking the road.

mg-nature.title: Varying nature
mg-nature.description: Madagascar's southern and central regions tend to be very arid, while the north is tropical and lush.

na-license-plates.title: Yellow plates
na-license-plates.description: Vehicles in Namibia typically carry yellow plates on both front and rear.

na-truck.title: White truck
na-truck.description: Namibian Street View coverage was captured using a white pickup truck equipped with a short front-mounted antenna that consistently tilts slightly to the left.

na-germanvibes.title: German colonial influence
na-germanvibes.description: Due to its history as a German colony, Namibia retains visible Germanic influence, particularly in place names and the architectural style of some older buildings.

na-nature.title: Desert landscape
na-nature.description: Desert-like landscape dominates most of Namibia, although there are a few exceptions to this.

ng-googletruck.title: Trucks
ng-googletruck.description: Most Nigerian coverage shows the Google car, a pickup truck with the cab and bed visible. The cab colour and other features vary.

ng-badcam.title: Bad camera
ng-badcam.description: Nigeria is currently the only mainland African country with official low-quality street view coverage.

rw-brakelight.title: Brake light
rw-brakelight.description: The Google car, a large pickup truck, is fully visible in most Rwandan imagery and distinctively has a visible brake light.

rw-nature.title: Red soil
rw-nature.description: Most soil across Rwanda has a noticeable reddish tint.

rw-bikers.title: Bikers wear red!
rw-bikers.description: In Rwanda, all motorcyclists are required to wear red vests and helmets.

st-badcam.title: Bad camera
st-badcam.description: The entire São Tomé and Príncipe street view coverage was done using official low-quality camera, with a blur completely covering the car.

st-language.title: Portuguese colonial influence
st-language.description: Portuguese is the primary language of São Tomé and Príncipe and can hence be seen on most signs.

st-yellowtaxi.title: Yellow taxis
st-yellowtaxi.description: All cabs in São Tomé and Príncipe are yellow.

st-nature.title: The tropics
st-nature.description: São Tomé and Príncipe is located on the equator so you'll find rainforest all over the country.

sn-googletruck.title: Big truck
sn-googletruck.description: In most of the Senegal coverage a silver, white or black truck is visible.

sn-language.title: French colonial influence
sn-language.description: In Senegal, French is the official language and dominates all visible signage.

za-language.title: Afrikaans
za-language.description: South Africa has eleven official languages. While English dominates signage, the Dutch-like language Afrikaans has had a big influence on for example city names.

za-direction-signs.title: Green directional signs
za-direction-signs.description: South African directional signs are green with yellow road numbers. Road-numbers starting with N or R are exclusive to South Africa.

za-security.title: High security
za-security.description: In South Africa, suburban homes in and around major cities are commonly enclosed behind tall walls, fences, and gates.

ug-capital.title: Go capital
ug-capital.description: Almost all Ugandan coverage is in or near the capital Kampala.

ug-license-plates.title: Yellow rear plates
ug-license-plates.description: Ugandan vehicles have white front plates and yellow rear plates.

ug-nature-red.title: Red soil
ug-nature-red.description: Soil in Uganda is distinctly red, even paved roads have a redlike tint.

tn-license-plates.title: Black license plates
tn-license-plates.description: Tunisian license plates are black with white text. They are the only African country to have that.

tn-language.title: French and Arabic
tn-language.description: Tunisia is the only street view country combining French and Arabic. Bilingual signage appears frequently, with Arabic identifiable by its lines and dots.

tn-nature.title: Arid landscape
tn-nature.description: Bordering the Mediterranean, the Tunisian landscape is in general dry.

bd-language.title: Triangular letters
bd-language.description: Bengali, the language in Bangladesh has got a lot of triangular shapes, something similar scripts do not feature.

bd-rickshaw.title: Rickshaws
bd-rickshaw.description: Rickshaws appear constantly throughout Bangladesh, with green motorized auto rickshaws being especially common.

bd-road.title: Roadside water and fields
bd-road.description: Ponds, canals, and agricultural plots running alongside the road are a common sight across Bangladesh.

bt-license-plates.title: Red plates
bt-license-plates.description: Bhutanese vehicles carry distinctive red license plates that are easy to spot even from a distance.

bt-road.title: Safety blocks
bt-road.description: Rows of stone blocks serve as barriers along rural roads, one of the most reliable visual cues for recognising Bhutan.

bt-flags.title: Prayer flags
bt-flags.description: Colorful prayer flags strung alongside roads are a common sight throughout Bhutan.

bt-architecture.title: Traditional buildings
bt-architecture.description: Traditional Bhutanese buildings have ornately painted wooden window and door frames.

kh-license-plates.title: White license plates
kh-license-plates.description: Cambodian plates are white with blue lettering, though the blue is often hard to see through the blur, making them look white.

kh-language.title: Khmer script
kh-language.description: The Khmer writing system has a highly recognisable script, with intricate, curvy letterforms in most fonts.

cx-license-plates.title: Yellow licence plates
cx-license-plates.description: Vehicles on the Christmas Island carry yellow license plates.

cx-bollards.title: Australian-style bollards
cx-bollards.description: Bollards on Christmas Island are identical to the Australian ones. White with a red vertical stripe on the front.

cx-crab.title: Crab rave
cx-crab.description: There are areas on Christmas island with large amounts of crabs. You can also find crab-related traffic signs throughout the island.

cy-license-plates.title: Three styles
cy-license-plates.description: License plates in Cyprus can come in many colors. White and yellow for regular cars and red for rentals.

cy-bollards.title: Triangular bollards
cy-bollards.description: Cyprus has white, triangular bollards with slanted tops. A small reflector on the front is red and white on the back.

hk-ac.title: Air conditioners
hk-ac.description: Wall-mounted air-conditioning units are a common sight in Hong Kong.

hk-language.title: Bilingual signage
hk-language.description: Signage in Hong Kong routinely pairs English text with traditional Chinese characters.

hk-taxis.title: Colour-coded taxis
hk-taxis.description: Taxis in distinct colors are often seen in Hong Kong. There are red, blue and green ones. They have green stickers on the bumpers.

hk-architecture.title: Towering apartment blocks
hk-architecture.description: Residential tower blocks in Hong Kong are exceptionally tall, visibly taller than their counterparts in nearby countries.

in-language.title: Underscore but above
in-language.description: India has many different languages. If you see written text with a continuous line running along the top of each word, you are in the central or northern parts of the country.

in-english.title: English
in-english.description: As one of India's official languages, English is widely present on signs and boards across the country.

id-road-signs.title: Yellow waystones
id-road-signs.description: In Indonesia you can find yellow distance markers tilted towards the road, with a notch cut near the top. They list shorthand names for three destinations.

il-license-plates.title: Yellow license plates
il-license-plates.description: License plates in Israel are yellow and have a blue strip on the left.

il-stop-signs.title: Literal stop signage
il-stop-signs.description: Israeli stop signs have no text. Instead they depict a raised hand, a common sign for stopping.

il-language.title: Written Hebrew
il-language.description: The most common text seen in Israel is Hebrew. It looks a bit blocky and has letters with mostly uniform height.

il-small-road-signs.title: Colorful small signs
il-small-road-signs.description: In Israel you can find these small sings alongside roads. They come in red, green and blue.

jo-language.title: Arabic
jo-language.description: In Jordan Arabic is the official language, recognisable by its connected script of lines and dots. Commercial signage rarely includes English.

jo-chevron.title: White and red chevrons
jo-chevron.description: The chevrons in Jordan are white with red arrows.

kz-license-plates.title: White license plates
kz-license-plates.description: Standard Kazakh plates appear mostly white when blurred, with a small blue patch visible on the left side.

kz-truck.title: White pickup truck
kz-truck.description: All Kazakh Street View imagery was captured using a white pickup truck, which may be fully visible or partially blurred out.

kz-crossing.title: Pedestrian crossing
kz-crossing.description: Kazakh pedestrian crossings use yellow and white stripes and have white dashes running along either side. Sometimes only the dashes appear without the stripes.

kg-googlecar.title: Silver car
kg-googlecar.description: A silver Google car with four visible bars is used for all coverage in Kyrgyzstan.

kg-winter.title: Winter imagery
kg-winter.description: All Kyrgyz Street View coverage was captured in winter, so expect bare trees, dull-looking terrain, and snow in many places.

kg-bollards.title: Kyrgyz bollards
kg-bollards.description: Kyrgyzstan uses white bollards featuring a diagonal black stripe near the top.

kg-religion.title: Mosques
kg-religion.description: Kyrgyzstan has a majority Muslim population, so mosques are a common sight across the country.

la-language.title: Lao script
la-language.description: Lao writing is compact and rounded, with diacritical marks above and below characters.

la-goolgecar.title: Visible car
la-goolgecar.description: In Laos the google car is visible with a bars sticking out. In the capital Vientiane the car is however not visible.

la-architecture.title: Buddhist temples
la-architecture.description: As a predominantly Buddhist country, Laos is filled with ornately decorated temples, often featuring gold leaf detailing.

la-stop-signs.title: Stop signs
la-stop-signs.description: Laotian stop signs display Lao script, sometimes with 'STOP' in Latin underneath. The Lao text uses only two characters.

lb-language.title: Arabic, French and English
lb-language.description: Lebanon's official language is Arabic, but French and English signage is widespread.

lb-license-plates.title: White and red plates
lb-license-plates.description: Lebanese plates come in long and short formats, each with a blue strip on the left resembling European plates. Taxi plates are deep red.

my-stop-signs.title: Unique stop signs
my-stop-signs.description: Stop signs saying "BERHENTI" are unique to Malaysia.

my-road-lines.title: White center lines
my-road-lines.description: Two-lane roads often feature double white center lines, Malaysia is the only Southeast Asian country that does this.

my-license-plates.title: Malay plates
my-license-plates.description: Malaysian plates are black with two white sections, easily visible even through blurring.

mn-stop-signs.title: Unique stop sign
mn-stop-signs.description: The Mongolian stop signs are written in Mongolian Cyrillic. They are unique to say "ЗОГС".

np-license-plates.title: Napal plates
np-license-plates.description: Nepal uses long plates. The standard versions are white, while private vehicles carry red plates and public transport uses black ones.

np-badcam.title: Bad camera
np-badcam.description: All imagery in Nepal comes from a notoriously poor camera, recognized by low sharpness and washed-out colors.

np-road.title: Yellow outer lines
np-road.description: Nepali roads frequently have yellow edge markings, either dashed or solid, paired with white dashed center lines on wider routes.

np-bollards.title: Concrete bollards
np-bollards.description: Roadside bollards in Nepal are concrete with alternating black and white stripes (between 3 and 5 bands) and typically have a red mark on the cap.

om-license-plates.title: Colored plates
om-license-plates.description: Omani private vehicles carry yellow licence plates, whereas commercial vehicles have red ones.

om-nature.title: Desert landscape
om-nature.description: Oman is dominated by arid, sparsely vegetated terrain. The central and southern interior is largely flat, while the northern coastline has dry, rugged mountains

om-road-signs.title: Chevrons
om-road-signs.description: Chevrons in Oman are yellow with black arrows and stand out for having an unusually high number of arrow markings.

om-googlgecar.title: White truck
om-googlgecar.description: All Omani Street View imagery was captured using a white pickup truck. As a result, a large portion of the vehicle or a prominent front blur is typically visible.

ph-language.title: English
ph-language.description: English is one of the official languages in the Philippines and appears on signs frequently.

qa-license-plates.title: Long and short
qa-license-plates.description: Qatari private vehicles carry long white plates with a maroon strip on the left. Trucks have square black plates, and police vehicles use blue plates.

qa-nature.title: Flat desert
qa-nature.description: Qatar is an almost entirely flat, arid desert with vast sand expanses and very little greenery.

qa-crossing-signs.title: Crossing sign
qa-crossing-signs.description: Qatari pedestrian crossing signs depict a man wearing a traditional thobe.

hr-stickers.title: Country stickers
hr-stickers.description: Oval stickers bearing the letters 'HR' can be sometimes be spotted on Croatian vehicles.

qa-football.title: Football fever
qa-football.description: Coverage taken before the 2022 FIFA World Cup frequently shows promotional banners for the event.

lv-bus-signs.title: Bus stop signs
lv-bus-signs.description: Latvian bus stop signs feature a bus icon with five windows, distinguishing it from the four-window design used in Lithuania and Estonia.

ar-chevrons.title: Argentina chevrons
ar-chevrons.description: Argentina is the only South American country that has white chevrons with red arrows.

ru-license-plates.title: Long, white plates
ru-license-plates.description: Russian plates are entirely white with black text and lack the blue EU-style strip found on most European plates.

ru-bollardspam.title: Bollard bonanza
ru-bollardspam.description: Intersections in Russia frequently feature unusually large clusters of bollards, far more densely packed than in most other countries.

ru-asian-vehicles.title: Asian cars
ru-asian-vehicles.description: Japanese-made vehicles with the steering wheel on the right become increasingly common the further east you go in Russia.

ru-language.title: Cyrillic script
ru-language.description: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet. It is the only script showing up on most signs.

sg-street-signs.title: Street name signs
sg-street-signs.description: Singaporean street signs are green with round edges. They have a very distinctive white font.

sg-vehicles-bus.title: Green buses
sg-vehicles-bus.description: In Singapore, most buses are lime-green.

sg-littering.title: No litter
sg-littering.description: Singapore is exceptionally clean and have orderly streets as there are heavy fines for littering.

sg-language.title: English
sg-language.description: English is the common language in Singapore, with exclusive use in numerous public services.

kr-polestripes.title: Pole markings
kr-polestripes.description: South Korean utility poles often carry black-and-yellow diagonal stripes near the base. The stripes do not reach the ground.

lk-license-plates.title: White and yellow
lk-license-plates.description: Sri Lankan license plates are white in the front and yellow in the rear.

lk-tapered-bollards.title: Tapered bollards
lk-tapered-bollards.description: In Sri Lanka you can find short, tapered stone bollards. They are white with a black base.

tw-language.title: Traditional Chinese
tw-language.description: Taiwanese signage uses Traditional Chinese, a complex script with intricate multi-stroke characters.

tw-polestripes.title: Pole markings
tw-polestripes.description: In Taiwan, nearly all utility poles carry diagonal black-and-yellow striped markings that most often run all the way down to the ground.

tw-bollards.title: Dotted bollards
tw-bollards.description: Taiwanese bollards feature two or three circular reflectors on a black rectangle.

tw-noparking.title: No parking
tw-noparking.description: Red-painted edge lines indicating no parking appear frequently, especially in urban areas, essentially unique to Taiwan.

th-flags.title: Many flags
th-flags.description: In Thailand, flags are commonly hung along streets. Besides the national flag, yellow royal banners appear frequently.

th-road-signposts.title: Signposts
th-road-signposts.description: Thai sign-mounting posts are thick and square-shaped, typically white, with the lower portion painted black.

th-license-plates.title: Thai plates
th-license-plates.description: In Thailand, passenger vehicles carry large white plates. Commercial vehicles have yellow plates instead.

ae-desert.title: Desert landscape
ae-desert.description: The natural terrain in UAE is predominantly flat and arid, with open desert stretching in every direction.

ae-unpaved-road.title: Unpaved roads
ae-unpaved-road.description: Despite the country's wealth, it is not unusual to encounter unpaved roads in residential areas.

vn-bollards.title: Concrete bollards
vn-bollards.description: Small concrete bollards are the most common ones in Vietnam. They have a red top.

vn-pole-box.title: Electricity boxes
vn-pole-box.description: Grey electricity boxes can be seen mounted to utility poles in Vietnam. They are tapered towards the bottom and have a few windows.

uy-bollards.title: Two faced bollards
uy-bollards.description: Bollards in Uruguay are fully white on the front, and fully yellow on the back,

uy-tridentpole.title: Trident poles
uy-tridentpole.description: A common variation of the many Uruguayan poles are the so-called trident poles with three insulators all pointing upwards.

co-paintedpole.title: Painted poles
co-paintedpole.description: Colombian poles can be found painted with black-yellow-black stripes.

co-fences.title: Rickety fences
co-fences.description: It is common to find wooden fences in Colombia, often made from various pieces of wood.

bo-license-plates.title: Short white plates
bo-license-plates.description: Bolivia uses short plates. They will look white or slightly blue.

bo-bricksonbricks.title: Red bricks
bo-bricksonbricks.description: Buildings featuring big exposed red bricks is a common sight in Bolivia.

bo-clothes.title: Traditional clothes
bo-clothes.description: Bowler hats and large skirts are outfits commonly seen in Bolivia.

cl-yellow-lines.title: Yellow or white lines
cl-yellow-lines.description: Chile can have either fully yellow or fully white lines. The two colors are almost never combined.

cl-bollards.title: Rare bollards
cl-bollards.description: Chilean bollards are white with a white reflector on the front, and a yellow on the back. They are overall quite a rare sight.

cl-concrete-pole.title: Concrete poles
cl-concrete-pole.description: You will find rectangular, indented concrete poles in Chile. The upper part typically has small pinholes.

ec-ladderpole.title: Ladder poles
ec-ladderpole.description: In Ecuador you can find these poles with a large amount of indents, referred to as ladder poles.

ec-concrete-road.title: Concrete roads
ec-concrete-road.description: It is fairly common to find concrete roads in Ecuador.

nz-bollards.title: New Zealand bollards
nz-bollards.description: Bollards in New Zealand feature a red strip that wraps around the back, extending partially across the front.

nz-triangles.title: Intersection triangles
nz-triangles.description: Triangles can be found painted on the road at intersections in New Zealand.

au-give-way.title: Black text
au-give-way.description: "Give way" signs in Australia have black text and a white outer border.

ca-metric.title: The metric system
ca-metric.description: Canada uses the metric system and thus displays speed in kilometers per hours (km/h).

ca-french-east.title: French to the east
ca-french-east.description: In Canada, written French will mainly be found in the provinces of Québec and New Brunswick.

cw-road-signs.title: Overflowing color
cw-road-signs.description: In Curaçao road signs borders can be seen wrapping over to the back. These borders are usually blue or red.

cw-googlecar.title: Unique car
cw-googlecar.description: The Curaçao images were taken by a black car with visible bars, a combination unique to this island.

cw-language.title: Far from home
cw-language.description: Curaçao is part of the Netherlands and uses the Dutch language.

do-stop-signs.title: Stop signs
do-stop-signs.description: The Dominican Republic stop signs say 'PARE'. This is unlike most other North American countries.

do-license-plates.title: Gradient plates
do-license-plates.description: License plates in the Dominican Republic fade from yellow at the top to white at the bottom.

do-googlecar.title: Rubberized bars
do-googlecar.description: If you see bars with thick rubber strips when looking down then you are guaranteed to be in the Dominican Republic.

gl-architecture.title: Colorful houses
gl-architecture.description: Most residential buildings on Greenland are painted in bright colors, often red, green or blue.

gl-barren.title: Cold barrens
gl-barren.description: The terrain on Greenland is entirely devoid of trees and tall plants. The ground is frequently blanketed in snow.

gl-shore.title: Close to water
gl-shore.description: You are bound to spot water in Greenland as almost all settlements are set on the shore.

gt-painted-pole.title: Painted poles
gt-painted-pole.description: Seeing utility poles painted pink is a common occurrence in Guatemala. Other colors such as green appears as well.

gt-googlecar.title: Visible bars
gt-googlecar.description: All vehicle-based coverage in Guatemala uses a grey car whose roof rack and side mirrors are visible through the blur.

gt-license-plates.title: Compact plates
gt-license-plates.description: Guatemalan plates are compact. When blurred, they typically show either a blue or green tint.

pa-stop-sign.title: Stop sign
pa-stop-sign.description: Like most other Spanish speaking countries in North America, stop signs in Panama say ALTO.

br-black-signs.title: Black signs
br-black-signs.description: Most road signs in Brazil have black backsides.

sz-tall-grass.title: Tall grass
sz-tall-grass.description: Eswatini features stretches of tall grass.

es-road-markers.title: Road markers
es-road-markers.description: Distance markers along Spanish roads are recognisable by their colourful borders and the road number printed at the top.

us-mail-boxes.title: Mailboxes
us-mail-boxes.description: Mailboxes with a small flag are a common sight in North America.

jp-overhead-arrows.title: Overhead arrows
jp-overhead-arrows.description: This arrow above the road marks the road during heavy snow and is mainly seen in Hokkaido.

bg-bilingual-signs.title: Bilingual signs
bg-bilingual-signs.description: Road direction signs in Bulgaria are blue, arrow-shaped, and printed in both Cyrillic and Latin script.

pa-license-plates.title: Panama plates
